sections.heading: What an in-home IB tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, and what the travel adds
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for this search publish no figure at all, and two of them quote United States dollars. Here is the market in dirhams, with each range attributed. Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the UAE puts in-home tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors going to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, and Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

The difference between those two bands is not teaching quality and it is not seniority. It is a car. A tutor driving from the island to Al Reef for a 17:30 hour has committed somewhere between ninety minutes and two hours of unpaid time to a sixty-minute lesson, and no rational person absorbs that. It is recovered in the rate, in a minimum booking length, or in a quiet preference for students who live nearby, which is how a family ends up with the closest tutor rather than the right one.

Monthly packages visible in the market make the gap concrete. Around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions. In-home packages of four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. None of these is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card on these pages: the free trial lesson and the conversation after it are where a quote comes from.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi drive, and what it does to a 17:00 start
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi is laid out as an island city with a mainland that keeps extending, which produces long, predictable journeys rather than short unpredictable ones. A tutor who lives on the island and teaches in Al Shamkha is committing to a real expedition, and the hour between 17:00 and 18:00 is when everyone else is making the same trip in the opposite direction. The table below is a planning assumption, not a measurement, and it should be checked against your own experience of the route at the hour you want.

What the drive does to the lesson is the part worth thinking about. A tutor who arrives nine minutes late has lost nine minutes of a paid hour, and will usually still leave on time because another student is waiting. A tutor who hits an unusually bad run arrives at 17:50 for a 17:30 session with a student whose attention is already gone. Across a term, a weekly session losing ten minutes to traffic has lost most of a lesson, and nobody records it anywhere.

The second-order effect is on the slot itself. In-home scheduling pushes sessions towards the earliest hour the tutor can physically manage after their own working day, which is frequently the worst hour for the student: straight off a school bus, before food, in the heat. Video scheduling has no travel constraint, so a session can sit at 19:30 after a break and a meal. Of all the arguments for online delivery in this emirate, that one produces the most visible difference in the first fortnight.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in Abu Dhabi?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody asks and the one with the clearest answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The ministry's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

The eligibility list is broader than most families assume. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. So a university student tutoring GCSE mathematics in the evening is not operating outside the system by definition, provided they hold the permit. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Two cautions belong here. No fine schedule is published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including us. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. Nobody should describe themselves as approved by a regulator unless they hold the specific permit and can show the number. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or licence of any kind, and says so.

sections.heading: The ethics rule that makes your child's own teacher the wrong choice
paragraphs: The most common in-home arrangement in this market is also the most problematic: paying a teacher at the child's own school. It is attractive for obvious reasons. They know the scheme of work, they know the cohort, and they may be the person who writes the predicted grade. That last point is the problem rather than the attraction.

ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document itself, so verify the current wording against ADEK before relying on it. The structural point does not depend on the citation: the person assessing your child should not also be invoicing you.

There is a quieter benefit to an outside tutor that families discover afterwards. A student who has misunderstood something taught by their own teacher often will not say so to that teacher, because the admission carries a social cost in a classroom they return to on Monday. A different adult, marking against the published criteria rather than against their own lesson, gets a straighter answer about what is not understood. That independence is worth more than familiarity with the scheme of work, which any competent subject specialist can reconstruct from the student's own exercise book.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for an Abu Dhabi household
paragraphs: Here is the comparison without the sales layer. In-home visiting wins on three things: physical management of a young child, a parent's ability to overhear, and the absence of any technology to go wrong. Online wins on pool size, scheduling freedom, cost, the existence of a recording, and the fact that nobody is in a car at 17:30 in August. For a Diploma student the second list decides it; for a seven-year-old the first list might.

The pool argument deserves a number rather than an adjective. Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is spread across many schools, and the subset of qualified specialists for any given Higher Level subject who also live within a reasonable drive of a specific community and are free at a specific hour is frequently empty. A family that insists on physical attendance has not chosen a better tutor; they have chosen from a shorter list, and in Higher Level Physics or a Group 2 language that list may contain nobody at all.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting households is a service we run only in India. That is stated on every country page on this site and it is not softened here. If your requirement is specifically that an adult sits in the room, the honest answer is that we are not the right provider, and the market rates in the first table of this page will help you negotiate with one who is.

sections.heading: Supervision without a stranger in the sitting room
paragraphs: The real loss when a tutor is not physically present is parental visibility, and it deserves a concrete replacement rather than reassurance. Four things do the job, and all four are better evidence than overhearing a lesson through a door. Sessions are recorded, so a parent can sample ten minutes of any hour they paid for rather than inferring from tone. A shared running document holds what was taught and what was set, so nothing depends on a teenager's account of it.

Marked work is returned rather than described. A script with dropped marks circled and the mark scheme's own phrasing written beside each is something a parent can hold, compare against the same exercise six weeks earlier, and show to a subject teacher. And a one-page note every fortnight says what moved, what did not and what the next fortnight targets, written for a parent who does not teach the subject.

Those four together answer a question that sitting in the room never quite does: is this working? A parent listening at the door learns whether the tutor is talkative and whether the child sounds engaged. Neither correlates reliably with marks. A dated pair of timed scripts four weeks apart, plus an error log showing the same mistakes disappearing, answers the question directly. The visibility is different in kind, and in practice it is more useful, because it is dated, comparable and written down rather than recalled afterwards from a doorway.

A shared document holding what was taught and what was set

A one-page fortnightly note written to be acted on

sections.heading: What a parent sitting in on a lesson actually learns
paragraphs: It is worth being precise about this, because it is the emotional centre of the in-home preference. A parent present for a lesson learns three things reliably: whether the tutor turned up, whether the hour was used, and whether their child seems comfortable. Those matter. A tutor who spends twenty minutes on small talk is easy to detect from the next room, and families who have been through a bad arrangement are right to want that tripwire.

What presence does not reveal is whether the teaching is correct. A confident explanation of a Chemistry mechanism sounds exactly like a confident wrong explanation of one, and no parent who does not teach the subject can tell them apart from the hallway. Nor does presence show whether the hour was pointed at the right thing. A tutor working patiently through a topic the student already understands sounds productive and is wasting the term.

That is why the substitutes above are designed around marked work rather than around observation. A recording covers the attendance-and-effort question that presence answers. The marked script and the error log answer the correctness-and-direction questions that presence never could. Families who move from an in-home arrangement to this one usually report the same thing after a month: they see less and know more. That is an unfamiliar trade, and for a student old enough to manage their own session it is the right one, because the thing a parent needs to know is whether marks are moving rather than whether the room sounded busy.

sections.heading: Honest limits on assessed work and materials
paragraphs: The in-home market in this region contains some of the worst practice in the sector, and a page about home tutoring has an obligation to name it. At least one site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student's own certification, not on the vendor. Proximity makes this worse rather than better: a tutor in the house, unsupervised, with a deadline on Monday, is the exact situation in which the line gets crossed quietly.

The permissible version is narrow and worth stating. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards and how many marks it carries. A tutor reads a draft the student has produced and writes down what the criteria would credit and refuse. The student then revises it, in their own words, with their own judgements. Nothing assessed is authored, supplied or edited to completion, and feedback is written rather than spoken so a supervisor or a parent can see exactly what was said.

Materials follow the same rule. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are referenced, linked and used on screen from the official source rather than reproduced as downloads or redistributed as files. That is the lawful position and it also means the student is working from the real document rather than from somebody's retyped version of it, which is a more common problem than families expect.

No assessed work is authored, supplied or edited to completion

sections.heading: Booking, and the coverage position stated up front
paragraphs: Send three things: the subject and level exactly as the school entered them, the most recent report or mock mark, and one piece of work a teacher has already annotated. The third is the one families leave out and the one that shortens the diagnosis most, because a teacher's own marks on a real script show how the department reads the work rather than how a single grade summarises a whole term of it.

The free trial lesson is a real lesson with the tutor who would teach the course, booked without card details. What it tests is whether your child will admit to this particular adult that they do not understand something. No amount of credential-reading answers that, and it is the single best predictor of whether the arrangement will produce anything.

Coverage is stated before you pay. Mathematics at either level, the three sciences, English A, Economics and Business Management are reasonably covered in UAE evening hours, with 17:00 to 19:00 the tightest band because every family wants it. Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish take longer. Higher Level Further Mathematics, Design Technology and Music are genuinely thin, and where nothing suitable is free you are told so and offered a later slot, a wait, or a straight no. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without ever mentioning where the tutor actually sits.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and your real evening window
process.description: Not the window you would like, the one that exists after the school run, food and a younger sibling's bedtime. In most Abu Dhabi households that is later than families first suggest, and a slot set honestly at 19:30 survives a term where an optimistic 17:15 collapses inside a fortnight.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: A real lesson on real content, with the person who would take the course rather than a coordinator, booked without card details. It answers the one question credentials cannot: whether your child will say out loud, to this particular adult, that they are lost.

process.title: A timed diagnostic before any teaching
process.description: Session one is a past-paper section at the correct level, marked against the published mark scheme while your child watches. It produces an error log classified by topic and command term, which becomes the planning document. Teaching that starts before this exists is teaching aimed at a described problem rather than a real one.

process.title: Visibility set up deliberately, not improvised
process.description: Recording on, shared document created, marked work returned to you rather than described, and a fortnightly note scheduled. These are the four substitutes for sitting in the room, and they work only if they are set up in week one rather than promised and forgotten.

process.title: A term review you can act on
process.description: At the end of a term the first diagnostic sits beside the latest one and the recurring-error count is compared. Where the comparison shows little movement, the useful options are a different tutor, a different approach, or stopping. We will say which we think it is rather than letting the arrangement drift.

whyPoints.title: The home-tutoring question answered, not deflected
whyPoints.description: Real market rates with sources, real drive times, the actual permit rules and the ethics position on a child's own teacher. A family comparing models deserves the information even where it points somewhere other than us, and the first table on this page is useful whoever you end up hiring.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the rate, because none is incurred
whyPoints.description: The gap between AED 180-500 for a visit and AED 150-300 for a qualified online tutor is mostly a car. Removing the journey removes the premium, the late arrival, the traffic cancellation and the quiet preference for students who happen to live close to the tutor.

whyPoints.title: A pool chosen by subject, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: For Higher Level Physics or a Group 2 language, the set of specialists within a drive of Al Shamkha who are free at 18:00 can be empty. Choosing by the paper the student sits rather than by distance is the single biggest determinant of whether the hours are worth anything.

whyPoints.title: Visibility by artefact
whyPoints.description: A recording to sample, a shared document, a marked script returned to you, an error log and a fortnightly one-page note. Parents who move from an in-home arrangement usually say the same thing after a month: they see less and know more.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work line stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and annotates; the student writes. Nothing assessed is authored, supplied or edited to completion, and the feedback is written down so a supervisor can audit it. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are openly on sale, this is a real difference rather than a slogan.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free in UAE evening hours, you are told before booking and offered a later slot, a wait, or nothing. Filling a Further Mathematics HL request with a generalist produces a cancelled arrangement in week three and a wasted month in between.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our house in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Visiting households is a service IB Gram runs only in India, and it is not offered anywhere in the United Arab Emirates. Everything delivered to an Abu Dhabi family is one-to-one and runs over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That position is stated on every country page on this site rather than buried here. If your requirement is specifically that an adult is physically present, which is a fair requirement for a young child, we are not the right provider and the market rates published on this page will help you negotiate with someone who is.

faqs.question: How much does an in-home IB tutor charge in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. Bestimate's 2026 UAE rate table puts in-home tutoring at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. By comparison a qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270. The difference between the two bands is travel rather than teaching quality. Those are market figures from published sources with the date attached, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is a visiting tutor more expensive if the lesson is the same length?
faqs.answer: Because the lesson is not what you are paying for in full. A tutor driving from Al Bateen to Al Reef for a 17:30 hour has committed ninety minutes to two hours of unpaid travel to a sixty-minute booking, and that time is recovered somewhere: in the hourly rate, in a minimum booking length, or in an unspoken preference for students who live nearby. The last version is the expensive one, because it quietly narrows your choice of tutor to whoever is geographically convenient rather than whoever teaches the paper your child sits.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing and lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be wary of any quoted amount.

faqs.question: Can we hire the teacher who actually teaches my son at his school?
faqs.answer: It is the most common arrangement in this market and the most problematic. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same thing. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. The structural objection stands anyway: the person who writes your son's predicted grade should not also be invoicing you, and a student rarely admits confusion to the teacher they face again on Monday.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Al Shamkha. Would a local tutor even cover Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and this is the clearest practical argument on the page. Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is spread across many schools, and the set of people who can teach Higher Level Physics to a high standard, hold a valid permit, live within a sensible drive of Al Shamkha and are free at 18:00 is frequently empty. A family insisting on physical attendance in that situation has not chosen a better tutor; they have chosen from a much shorter list, and sometimes from a list of one generalist. Online, the pool is everyone who teaches that paper.

faqs.question: How do I know the hour is being used if nobody is in the room?
faqs.answer: Four substitutes, all of them stronger evidence than overhearing a lesson. Sessions are recorded, so you can sample ten minutes of any hour you paid for. A shared document holds what was taught and what was set, so nothing depends on a teenager's summary. Marked scripts are returned to you rather than described, with dropped marks circled and the mark scheme's own wording beside each. And a one-page note every fortnight says what moved and what did not. Presence tells you whether a tutor is talkative. A dated pair of marked scripts tells you whether anything changed.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor better for a primary-age child?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it would be dishonest to argue otherwise. A six- or seven-year-old needs an adult physically managing the session: keeping them at the table, controlling the materials, handling the fifteen-minute attention ceiling. A video call demands self-regulation a young child does not reliably have, and a parent ends up supervising the supervision. Where that is the requirement, an in-home tutor at the market rates published on this page is a sensible purchase. IB Gram does not provide it in the UAE, and saying so now saves you a conversation later.

faqs.question: What equipment does my son need at home for a video session?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A laptop with a working microphone, a reliable connection, and some way to show handwritten working: a phone on a cheap stand pointed at the page, or a tablet with a stylus. For Mathematics and the sciences the handwriting channel matters more than video quality, because a tutor needs to see the working as it is produced rather than the finished answer. Headphones help in an apartment. A second screen is useful at Higher Level but not necessary. Nothing on that list costs more than a single in-home session at the market rate.

faqs.question: What happens to the session if the internet drops mid-lesson?
faqs.answer: The tutor reconnects, usually within a minute, and the lost time is made up at the end or in the following session. This is a smaller failure mode than it sounds, and worth comparing with its in-home equivalent: a tutor stuck in the 17:00 traffic does not arrive late and continue, they lose the first fifteen minutes and leave on time because another student is waiting. Where a connection genuinely fails, the session is rescheduled rather than charged. Recordings mean a partially completed session still leaves something usable behind.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arranging it in advance works better than improvising week by week. Most Abu Dhabi families shift to a later and shorter slot after Iftar, and because there is no travel involved the move costs nothing and does not depend on a tutor's willingness to drive at an awkward hour. The plan is compressed rather than paused, which matters because school-set internal deadlines for Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay do not move for the calendar. Agree the pattern before the month starts and the term survives it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor sit with my child while they finish their Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the skill the task assesses, explain what each criterion rewards and how many marks it carries, read a draft your child has produced, and write down what the criteria would credit and refuse in it. Your child then revises it themselves, in their own words. What never happens is authoring, supplying or editing assessed work to completion. The proximity question is relevant here: an unsupervised adult in the house with a deadline on Monday is exactly the situation in which that line gets crossed quietly, which is one reason written feedback is the safer format.

faqs.question: We have two children on different IB programmes. Does that work online?
faqs.answer: Better than it works in person, which is the counterintuitive part. Two children at different stages need two different specialists, and an in-home arrangement pushes a family towards one tutor who will cover both because a second visit means a second journey. Online, the sessions simply sit back to back in the evening with two different tutors, two separate plans, two diagnostics and two notes. Sibling bookings are common in Khalifa City and Shakhbout City for exactly this reason, and the convenience of one timetable no longer requires the compromise of one generalist.

faqs.question: How quickly can we start, and what if nobody covers our subject?
faqs.answer: Two to five days for the common subjects: Mathematics at either level, the three sciences, English A, Economics and Business Management. The 17:00 to 19:00 band is the tightest because every family wants it, so a later slot often starts sooner. Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish take one to three weeks. Higher Level Further Mathematics, Design Technology and Music are genuinely thin and can be unavailable, in which case you are told that before booking and offered a later slot, a wait, or nothing at all rather than a generalist.

faqs.question: What do you actually need from us before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Three documents and one honest answer. The subject and level exactly as the school entered them, because Higher and Standard Level are different courses and the school's entry is the only reliable record. The most recent report or mock mark. One piece of work a teacher has already annotated, which tells a tutor more in five minutes than a term of grades. And the evening window that genuinely exists in your household after the school run, food and a younger child's bedtime, rather than the one that sounds reasonable in an email.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Compare the models properly, then book a trial
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you came here for an in-home tutor, the figures on this page are yours to use with whoever you hire: AED 180 to 500 an hour from the published market tables, travel inside the rate, and a permit you are entitled to ask to see. If the real requirement was a specialist in your child's actual subject at a time that fits an Abu Dhabi evening, send the subject, the level and your honest window. The free trial lesson is a real lesson with the tutor who would teach, booked without card details, and the coverage position for your subject is stated before anything is paid. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.tutorsIntro: Profiles below show the courses and levels each tutor teaches. Fees in this market track level and scarcity far more closely than they track experience in years, so read the level first: Higher Level cover is priced differently from Standard Level in every provider's rate card.

intro.heading: A quote is four costs wearing one number
paragraphs: When a tutor in Abu Dhabi says AED 350 an hour, that figure is carrying several things at once and the proportions change dramatically depending on where you live. Part of it is the teaching hour itself. Part of it is the time the tutor spends driving to Saadiyat or out to Al Reef and back, which is unpaid unless it is inside the rate. Part of it is the marking and preparation done between sessions, which some tutors include and others quietly do not. And part of it is the risk the tutor carries on cancellations, which is why a flexible arrangement always costs more per hour than a committed term.

Market figures for this emirate are reasonably well established even though almost nobody publishes them. In-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE runs roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 survey of tutoring costs, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500. Qualified tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget platforms start lower: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Specialist IB and A Level cover runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are the market you are shopping in.

The gap between the in-home band and the online band is not a quality gap. It is mostly a transport gap. A tutor crossing from the mainland to the island for a single 60-minute lesson has committed two to two and a half hours of their working day, and no rational person prices that at one hour. Understanding this makes the whole market legible: the premium you pay for a visit buys presence in the room, not better teaching, and the same money buys more teaching hours or a scarcer specialist if you remove the car from the equation.

There is a second thing fees are quietly buying, and it is the one parents most often fail to ask about. A session where the tutor has already read and marked the student's work is a different product from a session where the first twenty minutes are spent finding out what happened last week. The first costs the tutor unbilled time and shows up as a higher hourly figure. The second looks cheaper per hour and delivers perhaps two thirds of the teaching. Ask explicitly whether marking between sessions is included, because the answer separates two things being sold at similar prices.

The rest of this page prices the pieces. A rate card by programme and level with the in-home and online columns side by side. A travel table for the real Abu Dhabi corridors, because a Khalifa City family and an Al Khalidiyah family are not shopping in the same market. What a 60 and a 90-minute session can actually finish, by assessment component. Tuition set against school fees and examination entry. And the extras that appear on a second invoice. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which is also why there is no travel line in anything we quote.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees track the programme because the assessment stakes track the programme. A Diploma hour and a Primary Years hour are priced differently in every rate card in this market, and the reason is what the hour has to achieve rather than how hard it is to teach.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive hour in any Abu Dhabi rate card, because externally marked papers and a fixed two-year window remove the option of trying again next term. Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, with a 45-point ceiling of which three points come from the core.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma fees in Abu Dhabi peak twice a year rather than rising steadily: once in the autumn when DP2 families realise the Internal Assessments are real, and again in February and March when the session is close. Booking either six weeks earlier than the peak usually buys the same person at a mid-band rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Lower hourly figures across the market and a longer sensible horizon. Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a 0-8 scale, with no external papers for most students, so the measurable return on an hour is slower and less dramatic than at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Abu Dhabi families get the best value per dirham, and where most of them do not spend. A Year 9 student whose criterion marks are fixed before the Diploma starts needs far fewer paid hours in DP1 and DP2, which is the cheapest Diploma strategy available and the least popular.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The lowest band in every rate card. Inquiry-based units with no graded examinations, so support is numeracy fluency, reading and writing stamina, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education strands running alongside the licensed curriculum.
programmes.countryNote: Paying a Diploma specialist rate for primary support is the most common overspend seen among Abu Dhabi families. A capable primary teacher who understands inquiry reporting does more for a Year 4 student, at a fraction of the figure, than any subject expert.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses plus a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fees generally follow the Diploma band for the DP subject components and are negotiated individually for the career-related elements, which few tutors cover.
programmes.countryNote: Because so few Abu Dhabi schools run this programme, there is effectively no local price benchmark. Families should expect to negotiate rather than compare, and to source the reflective project support online.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Fee levels differ by subject in this market, and the reason is usually what the assessment demands rather than how difficult the content is. Each note below names where marks are actually lost, because that is what determines how many paid hours a subject needs.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Marks are lost to narrative. Paper 2 and Paper 3 reward argument built from evidence, and students who know the period well frequently write chronology instead. The Internal Assessment is a 2,200-word investigation with a distinct source-evaluation section that is routinely under-written. Mid-band fees, high hours.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is cheap to fix and command-term handling is not. The fieldwork Internal Assessment needs supervision at the design stage rather than the writing stage, which means hours spent early are worth more than hours spent late. Mid-band fees locally.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: The engagement activity and, at Higher Level, the oral presentations carry marks students rarely rehearse. Lost marks come from describing a case rather than using it as evidence for a claim about a political concept. Fewer tutors cover it in Abu Dhabi, so fees run above the humanities average.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A transdisciplinary course where students lose marks by answering as scientists and ignoring the societies half, or the reverse. The Internal Assessment requires a genuine investigation rather than secondary data, and getting that decision right early saves several paid hours later.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application, not definitions. Students who can draw a framework but not apply it to the case study sit in the middle band indefinitely. One of the cheapest IB subjects to find cover for in Abu Dhabi, so the rate should be at the lower end of any quote you receive.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Writing task register and the individual oral are where the marks go, not vocabulary. Many Abu Dhabi students are fluent speakers who lose marks on text-type conventions, which is a short, cheap fix with the right tutor and an expensive one with the wrong one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling language and calculator technique decide more marks than algebra. Students arriving from American middle schools often meet the modelling vocabulary for the first time here. Plentiful cover at Standard Level in Abu Dhabi, which keeps fees moderate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Standard Level cover is widely available; Higher Level is not, and the fee gap between them in this emirate is wider than for any other science. Marks are lost in energetics and in organic mechanisms, and the Internal Assessment variable choice drives the final criterion scores.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The highest-fee science locally because Higher Level cover is thin. Lost marks are predictable: dropped units in multi-step problems, and extended responses where the physics is correct but no principle is stated before the algebra.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Content volume and a practical investigation. Students lose marks by treating the physiology as biology and skipping the application to performance. Very few Abu Dhabi tutors cover it, so expect individually negotiated fees rather than a rate card.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: The single biggest variable in an Abu Dhabi in-home quote is where you live, because a tutor prices their round trip into the hour. The notes below describe each corridor as a travel problem rather than as a neighbourhood.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A long trip from the island in evening traffic and the reason Khalifa City families see some of the widest quote variation in the emirate. The same tutor may charge one figure for a Tuesday 7pm and another for a 5pm slot in the same week.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Out past the airport, which puts it at the far end of most tutors' acceptable range. In-home quotes here sit near the top of the market band and some tutors decline outright, which narrows the choice before price is even discussed.

regions.name: Al Ghadeer
regions.note: On the Dubai side of the emirate boundary, so some tutors treat it as a Dubai job and others as an Abu Dhabi one, with very different figures. Worth asking which city a visiting tutor is driving from before accepting a rate.

regions.name: Al Samha
regions.note: Similar distance profile to Al Ghadeer with fewer tutors willing to make the trip. Families here routinely report that the choice is between a high in-home figure and an online session, with little in between.

regions.name: Baniyas
regions.note: Mainland and well connected, but a long way from where most independent tutors live. Group arrangements within a compound are common here as a way of splitting a travel-loaded fee across households.

regions.name: Shakhbout City
regions.note: Villa community with a steady flow of students transferring between curricula. The practical effect on fees is that transition planning sessions are often needed on top of subject hours, and families should budget for both.

regions.name: Al Falah
regions.note: Compact villa clusters where sharing a tutor across neighbouring households genuinely reduces the per-family travel loading. It works for revision and fails for Internal Assessments, which must be each student's own work.

regions.name: Mussafah and the industrial corridor
regions.note: Few tutors live here and fewer will travel to it in the evening. This is the clearest case in the emirate where online delivery is not a cost preference but the only route to a subject specialist at any price.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: The corridor where Diploma demand and travel cost collide hardest. Students we support here come from a mix of IB continuum and British curriculum schools, and families commonly compare an in-home quote with travel against two online sessions for the same money.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Mainland communities where local independent tutor supply is thin and travel-loaded quotes are the norm. Requests here skew towards Middle Years support and transfers into IB programmes from other curricula.

schoolClusters.city: The island centre
schoolClusters.note: The one part of Abu Dhabi where an in-home visit carries little travel loading, so quotes here are the closest thing the emirate has to a pure teaching rate. Useful as a benchmark when comparing a mainland quote.

modes.description: A fixed weekly slot with a subject specialist over live video, with the student's work marked between sessions. Market rates for qualified online tutors run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and specialists higher. There is no travel component because nobody travels, which is the entire reason this band sits below the in-home band.

sections.heading: The rate card: what Abu Dhabi charges, by programme and level
paragraphs: The table below is the thing almost nobody in this market publishes. Three of six competitor pages researched for Abu Dhabi and Dubai quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. Every figure here is in AED, attributed, and presented as the market rather than as our price list.

Read it as bands rather than as prices. Where a row shows a wide range, the spread is usually explained by three things: the level, how scarce that specialism is inside the emirate, and how close the examination session is. Higher Level sciences sit at the top of their band in February and in the middle of it in October, and that is a timing decision available to any family who plans ahead.

The small-group column is per student, and it is the honest budget option. It halves or quarters the hour without pretending to be one-to-one. What it cannot do is coursework, because an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay must be the individual student's own work and a shared session is the wrong place for it.

The indicative monthly column assumes one session a week. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, which lines up with the arithmetic in the table.

sections.heading: The travel component, corridor by corridor
paragraphs: This is the table that explains the fee difference nobody itemises. An Abu Dhabi tutor quoting for an in-home visit is pricing a round trip, and the round trip is frequently longer than the lesson. The figures below are typical evening driving estimates between a central Abu Dhabi base and each corridor, which is where most independent tutors in the emirate live.

The arithmetic is unforgiving. A 60-minute lesson in Al Reef costs the tutor around two and a half hours of their evening once both directions are counted. At a notional target of AED 200 for an hour of their professional time, that trip has to be priced near AED 400 to AED 500 before the tutor is earning what they would earn teaching three online hours from a desk. This is why the top of the in-home band exists, and it is not greed; it is a diary.

It also explains something families find puzzling: why the same tutor quotes differently for different slots. A 5pm start in Khalifa City crosses the worst of the evening, and a 7.30pm start does not. Where a tutor offers you two figures for the same lesson, the difference is almost always the traffic between them.

The final column is the point of the exercise. Removing the car does not reduce the teaching; it removes a cost that buys nothing educational. A family in Al Samha choosing between one in-home hour and two online hours for roughly the same money is choosing between presence and twice the teaching, and for a Diploma student the second is usually the better purchase.

sections.heading: What a 60-minute session can actually finish, and what needs 90
paragraphs: Families buy hours and tutors deliver tasks, and the mismatch between those two units wastes a surprising amount of money. Some pieces of IB work simply do not fit into sixty minutes once you include the student explaining where they got stuck, and buying them in sixty-minute units means paying twice for the same ramp-up.

The pattern is consistent. Anything diagnostic, iterative or involving a long piece of writing benefits from ninety minutes. Anything drill-like, topic-sized or focused on timed technique fits sixty comfortably and often leaves the student fresher. The worst value in this market is a ninety-minute session spent on content explanation, where attention falls away after the first hour, and a sixty-minute session spent on a full extended-response cycle, which cannot be completed.

The practical consequence for a budget is that a mixed pattern costs less than a uniform one. A Diploma student might take a weekly sixty-minute session for technique and a monthly ninety-minute session when a piece of coursework needs a proper read-through, rather than paying for ninety minutes every week on the assumption that more is better.

The table below is a planning aid rather than a rule. Use it to challenge a quote expressed only in months: a provider selling eight sessions a month without asking what those sessions are for has not thought about this, and the family is the one paying for the mismatch. It is also worth asking the tutor which length they would choose for your child's specific weakness, because a tutor who has a view on that question has thought about the teaching and one who defers to whatever you prefer has not.

sections.heading: The extras that appear after the first invoice
paragraphs: Most complaints about tutoring fees in this market are not about the hourly figure. They are about things that were not in the conversation and then were on the bill, or about services the family assumed were included and were not. All of them are avoidable with four questions asked before the first session.

Marking between sessions is the big one. If it is not included, a sixty-minute session has to contain the reading, the marking and the teaching, and a family is buying perhaps forty minutes of instruction. Ask directly whether work set between sessions is marked and returned, and whether that time is billed. A rate that looks ten per cent higher and includes it is usually the cheaper product.

Then there is the cancellation window, which for an in-home tutor is reasonably tight because a wasted trip costs them a whole evening. Twenty-four hours is common; some ask for forty-eight. A family with unpredictable work travel should establish this before committing, because the cost of two cancelled sessions a term is a meaningful share of the annual spend. Report writing, school liaison, mock marking outside sessions and holiday retention fees are the other four that appear on second invoices in this market.

Finally, ask what happens to the rate if you add a second subject or a second child. Many tutors will hold a rate for a second subject with the same student and almost none will reduce it, because the preparation doubles. Sharing a session between two children of different levels is where families most often get poor value: both get a diluted hour and the saving is smaller than it looks.

sections.heading: Tuition against school fees and examination entry
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest education line in an Abu Dhabi household budget, and seeing it next to the others changes how families decide. The table sets out the items that recur, with the figures stated as ranges and the ones that are not ours clearly attributed.

A useful anchor from the neighbouring emirate: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, and Abu Dhabi fee regulation sits with ADEK, but it tells you something about the direction of the regional conversation on education costs.

The two-year Diploma line in the table is the number worth calculating before DP1 rather than during DP2. A single weekly specialist hour across two academic years is a substantial commitment, and a family who sees that total in advance usually makes better decisions: fewer subjects supported, earlier start, more use of the Middle Years years when hours are cheaper and the return lasts longer.

Examination entry as a private candidate is included because it occasionally becomes relevant for retakes or for a student outside a school system. Entry fees are set by the board and the examination centre, not by a tutor, and should be confirmed with the centre directly rather than estimated from a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, and what each fix costs in hours
paragraphs: A fee only makes sense against a job. The most expensive tutoring in Abu Dhabi is the kind bought without a diagnosis, because it pays for a general improvement across a whole subject when the actual loss is concentrated in two or three identifiable places.

Across IB subjects the losses cluster in a small number of patterns. Content gaps, usually inherited from an earlier year, which are bounded and relatively cheap: the syllabus is finite and a tutor can work through it. Command-term handling, where a student who knows the material answers the wrong question, which is the cheapest fix of all and frequently takes four sessions. Working presentation in the quantitative subjects, where units, rounding and unstated method lose marks the student has earned. And coursework judgement, where the Internal Assessment was framed in a way that caps its ceiling regardless of execution.

The last of those is the one with the worst cost profile, because it is cheap to fix in week one and nearly impossible to fix in month four. Two ninety-minute sessions on the plan and the variable choice, bought early, prevent a situation in which no amount of later tutoring can lift the criterion scores. Families who buy those two sessions and nothing else often get better value than families who buy a term of weekly hours starting in February.

So the sequence that costs least is: get the marked evidence read, identify which of those four patterns is dominant, buy the narrow fix for it, then reassess. What costs most is buying a monthly package across three subjects and hoping the right thing gets worked on.
bullets: Content gaps: bounded, four to twelve sessions depending on how much is missing
Command-term handling: the cheapest fix, often four sessions and transferable
Working presentation and units: two to three sessions, immediate mark return
Coursework framing: two sessions in week one, or unfixable later
Timing and paper strategy: one or two sessions with timed practice

sections.heading: Packages, commitments and the questions that reduce the bill
paragraphs: Packages exist because they solve the tutor's problem, which is an unpredictable diary, and they can solve the family's problem too if the arithmetic is checked. A monthly figure for eight sessions is only good value if eight sessions a month is the right pattern, and for most Diploma students working on one subject it is not; four is.

The commitments that genuinely reduce an hourly figure in this market are the ones that reduce the tutor's risk. A term booked in advance at a fixed weekly slot is worth a real discount and most tutors will give one, because it removes diary uncertainty. Paying for a block up front is worth less than people assume and carries the obvious risk of a tutor who turns out to be the wrong match. A longer single session is not usually cheaper per hour, and for younger students it is worse teaching.

Three questions reliably move a quote. Whether a term commitment at a fixed slot attracts a lower rate, which it usually should. Whether a fortnightly pattern at ninety minutes costs less in total than a weekly sixty for coursework work, which it often does. And whether the tutor would rather hold a quieter slot at a lower figure than a contested 5pm one at a higher figure, which for anybody who can study at 8pm is the single largest saving available in this emirate.

One question to avoid: asking a tutor to beat a figure from somebody at a different tier. A specialist is not going to match a university student's rate, and the conversation signals that you are buying on price alone, which changes what you are offered. Ask for a structure that costs less instead.

sections.heading: Invoices, VAT and paying somebody who is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Two administrative points are worth settling before money changes hands, and neither takes long. The first is whether the figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay. The second is whether the person you are paying is permitted to charge for lessons in the UAE at all.

On tax: this page does not state how value added tax applies to tuition in the UAE, because that treatment should be read from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring website, and several sites in this market state it confidently and inconsistently. What a family can and should do is ask any provider a direct question: is the quoted AED figure inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and if tax is being charged, what is the provider's registration number. A provider who cannot answer that clearly is telling you something about their invoicing.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through MoHRE, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which created a private tuition work permit granted free of charge for two years. Those offering private lessons without it are, in the ministry's wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so nobody can tell you the amount. Ask to see the permit before the first paid session. It costs the tutor nothing to hold and nothing to show.

Keep a simple record either way: dates, duration, subject and amount, with a receipt or transfer reference. It matters if a dispute arises, it matters more if a tutor stops responding mid-term, and for a family running support across two Diploma years it is the only reliable way to know what the whole thing actually cost.

process.title: Send marked work before asking for a figure
process.description: A quote given without evidence is a guess, and guesses in this market are high. A marked paper with component marks, or criterion scores for a Middle Years student, lets a tutor say how many sessions the job needs. That number, not the hourly rate, is what determines the bill.

process.title: Ask what the hour includes
process.description: Marking between sessions, work set, written feedback, cancellation window, and whether the rate changes in the examination term. Four questions, two minutes, and they separate two products that are sold at similar figures and deliver very different amounts of teaching.

process.title: Take the free trial with the papers open
process.description: Forty-five minutes, no cost and no card details. Judge it on whether the tutor named a specific lost mark and said how many sessions the fix needs. A trial spent on reassurance has given you no information about value.

process.title: Pick the slot nobody else wants
process.description: The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested in the emirate. A family that can study at 8pm, or on a weekend morning, has more choice of specialist and more room on price than one that cannot. It is the largest single saving available here.

process.title: Review the spend against the evidence at four weeks
process.description: Compare newly marked work with the baseline on the specific component that was targeted. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the tutor or narrow the brief rather than buying more hours, which is how tutoring budgets in Abu Dhabi quietly double.

whyPoints.title: AED figures, with sources, in the currency you pay in
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. Every band here is in AED and attributed to the provider or survey it came from, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

whyPoints.title: The travel cost made visible
whyPoints.description: The gap between in-home and online rates in Abu Dhabi is largely a driving cost. Pricing it per corridor lets a family see what the premium buys, which is presence rather than teaching, and decide whether that is what they want for the money.

whyPoints.title: No travel billed, because nobody travels
whyPoints.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so there is no commute inside the figure and no slot priced by how bad the bridge traffic is that evening.

whyPoints.title: Hours tied to a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Every session count on this page starts from what the marked evidence shows rather than from a package structure. That makes a budget checkable before it is spent, and makes it obvious when a narrow two-session fix would do the work of a term.

whyPoints.title: Straight about tax and permits
whyPoints.description: This page does not assert how VAT applies to tuition, because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority. It does tell you to ask whether a quote includes tax, and to ask any tutor for the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: What do IB home tutor fees in Abu Dhabi usually include, and what sits outside them?
faqs.answer: Typically included: the teaching session itself and the tutor's travel, which is usually inside the hourly figure rather than itemised. Frequently outside: marking of work set between sessions, written progress reports, liaison with the school, marking of mock papers that are not done in the session, and any materials. Cancellation terms are the other variable, and for an in-home tutor they tend to be tighter because a wasted trip costs an entire evening. Ask about all five before the first session; a rate that looks higher and includes marking is often the cheaper product.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home tutor cost than an online one in this emirate?
faqs.answer: The market bands overlap but the centres are clearly apart. Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500, while qualified tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Most of that gap is driving time rather than teaching. For a family in Al Reef or Al Ghadeer the gap is widest, because the round trip is longest. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is tuition in Abu Dhabi charged per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both conventions exist in this market and the difference matters when sessions are not sixty minutes. A tutor quoting per session at ninety minutes may be cheaper per hour than one quoting hourly, or considerably more expensive, and families comparing two numbers often compare different units. Convert everything to a per-hour figure before deciding, then convert again to a monthly total using the session pattern you actually intend to run. A quote expressed only as a monthly package should be unpacked into hours before it is compared with anything.

faqs.question: Does a visiting tutor charge separately for travel to Saadiyat or Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Usually it is not itemised, which is precisely why it is easy to miss. The travel sits inside the hourly figure, which is how the same tutor can quote one rate for a lesson in Al Bateen and a noticeably higher one for Al Reef or Al Ghadeer. A 60-minute lesson in the airport corridor costs the tutor around two and a half hours of their evening once both directions are counted. Where a tutor gives you two figures for different times on the same day, the difference between them is the traffic.

faqs.question: Do tuition fees in the UAE carry VAT?
faqs.answer: This page will not state the tax treatment of tuition, because it should be read from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring site, and several sites in this market state it confidently and inconsistently. What you should do is ask the provider two direct questions: is the quoted AED figure inclusive or exclusive of tax, and if tax is charged, what is your registration number. Any provider invoicing properly can answer both in a sentence. Keep the written answer with your records.

faqs.question: Are monthly packages better value than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Only when the package matches the pattern your child actually needs. Packages seen in this market run from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Eight sessions a month is right for a student working on two subjects and wrong for one working on a single subject, where four is the sensible pattern. A term booked at a fixed weekly slot is the commitment that genuinely earns a lower hourly figure, because it removes diary uncertainty for the tutor.

faqs.question: What does a late cancellation cost in this market?
faqs.answer: For an in-home tutor, commonly the full session fee inside twenty-four hours, and some ask for forty-eight. The logic is straightforward: a cancelled visit cannot be refilled at short notice and the tutor has lost the whole evening, travel included. Online arrangements tend to be more forgiving because the slot can sometimes be reused. If your household has unpredictable travel, establish this in writing before committing to a term, because two lost sessions a term is a meaningful fraction of the annual spend.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level cost more per hour than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and neither is that the tutor works harder. First, fewer people in Abu Dhabi can teach Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches to completion, and the market prices that scarcity, which is why the specialist band runs to AED 450 and above. Second, the work itself is different: Higher Level marks sit in extended responses that have to be marked repeatedly, which costs the tutor unbilled time between sessions. A quote that treats both levels identically has not accounted for either.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Do the arithmetic rather than trusting a monthly figure. One weekly online session with a specialist across two academic years, term time only, lands somewhere around AED 12,000 to AED 30,000 depending on where in the band your subject sits. Two subjects double it. That total is worth calculating before DP1 begins, because families who see it in advance generally support fewer subjects, start earlier, and use the cheaper Middle Years years when an hour buys more lasting benefit.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one paid Diploma session to halve the fee?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per family, usually worse per child, and sometimes not allowed at all. Where both children are at the same level in the same subject and working on content or timed practice, a shared session can be genuinely good value and splits both the fee and any travel. Where they are at different levels, both get a diluted hour. And it cannot be used for Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge work, which must be each student's own work. A small group of two to four at a similar level is the structured version of this.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates rise closer to the examination session?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, even when published figures do not move. Demand across the emirate spikes in February and March, specialist slots close first, and families buying late find that the only availability is at the top of the band or in an inconvenient slot. The practical consequence is that the same person costs a family who books in October less than a family who books in March, for identical teaching. Booking early is the largest structural saving available in the Abu Dhabi tutoring market.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to move a Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Fix the command-term problem first, because it is usually the largest pool of recoverable marks and the cheapest to address: four sessions, and it transfers to every other subject the student takes. Then fix working presentation in the quantitative subjects, which is another two or three sessions with an immediate return. Only then buy content coverage, which is the expensive part because the syllabus is large. Buying in that order typically costs a third of what buying a general monthly package across three subjects costs.

faqs.question: How much does Internal Assessment support usually cost?
faqs.answer: Budget it as a block rather than a monthly commitment: four to six sessions at the specialist band, which puts it roughly in the AED 1,200 to AED 2,700 range at market rates. The timing matters more than the amount. Two ninety-minute sessions spent on the plan and the variable choice before any data is collected prevent a situation where the framing caps the criterion scores no matter how well the write-up is done. The same money spent in month four buys far less. A tutor gives feedback on the student's own work only.

faqs.question: What should we send to get an accurate quote rather than a range?
faqs.answer: Four things. The course name and level, written exactly as the school writes it. A recent marked paper with the component breakdown, or criterion scores task by task for a Middle Years student. The school's internal deadline list for any coursework. And the two or three slots your household can genuinely keep each week. With those, a tutor can tell you the session count as well as the rate, which is the figure that actually determines what you spend.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge for the first lesson?
faqs.answer: No. The trial runs 45 minutes over live video, costs nothing and takes no card details to book, and you are free to take it, decline and try a different tutor. The condition worth stating is that it is one trial per subject match rather than an open series. Use it with marked work in front of the tutor, because the only question worth answering in forty-five minutes is whether this person can locate what is actually going wrong. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so the trial is online like everything else.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Price the job, not the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: The hourly figure is the least useful number in a tutoring decision. What costs money is the number of sessions, and that comes from a diagnosis rather than from a package. So send the marked work first, ask what the hour includes, convert every quote to the same unit before comparing, and take the free trial with the papers open. Remember that a large part of any in-home figure in this emirate is a car journey that teaches nobody anything. Every AED band on this page belongs to the market and carries its source, so you can hold any quote against it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed by the components they mark rather than by the subjects they cover, because that is the unit of evidence. A profile that says Paper 2 extended response and criterion D of the scientific investigation tells you something a profile that says Physics does not.

intro.heading: What parents are really buying when they ask for a home tutor
paragraphs: Ask an Abu Dhabi parent why they want a home tutor rather than an online one and the answer is almost never about pedagogy. It is about being able to see what is happening. A tutor at the dining table can be overheard. You can tell whether the hour was work or conversation. You can ask on the way out whether the Chemistry is actually improving. That instinct is sound: tutoring is one of the few significant purchases a family makes where the product is invisible and the result arrives months later.

The problem is that presence is a poor proxy for progress. A tutor in your house for ninety minutes a week can produce nothing you could show a subject teacher, and a tutor on a screen can produce a marked script, an annotated internal assessment draft and a six-week error log that any teacher would recognise immediately. The question worth asking a provider is not where the tutor sits. It is: at the end of six weeks, what documents will exist that did not exist before, and what will they show?

That is the question this page answers, and it answers it with the specifics of the Diploma rather than in general terms. A DP student is assessed on written papers at the end of DP2 and on eight or nine pieces of internal coursework spread across two years. Each of those has criteria with fixed mark allocations - the sciences investigation carries twenty-four marks across four criteria of six, the Extended Essay carries thirty-four with twelve of them in critical thinking alone, the mathematics exploration carries twenty with six for use of mathematics. Evidence of progress in the IB means movement against those specific numbers, not a general sense that things are going better.

Abu Dhabi families also have a scheduling reality that changes the maths. Private schools in the emirate, overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, release students between about half past two and half past three. In the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor the drive home is short. From Al Reef, Al Samha or Al Shamkha it is frequently forty minutes or more. An in-home tutor has to cross that same city, which is why the market prices in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and why in-home work is commonly sold in two-hour blocks that make the journey worthwhile.

So the honest position, stated before anything else: IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Abu Dhabi families, sessions run one-to-one over live video, and the accountability that a parent wanted from presence is supplied in writing instead. What follows is the detail of that - how to read a marked DP script, what an error log looks like after six weeks, how internal assessment drafts are commented on without crossing the academic-honesty line, and what can and cannot honestly be said about grade movement.
