abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage of the IB, because the assessment looks different. A Primary Years student produces no marks at all; a Diploma student produces a marking record in nine places at once. Here is what progress can actually be shown as, programme by programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is marked against four criteria on an eight-point scale and converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The evidence to ask for at this stage is a piece of the student's own work scored against the school's published descriptors, with the gap between the current band and the next one named in words. Movement from a 5 to a 6 in criterion C is a documentable change; "more confident" is not.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 generate most of our Abu Dhabi evidence requests, because that is where criteria marking starts deciding grades and where the personal project lands. Families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often arrive with a report showing four different criteria scores and no explanation of what any of them mean, which is itself the first piece of work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of the grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Evidence here is concrete: marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them, drafts annotated by criterion, and a comparison between a mock script and the work produced eight weeks later on the same paper type.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session, and the school's mock window usually falls between December and February of DP2. That mock is the most valuable evidence document the student will produce before the real papers, and it is the one most families never fully read. Confirm examination and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external assessment, so there is no mark to track. Evidence at this stage is fluency measured directly: reading accuracy and rate on an unseen passage, number facts recalled under time, a piece of writing with its structure marked. Any provider offering exam preparation to a PYP student has misread the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in Abu Dhabi cluster in the newer mainland communities, where adding a second car journey to the afternoon is the thing families most want to avoid. Two short sessions a week produce more measurable fluency gain than one long one, and that pattern is only practical when nobody is driving.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The grid below names, for each subject, the document that shows whether tutoring is working. It is deliberately component-level: the point of hiring a specialist is that they can tell you which eleven marks are missing and from where.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Evidence is a timed Paper 3 attempt with the method marked rather than the answer. The diagnostic signature is a student who scores well on part (a) and loses everything after it, which shows up as a mark distribution rather than as a total.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Evidence is an interpretation sentence written next to a correct calculation. The common pattern is full method marks and zero context marks, visible only when somebody reads the script against the mark scheme line by line.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Evidence is a Paper 2 extended-response answer rewritten against the command term, with the original kept for comparison. Describe-instead-of-explain is the single most common cause of lost marks and the easiest to document.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Evidence is a set of mechanism drawings with charges and lone pairs marked, and energetics cycles with the sign convention checked. Both are visual, both are gradeable, and both change within weeks when corrected consistently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Evidence is a criterion A justification for the scientific investigation, before and after. Research design described but not justified is the most frequent cap on the 24-mark total, and the rewrite is a one-page document you can read yourself.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evidence is an evaluation paragraph added to an otherwise complete Paper 3 answer. Students reliably produce the calculation and stop, and the added paragraph is where the top band becomes reachable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Evidence is an annotated unseen text next to the essay it produced. The failure is writing about content rather than the writer's construction, and an annotation protocol makes the change visible on the page.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Evidence is a Paper 1 four-part answer with a mark-per-minute budget written on it. Overwriting part (a) and underwriting part (d) is a timing fault, and the proof it has been fixed is on the clock, not in the content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Evidence is the justification of the statistical test in the internal assessment, which is marked on method rather than on results. A tidy experiment with a weak justification scores poorly and the rewrite is short.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Evidence is design documentation for the developed solution, which is where marks sit. Students build something functional and under-record the decisions the criteria reward, and the fix is written rather than coded.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities we work with
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: Where a family lives does not change who teaches their child, since delivery is online. It does change the honest comparison with in-home tuition, because the length of the drive is what a parent would be paying for inside an in-home rate.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: The tightest school cluster in the emirate, so in-home tutoring here is the most defensible it gets: a short drive and a real local pool. Even so, the subject-specialist shortlist inside a twenty-minute radius stays small at Higher Level.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Ten minutes from Khalifa City, next to long-established IB continuum provision. Many students arrive mid-MYP with a report card of criteria scores nobody has translated for them.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: One causeway run to most schools. Families here often weigh in-home tuition against a two-hour minimum block, which is how the market prices a journey rather than a lesson.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Short apartment-to-school runs, so a half past three session is genuinely possible. Students are often the only Diploma candidate in the building, which removes the study-group effect entirely.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods with Diploma provision close by. Short distances, but pickup queues and parking take back the time, which pushes most sessions to five o'clock.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Thirty to forty minutes each way at the afternoon peak. This is where an in-home rate stops describing teaching and starts describing a car, and where the evidence case for online is easiest to make.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: The longest afternoon runs to island schools. The subjects families here most need - Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Economics - are precisely the ones with the thinnest local pool.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer housing and newer schools, with a steady share of students arriving mid-year from other curricula. Transition evidence - what the gap actually is, subject by subject - is the first document these families need.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Three shapes of work, each defined by the document it produces. The tutors and the delivery are the same in all three; what changes is what exists at the end and what it proves.

modes.title: Weekly session with a written record
modes.description: One subject, one level, the same hour each week. Each session ends with a short note naming what was covered, what was corrected and what is still open, and every two or three weeks a marked past-paper question is returned with the mark scheme beside it. The record is the product as much as the teaching is, because it is the only thing a subject teacher or a sceptical parent can actually examine.
bullets: A note after every session, in plain words, not a score out of ten
A marked past-paper question returned every two to three weeks
An error log that accumulates rather than resetting each week
A six-week review against fresh marked work

modes.title: Internal assessment draft clinic
modes.description: Short blocks timed to the school's own internal deadlines. The tutor reads the draft the student has written, scores it against the criteria by letter, and names which criterion is capping the mark and what skill it is asking for. The student then rewrites. No prose is supplied, no paragraph is replaced and no research question is chosen on the student's behalf.

sections.heading: The honest answer on home tutors in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: In-home tuition in the UAE is a real market with real prices, and anyone comparing options deserves the numbers rather than a redirection. The published bands for 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included: Bestimate's rate table shows 180-350, and independent home tutors advertise between 200 and 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270.

Three things sit inside the in-home premium. Travel is the obvious one: a tutor crossing Abu Dhabi to reach Al Reef or Al Shamkha at the afternoon peak spends forty to eighty minutes in a car per visit, and that time is in the fee whether it is itemised or not. The two-hour minimum is the second, which is why in-home work is sold in blocks rather than as single focused hours. The third is scarcity pricing: inside a twenty-minute radius of any Abu Dhabi community, the number of tutors who teach a specific subject at a specific level is small, and small supply prices accordingly.

How families actually choose, in our experience, splits cleanly by what the tutoring is for. For a younger child who needs supervision and company while working, presence genuinely helps and the premium is defensible. For a Diploma student losing marks on a named component, presence does nothing that a shared screen does not do better, because the work being examined is a script and the thing being corrected is a method. The fastest way to decide is to look at the most recent marked paper: if you can see which component the marks came out of, you need a specialist. If you cannot, you may just need someone in the room to stop the phone being picked up.

IB Gram's own position is fixed and stated before any comparison: we do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Abu Dhabi families everything is one-to-one over live video. The table below is the comparison we give parents rather than a pitch, and the row that matters most is the last one.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Diploma script
paragraphs: Most families receive marked work and read only the total. The total is the least informative thing on the page. What matters is the distribution: which questions produced full marks, which produced method marks without answer marks, and which produced nothing. Those three patterns have different causes and different fixes, and a tutor who cannot name which one is happening is guessing.

Full marks on short questions and zeros on extended response is almost always a command-term problem rather than a knowledge problem. The student knows the content, answers in the wrong register, and the examiner has nowhere to award. Method marks without answer marks is an accuracy or units problem, often significant figures or a sign. Nothing at all on the later parts of a multi-part question is usually timing or a misread stem, and it shows up most clearly in Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, where two extended problems reward reading the whole question before starting.

The annotations themselves carry information that parents are rarely shown how to read. A tick on a working line is a method mark awarded for the approach. A mark on the answer line only is an accuracy credit. "BOD" style benefit-of-the-doubt annotations mean a borderline answer was accepted and would probably not be accepted twice. A circled command term in the question margin means the examiner is signalling the answer did not engage with the verb. None of this is secret - it is in the mark schemes the boards publish - but it is not taught to families.

This is work that is done better on a shared screen than across a table, which is worth saying plainly because it runs against the instinct this page started with. On a screen the script is scanned, enlarged, annotated by both people and saved. Six weeks later the same question type can be put next to the first attempt. In a living room, the paper goes back in the bag.

sections.heading: What six weeks of evidence looks like
paragraphs: Six weeks is the review period we set, and it is chosen because it is long enough for a pattern to appear in fresh marked work and short enough that a plan which is not working gets changed before a term is gone. The point of fixing it in advance is that families are reluctant to act on a bad match. They wait, hoping, and in a two-year programme that patience is expensive. A date in the calendar and a document to judge removes the need to have an awkward conversation based on a feeling.

What accumulates over those weeks is deliberately boring. A session note each week, written in sentences a subject teacher would recognise. An error log that carries forward rather than resetting, so that the third occurrence of the same sign-convention mistake is visible as the third occurrence. Two or three marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them. Where the student is working on an internal assessment, a criterion score sheet on their own draft at each stage.

The table below is drawn from the shape of a typical Higher Level Chemistry block, which is the single most requested Higher Level science in Abu Dhabi. The detail will differ by subject. The structure should not: there should be a document at each stage, and by week six there should be a second attempt at the same task type that can be laid next to the first.

One caution about what this evidence can prove. It can show that a specific error has stopped recurring, that a criterion score on a draft has moved, and that a timed attempt now reaches the end of the paper. It cannot promise a final grade, and we do not offer one. The variables between a corrected error log in November and a Diploma grade in July include a school, a cohort, a mock season and an examination the student sits alone.

sections.heading: Internal assessment drafts: criterion letters and the honesty line
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the largest number of recoverable marks sit and where the largest number of families get help that puts the student at risk. The criteria are public, fixed and specific. The sciences investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, twenty-four in total, within a three thousand word limit. The mathematics exploration carries twenty marks, six of them for use of mathematics, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. The History investigation is twenty-five marks across identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself and reflection, inside 2,200 words. The Extended Essay carries thirty-four, and critical thinking alone is twelve of them, inside four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is a single ten-mark global judgement inside 1,600 words.

Useful feedback on a draft is a score against each of those letters and a sentence naming the skill the lowest-scoring criterion is asking for. "Criterion D asks you to weigh your limitations against your conclusion; you have listed three limitations without saying which one most affects your result" is teaching. It gives the student something to do and leaves the doing to them. A document returned with replacement sentences in it is not teaching, and it is not safe.

The IB treats authenticity as a condition of assessment rather than as advice, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student: a subject grade, and in serious cases the Diploma. That is worth stating bluntly in a market where one researched competitor openly advertises completed internal assessments at around AED 3,750 each. A tutor may teach the criterion, model the technique on a different question, read what the student wrote and score it, and check referencing. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into the submission, choose the research question, or hand over finished work in any state.

There is a practical reason beyond the rule. Several components involve the student discussing their own work with a supervisor or in a reflection session. A student who did not produce their own draft cannot talk about it, and the gap is obvious to anyone who has sat through one of those conversations.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what can be claimed and what cannot
paragraphs: This section exists because the market is full of grade promises and families deserve a clear statement of what is actually knowable. No tutor can promise a specific Diploma grade, a specific point total or a specific improvement, and any page that does is telling you about its marketing. The IB grade is produced by an examination the student sits alone, marked externally, against boundaries set after the session. Several large variables sit outside any tutor's reach.

What can be honestly described is intermediate and documented. A named error can be shown to have stopped recurring in the error log. A criterion score on a draft can be shown to have moved from one band to another, against the published descriptors. A timed attempt that previously stopped two thirds of the way through a paper can be shown reaching the end. A mark distribution can be shown shifting from zeros on extended response to partial credit. These are real, checkable changes and they are the mechanism by which grades move, but they are not the grade.

The second honest caveat is about timing. The amount of change available depends heavily on when the work starts. A student beginning in October of DP1 has access to content repair, internal assessment process and two mock seasons. A student beginning in March of DP2 has access to paper technique on a narrow set of components and little else, because the internal assessments are submitted and the content window has closed. Both are worth doing; they are not the same purchase, and a provider who prices and describes them identically is being unhelpful.

The third is about attribution. If a grade does move, nobody can cleanly say how much of it was the tutoring, the school, the student's own work or the cohort. We write session notes so a family can see what was taught and what changed in the evidence, and we leave the causal claim alone. That is less satisfying than a percentage, and it is the only version that survives scrutiny.

sections.heading: The session record, and who gets to see it
paragraphs: A parent who wanted a tutor in the house wanted oversight. The written record is how oversight works when the tutor is on a screen, and it only works if the record says something. A note reading "covered calculus, good progress" is worse than nothing, because it looks like information. A note naming the question attempted, the error that recurred, the correction taught and the practice set for the week is a document a subject teacher can act on.

Who sees it matters as much as what it contains. The parent sees the note. The student sees the note, which is not a formality: a student who reads "sign convention reversed again in question 4b" three weeks running starts checking it themselves, and that is the mechanism by which tutoring eventually stops being needed. Whether the school sees it is the family's decision, not ours, and many families do share the notes with a subject teacher productively.

Record-keeping also touches a legal duty that competitor pages in this market generally ignore. Tutoring enquiries collect personal data about a minor - name, school, year group, marks, sometimes photographs of work. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs that. A provider should be able to tell you what it collects, why, how long it keeps it and how to have it deleted, and a privacy link should sit on every page. Never hand over a child's school, grades and photograph to a form that does not state its purpose.
Our practical rule is that nothing goes in a record that we would not be comfortable showing the student, the parent and the school simultaneously. That constraint tends to produce better notes.

sections.heading: The tutor at your child's school, and the permit question
paragraphs: Among home tutors near you, the most sought-after is the one who already teaches your child, and it is the one arrangement we will not help with. Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition work permit issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation carries a code of conduct reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Both should be verified against the current policy documents rather than taken from a tutoring page.

The evidence argument against it is simpler than the regulatory one. If the person being paid to improve the work is also the person marking it, the family has lost its only independent reading. A predicted grade cannot be questioned. A draft cannot be criticised freely. The whole purpose of the documents described on this page is to give a parent something an insider has not already shaped.

On permits generally, the position is worth stating because so many pages skip it. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit: it was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or registration from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim any. What we can do is explain the rules, show you where to check them, and keep producing documents you can judge us by.

sections.heading: Where the mock paper fits, and why most of them go unread
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts usually sit school mocks between December and February of DP2. By the time the scripts come back the student has moved on, the holidays have intervened, and the paper is filed. That document is the single richest piece of evidence the student will produce before the real examinations, and leaving it unread is the most common avoidable mistake we see in this emirate.

What a properly read mock produces is a ranking. Across six subjects there are a fixed number of marks available in the remaining weeks and they are not evenly distributed. A subject where fifteen marks are being lost to command-term register is a better investment than one where four marks are lost to a genuine content gap in a minor topic, because the first is a technique fix with a short feedback loop. Families almost always rank by anxiety instead, which puts the hours into the subject that feels worst rather than the one with the most recoverable marks.

The second thing a read mock produces is a comparison point. Eight weeks later the same paper type, sat to time and marked, is a measurement rather than an impression. That pair of documents is what we mean by evidence, and it is the thing we would want to see as a parent before paying for a second term.

The practical sequence we recommend is narrow. Read every returned script against the mark scheme with the student present, not alone. Sort the marks lost by cause rather than by topic. Rank the subjects by marks recoverable per hour of work. Set an end date for the block. Then repeat the measurement.

process.title: Send the marked work before the conversation
process.description: A photograph of the most recent marked paper or the returned internal assessment draft, with the teacher's comments visible, is worth more than a half-hour call. A specialist can read it in ten minutes and arrive at the trial lesson with a written hypothesis about which component is leaking marks.

process.title: Agree what will exist in six weeks
process.description: Before paying anything, settle what documents the work will produce: session notes, a carried-forward error log, marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme, and criterion score sheets where coursework is involved. If a provider cannot name the documents, there is nothing to judge them by later.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a working session on the component the script identified, not a sales call. It ends with the tutor stating, in plain words, what the next six weeks would address and in what order. No payment is taken before it happens, and a wrong match is replaced rather than defended.

process.title: Review against new marked work, not impressions
process.description: At six weeks, look at a fresh marked attempt at the same task type as week one. Check the mark distribution rather than the total. If the named error is still recurring, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we expect to reduce hours in some subjects as well as add them.

process.title: Rebuild the plan after the school mocks
process.description: Read every returned script, sort the lost marks by cause, and rank the subjects by marks recoverable rather than by how worrying they feel. The mock is the most informative document of the two years, and the block built on it is the highest-value work available in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, stated before anything else
whyPoints.description: Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs live over video with one tutor and one student. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. You can then judge the rest of this page knowing exactly what is being sold.

whyPoints.title: Accountability in documents rather than in presence
whyPoints.description: A note after every session, an error log that carries forward, marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them, and criterion score sheets on coursework drafts. These are things a subject teacher can read, which is a higher standard than being overheard in a kitchen.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A Physics specialist who marks Paper 2 extended response and a general science tutor are different people. We match on the component the marked script identifies, because that is the unit in which Diploma marks are actually lost and recovered.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, and a clear statement of why
whyPoints.description: We describe documented changes: an error that stopped recurring, a criterion score that moved band, a timed attempt that now reaches the end of the paper. We do not promise a grade or a point total, because the examination is sat alone and marked against boundaries set after the session.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Tutors score criteria, name the capping skill and teach it. They do not supply prose, choose a research question or submit anything. In a market where completed internal assessments are advertised openly, that boundary is what protects the student from a malpractice finding.

whyPoints.title: Data about a minor handled deliberately
whyPoints.description: Enquiries involve a child's school, year group and marks. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs that, and a provider should be able to say what it collects, why, how long it keeps it and how to have it removed. Ours is on the privacy page linked from every page.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs one-to-one over live video, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time around your child's school run. We say this before the comparison rather than after it, because a page that lets you assume otherwise and then explains later has wasted your time. If presence in the room is genuinely the requirement - for a young child who will not work alone - an in-home provider is the right choice and the market rate for it is AED 180-500 an hour.

faqs.question: What does in-home tuition cost per hour here compared with online?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in this market runs AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the fee: Bestimate's 2026 table shows 180-350 and independent home tutors advertise 200-500. Monthly in-home packages run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online, a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The gap is largely travel and the two-hour minimum that a journey across the city requires. Our own fee depends on subject, level and session length and is quoted after a consultation.

faqs.question: What evidence will I actually see that my child is improving?
faqs.answer: Four documents. A written note after each session naming the task attempted, the error that recurred, the correction taught and the practice set. An error log that carries forward, so a repeated mistake is visible as a repeat. Marked past-paper questions returned every two or three weeks with the mark scheme beside them. And where coursework is involved, a criterion score sheet on your child's own draft with the gap to the next band written out. By week six there should also be a second attempt at the same task type as week one, which makes the change a measurement rather than an impression.

faqs.question: How often should marked work come back, and marked against what?
faqs.answer: Every two to three weeks is the pattern we aim for, and the marking should be against the published mark scheme for that paper, returned alongside the script rather than summarised. The reason to insist on the mark scheme is that it shows where credit was available and not taken, which is the information you are paying for. A total with a comment is not useful. What you want to be able to see is that four marks were lost to units, six to command-term register and three to an actual content gap, because those three numbers point at three different pieces of work.

faqs.question: What should a good session note say, and what is a bad one?
faqs.answer: A good note names the paper and question attempted, the specific error and whether it has appeared before, the correction in the words used with the student, and the practice set with a time limit. A bad note says "covered calculus, good progress", which looks like information and contains none. The test we apply internally is whether the note could be handed to a subject teacher who would know immediately what was done. We also write notes on the assumption that the student reads them, because a student who sees the same error named three weeks running starts checking for it unprompted.

faqs.question: Can I see the internal assessment feedback my child receives?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be a score sheet rather than an edited document. For the sciences investigation that means a score out of six against each of research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a sentence naming which criterion is capping the mark and what skill it is asking for. For the Extended Essay it means scores against the five criteria, including critical thinking, which carries twelve of the thirty-four marks. What you should not see is a draft with replacement sentences in it. That is not feedback, it is a risk transferred to your child, and the consequences of an authenticity finding fall on them.

faqs.question: How long before a grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: Honestly, it depends on which of the three problems your child has, and the marked script tells you. A command-term register problem on extended response can show measurable change in four to six weeks, because it is a short feedback loop. A timing fault on multi-part questions is similar. A genuine content gap across two topics takes a term, and technique work on top of a content gap is wasted money. We do not promise a final grade at any horizon: the examination is sat alone and marked against boundaries set after the session. What we commit to is a documented change in the evidence at six weeks.

faqs.question: Is online as effective for a child who needs someone watching them work?
faqs.answer: For supervision alone, presence in the room is genuinely better and we would say so. A tutor at the table stops a phone being picked up in a way a screen cannot. What a screen does better is diagnosis: the script is scanned, enlarged, annotated by both people and saved, so week six can be laid next to week one. If your child's problem is attention rather than method, the useful purchase may be a study supervisor locally plus a short specialist block online for the components losing marks, rather than paying specialist rates for supervision.

faqs.question: My child's mock came back two grades below the predicted grade. What happens first?
faqs.answer: The script gets read, with the student present, against the mark scheme. Before any teaching, the lost marks are sorted by cause: content, command-term register, accuracy, or timing. A two-grade gap usually turns out to be one or two causes concentrated in one or two components rather than a general collapse, and that is a far smaller problem than the grade suggests. The output is a ranking of subjects by marks recoverable per hour, which is almost never the same as ranking by how worrying each subject feels. Then an end-dated block, not an open commitment.

faqs.question: Who keeps the marked papers and the error log?
faqs.answer: The family and the student keep copies, and the tutor keeps a working copy so the log carries forward between sessions. The log is the thing most worth preserving: it is what turns a slip into a pattern, and a pattern is what can be taught against. On data, enquiries about a child collect a name, a school, a year group and marks, which Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection covers. A provider should be able to tell you what it holds, why, for how long and how to have it deleted, and that should be written down rather than described on a call.

faqs.question: Do you share progress notes with my child's school?
faqs.answer: Only if the family chooses to. The notes belong to you. Many families do pass them to a subject teacher and it tends to be productive, because the teacher can say whether the component we have identified matches what they see in class, and they set the internal deadlines any plan has to fit. What we will not do is approach a school on your behalf or present ourselves to a school as connected to it. IB Gram is independent of every school named anywhere on this site and holds no affiliation, partnership or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: How do you measure progress when the real examinations are months away?
faqs.answer: By using the same task types the examination uses, under the same conditions, repeatedly. A past-paper section sat to time in week one and the same section type in week six is a measurement. A criterion score on a coursework draft before and after a rewrite is a measurement. An error log showing a sign-convention mistake in weeks two and three and not in weeks five and six is a measurement. None of these is a grade, and none of them should be sold as one, but together they are the only honest answer to whether the hours are working.

faqs.question: What if the evidence shows no improvement after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Then something changes, and the change is ours to propose rather than yours to request. Either the hypothesis was wrong - the marks were not going where we thought - or the match is wrong, or the problem needs a different kind of work, such as topic repair before technique. We would rather replace a tutor than argue for the first choice, and we would rather tell you to reduce hours in a subject than keep billing them. The reason the review point is fixed in advance is precisely that families tend to wait and hope, and waiting is the expensive option in a two-year programme.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read it and score it against the five published criteria, name which one is capping the mark, and teach the skill that criterion is asking for - most often critical thinking, which carries twelve of the thirty-four marks. A tutor cannot supply prose, restructure the argument into the submission, or choose the research question. The student rewrites in their own words, which is also the only version that survives a reflection session with a supervisor. Word limit is four thousand, and going over it earns nothing. The Theory of Knowledge essay works the same way inside 1,600 words, assessed as a single ten-mark judgement.

faqs.question: Is one free trial lesson really enough to judge a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is enough to rule one out, which is most of the value. In a working trial the tutor should arrive having read the marked script you sent, teach the component it identified rather than introducing themselves, and finish by stating what the next six weeks would do and in what order. If any of those three is missing, you have learned something useful. What a trial cannot tell you is whether the plan works, which is what the six-week review against fresh marked work is for. No payment is taken before the trial happens, and a wrong match after it is replaced.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask what documents will exist in six weeks
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB home tutor near me in Abu Dhabi, the question that separates providers is not where the tutor sits. Ask what will exist in six weeks that does not exist now, and whether a subject teacher could read it. Then send the most recent marked paper or returned coursework draft with the subject and level, and a specialist will read it before a free trial lesson. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed in Gulf Standard Time around your community's school run, and no payment is taken before that first lesson happens.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: These are coaches who work from the specification and the mark scheme outwards. Each one names the board, the paper and the component they coach, and each one marks the student's own timed work rather than talking over a textbook chapter.

intro.heading: Coaching is a cycle, not a conversation
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi households arrive at coaching after a report card that says something vague. A 5 where a 6 was expected. A B where the mocks suggested an A. The report tells you the outcome and nothing about the cause, and a tutoring hour spent re-explaining the chapter the student already half-knows changes neither. Coaching, used properly, is the opposite of that hour. It starts by finding out which marks are actually missing, in which component, for which reason, and then spends the available time on that and nothing else.

The cycle has five stages and it repeats weekly. The student sits a timed section of a real paper. The coach marks it against the published criteria and shows the marking live, cell by cell on the mark scheme. One error type is isolated. The student drills that error on three or four short items. Then the same question type is sat again, cold, a week later. What changes is recorded. Over a term that record becomes an error log: a page that shows which mistakes have been retired and which keep coming back.

This page is written for households running two boards at once, because that is common here. An older child in Diploma Year 2 and a younger one in Year 10 Cambridge IGCSE sit different papers, marked by different people, against different criteria, on different calendars. The Diploma's internal assessment is marked by the school and moderated by the board. An IGCSE paper is marked externally, in a series whose entry deadline sits months before the exam. A single coaching plan has to respect both, and the sections below set out exactly where the two diverge.

Everything here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video and timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a coach to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation, and the reason is in the coaching itself. A script marked on a shared screen, with the mark scheme open beside it and the whole thing recorded, is better evidence than the same hour at a kitchen table where nobody can rewatch what was said.

What you should expect from the first month is artefacts, not assurances: a marked diagnostic, an error log with at least four entries, a written note naming the component being worked on, and a second attempt at the same question type with the mark recorded. If those four things do not exist after four weeks, the coaching is not working, and the sections below say plainly what to do about that.

One practical note before the detail. Coaching works best when the household treats it as a standing appointment rather than a response to a bad week. The cycle depends on a cold re-sit seven days after a drill, and a session moved twice in a month breaks that measurement without anybody noticing. Pick the slot that survives a late bus and a long homework night, even if it is later in the evening than you would prefer.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi households rarely sit inside one programme for long. A child moves from Middle Years into the Diploma, or from Cambridge IGCSE into A Levels or the Diploma, and the coaching has to change shape at each handover. These are the four programmes coaching covers here, and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated externally, which means part of the grade is decided months before any examination hall opens. Coaching for the Diploma therefore splits in two: the written papers, which respond to timed practice and command-term drilling, and the coursework, which responds to criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a concentrated Diploma market rather than a broad one, with the programme running at schools clustered on Saadiyat, in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and on Al Reem and Yas. The practical effect is that less common Higher Level courses are taught by one or two teachers in the whole emirate, so the student who needs a second opinion on Higher Level Chemistry Paper 3 often cannot find one within driving distance.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year external qualification sat subject by subject, with Cambridge and Pearson running separate specifications for the same named subject. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics and sets some sciences as single-tier. Papers are marked externally, so what the student writes on the day is the entire grade in most subjects, and command-term discipline is worth more here than in any other qualification a UAE teenager sits.
programmes.countryNote: The British curriculum is the largest single stream in UAE private education, and in Abu Dhabi it runs across the Al Raha and Khalifa City schools, Al Bateen, Al Reef and the newer Shakhbout City and Al Falah communities. Because schools choose their own board, two neighbours in the same compound can be sitting Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry in the same June series, with different paper structures and different practical arrangements.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked on an eight-point scale by the school rather than by an external board. There are no public examinations, which is why Middle Years reports are hard for parents to read and easy to under-react to. Coaching at this stage is about criterion literacy: teaching a student to read criterion B or criterion C and work out what the descriptor is actually asking for, which is the same skill the Diploma will demand two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Middle Years into Year 11 and then hand students straight into Diploma Year 1 without an external examination in between. That gap matters: a student can reach DP1 having never sat a two-hour externally marked paper. Coaching in Middle Years Year 5 here is usually about building timed-writing stamina before the Diploma asks for it in earnest.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework with no external assessment, reported against learner-profile attributes and transdisciplinary themes. Coaching here is narrow and specific: number fluency, reading comprehension speed, and written structure. The useful work is diagnostic rather than remedial, because a primary gap in place value or in sentence construction is cheap to fix now and expensive to fix in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Primary coaching demand in Abu Dhabi is shaped by relocation. A child arriving mid-year from a different system can be a full strand behind in written mathematics method while being ahead in mental arithmetic, and the school's own baseline test will not always separate the two. A short online diagnostic in the first fortnight after arrival is usually all that is needed.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Coaching is bought by subject and level, not by programme. Below are the Diploma courses Abu Dhabi families request most, with what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go. The IGCSE grid that follows lists the specifications by code, because the code is what determines the paper structure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic, proof-heavy and calculus-dense, with Higher Level adding a third paper that rewards unfamiliar problem framing. The exploration carries twenty criterion marks. Marks are lost on unjustified steps, on notation that the marker cannot follow, and on calculator work shown as an answer with no visible method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led, with graphical display calculator fluency assumed throughout. Students who chose this course to avoid proof often underestimate the statistical reasoning in Paper 2. Marks go on misread context, on reporting a regression result without interpreting it, and on rounding before the final step.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptual questions sit alongside extended calculation, and the scientific investigation carries twenty-four marks across four criteria. The common failure is not the mathematics but the explanation: a correct number with an explanation that never names the physical principle scores a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most lost marks at Higher Level. Paper 1 penalises shallow recall of definitions; Paper 2 penalises explanations that describe a trend without giving its cause. Coaching here is mostly mechanism drawing and the discipline of answering the command term as written.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the obvious problem and data analysis is the hidden one. Extended-response questions reward structure: a named process, a stated mechanism, a consequence. Students who revise by rereading notes rather than by answering past questions plateau quickly in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. A correctly drawn and fully labelled diagram with an explanation tied to the axis labels scores where a verbal answer does not. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper that rewards disciplined evaluation rather than a longer answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure, with marks concentrated in applying a framework to the stimulus rather than defining it. The research project rewards a tightly bounded question. Students lose marks by writing textbook definitions that the stimulus material never asked for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two externally marked papers plus an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. Analysis of how meaning is made beats summary of what the text says. The oral is the most coachable component in the course because its structure is published and its timing is fixed.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these can move the Diploma total by up to three points. Coaching is process work: narrowing a research question, planning an argument, and reading a draft against the published criteria. The writing stays the student's, start to finish, and a coach who offers otherwise should be declined.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE coaching is only as good as its specification match. Two schools in Abu Dhabi can teach the same named subject under different codes, with different paper counts and different tiering, so the first question any coach should ask is which code appears on the entry form.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers per tier, with Extended reaching grade A* and Core capped. Extended Paper 4 rewards multi-step problem solving and penalises unshown method. The most reliable gain available is accuracy under time, not extra content.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
igcseSubjects.description: Three papers including an alternative-to-practical component that tests experimental reasoning rather than content recall. Students who have never practised reading a results table against a stated aim lose marks they could keep with four sessions of focused work.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
igcseSubjects.description: Qualitative analysis, moles and organic families account for the bulk of lost marks. The alternative-to-practical paper is worth real attention because it is predictable in structure and rarely practised in school.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
igcseSubjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage here. A question that says describe and a question that says explain want different answers, and the difference is routinely worth more than the content being tested.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two equally weighted papers per tier with no coursework. The Higher tier assumes fluency in algebraic manipulation that Foundation never tests, so the tier decision taken in Year 10 sets the grade ceiling for the whole course.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers with practical skills assessed in writing. The specification's formula list differs from Cambridge's in what is given and what must be recalled, which is a cheap source of lost marks when a student revises from the wrong board's resources.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
igcseSubjects.description: Calculation-heavy by comparison with its Cambridge counterpart, with extended writing on industrial processes. Marks go missing on units, on significant figures, and on explanations that stop one step short of the reason.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and First Language English 0500
igcseSubjects.description: Two very different courses often confused by parents. Second Language rewards register and task fulfilment; First Language rewards directed writing and analysis of effect. Entering a student for the wrong one costs more than any amount of coaching recovers.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsTitle: Where coaching runs across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so a coach is never limited by a drive time. What the district does change is the realistic start time of a session, which school calendar the household is working to, and which subjects turn out to be scarce locally. These are the communities most of the coaching here serves.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs and a high concentration of Diploma and A Level cohorts. Sessions here usually start at 16:30 or 17:00, and demand skews towards Higher Level sciences and the Extended Essay in the autumn of Diploma Year 2.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Bus routes from several schools converge here and arrival times vary by up to half an hour, so a fixed 17:30 slot with a recorded session works better than an earlier one. IGCSE mathematics and the double-award sciences dominate requests.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A dense British-curriculum corridor where Year 10 and Year 11 coaching demand peaks between October and February. Families often coach two subjects at once here, and the limiting factor is homework volume rather than tutor availability.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living, short commutes and a mix of Diploma and IGCSE students in the same building. Evening slots after 18:00 are common because many parents work on the island and prefer to be home for the session.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with growing senior cohorts, which means fewer alumni cohorts to borrow past-paper culture from. Coaching here spends more time than usual on examination technique that an established school would have drilled already.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche
regions.note: The oldest school cluster in the emirate, with established Diploma provision. Requests tilt towards individual components rather than whole subjects: Paper 3, an oral, a single internal assessment criterion.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Ghadeer and Al Samha
regions.note: Long bus journeys and a later effective start to the evening. A 19:00 slot is normal here and works perfectly over video, where a visiting coach would be arriving at the end of a long drive.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: A wide spread of curricula and the part of the emirate where a local specialist in a less common Diploma course is hardest to find. Online coverage changes that position entirely.

schoolClusters.note: The established cluster, with long-running Diploma cohorts and experienced coursework supervision. Students here usually arrive at coaching with a clear diagnosis from school and want a second specialist opinion on one component.

schoolClusters.note: The largest block of British-curriculum and Diploma enrolment in the emirate. Coaching demand here is heavily IGCSE in the autumn and heavily Diploma coursework in the winter, with a real crossover in households running both.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.modesIntro: Coaching is sold in three shapes here, and the right one depends on where the student is in the year rather than on how much help they seem to need. Each shape runs one-to-one over live video, with the session recorded and a written note following it.

modes.title: Weekly cycle, one subject at a time
modes.description: The default. Sixty or ninety minutes a week on a single subject, following the five-stage cycle, with a marked script and an error-log update every fortnight. Running two subjects in parallel is possible but it halves the number of complete cycles each subject gets, which is usually the wrong trade in the first term.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes weekly, same slot, same coach
Timed section sat cold at the start of every third session
Error log updated in writing and shared with you
Fortnightly note naming the component being worked

modes.title: Coursework clinic
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions around the internal assessment, the Extended Essay or a Middle Years project. The work is read against the published criteria and commented on criterion by criterion. Authorship stays entirely with the student: a clinic produces annotated feedback on their draft and a plan for the next version, never prose that the student did not write.
bullets: Draft read against criterion letters, with marks indicated
Comments only on the student's own submitted text
Version history kept so progress is traceable
Timed to the school's internal deadlines, not ours

modes.title: Series sprint
modes.description: An intensive block in the eight weeks before a Cambridge, Pearson or IB session. The ratio inverts: less teaching, more timed papers, each one marked live. A sprint is only worth buying when the student already has most of the content and is losing marks to technique, and the diagnostic in week one says plainly whether that is the case.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week in the final block
A full paper under conditions at least once a fortnight
Marking done live, mark scheme visible on screen
Honest stop point if content gaps are too wide to close

sections.heading: The five stages of one coaching cycle
paragraphs: A coaching hour that begins with the coach talking is an hour spent on the coach's guess about the problem. The cycle inverts that. The student writes first, under time, on a question type chosen from the last marked script. Only then does anyone explain anything, and what gets explained is whatever the writing exposed.

Marking live is the part most families have never seen. The coach shares the mark scheme, reads the student's answer line by line against it, and says aloud where a mark was awarded and where it was not. This is uncomfortable for about two sessions and then it changes how the student reads questions, because they have watched an answer being judged rather than being told a score afterwards.

The drill stage is deliberately narrow. If the error was unshown method in simultaneous equations, the drill is four simultaneous-equation items with method marks the only thing being counted. The re-sit comes a week later, cold, on the same question type with different numbers, and the mark is written into the error log beside the first attempt. That pair of numbers is the only honest evidence that anything has changed.

Recording matters more here than on a conversational tutoring hour. A student who has watched a marker reject their own wording usually wants to see that moment again a day later, and a parent who was not in the room can watch the two minutes where the mark was lost rather than reading a summary of it. The recording is also how a second coach, picking up the subject later, learns the diagnosis without starting again.

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: codes, papers and who marks what
paragraphs: The single most common avoidable problem in an Abu Dhabi household running both boards is revision from the wrong resources. A Year 11 student working from Cambridge 0625 material when the school has entered them for Pearson 4PH1 will meet a different formula list, a different practical arrangement and a different paper structure. None of that shows up until a mock paper comes back oddly.

The fix is administrative, not academic: find the entry code. It appears on the school's examination entry confirmation, on the statement of entry the student receives before a series, and usually on the department's course outline. Ask the examinations officer directly if none of those are to hand. A coach who cannot tell you which code they are coaching to is coaching to a textbook rather than to a specification.

Who marks the work matters just as much. An IGCSE grade in most subjects is decided entirely by externally marked scripts written on the day. A Diploma subject grade is part externally marked paper and part internal assessment marked by the school and then moderated by the board. That difference changes the shape of a sensible coaching plan: for IGCSE, timed technique dominates; for the Diploma, a portion of the grade is banked long before study leave begins.

There is a second administrative trap worth naming. Schools occasionally change board between cohorts, so an older sibling's textbooks and notes can be the wrong resource for the younger one in the same house. Check the code each year rather than assuming continuity, and keep the two children's material physically separate if they are on different boards for the same subject.

sections.heading: An error log that separates four kinds of lost mark
paragraphs: Every lost mark looks the same on a report card and they are not the same thing at all. A student who does not know the content needs teaching. A student who knows it and misreads the command term needs vocabulary work. A student who knows it, reads correctly, and runs out of time needs pacing. A student who does all three well and drops the mark on units or a rounding step needs a checking routine. Four different problems, four different fixes, four different costs in hours.

Sorting a marked script into those four buckets takes about ten minutes and is the highest-value ten minutes in the whole cycle. It also gives a parent something checkable. If the log says eleven of the last fourteen lost marks were command-term errors, then the next four sessions should be about command terms, and if they are not, you have grounds to ask why.

The log is kept as a running document rather than rebuilt each week, because the useful signal is which error types disappear and which keep returning. An error that has been drilled twice and still recurs is usually not the error it appears to be: unshown method that survives two drills is often a confidence problem about what counts as working, which is a different conversation.

A log also protects the household from a common billing pattern. When nobody writes down what the problem was, every session can plausibly be about something new, and a term passes with twelve plausible hours and no evidence. The log makes the plan auditable: four categories, dated entries, two marks per question type. That is a short document, and reading it takes a parent about three minutes a fortnight.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides the mark
paragraphs: Both boards publish command-term glossaries and both expect students to have internalised them. In practice most students learn them by accident, from whichever teacher happens to enforce them. The result is a Year 11 who answers a state question with a paragraph and an explain question with a single line, losing marks in both directions on content they know perfectly well.

Coaching this is fast and the gain is unusually durable. The drill is to read twenty past questions and sort them by command term without answering any of them, then to write the first sentence only of the answer each term demands. A describe answer names features. An explain answer gives a cause. An evaluate answer reaches a judgement and supports it. A student who can produce the first sentence correctly almost always produces the rest.

The terms are not identical across boards and levels, which is another reason the specification match matters. The Diploma's analyse and the IGCSE's analyse are used with different expectations about depth, and a Diploma Higher Level discuss question wants a weighted argument where an IGCSE describe wants a list. Teaching a student the superset of terms and then telling them which board's conventions apply is more efficient than teaching one board's list twice.

Parents can run this drill themselves, which is unusual in coaching and worth saying. Take any past paper, cover the content, and ask the student only what each question is instructing them to do. A student who can answer that reliably has already recovered a meaningful share of the marks a marked script was losing, and the coaching hour can then be spent on content rather than on vocabulary.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma bridge, subject by subject
paragraphs: In households running both boards, the younger child's coaching is often really preparation for the older child's problem. The step from a strong IGCSE grade into Diploma Higher Level is bigger than the step from Year 10 to Year 11, and it is bigger in some subjects than others. Knowing which gaps are real saves a term of guessing in Diploma Year 1.

Mathematics is the clearest case. An Extended 0580 student who scored well has met most of the algebra that Analysis and Approaches assumes, but has met almost none of the calculus, and has never been asked to justify a step as a proof. That is roughly six to eight weeks of targeted work, best done in the summer between the two courses rather than in October when the Diploma has already started moving.

The sciences split differently. Content continuity is good, but the Diploma's internal assessment asks for an independently designed investigation, and nothing at IGCSE requires that. The alternative-to-practical paper trains experimental reasoning, not experimental design. A student who has only ever followed a given method needs explicit work on formulating a research question, and that work is cheap in the summer and expensive in Diploma Year 1.

English is the quiet exception in both directions. A student who did well on First Language English 0500 is not automatically ready for Diploma English A: Language and Literature, because the Diploma asks for analysis of how meaning is constructed across unseen text types and adds an individual oral with published criteria. Conversely a Second Language 0510 student can be stronger than expected on the Diploma's language-focused components. Neither case is predictable from the IGCSE grade alone, which is why a diagnostic matters more in English than anywhere else.

sections.heading: How far coaching may go on an internal assessment draft
paragraphs: This is the boundary that matters most and the one competitors in this market are least clear about. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by the school supervisor. A coach may teach the skills the task needs, may read what the student has written, and may comment on it against the published criteria. Authorship does not transfer, at any point, for any reason.

In practice that means feedback phrased as a question or a criterion reference rather than as replacement text. Criterion C asks for critical thinking: where in this paragraph is the counter-argument considered? Your method section does not state how the variable was controlled; the criterion requires it. That is legitimate, useful and exactly what a school supervisor also does. Supplying a paragraph for the student to paste in is not, and it puts the diploma at risk rather than the coach.

Keeping version history solves the authentication problem before it becomes one. If each draft is saved with a date and the feedback sits as comments beside the student's own text, the progression from first draft to final is visible and attributable. Any provider in this market offering finished coursework should be declined on the spot; that is an academic-integrity breach and the student carries the consequence.

The same boundary applies to past material, and it catches people out. Published syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and past papers belong to the boards. A coach may reference them and point you to the official page they sit on; reproducing or supplying them as downloads is a copyright problem, and in the case of unreleased material an academic-integrity one. Ask for the link, not the file.

sections.heading: What coaching costs in Abu Dhabi, and who published those figures
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for UAE queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. That is not useful to a household budgeting in dirhams, so the bands below are set out plainly with the source of each figure named. They are market rates rather than IB Gram's own: the honest answer to what we charge is that it depends on subject, level and cadence, and the free trial lesson exists so you can see the coaching before any of that is discussed.

What moves the number in this emirate specifically is scarcity rather than distance. A Standard Level Business Management coach is easy to find in Abu Dhabi and priced accordingly. A Higher Level Physics Paper 3 specialist is not, and the rate reflects it. Travel is the other multiplier: a visiting tutor is pricing the drive as well as the hour, and in this emirate the drive between the island and the mainland communities is the expensive part.

Session length is where households most often overpay. A sixty-minute slot can run one full cycle on a short question type. It cannot sit a full Diploma Paper 2, mark it live and drill the error, which needs ninety minutes or two sessions. Buying sixty-minute slots and then using them to review a paper the student sat alone is the most common way to spend money on coaching without changing anything.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what a term of coaching can honestly show
paragraphs: No coach can promise a grade and any provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be shown is narrower and more useful: component marks on repeated question types, under comparable conditions, over time. A student who scored four of eleven on a question type in September and nine of eleven on the same type in December has moved measurably, whatever the report card eventually says.

Component marks move before subject grades do, and they move at different speeds. Technique errors clear in two to four weeks because the fix is a habit. Content gaps clear in six to twelve weeks because the fix is teaching plus spaced recall. A student with a wide content gap three weeks before a series will show almost no grade movement, and the honest thing to say in week one is that the available time buys partial coverage rather than a transformation.

The termly review compares the error log against the start point and says one of three things: the logged errors are retiring and the plan continues; the errors are retiring but new ones keep appearing, so the diagnosis needs redoing; or nothing is moving, in which case the coaching should stop or change hands. The third answer is given as readily as the first two, because the alternative is billing a household for a plan that is not working.

One more measurement caution. Marks only compare when the conditions do, so a paper sat at a desk with a timer against one sat on a sofa with a phone nearby are not the same data point. Keep the conditions dull and identical: same place, same time limit, no notes, no device except the permitted calculator. A term of comparable marks is worth more than a term of flattering ones.

sections.heading: Coaching to the right series: June, November and March
paragraphs: A surprising number of Abu Dhabi families discover the series calendar late. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series a student sits is the school's decision, taken at entry, months before the papers.

Cambridge also publishes a March series, and its key dates make the point about entry deadlines better than any explanation. For the March 2027 series the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry deadline therefore sits more than two months before the first paper.

One Cambridge rule is worth knowing because getting it wrong is irreversible. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Always work from the timetable the school's examinations officer issues, not one downloaded from a search result. For IB sessions, UAE schools sit the May session; confirm any specific IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, because those dates are set by the board and revised.
