abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Private tuition is bought against a programme's assessment model, and the four programmes below are assessed in four different ways. Knowing which parts of your child's grade are already decided, and by whom, is what stops an arrangement being sold to you in the wrong shape.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: In most subjects the entire grade comes from externally marked papers written during a series. There is no coursework safety net, no moderation conversation and no second chance inside the same series. A private arrangement for IGCSE should therefore be judged almost entirely on timed written work and the marks it earns, and the tier decision taken in Year 10 is the single most consequential academic choice in the course.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum enrolment is the largest stream in Abu Dhabi private education and the two boards are split unevenly across schools. A household with children at two schools in the same district can be managing Cambridge in one and Pearson Edexcel in the other, which means two sets of specification codes, two formula conventions and two examination officers to email.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Part of every subject grade is an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated by the board, which means a share of the result is settled well before study leave. A private arrangement here should show draft history as well as marked papers, since those are the two separate things being bought.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision in the emirate is concentrated rather than widespread, and in several schools a Higher Level course is taught by a single teacher. That shapes what private tuition is actually for here: not a replacement for teaching, but a second specialist view on a component where the school has no second specialist to offer.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed internally against four published criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, with no external papers. A private arrangement at this stage is easy to sell and hard to evaluate, because there is no external mark to compare against. The honest evidence is criterion-referenced: which descriptor band the work sat in, which one it sits in now, and what the tutor did between those two points.
programmes.countryNote: Because several Abu Dhabi schools run Middle Years directly into Diploma Year 1, a student can reach the Diploma without ever having sat a two-hour externally marked paper. That is the most useful thing a private tutor can address in Middle Years Year 5 here, and almost nobody is sold it.

programmes.name: A Level, where the school continues post-16 on the British route
programmes.description: Linear, externally examined and modular only in the limited sense that some boards allow component resits. The step up from IGCSE is in analytical depth rather than volume, and the first-term grades in Year 12 are frequently a shock to students who found IGCSE straightforward. Private arrangements here are usually bought late, in the January of Year 13, when earlier work would have cost less and achieved more.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools run A Levels alongside or instead of the Diploma, and some offer both. A household choosing between them in Year 11 is really choosing between breadth with coursework and depth with examinations, and the right private tuition question at that point is about the choice rather than about a subject.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the components Abu Dhabi families most often hire a private tutor for, chosen because each one is diagnosable. A request for help with maths is hard to act on. A request about Paper 3 unfamiliar-context questions, or about criterion B in a science investigation, is specific enough to match properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Paper 3
subjects.description: The Higher Level extended-response paper, built around unfamiliar problem framing rather than new content. It rewards students who can read a scaffolded problem and see where it is going. This is the single most frequently requested component in the emirate and the hardest to staff with a genuine specialist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, statistics strand
subjects.description: Regression, hypothesis testing and confidence in reading calculator output. Students who chose this course expecting less rigour meet it here. Marks go on interpreting a result in context rather than on computing it.

subjects.name: Physics, the scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty-four marks across four criteria, marked by the school and moderated externally. Research question formulation and the treatment of uncertainty account for most of the lost marks. The work must be the student's own, which makes this a coaching task rather than an editing one.

subjects.name: Chemistry, organic mechanisms and energetics
subjects.description: The two topics that separate a 5 from a 7 at Higher Level. Mechanism drawing is a drillable skill with a published convention, and energetics rewards students who can set out a cycle before attempting a number.

subjects.name: Biology, extended response
subjects.description: Volume is the visible problem and structure is the real one. A scoring extended answer names a process, states a mechanism and gives a consequence, in that order. Students who revise by rereading reach a ceiling quickly in this subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature, individual oral
subjects.description: The most coachable component in the Diploma, because its structure, timing and criteria are published and its content is chosen by the student. Rehearsal against the criteria moves marks reliably, and the extract pairing is where most of the thinking happens.

subjects.name: Economics, evaluation and diagram accuracy
subjects.description: A fully labelled diagram with an explanation tied to the axes scores where prose does not. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper that rewards weighted judgement rather than length.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Extended Paper 4
subjects.description: Multi-step problem solving under time, with method marks available throughout. The most reliable improvement available is in shown working and pacing rather than in additional content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sciences 0620, 0625 and 0610, alternative to practical
subjects.description: A predictable, rarely practised paper that tests experimental reasoning rather than recall. Four focused sessions typically recover marks that months of content revision do not touch.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Different formula provision and a different balance of calculation from their Cambridge equivalents. A student revising from the wrong board's material loses marks that have nothing to do with ability.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points on the Diploma total between them. Private tuition here is process work: narrowing the question, planning the argument, and reading the student's own draft against the published criteria.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the main curriculum
subjects.description: Required subjects running in parallel with an international curriculum, and the most common reason a timetable has no spare evening. Private support is usually about keeping pace rather than about examination technique.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi districts this page serves
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Because lessons run over live video, the district does not change who is available. What it changes is the earliest realistic session time, the school calendar the household is working to, and how far a visiting tutor would have to drive if you chose that route instead. These are the communities most enquiries come from.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central, established and close to several long-running school cohorts. Enquiries here skew towards a single named component rather than a whole subject, which usually means the school has already diagnosed the problem accurately.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Short commutes and a working-parent pattern that pushes sessions past 18:00. Apartment living makes a quiet room the scarce resource, and a recorded session is often watched again later in the evening.

regions.name: Al Wahda and Al Karamah
regions.note: A dense mix of curricula within a small radius, which makes a specification check essential before any tutor is hired. Two students in neighbouring buildings can sit the same subject under different boards.

regions.name: Masdar City and Al Falah
regions.note: Longer bus journeys and a later effective evening. A 19:00 start is normal and works well over video, where a visiting tutor would be arriving after a substantial drive across the mainland.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Fast-growing communities where local availability of a named Higher Level specialist is thinnest. This is where the difference between hiring locally and hiring online is most visible in the shortlist.

regions.name: Al Jubail Island and Hudayriyat Island
regions.note: Small populations and long single-route journeys. Scheduling here benefits from a fixed weekly slot that nobody has to drive to, and from a recording for the nights when the slot has to move.

regions.name: Baniyas and Madinat Zayed
regions.note: Enquiries arrive later in the academic year than the island average, often after a mock result. The honest first conversation is usually about how many weeks remain and what that buys.

regions.name: Eastern Mangroves and the Corniche
regions.note: Established schooling nearby and the shortest school runs in the emirate, so earlier slots at 16:30 are genuinely available here in a way they are not further out.

schoolClusters.city: The island: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif, the Corniche and Al Maryah
schoolClusters.note: Long-established provision with experienced coursework supervision. Households here usually arrive with a clear school diagnosis and want a second specialist opinion rather than general support, which makes the engagement easier to scope and easier to audit.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Falah
schoolClusters.note: The densest block of British-curriculum and Diploma enrolment in the emirate, and the source of most dual-board households. Enquiries peak twice: October for IGCSE technique, and January for Diploma coursework deadlines landing together.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem, Yas and the southern mainland
schoolClusters.note: Newer senior cohorts still thickening their subject offer. This is where scarcity of a named specialist is reported most often, and where an online shortlist changes the available choice rather than merely the convenience.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.modesIntro: Private tuition is bought in three shapes and the shapes carry different obligations. Each runs one-to-one over live video with a written record afterwards, and each should be quoted separately rather than folded into a single hourly figure.

modes.title: A standing weekly engagement
modes.description: One subject, one slot, one tutor, reviewed at the end of each term. This is the arrangement that produces comparable evidence, because the conditions stay constant. It should come with a stated replacement route, a cancellation window that applies to both sides, and a written note on a fixed cadence rather than on request.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, reviewed termly against the start point
Cancellation window that binds the tutor as well as the family
Written note on a fixed cadence, not when asked for one
Replacement route agreed before it is ever needed

modes.title: A scoped block of hours
modes.description: A fixed number of sessions against a named target: one component, one topic, one draft cycle. Blocks are easier to evaluate than open-ended arrangements because the question at the end is simply whether the named target moved. They also protect a household from drift, where a tutor remains booked long after the original problem was solved.
bullets: A written target naming the component, not the subject
Agreed number of sessions with an end date
A short report at the end against that target
Renewal as a fresh decision, not an automatic rollover

modes.title: A coursework review cycle
modes.description: Scheduled reading of the student's own drafts against the published criteria, timed to the school's internal deadlines. The deliverable is annotated feedback and a plan for the next version. Authorship stays with the student at every stage, and the version history is kept precisely so that authorship is demonstrable if anyone asks.

Dated draft versions retained for the whole cycle

sections.heading: Ask the school first: the support that may already exist
paragraphs: Before hiring anyone, ask your child's head of department one question: what targeted support is already running for this subject and this year group. Most Abu Dhabi schools run something, and much of it is poorly advertised internally. Intervention sessions, subject clinics at lunchtime, Saturday revision in the term before a series, departmental past-paper sessions, learning-support screening and English-as-an-additional-language provision all exist in different combinations.

The honest reason to ask first is arithmetic. School-run support is already paid for inside the fees, and it has one advantage no external tutor can match: the person delivering it is also the person marking the internal assessment and setting the predicted grade. If the same gap can be closed inside the school day, closing it there is both cheaper and better connected.

What school support is usually bad at is individual diagnosis and pace. A clinic serving twelve students cannot sit one of them down with their own marked script for twenty minutes, and a departmental revision session moves at the median. That is the actual gap a private arrangement fills, and defining it that way makes the engagement much easier to scope: you are not buying teaching, you are buying diagnosis and individual pace.

There is one request worth making explicitly. Ask for the subject's assessment breakdown and the department's view of where this particular student is losing marks, in writing. Schools generally provide it when asked directly, and it is the most useful single document a private tutor can be handed at the start. It also makes the first session substantive rather than exploratory, which is an hour saved.

sections.heading: Comparing provider models without comparing rates
paragraphs: Four models compete for this enquiry and they differ in ways an hourly rate hides. A specialist agency screens and replaces but carries an overhead. An international marketplace offers breadth and leaves vetting to you. An independent freelancer is cheapest per hour and has no bench, so illness or departure ends the arrangement. A tuition centre offers group delivery at a lower unit cost and less individual diagnosis.

The two columns that actually predict how an engagement goes are replacement and evidence. Replacement answers what happens in week six when the match turns out to be wrong, and the honest answers range from a new shortlist within days to nothing at all. Evidence answers what you will be able to read at the end of the month, and the range runs from marked scripts and dated drafts to a WhatsApp summary.

Published rates are worth comparing only when the source and date are attached. Most competitor pages in this market either publish no rate or quote in US dollars, which is of no use to a household budgeting in dirhams. The table below names a source for every band, and nothing in it is an IB Gram price list; our own figure depends on subject, level and cadence, and the free trial exists so that the teaching can be judged before the number is discussed.

One warning sign is worth stating plainly. Any provider asserting a star rating, a review count or a success percentage without naming the sample, the date and the method is making a claim that cannot be checked. Two pages found in this market show different aggregate ratings in different places on the same page. That is not a small inconsistency; it is a sign that the figure was decorative.

sections.heading: Nine things worth settling in writing before the first invoice
paragraphs: None of these requires a lawyer and all of them prevent a specific, common dispute. Put them in a message and ask for a reply in the same thread; a provider unwilling to answer in writing has told you something useful. The list is deliberately short and each item exists because of a failure that happens often enough to be predictable.

The most frequently skipped item is the cancellation window applied in both directions. Families generally accept a twenty-four hour notice rule for themselves and never think to ask what happens when the tutor cancels at short notice, which over a term is the more common event. A symmetrical rule, written down, removes the entire argument.

The second most skipped is scope. An engagement that says mathematics will drift; one that says Paper 3 unfamiliar-context questions, reviewed after eight sessions, will not. Scope is also what makes a replacement tutor possible, because a specific target can be handed over whereas a general relationship cannot.

The last three items are about your child rather than about money. What is recorded, where it is stored, how long it is kept and how you have it deleted are reasonable questions under UAE personal-data law, and any provider handling a minor's work should be able to answer them without hesitation. So should the question of what the tutor will and will not do with assessed work.

None of this makes the relationship adversarial. A good tutor welcomes a written scope, because it protects them from the drift where a family quietly expects coursework help, examination technique and homework supervision from a single weekly hour. Clear terms mean the hour can be spent on the thing it was bought for, and the termly review has something to be measured against.

sections.heading: The permit a private tutor in the UAE must hold
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not unregulated and a permit is not optional. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the page to check rather than any provider's description of it. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the government's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Two things follow for a parent. First, no fee should ever be mentioned in connection with the permit itself, so a tutor who says the permit is expensive has not applied for one. Second, no amount can be quoted for the penalty, because no schedule of fines has been published; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, and it is left off this page for that reason.

A separate point catches Abu Dhabi families specifically. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and requires an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant authority. That permit is issued to institutions with premises. No provider, IB Gram included, should describe itself as approved by a regulator unless it holds the specific permit and can show the number.

sections.heading: Continuity: what happens when the tutor changes mid-course
paragraphs: Tutors leave. They relocate, change jobs, or run out of availability in February when everyone wants the same slot. In a Diploma course that lasts two years, a change of tutor partway through is likely rather than exceptional, and almost no private arrangement in this market plans for it. The cost of not planning is a new tutor spending three paid sessions rediscovering a diagnosis that already existed.

What makes a handover cheap is a small, boring pack: the error log or equivalent record of what has been diagnosed, the last three marked scripts, the dated draft history for any coursework, and a one-paragraph statement of the current target. That pack takes the departing tutor twenty minutes to assemble and saves the household several hundred dirhams. Ask for it to be a condition of the engagement from the start.

Draft history deserves particular attention on a Diploma coursework piece. If the versions are dated and the feedback sits as comments beside the student's own text, a new tutor can see exactly where the work stands against each criterion, and the student can demonstrate authorship if the school ever asks. If there is no version history, both of those advantages are gone and the new tutor is reading a finished-looking document with no idea what was contributed by whom.

The same pack is what makes an honest termly review possible. A review that compares the current position against a written start point can reach a real verdict, including the verdict that the arrangement should end. A review with no start point on record can only ever be a conversation about whether everyone feels positive, which is the conversation that keeps unproductive arrangements running for a year.

sections.heading: Reading the first month's records without being a subject teacher
paragraphs: Parents routinely say they cannot judge the work because they do not know the subject. In practice almost all of the useful judgement needs no subject knowledge at all. You are reading for specificity, for comparability and for whether the same problem keeps reappearing under a new name.

Specificity first. A note that says we worked on algebra tells you nothing. A note that says the student lost four method marks on simultaneous equations, drilled three items and scored full method marks on the re-sit tells you what was wrong, what was done and what happened. You do not need to know the mathematics to see that one is accountable and the other is not.

Comparability next. Two marks are only comparable if the conditions were. Ask where the paper was sat, how long was allowed, whether notes were available and what the first attempt scored. A rising set of marks collected under steadily easier conditions is not progress, and this is the most common way a month of records flatters an arrangement.

Finally, recurrence. Read the notes in sequence and look for the same problem in different words. Careless errors in week one, needs to slow down in week three, silly mistakes in week five is one unresolved problem described three times. A tutor who has genuinely diagnosed it will have named it the same way each time and shown what the drill changed.

If a month produces none of these, the useful move is not to complain but to ask for one specific thing: the last marked script, with the marks shown where they were awarded. The response to that request tells you most of what you need. A tutor who sends it within a day was already working that way; a tutor who sends a summary instead has told you that nothing of the kind exists.

sections.heading: Where a private tutor must stop
paragraphs: Two boundaries are absolute and both protect your child rather than the tutor. The first concerns assessed work. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and any Middle Years project must be the student's own work, authenticated by the school supervisor. A tutor may teach the skills, read what the student has produced and comment against the published criteria. Authorship does not transfer in whole or in part, and a provider offering finished coursework should be declined on the spot.

What legitimate feedback sounds like is narrower than people assume and more useful. The criterion asks for the method to state how the variable was controlled, and yours does not. This paragraph asserts a conclusion the data does not support; which part of your results would a sceptical reader challenge first? Both comments are specific, both are criterion-anchored, and neither supplies text. That is the line, and it is the same line a school supervisor works to.

The second boundary concerns board material. Syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and past papers belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor may reference them and send you the official page where they sit. Reproducing them as downloads is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well. If a provider offers a drive folder of papers, ask where the material came from.

A third caution sits alongside these. A tutor who describes themselves as an examiner for a board should be able to evidence current status, and examiner status must never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it is not. The honest value of examiner experience is familiarity with how answers are credited, and that is worth something without needing to be oversold.

sections.heading: One tutor for both boards, or two?
paragraphs: Households running an IGCSE child and a Diploma child reasonably ask whether one tutor can cover both. The answer depends on the subject rather than on the tutor's enthusiasm. In mathematics the content overlap is genuine: the algebra that Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tests is the foundation Analysis and Approaches assumes, and a tutor strong in Diploma mathematics will teach the IGCSE material competently.

In the sciences the overlap is weaker than it looks. The content continues, but the assessment models diverge sharply: an IGCSE science grade rests on externally marked papers including an alternative-to-practical component, while a Diploma science grade includes an independently designed investigation worth twenty-four criterion marks. A tutor can know both and still be much better at one, and the right question is which component each child actually needs.

In languages and humanities the two should usually be separated. Diploma English A: Language and Literature and Cambridge First Language English 0500 reward different things, and a tutor who coaches the Diploma individual oral well is not therefore the right choice for IGCSE directed writing. The same holds for Economics and Business Management, where the Diploma's evaluation demands have no real IGCSE equivalent.

Where two tutors are the answer, the thing to insist on is a shared schedule and visible records for both, so that the household is managing one plan rather than two relationships. Where one tutor genuinely covers both, ask for the records to be kept separately by child and by specification, because the two will be judged against completely different evidence.

process.title: Ask the school what already exists
process.description: One email to the head of department asking what targeted support is running for this subject and year group, and for the department's written view on where this student is losing marks. Much of this is funded inside the fees and poorly advertised, and the written view makes any first private session substantive.

process.title: Send the specification, not the subject
process.description: Tell us the board, the code, the tier or level and the component in question, plus one marked script. That identifies what is actually being taught against. A tutor who does not ask which code the school entered your child for is teaching to a textbook rather than to a specification.

process.title: Settle the nine terms in one message
process.description: Scope, session length, cancellation both ways, replacement route, evidence cadence, the assessed-work boundary, the permit position, data and recordings, and what the rate excludes. Ask for a written reply. The answers take a provider ten minutes and prevent every common dispute.

process.title: Use the free trial as an audition
process.description: One full session with the tutor who would actually teach, at no charge and with no card details. Watch for whether they ask to see work before explaining anything, whether they name the component, and whether a written note arrives afterwards without being requested.

process.title: Review at the end of term against a written start point
process.description: Compare the records against the diagnosis made in week one. The verdict is continue, re-diagnose, or stop, and all three are given plainly. If the arrangement ends, the handover pack is assembled so that nothing already paid for has to be rediscovered.

whyPoints.title: Coverage and limits stated before the invoice
whyPoints.description: If no specialist currently covers the component you need, you are told that, with the realistic wait and the alternative, before anything is booked. A coverage limit disclosed in week one costs far less than the same limit discovered in week six.

whyPoints.title: A replacement route that exists on paper
whyPoints.description: A wrong match is a normal event over two Diploma years, not a failure to be argued about. The route to a new shortlist, and the handover pack that goes with it, are agreed at the start rather than improvised when it happens.

whyPoints.title: Records a parent can audit
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts in the student's own hand, written notes naming a component and an error type, comparable second attempts with conditions stated, and dated coursework drafts. Specific enough to check without knowing the subject.

whyPoints.title: The permit position, with its source
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free for two years, with the official application page named so you can verify rather than take our word for it. No invented fee, and no invented penalty figure.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider or report that published it, with the year. They are market observations rather than our price list, so that a household budgeting in dirhams has something real to compare against.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work line held in both directions
whyPoints.description: Drafts are read and commented on against the published criteria, with version history kept so authorship is demonstrable. No board material is reproduced; the official link is sent instead.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's Abu Dhabi school before hiring a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Two things, by email, to the head of department. First, what targeted support already runs for this subject and year group: intervention sessions, lunchtime clinics, past-paper sessions, learning-support screening or language provision. Much of it is funded inside the fees and poorly advertised. Second, ask for the department's written view on where this particular student is losing marks, and for the subject's assessment breakdown. Schools usually provide both when asked directly. That document is the most useful thing you can hand a private tutor, and it turns the first session from exploratory into substantive.

faqs.question: Does an independent freelance tutor or an agency make more sense for a two-year Diploma?
faqs.answer: Over two years the deciding factor is usually the bench rather than the rate. A freelancer is cheaper per hour and has no cover, so illness, relocation or a full February diary ends the arrangement with nothing behind it. An agency carries overhead and should, in exchange, provide a replacement shortlist and a handover pack. Ask both the same question: what happens in week six if this match is wrong, and what will I be able to read at the end of the month. The answers separate the models more reliably than any price comparison.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing and lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold it. Anyone describing the permit as expensive has not applied, since there is no fee.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for tutoring in the UAE without a permit?
faqs.answer: The government's position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, and reporting on the subject has stated explicitly that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. Figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so no amount appears on this page. What matters practically for a family is simpler: ask whether the permit is held, and treat an evasive answer as an answer.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at an Abu Dhabi school tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: It should be ruled out. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Beyond the rule, there is a structural reason to avoid it: the same person would be teaching, marking the internal assessment and setting the predicted grade, with a paid interest in the outcome. Verify the current policy wording with the school before acting on any arrangement of this kind.

faqs.question: What should be settled in writing before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Nine items, and a short message covers all of them. The scope, named as a component rather than a subject. Session length and what realistically fits in it. A cancellation window that binds both sides equally. The replacement route if the match fails. The evidence cadence. The boundary on assessed work. The permit position. What is recorded, where it is stored, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted. And what the quoted rate excludes, itemised. A provider unwilling to answer those in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor leaves halfway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Over two years it is likely rather than exceptional, so it should be planned for at the start. Ask for a handover pack to be a condition of the engagement: the record of what has been diagnosed, the last three marked scripts, the dated draft history for any coursework, and a one-paragraph statement of the current target. It takes a departing tutor twenty minutes to assemble and saves a new one three paid sessions of rediscovery. Without it, a replacement reads a finished-looking document with no idea what has already been tried.

faqs.question: How can I judge the records when I do not know the subject?
faqs.answer: Almost all of the useful judgement needs no subject knowledge. Read for specificity: we worked on algebra tells you nothing, while four method marks lost on simultaneous equations, three items drilled, full method marks on the re-sit tells you everything. Read for comparability: ask where the paper was sat, how long was allowed and whether notes were available, because marks only compare when conditions do. And read the notes in sequence for the same problem renamed. Careless, then slow down, then silly mistakes is one unresolved problem described three times.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for a tutor who says they are an examiner?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced and only for what it genuinely buys. Current examiner status should be verifiable, and it must never be presented as access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content, because it is not. What examiner experience honestly provides is familiarity with how answers are credited, which is worth something on a component where students lose marks to phrasing rather than to knowledge. At the premium end the market reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED, so the question is whether that specific component needs it.

faqs.question: What does a private IB or IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market bands in 2026, each attributed on this page: a qualified subject tutor working online sits broadly between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits carry the drive inside the rate and published bands reach AED 500. The premium end reaches AED 650. These are market observations rather than IB Gram's prices, and the free trial lesson exists so that teaching can be judged before rates are discussed.

faqs.question: Should I buy a block of hours or an open-ended weekly arrangement?
faqs.answer: A block is easier to evaluate and a standing arrangement produces better evidence, so the sensible pattern is a block first and a standing arrangement afterwards if the block worked. A block has a named target, an agreed number of sessions and an end date, which forces a real verdict instead of a drift. A standing arrangement keeps the conditions constant, which is what makes marks comparable across a term. What should be avoided is an open-ended arrangement with no named target, because nothing in it ever triggers a decision.

faqs.question: What is my child's tutor allowed to do with an Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the skills the task requires, read what the student has written, and comment against the published criteria. Legitimate feedback is a criterion reference or a question: the criterion requires the method to state how the variable was controlled, and yours does not; this paragraph asserts a conclusion the data does not support. What may never happen is authorship transferring in whole or in part. Keeping dated draft versions with comments beside the student's own text protects them, because progression becomes visible and attributable if the school asks how the work developed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor send us past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: A tutor should send you the official page where that material sits rather than the files themselves. Syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and past papers belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing them as downloads is a copyright problem; for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well. If a provider offers a shared folder of papers, it is reasonable to ask where the material came from. Working from official sources also avoids the common error of revising from the wrong board's resources.

faqs.question: What is kept about my child, and how do we have it deleted?
faqs.answer: Ask and expect a straight answer, because this is a reasonable question under UAE personal-data law. A sensible arrangement collects the subject, the board and level, the school year, the work submitted for feedback and the session records, and nothing else. Recordings, where they exist, should have a stated retention period and a route to deletion on request. What should never be collected without a stated purpose is a child's photograph, grade history and school in a single form. If the purpose cannot be explained, the field should not be there.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE and a Diploma child in the same household?
faqs.answer: In mathematics, often yes: the algebra tested by Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher is the foundation Analysis and Approaches assumes, so a strong Diploma tutor teaches it well. In the sciences the overlap is weaker than it looks, because a Diploma grade includes an independently designed investigation worth twenty-four criterion marks and an IGCSE grade does not. In languages and humanities the two usually need separating. Where two tutors are the answer, insist on a shared schedule and separate records per child and per specification.

faqs.question: Do private tutors come to our home in Abu Dhabi, or is this online?
faqs.answer: IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are offered only in India. If you prefer a visiting tutor, the questions on this page still apply to whoever you hire: the permit, the replacement route, the records, the assessed-work boundary and what the rate excludes. One practical difference is worth weighing. A video session can be recorded and rewatched, and a household in Al Shamkha gets the same shortlist as one on the Corniche.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Hire on terms, not on a rate
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: The gap between a private arrangement that works and one that quietly does not is rarely the hourly figure. It is whether the scope was named, whether the records exist, whether a replacement route was agreed before anybody needed it, and whether the person teaching your child holds the permit UAE law requires. All four are settled in one written exchange before the first invoice. Send the board, the specification code, the level and one marked script, and the trial lesson that follows is one full session with the tutor who would teach, free, with no card details and no obligation.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and IGCSE subjects that Abu Dhabi families ask for most often. Each one teaches a named syllabus rather than a general subject, and each works from your child's own marked scripts, school deadlines and assessment calendar rather than a fixed course of their own.

intro.heading: What a search for tuition near me can and cannot tell you
paragraphs: A map search is a proximity filter. It sorts providers by how far they sit from the device you are holding, which is a measure of driving time and nothing else. It does not know that your daughter is sitting Chemistry at Higher Level and losing marks on enthalpy cycles rather than on organic mechanisms. It does not know that your son's Edexcel International GCSE maths paper is the modular route and his cousin's Cambridge paper is not. Distance is the one variable that has no relationship at all to the thing you are buying.

Abu Dhabi makes this sharper than most cities. The emirate's private-school population is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Al Reem, and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Al Falah. A family in Al Raha Gardens and a family in Al Mushrif are forty minutes apart at the wrong hour of the afternoon. Draw a twenty-minute radius around either house and you have drawn a circle that contains a handful of generalist tutors and almost no specialists in any single Diploma subject at Higher Level.

So the honest version of IB IGCSE tuition near me in Abu Dhabi is this: the tutor pool that matters is the one your child can see and hear, not the one that can reach your door. Lessons at IB Gram run live, one to one, over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the Abu Dhabi school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a driver and a doorbell, would be selling something we do not sell.

Removing distance from the equation leaves a gap, and the gap is accountability. A tutor who sits at your kitchen table is at least visible. A tutor on a screen has to prove the hour was worth it, and the only way to prove it is on paper. That is the whole design of this page. Every section below is about an artefact: a marked script with the mark-scheme reference next to each lost mark, a session note naming the error class worked on, a draft history that shows an Internal Assessment belongs to the student, a twelve-week record a parent can read without knowing the subject.

None of this is unusual practice among good teachers. It is unusual among tutoring providers, which is the point. Of the ranking pages we examined for the UAE tutoring queries in October 2026, none published what a parent should expect to receive after a month of lessons. Most published a photograph of a smiling child and a contact form. A record you can audit is the difference between a service and a subscription, and it is also the only reliable way to decide whether to continue, change subject focus, or change tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families arrive on this page from four different programmes, and the evidence that tuition is working looks different in each. A PYP parent wants to see a reading behaviour change. A DP parent wants to see a Paper 2 mark move. The programme decides what counts as proof.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year qualification most British-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi run before Sixth Form or the Diploma. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes, Edexcel International GCSE codes begin with a digit and a subject letter pair. The tiering question matters: Cambridge maths 0580 splits Core and Extended, Edexcel 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher, and the tier a school entered your child for caps the grade available.
programmes.countryNote: Evidence on an IGCSE subject is unusually easy to collect because past papers are plentiful and mark schemes are published. A parent in Abu Dhabi can ask for the script, the mark scheme page reference and the running total of marks lost by question type. Within a term that becomes a clear picture: a child losing marks on method rather than knowledge needs a different set of sessions from one losing marks on recall.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. The written papers are sat in a single session, which is why a two-year plan with visible checkpoints matters more here than in any other programme.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is concentrated in a small number of schools, so a subject combination that is ordinary nationally can be rare locally. A student taking Economics HL with Chemistry HL and Spanish B may be the only one in their year group doing so. Proof of progress then has to come from the subject's own criteria and from marked papers, because there is no useful class average to compare against.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with the criteria wording doing most of the work. MYP reports often read as a wall of letters and numbers, and parents frequently cannot tell whether a 5 in Criterion C is a problem. It usually is, and it is usually a specific, fixable problem.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is where Abu Dhabi families most often ask for help, because the assessment language changes completely. We treat the criteria letters as the evidence base: a student scoring well on Criterion A knowledge and poorly on Criterion D reflection in Sciences has a writing problem, not a science problem, and the session plan says so in writing.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, so progress is recorded through observation, portfolios and conferences rather than marks. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habits that make the MYP survivable, and it is deliberately light touch.
programmes.countryNote: Because there is no mark to track, the evidence record for a PYP child in Abu Dhabi is behavioural and specific: words read per minute on an unseen passage, the number of steps a child can hold in a multi-step problem, whether they can explain a method back. Those are the numbers that go in the session notes, and a parent can check them at home in five minutes.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families bring to us most often, described by where marks actually leave the paper. Each description is the thing a tutor would write in the first session note after reading a marked script.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks leave on the non-calculator paper and on the reasoning questions where a correct answer with no visible method earns little. The recoverable pattern is almost always method presentation and algebraic fluency rather than topic ignorance, which is why a marked script is more diagnostic than a test score.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavy on modelling, statistics and technology use. Students lose marks by giving un-rounded answers, omitting units, or failing to interpret a result in context after calculating it correctly. The fix is a checklist habit, and progress on it is visible within three or four marked papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks at Higher Level. At IGCSE the losses cluster in mole calculations and in the practical paper's planning and evaluation questions. Both patterns show up clearly once two papers are marked by question type rather than by total.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where IGCSE candidates lose most, and the extended-response questions are where they lose silently because partial method goes unwritten. At Diploma level the loss moves to the data-analysis and uncertainty questions, which are teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The content is learnable and the marks are lost on command terms. A question that says outline, explain and discuss wants three different shapes of answer, and a student who writes the same paragraph for all three caps their own grade. Marked scripts make this obvious in one sitting.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in Abu Dhabi, and the one where tier matters most. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, so the first useful question is which paper your child is actually entered for. After that, the losses are usually in algebra, bearings and compound measures.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0500 and 0475
subjects.description: Reading marks come back fastest because they depend on technique a tutor can demonstrate: annotation, question order, and using the extract rather than remembering the text. Writing marks move more slowly and need marked drafts rather than lessons about writing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation sentence carry more marks than the content. Students who can define everything and evaluate nothing sit at a predictable ceiling, and lifting it is a drilling job with a clear before-and-after on marked answers.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole game. Generic answers that never mention the stimulus material lose application and analysis marks regardless of how much theory they contain, and the correction is mechanical once a tutor shows it on the student's own script.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0478 and 0417
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the precise wording of definition questions are where IGCSE marks go. At Diploma level the internal assessment carries the risk, because a working program with a thin success-criteria record scores badly against the criteria.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi districts, and what proximity actually costs in each
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: These notes are about one thing only: what a search for a nearby tutor returns in each district, and what the drive does to a weekday session. They are written from the scheduling problem, not from the property brochure.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The densest school corridor in the emirate and the one where the school run eats the usable afternoon. A session that starts at 16:00 for a family here is realistic online and optimistic for anyone driving in from the island.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short bridge from the island but a long way from the mainland tutor pool. Families here routinely find that the nearest person offering Diploma Chemistry is a generalist, while the nearest subject specialist is not in the emirate at all.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers with a growing school presence. Lift queues and building access genuinely affect arrival times for in-home tutoring, which is one reason families here switch to video sessions after a term of trying both.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established island districts close to several long-standing British-curriculum schools. Proximity to schools is high, proximity to specialist Higher Level subject tutors is not, and the two are easy to confuse in a map search.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central, well served by schools, and badly served by afternoon traffic in both directions. A 17:00 slot booked with someone travelling from the mainland is a 17:20 slot in practice, and the lost twenty minutes is paid for.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Mainland communities where the nearest tuition centre may be a twenty-five minute drive. Several families here run two children in different programmes, and a fixed online slot for each is the only arrangement that survives a full term.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Jubail Island
regions.note: Newer residential pockets with limited local tutoring supply. The practical choice is between a generalist who happens to be nearby and a syllabus specialist who is not, and the evidence record is how you tell which one earned the hour.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Villa communities out towards the airport road with long school commutes already built into the day. Adding a tutor's travel time to a child who has been in a bus since 14:30 is the scheduling mistake families here most often describe.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British and American curriculum schools sit close together here, which makes the island look well supplied. Supply of classroom teaching is not supply of one-to-one specialist support, and the ADEK professional-ethics position reported in the UAE press means a child's own school teacher is not the route to it.

sections.heading: What typing near me actually returns in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A local search for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Abu Dhabi returns three kinds of result, and only one of them is a tutor. The first kind is a tuition centre with premises, which is a business holding a permit to operate from a location and employing whoever it has recruited. The second is a marketplace listing that sorts by distance because distance is the only field it reliably holds. The third is a blog post written to rank, with a contact form at the bottom and no named tutor anywhere on it.

None of those three tell you the thing you need. A centre two streets away may be excellent at IGCSE maths and have nobody at all for Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level. A marketplace listing ranked first for your district may be first because the tutor set their location to the city centre. And the blog post will quote a rate range without saying who charges it, which the October 2026 competitor audit found on page after page: three of six ranking pages in this cluster published no price at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars.

What a parent actually wants from a near-me search is a shortlist filtered by subject, level and syllabus code, then checked for whether the person is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE, then tested in a trial lesson. Distance belongs nowhere in that sequence once lessons are delivered over video. The table below sets out, district by district, what the map gives you and what it leaves out.

The honest conclusion is that proximity is a convenience variable that stopped mattering when the delivery moved to video, and that the variable it was standing in for, accountability, now has to be supplied directly. That is what the rest of this page is about.

sections.heading: Proximity against specialism: the twenty-minute radius problem
paragraphs: Put a compass point on any Abu Dhabi address and draw a twenty-minute drive. Inside that circle you will find people who can teach Key Stage 3 maths, people who can teach IGCSE maths, and with luck one person who has taught Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the last two years. Widen the circle to the whole emirate and the Higher Level count rises, but so does the travel time, and travel time is the thing that kills a weekly slot by November.

Now remove the circle. The pool becomes every tutor who can be on a video call at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, which includes specialists based in the UAE and specialists based elsewhere who teach the same syllabus. For a mainstream subject such as IGCSE maths the difference is marginal, because supply is good locally. For a narrow combination such as Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Chemistry, or an Edexcel International GCSE modular route, the difference is the whole decision.

This is the trade a family makes without being told they are making it. The convenience of a nearby tutor is real and immediate. The cost of it is paid later, in a term spent with someone who knows the subject but not the syllabus, or knows the syllabus but not the tier. We publish the trade openly because the alternative, pretending a local generalist and a syllabus specialist are the same purchase, is how a parent ends up three months in with no movement and no explanation.

Availability transparency matters here too. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject and level, we say so and offer the specialist we do have, with the time zone and the rate stated before anything is booked. No competitor page in the ten query clusters we audited discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without mentioning it.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: six artefacts and what each one proves
paragraphs: A parent cannot sit in on every lesson, and should not have to. What they can do is ask what the arrangement produces, and then read it. Six artefacts cover almost everything worth knowing, and all six are cheap for a competent tutor to produce because they are the by-product of teaching properly rather than extra administration.

The first is the diagnostic note from the opening session, which should name the error classes found and the evidence for each. The second is the weekly session note. The third is a marked script with mark-scheme references. The fourth is an error log that tracks each identified weakness from first appearance to retirement. The fifth is the dated draft history on any Internal Assessment or Extended Essay work. The sixth is a termly summary that compares the student against their own earlier papers rather than against a class.

What makes these useful is that each one has a limit. A session note proves attendance and focus, not learning. A marked script proves a mark on one paper on one day, not a trend. An error log proves a pattern, which is the closest thing to proof available before results day. Knowing the limits stops a parent over-reading a good week and panicking at a bad one, and it stops a provider using a cheerful note as a substitute for a mark.

Ask for the pack at the start rather than at the end. A provider who cannot describe what you will receive after four weeks is telling you something, and a provider who promises a specific grade in exchange for a specific number of hours is telling you something worse. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be read as making a sales claim rather than an academic one.

sections.heading: How to read a marked script when you do not know the subject
paragraphs: This is a skill, it takes about fifteen minutes to learn, and it changes the conversation with any tutor permanently. Start at the back of the script rather than the front. The final questions carry the most marks and are the ones most often abandoned, and a pattern of blank final questions is a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem. Timing problems are among the fastest things to fix, and a tutor who has not noticed is not reading the script either.

Next, look only at the command term in each question where marks were lost. Examination papers use a controlled vocabulary: state, outline, describe, explain, analyse, discuss, evaluate, justify, deduce, show that. Each one demands a particular shape of answer, and each is worth a predictable number of marks. A student who writes a description when the paper said explain has lost marks on a translation error, not on content. Group the lost marks by command term and the diagnosis usually writes itself.

Third, check whether the method is visible. In maths and the sciences, a correct final answer with no working shown earns fewer marks than an incorrect answer with full method. This single habit accounts for a large share of avoidable loss in both Cambridge and Edexcel scripts, and it is a presentation discipline rather than an intellectual one. Ask the tutor to show you three examples on your child's own paper. If they cannot find three, ask why not.

Finally, ignore the total. A total tells you where a child stood on one morning against one paper, and nothing about direction. Two scripts marked three weeks apart, grouped by question type, tell you far more than a mock percentage. This is why our marking returns the grouping rather than only the number, and why the termly summary compares a student against their own earlier scripts rather than against a cohort we have no business publishing figures about.
bullets: Read the script from the last question forwards
Group lost marks by command term, not by topic
Check whether method is written down, not just the answer
Count abandoned questions separately from wrong ones
Compare two scripts by question type before reading either total

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of a record, week by week
paragraphs: Abstract promises about progress tracking mean very little, so here is the concrete version: what a term of one weekly session on one IGCSE subject looks like on paper, with what gets filed each week. This is a model, not a guarantee, and the pace varies with the student, the subject and how much of the syllabus has been taught at school by the time the sessions begin.

The shape matters more than the specific weeks. The first three weeks are diagnostic and produce more evidence than teaching. Weeks four to eight are where error classes are worked and retired, and where the marked work starts to show movement by question type. Weeks nine to twelve are consolidation under timed conditions, where the question is no longer whether the student knows something but whether they can produce it in the time available with the method written down.

A parent reading this record should be able to answer three questions at any point: what is currently being worked on, what evidence exists that it has changed, and what is next. If the answer to the second question is a feeling rather than a document, the arrangement is not being run properly, whoever is running it and however near your home they live.

Note what is absent from the table. There is no predicted grade, no percentage improvement and no promise about results day. Those numbers are available from nobody honestly, and the competitor audit found several pages publishing exactly that kind of figure with no sample size, date or method attached to it. A record of work done and change measured is a smaller claim and a true one.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection reports and what a rating does not tell you
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge. The UAE government's own description is that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK publishes inspection outcomes for the schools it oversees. This matters to a tuition decision in a narrower way than most parents assume, and it is worth being precise about why.

An inspection rating is a whole-school judgement built from many strands: leadership, provision, safeguarding, outcomes across phases, and progress against previous recommendations. It is a statement about an institution. It is not a statement about the Higher Level Chemistry teaching your daughter receives in a set of eleven students on a Tuesday afternoon, and it cannot be. A strongly rated school can have one subject with a staffing gap, and a mid-rated school can have an outstanding maths department.

What an inspection report is genuinely useful for is the narrative detail rather than the headline band. Reports name strands where attainment lags, and if the strand named is the subject your child is struggling in, you have independent corroboration of something you suspected. If the report names something else entirely and your child is still losing marks, the problem is more likely to be individual, which is precisely the case tutoring addresses.

The regulator map across the UAE is worth knowing if your family moves between emirates, which happens often. Dubai sits under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or endorsement from any of them, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment drafts: the record that protects the student
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and every one of them must be the student's own work. The IB's academic-honesty framework makes the student responsible for authenticity, and a school supervisor signs to confirm it. That places a hard boundary around what any tutor may do, and the boundary is not a matter of opinion or of house style.

A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss the suitability of a research question, read a draft and give feedback, and ask questions that make the student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sentences, restructure a section on the student's behalf, or hand over a finished piece of work. The difference is visible in the artefact: feedback keyed to criterion letters and questions for the student to answer, rather than tracked changes inside their document.

The practical protection is the draft history. Each review session works from a dated copy of what the student has produced, and the copies are retained. If authorship is ever questioned, the sequence of drafts shows a piece of work developing in one person's hands, with the tutor's comments visible as comments rather than as text. This is a defence a student can actually use, and it costs nothing to maintain.

The reason this section exists on a page about finding nearby tuition is that the UAE market contains providers selling the opposite. The October 2026 audit found a provider openly offering completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and, for the student, an IB malpractice exposure that can end a Diploma. No IB Gram tutor supplies assessed work, edits a draft to completion, or acts as an author on any coursework.
bullets: Feedback is keyed to criterion letters and mark bands, never inserted as text
Every review works from a dated draft that the student produced
Draft copies are retained so the development sequence is visible
The school supervisor's deadlines and process take precedence
A request to supply finished coursework is declined, and the reason explained

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached to it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The u.ae guidance states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the words of the same guidance, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

For an Abu Dhabi family there is a second consideration. UAE press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carrying a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and verify it against the current policy document if it affects a decision you are about to make. The practical upshot is simple: your child's own subject teacher is not the right person to pay privately.

A tuition business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, and in Dubai needs an educational services permit from KHDA for a training institute. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, so any provider describing itself as regulator-approved should be asked to show the permit number. This is also the single most common overstatement in the UAE tutoring market.
