sections.heading: When the evidence says pause, change focus, or change tutor
paragraphs: The point of keeping a record is that it can tell you to stop. Most tutoring arrangements end because somebody loses interest, which means the decision was never made, only drifted into. A record makes the decision available, and there are three distinct versions of it that families confuse with each other.

The first is pause. Pause is right when the evidence shows the error classes have been retired and the student is working independently at the level they need. Paying for maintenance sessions after that point is buying reassurance, and it is better to stop and re-book before the next assessment block than to keep a slot running out of habit. Several of our Abu Dhabi families run exactly this pattern across a two-year Diploma.

The second is change focus. Change focus is right when the marked work shows one error class stubbornly unmoved while others have cleared. That usually means the diagnosis was wrong rather than the teaching: a student losing marks in Physics extended-response questions may have a writing problem that a Physics tutor will keep treating as a Physics problem. Moving the work to the actual weakness is cheaper than adding hours to the wrong one.

The third is change tutor. Change tutor is right when four or more weeks have produced session notes but no measurable change by question type, or when the student cannot explain what they worked on last week. Neither of those is a character judgement; some pairings simply do not work. We treat a replacement request as routine, and we do not ask a family to justify it. What we do ask is that the next tutor receives the error log, so the twelve weeks already spent are not re-spent from scratch.
bullets: Pause when error classes are retired and the student works independently
Change focus when one weakness stays unmoved while others clear
Change tutor after four weeks of notes with no measured change
Carry the error log across to the next tutor rather than restarting
Re-book before a mock or assessment block rather than holding a slot all year

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Cambridge or Edexcel, the four-digit or alphanumeric code, the tier, and the school's assessment dates. A Year 11 student on Edexcel 4MA1 Higher needs a different tutor from one on Cambridge 0580 Core, and the two are easy to confuse from a school report alone. If you do not know the code, send a photograph of a past paper cover.

process.title: Send one marked piece of work
process.description: One recent marked paper, test or assignment is worth more than a page of description. It is what the first session is built from, and it is what the diagnostic note refers back to. If nothing has been marked recently, we will set a short unseen paper in the trial lesson and mark that instead.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full-length first session with the matched tutor at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. It is a working lesson rather than a sales call, and it produces the diagnostic note whether or not you go on to book. If the pairing is wrong, say so and we will match somebody else.

process.title: Read the diagnostic note before you decide
process.description: The note names the error classes found, the evidence for each, and what a term of work would address first. Read it against your own sense of the problem. A note that reads as generic encouragement rather than specific diagnosis is a reason to ask for a different tutor, and we would rather you asked at this stage.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep the record running
process.description: A weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time, a session note after each lesson, marked work returned with scheme references, and an error log updated as classes are retired. At the end of each term you receive a summary comparing your child against their own earlier scripts rather than against anybody else's children.

whyPoints.title: The record is the product
whyPoints.description: Session notes, marked scripts with mark-scheme references, an error log and a dated draft history are produced as a matter of course, not on request. A parent who cannot attend lessons can still audit them, which is the only honest answer to the accountability gap that online delivery creates.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by distance
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Cambridge 0620 or Edexcel 4CH1 or DP Chemistry HL specifically, with the tier confirmed before the first session. Removing distance from the filter is what makes that possible for a family in Al Shamkha or on Saadiyat, where local specialist supply in a single Higher Level subject is thin.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject and level, we say so, name the alternative, and state the time zone and rate before anything is booked. No page in the competitor set we audited in October 2026 discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE numbers without mentioning it.

whyPoints.title: Academic-honesty boundaries in writing
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and coursework support is feedback on the student's own dated drafts, keyed to criterion letters. No tutor supplies text or finishes a piece of work. The draft history exists so that the student can demonstrate authorship if it is ever questioned.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction percentages, no self-published star ratings, no regulator approval we do not hold. Every AED figure on this page is a market rate attributed to its source rather than a price of ours, and anything about IB exam dates is left to the IB and your child's coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Abu Dhabi school day
whyPoints.description: Slots are set on Gulf Standard Time around actual school finish times and the eastern-corridor commute, with session timing shifted during Ramadan and around assessment blocks. A slot that works in October and not in March is not a slot, and a record that stops in March is not a record.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to live near us in Abu Dhabi to be useful?
faqs.answer: No. Distance affects convenience and nothing else once lessons are delivered live over video, and it has no relationship to whether a tutor has taught your child's syllabus and tier. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition online to Abu Dhabi families and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What proximity used to supply was visibility, and that is replaced here by a written record: session notes, marked scripts with mark-scheme references, and an error log you can read without knowing the subject.

faqs.question: What should I ask to see after four weeks of lessons?
faqs.answer: Four things. A diagnostic note from the first session naming the error classes found and the evidence for each. Four session notes saying what was taught and what was set. At least one marked piece of work with references to the published mark scheme beside the lost marks. An error log showing which weaknesses have moved. If all four exist and nothing has changed by question type, that is a reason to change focus or change tutor. If they do not exist at all, the arrangement is not being run properly, however good the lessons feel.

faqs.question: How do I read a marked paper if I do not know the subject myself?
faqs.answer: Start at the last question and work backwards, because abandoned final questions indicate a timing problem rather than a knowledge one. Then look only at the command term in each question where marks were lost: state, explain, analyse and discuss each demand a different shape of answer, and mismatches cluster. Then check whether method is written down, since a correct answer with no working earns less than a wrong answer with full method. Ignore the total. Two scripts a few weeks apart, grouped by question type, tell you far more than any single percentage.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a few streets away better than a specialist on a video call?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject. For IGCSE maths, local supply in Abu Dhabi is good and a nearby centre may be a reasonable choice. For Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Economics or an Edexcel modular route, the nearest centre is unlikely to hold a specialist, and you would be paying for convenience rather than expertise. Ask the centre which syllabus code and tier the assigned tutor has taught, and how many times. A centre that cannot answer at subject level is selling rooms and hours rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What counts as evidence that tuition is working rather than just a feeling?
faqs.answer: Movement in lost marks grouped by question type, measured across at least two marked papers sat under similar conditions. Everything else is a leading indicator: fewer abandoned questions, method written down without prompting, the student able to explain last week's work unprompted. Those are real and they usually arrive first. What is not evidence is a cheerful session note, a child who enjoys the lessons, or a single good mock. A term that produces three marked scripts and an error log gives you something you can actually read a trend from.

faqs.question: How long before any of this shows up in a school report?
faqs.answer: School reports are slow instruments. They are usually written on data gathered weeks earlier, they aggregate several components, and they compare a student against a cohort rather than against their own earlier work. A change visible in marked papers in week six may not appear in a report until the following term. That is why we track against the student's own previous scripts. If you want an earlier signal, ask the subject teacher directly what has changed in class, which is quicker and more specific than waiting for a report cycle.

faqs.question: Can we see what the tutor writes about our child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should read it rather than filing it. The session note is written for a parent, not for a teacher audience, and it names the error class worked on, the material used, and what the student should attempt before the next lesson. The diagnostic note and the error log are the same. Nothing is written in the record that we would not say to you directly. If a note is vague enough that you cannot tell what happened in the hour, that is worth raising, and it is usually a sign the hour was vague too.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection band tell me about my child's lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents expect. An inspection outcome is a whole-school judgement covering leadership, provision, safeguarding and outcomes across every phase. It is not a judgement about the teaching your child receives in one subject set. The useful part of a report is the narrative: if it names a strand where attainment lags and that is the subject your child is struggling in, you have independent corroboration. If the report praises that department and your child is still losing marks, the problem is probably individual, which is the case one-to-one work addresses.

faqs.question: My child says the sessions are useful but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnosis problem before treating it as a teaching problem. Pull the error log and check whether one class has stayed unmoved while others cleared. A common pattern is a student losing marks in extended-response questions across several subjects, which is a writing and structure issue that each subject tutor keeps treating as their own subject's issue. Moving the work to the real weakness is cheaper than adding hours. If the log shows no movement anywhere after four weeks of notes, ask for a different tutor and send the log with the request.

faqs.question: What record should exist of Internal Assessment supervision?
faqs.answer: A dated copy of each draft the student produced, plus the tutor's feedback keyed to criterion letters and kept separate from the student's text. That sequence demonstrates a piece of work developing in one person's hands, which is a defence the student can use if authenticity is ever questioned. What should not exist is tracked changes inside the document from the tutor, or a version where sentences appeared that the student cannot explain. No IB Gram tutor supplies text, edits to completion or acts as an author on any assessed component, and the school supervisor's process always takes precedence.

faqs.question: Should we compare our child to the class average or to their own last paper?
faqs.answer: To their own last paper, for tutoring purposes. A class average tells you about a cohort, which changes between sets, between years and between schools, and tells you nothing about which marks your child can recover. Self-comparison by question type tells you exactly that. The cohort comparison does matter for one decision, which is whether a subject choice or tier is right in the first place, and that is a conversation for the school. Our termly summaries deliberately compare a student only against their own earlier scripts.

faqs.question: How many past papers should be marked before a June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, marked far more carefully than most families imagine. Three or four full papers sat to time and marked properly against the published scheme, with lost marks grouped and then actually worked on, beats a dozen papers skimmed for a percentage. The marking is where the value sits, not the sitting. The one thing worth adding in the final fortnight is a timed paper with no marking attached, purely to practise pacing, because pace under pressure is a separate skill from accuracy.

faqs.question: What does a weak evidence trail from a tutoring provider look like?
faqs.answer: Session notes that could describe any student, feedback expressed only as encouragement, no marked work returned, no reference to a mark scheme, and no record of what has changed. Add to that any promise of a specific grade, any published satisfaction percentage without a sample size and date, any claim of regulator approval, and any offer to help produce coursework. Each of those is a sales artefact rather than an academic one. Ask what you will receive after a month before you pay for a month, and compare the answer with what arrives.

faqs.question: Does the free trial lesson produce anything we can keep?
faqs.answer: Yes. The trial is a full-length working lesson with the matched tutor, not a sales call, and it produces the diagnostic note whether or not you continue. If nothing marked has been available to send in advance, the tutor sets a short unseen paper during the session and marks it, so the note has evidence behind it. No card details are taken and there is no obligation to book. If the pairing does not feel right, tell us and we will match a different tutor, which costs you another trial lesson and nothing else.

faqs.question: When is adding hours the wrong answer?
faqs.answer: When the error log shows the diagnosis is wrong, when the student cannot use the work already set, or when fatigue is the actual limiting factor. A Year 11 student in Al Reef who leaves home before seven and gets back after four has a finite amount of attention left, and a second weekday session can reduce output rather than increase it. In those cases the better moves are to change focus, move the session to a weekend block, or stop and re-book closer to the assessment. More hours is the easiest thing to sell and often the least useful thing to buy.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IGCSE at Core and Extended tier and IB at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works to a named syllabus version rather than a generic subject outline, and the first session produces a written list of the topics and paper skills that are actually costing marks.

intro.heading: Two exam systems, one timetable, one child
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families often run both curricula at once. A British-curriculum school takes a student to IGCSE in Year 11, then a sibling or a school move puts the next child into the IB Middle Years Programme and on towards the Diploma. Parents end up holding two assessment vocabularies in their heads: tiers, grade scales and command words on one side, Higher Level, Internal Assessments and the three core components on the other. Searching for an IB IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is usually what happens when those two vocabularies stop making sense together.

The honest position is that the two systems reward different habits. IGCSE rewards precision against a mark scheme: the right command term, the unit written in, the working shown in the order the marker expects. The Diploma rewards extended reasoning and a tolerance for being partly wrong on the way to being right. A student who has spent five years learning to produce the exact phrase an IGCSE marker wants can struggle in a Diploma essay that asks for an argument. A tutor who knows both assessments can name that gap in one session instead of circling it for a term.

This page does not open with the usual list of reasons tutoring is good. It opens with the exam. Below you will find the grade scales side by side, the Core and Extended tier decision with its grade ceiling stated plainly, a paper-by-paper breakdown of where IGCSE marks are lost in the subjects Abu Dhabi students take most, a comparison of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for the same subject, and the entry deadlines that sit months before the exam window and catch private candidates every year.

Delivery is the one thing to settle early. Tuition for families in Abu Dhabi is delivered online, one to one, over live video with a shared screen and a marked-up paper the student keeps. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a subject like Chemistry at Higher Level or Pearson Further Pure Maths 4PM1 that matters more than it sounds, because the pool of people who can teach that specification well is not the pool of people who live a twenty-minute drive from Al Reem Island.

Every figure on this page is either from an examination board's own published material or from a named market source with its date. Where a number could not be verified, it is not here. That applies most sharply to IB session dates: the IB does not permit automated reading of its site, so this page describes the May session as the one Abu Dhabi schools sit and asks you to confirm specific dates with your child's Diploma coordinator.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every request that arrives from Abu Dhabi: the IB Middle Years Programme, the IB Diploma Programme, and IGCSE under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Each is described below with what it actually assesses and what that means for a student sitting it in this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and reported on a 1-7 scale after a grade boundary conversion the school sets. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment at MYP 5. Students are graded on investigation, communication and reflection as much as on content recall, which is why a strong MYP report does not always predict a strong first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the MYP alongside a British-curriculum stream in the same building, so cousins and neighbours in the same community can be sitting entirely different assessments in the same school year. Families on Yas Island and in Al Raha regularly ask us to compare an MYP criterion report against an IGCSE predicted grade, which cannot be done directly: one measures process against descriptors, the other measures marks against a boundary.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each graded 1 to 7, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge which together contribute up to three additional points. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework: in the sciences it adds further topics and a longer second paper, and in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches it adds Paper 3, a two-problem extended-response paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session, in line with the northern-hemisphere calendar most private schools here follow. The practical consequence is that Internal Assessment deadlines land in the same autumn and winter weeks across almost every school in the emirate, so specialist tutoring capacity for Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics is tightest between October and February. Confirm your own school's internal deadlines with its Diploma coordinator rather than assuming the published external ones.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate qualifications that parents treat as one. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different papers and different grade ranges. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is largely untiered in its science and English specifications but tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Both are externally examined, and in most subjects the final grade comes entirely from written papers with no coursework component.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi student may sit Cambridge in one subject and Pearson Edexcel in another within the same school, because departments choose their own specification. Check the syllabus code on the statement of entry, not the school prospectus. A tutor working from 0625 material when the student is entered for 4PH1 will teach competently against the wrong paper structure, and the first time anyone notices is the mock.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most, described by what the assessment actually demands. Each line names where marks are commonly lost rather than listing topics, because the topic list is on the board's website and the failure pattern is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Extended tier carries the full grade range. Marks are lost in two predictable places: algebraic manipulation under time pressure on the non-calculator paper, and the multi-step problems that combine trigonometry with bearings or similar shapes. Working shown out of order scores zero on method marks even when the final answer is right.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, both calculator-permitted, which changes revision strategy against Cambridge entirely. Higher tier questions on vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and iterative methods are the usual sticking points. Students coming from Cambridge often over-practise non-calculator arithmetic they will not need.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper carries roughly a fifth of the total and is the most teachable component on the whole specification: it rewards knowing how to describe a method, identify a variable and read a results table. Electricity and the thermal physics definitions are where theory marks disappear.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the mole calculations account for most of the lost marks at Extended tier. Students can usually balance an equation and still fail to convert between moles, mass and concentration under exam conditions. Separation techniques and the tests for ions are pure recall and are routinely left unrevised.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: A recall-heavy specification where the command words decide the mark. Describe, explain and suggest each require a different answer shape, and a student who writes a description when the paper asks for an explanation loses marks on content they know. Osmosis experiments and genetic crosses need drilling, not reading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade, with two extended investigations that resemble no other paper the student has sat. Standard Level is examined over two papers plus the exploration. Proof by induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series are the Higher Level topics that most often need separate tutoring.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: Under the current guides both levels are assessed through two papers plus a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level depth in equilibrium, energetics and organic mechanisms is where the HL-only questions sit. The data-based section rewards practice with unfamiliar graphs rather than more content revision.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: The step from IGCSE to Diploma Physics is mathematical before it is conceptual. Students who were comfortable with 0625 often stall on vector resolution and the use of calculus-adjacent reasoning in the HL fields topic. Paper 2 extended responses need structured practice against the markbands, not more reading.

subjects.name: English Language (Pearson Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing, assessed against level-based criteria rather than point-scoring. The common failure is a strong writer producing an unfocused answer because the question's audience and purpose were skimmed. Anthology texts reward annotation drills more than rereading.

subjects.name: Economics and Business (0455 and 4BS1)
subjects.description: Both specifications are won on the eight- and twelve-mark evaluation questions, where students lose marks by explaining two advantages and never weighing them. Diagram accuracy in Economics is a mark-scheme item: axes labelled, curves shifted the right way, the new equilibrium marked.

sections.heading: What a parent actually means by an IB and IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is a subject specialist who can teach to a named syllabus version in either system and who knows how that syllabus is marked. That is the whole definition. It is not a general academic coach, and it is not somebody who knows the subject at university level but has never read a mark scheme. The second kind of tutor can explain electromagnetic induction beautifully and still leave a student scoring four out of seven on a question about it.

The reason the two systems get searched together is practical rather than academic. A family typically has one child finishing IGCSE and another starting or inside the Diploma, or a single child who has just moved from an IGCSE Year 11 into DP1 and lost their footing. Those are different problems. The first needs two tutors working to two specifications. The second needs one tutor who can diagnose which habits learned for IGCSE are now actively costing marks, which is a narrower skill than it sounds.

There is a third case that arrives regularly from Abu Dhabi. A student is partway through the Diploma, has chosen a Higher Level subject on the strength of an excellent IGCSE grade, and is now finding that the IGCSE grade predicted very little. A grade 8 or an A in Cambridge Chemistry 0620 says a student can recall and apply a bounded body of content accurately. Higher Level Chemistry asks for mechanistic reasoning across topics. The gap between those two things is where most of the autumn-term panic in DP1 comes from.

What a tutor does about it is specific. First session: a diagnostic on real questions from the actual specification, not a chat. Second session: the two or three habits that are costing the most marks, named and drilled. After that, a weekly rhythm of taught content, timed practice and marked feedback against the published criteria. Everything on this page is organised around making that diagnostic accurate, because a tutor working on the wrong problem is an expensive way to feel reassured.

sections.heading: The grade scales, side by side, and the floor that matters in the UAE
paragraphs: IGCSE grading confuses Abu Dhabi parents for a good reason: two scales are in active use. Cambridge reports some syllabuses on the 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. The scales are not interchangeable at every point, and the mapping that matters most to families here is not the one between the two scales but the one between either scale and the UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency floor.

The ministry's British-track requirement, as reported in July 2026, is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competing tutoring site currently publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

That matters for tier choice and for subject count. A family entering a child for the Core tier in several sciences is capping the grade available in each, and while Core-tier grades can clear the equivalency floor comfortably, they may not clear a university's subject prerequisite. The sensible order of decisions is: check the university destinations first, then the subject prerequisites, then the tier. Doing it in the other order is how a student ends up with five perfectly adequate grades that do not open the door they wanted.

A tutor's job in this conversation is informational, not administrative. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry of Education runs, and nobody at IB Gram performs them, influences them or speeds them up. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the school's university counsellor before making a tier or subject decision on the strength of anything written on a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, the entry decision made months before the exam fixes the highest grade the student can be awarded. Core-tier papers do not contain the questions that separate the top grades, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded them however well they perform. This is the single most consequential administrative choice in an IGCSE year, and it is routinely made on the basis of a mock result taken before half the specification has been taught.

Schools in Abu Dhabi generally take a defensible view: enter a borderline student at Core and secure a solid grade rather than risk an Extended paper the student cannot access. For a student whose next step needs a strong grade in that subject, the calculation is different. Extended tier with eight months of targeted work is often a better bet than a capped grade that closes a Higher Level or A-Level route. The deciding question is not confidence; it is how much of the Extended-only content is genuinely out of reach and how many weeks remain.

A tutor earns their fee in this conversation by being specific. Extended-only material in the sciences is identifiable and finite. In Mathematics 0580 it is the algebraic and trigonometric work that Core never reaches. A diagnostic that tests exactly those topics gives a family evidence instead of a feeling, and it gives the head of department something concrete to respond to when a tier change is requested. Tier decisions can usually be revised before the final entry deadline, which is why the deadline dates in the calendar section below matter.

Pearson Edexcel works differently and parents should not assume the Cambridge pattern. Its International GCSE sciences and English specifications are largely untiered, while Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher. A student entered for 4MA1 Foundation faces the same capped-ceiling logic as a Cambridge Core candidate; a student entered for 4CH1 Chemistry faces no tier decision at all. Read the specification code on the statement of entry before having this argument with anybody.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, paper by paper
paragraphs: Lost marks are not randomly distributed. In every cohort the same components leak the same marks for the same reasons, and most of those reasons are procedural rather than conceptual. A student who knows the content can still lose a fifth of the available marks on a paper by answering the wrong question type, omitting units, or writing a description where the command word asked for an explanation. This is the cheapest ground a tutor can recover.

The alternative-to-practical paper is the clearest example. In Cambridge physics and chemistry it carries roughly a fifth of the total mark and tests a narrow, predictable set of skills: describing a method so another person could repeat it, identifying independent and dependent variables, spotting an anomalous result, reading a scale correctly, and drawing a line of best fit. Almost none of that requires new content knowledge. Students lose marks there because nobody has ever taught them the paper as a paper.

The second pattern is command terms. Describe, explain, suggest, state, calculate and compare each have a defined answer shape in the mark scheme, and the difference between describing a trend and explaining it is the difference between one mark and three. Diploma students meet the same issue in a harsher form, because markbands reward sustained reasoning and a bullet-point answer cannot reach the top band however correct its content.

The third is arithmetic under pressure, which is where the non-calculator component in current Cambridge mathematics bites. Students who have practised exclusively with a calculator lose method marks on manipulation they can do slowly. The fix is drills, timed and marked, not more explanation. sections.heading: The step from MYP 5 into DP1, and why August is late to start
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme and the Diploma are both IB, which leads families to assume the transition is gentle. For the students who struggle, it rarely is. MYP assessment is criterion-referenced: a student is judged against descriptors for investigating, communicating and reflecting, with marks out of eight converted to a 1 to 7 grade by boundaries the school sets. Diploma assessment is externally examined against mark schemes and markbands, with a fixed syllabus and a fixed exam window.

That difference shows up in three places. Content coverage, because the MYP does not prescribe content in the way a Diploma subject guide does, so two students arriving in the same DP1 class from different MYP schools can have genuinely different starting knowledge. Mathematical fluency, because the Diploma sciences and both mathematics routes assume manipulation speed the MYP never tested under time pressure. And writing stamina, because an MYP task is usually shorter than a Paper 2 extended response.

The route choice compounds it. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation are different courses, and the choice has consequences for university applications in engineering, mathematics, economics and some sciences. A student who picks Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because it sounds more serious, without the algebraic fluency to carry it, spends two years in difficulty. Check the specific entry requirements of the universities the student is aiming at before the choice is locked, because requirements differ by institution and by year.

The practical advice is to use the months before DP1 rather than the first term of it. A short block of sessions in the spring or summer before the Diploma starts, aimed at manipulation speed, the specific content gap between the student's MYP subject and the Diploma guide, and extended-writing structure, is worth more than twice as many sessions in November when the first Internal Assessment deadlines are already moving. Diagnosing this needs the subject guide and the student's own work, not a general assessment.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel - the same subject, two different exams
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools choose specifications department by department, so a single student can hold a Cambridge entry in one subject and a Pearson Edexcel entry in another. Parents sensibly treat IGCSE as one qualification; examiners do not. The structures differ in ways that change how a student should revise, and a tutor working from the wrong board's past papers will produce good work that does not fit the paper the student will sit.

The differences worth knowing are concrete. Tiering: Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, while Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher and leaves most sciences untiered. Practical assessment: Cambridge offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the written route. Calculator policy in mathematics: current Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component, while Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which changes revision priorities substantially.

Series availability matters too. Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and it also runs a March series used by some centres. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Both publish provisional timetables ahead of each series, and both expect candidates to work from the correct official timetable rather than a restated date on a third-party site.

Cambridge adds one administrative trap that catches private candidates and new families. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school or the examination centre which zone it sits in, and work from that timetable only.

sections.heading: The deadlines that sit months before the exam
paragraphs: Every year a family discovers that the decision they wanted to make in February was locked in November. Examination entries, tier choices and private-candidate registrations all close well before the exam window, and the boards publish those dates openly. This is the single most useful planning fact on this page, and no competing tutoring page in the research set names a single session, deadline or results date.

Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series make the gap concrete. The examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results are released on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May, and certificates follow in late June. Read that sequence backwards and the planning implication is obvious: a tier change argued in January 2027 is already too late for that series.

Pearson's dates for its own series show the same shape. The November 2026 final International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can still be revised.

IB dates are deliberately absent from the table below. The IB's own site does not permit automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified examination date on a page parents plan around would be worse than publishing none. Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session; for the exact window, your school's Diploma coordinator and ibo.org are the only sources worth using.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the line that separates legitimate tutoring from a service that can get a student's diploma withheld. Under IB academic-honesty rules the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by the supervising teacher. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the method, challenge the reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs to completion, or hand over a worked investigation for the student to submit.

The distinction is easy to apply in practice once it is stated. Teaching what Criterion C rewards in a Mathematics exploration is instruction. Explaining why a chosen research question cannot be answered with the data available is instruction. Pointing out that a paragraph asserts a conclusion the evidence does not support is feedback. Producing the corrected paragraph is not feedback, and no amount of framing makes it so. One site in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; a family who buys one is buying an academic-misconduct finding with a document attached.

Criteria knowledge is where honest support pays off most, because the marks are published and specific. A Mathematics exploration is assessed across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with different mark allocations and a combined total of twenty, and the component contributes a fifth of the subject grade. The Extended Essay is marked across criteria covering focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. Students routinely lose marks on the criteria that reward process, because nobody has shown them that reflection is assessed.

Our position is published because it is a differentiator in this market rather than a disclaimer. IB Gram's tutors do not write any part of assessed coursework, do not supply model answers to be submitted, and do not distribute board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and should be read from the boards' own sites. If a provider offers more than that, the thing being sold is risk.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection ratings, and reading a school report honestly
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are regulated by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. This is worth knowing for two reasons: it is the authority whose published ratings tell you something checkable about a school, and it is the body whose professional-conduct rules bear on who may tutor your child. ADEK is named by none of the competing tutoring pages in the research set, which is a strange gap on pages written for Abu Dhabi parents.

Across the UAE the regulator map is worth having straight. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge; both of those authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the ministry's general regulations.

On who may tutor, the relevant facts are federal. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point parents ask about often. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than quoted policy, and verify it against ADEK's current published document before acting on it. The practical reading is simple: your child's own classroom teacher is not the right person to hire privately.

process.title: Tell us the specification, not just the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the statement of entry or the school's subject guide, the tier or level, and the next assessment date. A request that says Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended, mock in six weeks is actionable immediately. A request that says help with science takes two more emails to become useful.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written diagnostic
process.description: The first session is a free trial run on real questions from the student's own specification. It ends with a written note of the two or three things costing the most marks and what the first month would target. The trial is free with no card required; if the match is wrong, say so and nothing follows.

process.title: A plan counted back from the exam date
process.description: Sessions are sequenced from the assessment date backwards, not from the start of the textbook forwards. That means the entry deadline, the mock window and the school's internal coursework deadlines are in the plan from the first week, and the final weeks are reserved for timed papers rather than new content.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked work in between
process.description: A fixed slot each week on Gulf Standard Time, with work set and marked between sessions. The tutor keeps an error log so a repeated misconception is visible rather than remembered, and a short written note after each session tells you what was covered and what was set.

process.title: Review every half term, change if it is not working
process.description: At each half term the tutor, the student and you look at marked evidence: paper scores, error-log patterns and the gap to the target grade. If the evidence does not show movement, the sensible response is a different tutor or a different plan, and we will say so rather than sell another block.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus-level teaching, not subject-level
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to the specification the student is entered for, including the board and the tier. That sounds administrative until you see the difference between 0580 and 4MA1 revision: one needs non-calculator drilling the other does not. Working from the wrong board's papers is the most common invisible waste in private tuition.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited by a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Higher Level Chemistry specialist or the Pearson Further Pure Maths teacher can take a session with an Abu Dhabi student regardless of where either of them is. Families in Yas Island and Mohammed Bin Zayed City get the same subject choice as families two streets from a school.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work is taught by criterion, questioned and given feedback on. No text is supplied for submission, and no board material is redistributed. That boundary is published here because it is the thing most worth checking before paying anybody in this market.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can inspect
whyPoints.description: Marked papers with the mark scheme applied, an error log carried across sessions, and a short written note after each lesson. Progress claims on this page are deliberately absent; what we offer instead is the marked work, so you can form your own view rather than take ours.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every date and requirement on this page names the board or authority it came from, and anything unverified is marked as such rather than smoothed over. That includes the inconvenient cases: IB examination dates are not published here because they could not be confirmed from the IB itself.

whyPoints.title: A clear answer about delivery
whyPoints.description: Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is online, one to one, over live video with a shared screen. IB Gram does not operate a centre in the UAE and does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi. Saying that plainly saves everybody a phone call, and the comparison tables on this site make the case on merit.

faqs.question: What does an IB and IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi actually do in the first session?
faqs.answer: The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The tutor works through real questions from the student's own specification, at the tier or level the student is entered for, and watches where the answer breaks down: content gaps, command-term mismatch, method marks lost to disordered working, or arithmetic under time pressure. It ends with a written note naming the two or three issues costing the most marks and what the first month of sessions would target. That note is yours whether or not you continue. The trial session is free and no card is required to book it.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 graded 9 to 1 or A* to G?
faqs.answer: Both scales are in use across Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses, which is why parents get conflicting answers. Some syllabuses report on the 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. The only reliable source is the statement of entry or the current syllabus document for the exact code the student is sitting. For planning purposes the useful anchors are that grade 7 is broadly the old A, grade 4 to 5 covers the old C, and grade 3 maps to E, which is the grade the UAE Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency rule names as the minimum for each counted subject.

faqs.question: Should my child sit the Core or the Extended tier in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Decide it against the destination, not against last term's confidence. Core tier caps the grade available, so if the next step is a Higher Level Diploma subject or an A-Level in the same science, a capped grade can close that route even when it clears the UAE equivalency floor comfortably. The practical test is how much Extended-only content is genuinely out of reach and how many teaching weeks remain before the final entry deadline. A diagnostic on exactly those topics gives you evidence to take to the head of department. The decision locks at entry, months before the exam.

faqs.question: How much is the alternative-to-practical paper worth in Cambridge IGCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: In the Cambridge IGCSE sciences the practical component, whether sat as a practical test or as the alternative-to-practical written paper, carries roughly a fifth of the total mark, and most international centres use the written route. Check the exact weighting in the current 0625 syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org, because weightings are revised between syllabus versions. It is the most teachable component on the specification: describing a method reproducibly, identifying variables, spotting anomalous results, reading scales and drawing a line of best fit are all format skills rather than content, and eight to ten marked past-paper questions move the mark noticeably.

faqs.question: My child moves from MYP 5 into DP1 next year. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. Mathematical manipulation speed, because both Diploma mathematics routes and all the sciences assume fluency the Middle Years Programme never tested under time pressure. The specific content gap between what the student's MYP subject covered and what the Diploma subject guide prescribes, which differs by school. And extended-writing stamina for Paper 2 style responses, which are longer than most MYP tasks. A short block of sessions in the months before DP1 starts is worth more than twice as many in November, when the first Internal Assessment deadlines are already moving.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge entry deadline really fall three months before the exam?
faqs.answer: For the March 2027 series it falls further out than that. Cambridge's published key dates put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read backwards, that means any tier change or subject addition has to be settled in November for a February exam. Deadlines differ by series and by centre, so confirm your child's dates with the examinations officer and work from the official timetable for the centre's administrative zone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my child's Mathematics exploration before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, question whether the research question is answerable with the data available, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, and cannot supply text for submission. That boundary comes from IB academic-honesty rules, and the supervising teacher authenticates the work. The useful work is usually criterion knowledge: the exploration is marked across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and students lose marks most often on the ones that assess process.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection rating tell me about my child's IGCSE teaching?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, so a rating is a checkable judgement about the school as a whole. It is not a statement about one department in one year. A school with a strong overall rating can still have a science department that has lost two teachers mid-year, and that is the situation most tutoring requests come from. Read the published report for the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band, and compare it against your child's own marked work.

faqs.question: How many weekly hours does a Year 11 IGCSE student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one hour a week per subject and add a second hour in the eight to ten weeks before mocks or finals. Beyond two hours a week in a single subject, the limiting factor is usually independent practice rather than teaching time: a student who is not completing marked work between sessions will not convert a third hour into marks. Two subjects at one hour each is a common and workable commitment through an IGCSE year. The realistic planning question is how many weeks remain before the entry deadline and the examination window, not how many hours sound reassuring.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades treated the same way?
faqs.answer: For the UAE Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency rule, what matters is that the subjects are accredited and meet the stated minimum grade, with five counted subjects required at no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five. Universities set their own view and may state subject prerequisites rather than board preferences. Where the two boards genuinely differ is in structure: tiering, calculator policy in mathematics and practical assessment are not the same, so revision has to follow the board the student is actually entered for.

faqs.question: My child takes nine IGCSE subjects. How many should we tutor at once?
faqs.answer: Two, in most cases, and rarely more than three. Tutoring four subjects at once produces a timetable with no space for the independent practice that converts teaching into marks, and it is also where family budgets break mid-year, which usually ends the whole arrangement. Choose by consequence rather than by lowest grade: the subject that gates the next step matters more than the subject with the weakest mock. The remaining subjects can be supported with a marked-paper block closer to the examination window rather than a weekly slot all year.

faqs.question: What if nobody covers Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 at the level we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than matching you with somebody adjacent to the subject. Niche requests are where this matters: Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, Higher Level Theatre, Arabic as a first language at Diploma level, and Computer Science at Higher Level all have thin specialist supply. In those cases you will be told the realistic wait, offered a specialist who teaches online from outside the UAE, or told plainly that we cannot cover it. Being matched with a tutor who is learning the specification alongside the student is the worst outcome of the three.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a past paper if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans their written work and sends it before the session. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, then shares the annotated script on screen during the lesson and talks through where each mark was awarded or lost. The marked file stays with the family. In practice this is more useful than marking across a kitchen table, because the annotated script is permanent, searchable and available to the student during revision rather than existing only in that session's memory.

faqs.question: Do we have to commit to a term of IGCSE tutoring in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Sessions are booked as you go, and most families start with a free trial followed by a four to six week block aimed at one specific thing: a mock, a tier decision, or a paper skill. Longer plans make sense when the target is a grade shift across a full year, because that needs work set and marked between sessions over months. What we would not recommend is paying for a large package before a trial, which is a pattern worth questioning in any provider's pricing, not only ours.

faqs.question: What is the minimum IGCSE grade the UAE counts towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, as reported in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that no tutoring provider performs or influences, so verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the school's university counsellor before relying on it.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the specification and the next date in the diary
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi, the fastest route to a useful answer is to send three things: the syllabus code and tier or level, the next assessment date, and a photograph of a recent piece of marked work. That is enough for a specialist to say what the real problem is and whether an hour a week will move it. The first session is a free trial and ends with a written diagnostic you keep either way. Lessons run online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time, and if the subject is one we cannot cover properly we will say so rather than match you with somebody close enough.

intro.heading: Distance is the one variable that stopped mattering
paragraphs: A parent in Al Reef searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi is asking a reasonable question that the search engine answers badly. What comes back is a distance-sorted list: directory entries, tuition centres with a map pin, agency landing pages that mention the district without covering it, and individuals advertising on classified sites. Sorted by kilometres. None of those columns is the one that predicts whether a grade moves.

The variables that do predict it are the exam board and syllabus code, whether the tutor teaches the specific component failing, whether they can hold a recurring evening slot through February to April, and whether they mark the student's own written work against the published scheme. Proximity correlates with none of them, and in an emirate this spread out it actively works against them. Abu Dhabi runs from the island through Khalifa City and Al Raha out to Al Shamkha, Al Samha and Al Reef. A ten-kilometre radius around Al Reef contains very few people who teach Higher Level Chemistry.

That is the practical case for the delivery model on this page, and it is a trade rather than a free gain. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi — that is a service we run only in India — and lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. What a family gives up is an adult physically in the room, which matters for a nine-year-old and matters very little for a Year 11 student working on Pearson 4PH1 Paper 1. What a family gets back is the whole pool instead of the nearby slice of it.

So this page spends its length on the things distance was standing in for. It maps the districts against commute reality, because the school run is what actually decides when a session can start. It names the subjects with thin coverage across the UAE rather than promising everything. It explains what the Department of Education and Knowledge governs in this emirate, because ADEK is mentioned by none of the competitor pages researched for this project and parents are regularly told things about it that are not true.

It also covers two things families searching this phrase usually have further down the list and will need: the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement that runs alongside an international curriculum in UAE private schools, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether a set of IGCSE grades is recognised here. Neither has anything to do with how near a tutor lives, and both change decisions about subject choice that are made in Year 10 and cannot easily be undone in Year 11. One of them is published incorrectly by a site currently outranking this one, which is the sort of gap worth filling properly.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Which programme your child is on changes what a local search should be looking for. These are the four running in Abu Dhabi private schools, with the staffing reality behind each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The best-supplied level in the emirate. Maths, English, Biology, Business Studies and Economics can all be covered by tutors who live within a short drive of most Abu Dhabi districts. The harder asks are Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 and the top end of Physics and Chemistry Extended, where local supply thins quickly outside the island.
programmes.countryNote: The board matters more than the postcode. Abu Dhabi schools split between Cambridge and Pearson, sometimes within one science department, and a tutor who assumes the wrong one will drill an alternative-to-practical paper a Pearson candidate never sits. Establish the code on the entry sheet before anything else, including location.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where proximity breaks down completely. Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, means a student may need two or three specialists rather than one generalist. The probability that all of them live near you is low in any city and very low across Abu Dhabi's geography.
programmes.countryNote: Most Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates sit the May session, which concentrates demand into January to April. A family that books a nearby generalist in September and discovers in February that Higher Level Maths needs a specialist is competing for slots at the worst possible moment.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with no external paper in most schools. Supply is reasonable because the work is criterion-matching rather than board-specific. A tutor needs the school's own assessment task and the published criterion descriptors, not a past paper archive.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, so those students never sit an IGCSE paper. Searching for an 'IGCSE tutor near me' for such a child produces the wrong match entirely; what they need is exam-condition practice before Year 12 begins.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The one level where proximity has a genuine argument behind it, because a young child often needs an adult physically present rather than on a screen. No external assessment applies, so the work is number fluency, reading stamina and written structure rather than paper technique.
programmes.countryNote: Families with a primary-age child should treat the free trial lesson as the decisive test rather than as a formality. Some children engage with a screen for thirty minutes and some do not, and no amount of tutor quality changes that. Where the answer is no, an in-person arrangement locally is the better route and we will say so.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: What each Diploma subject needs from a tutor, and how easily that is found in the UAE. The scarcity column is the one a distance-sorted search cannot show you.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs someone fluent in Higher Level Paper 3, where two extended problems build on each other and an early slip propagates through both. Supply across the UAE is reasonable at Standard Level and noticeably thinner at Higher Level, which is the single most-requested specialism in Abu Dhabi.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs organic pathway fluency and the ability to question an Internal Assessment research design before data collection. Higher Level supply is thin across the whole country, not just this emirate, which is the clearest case on this page for ignoring distance entirely.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Needs someone who marks for units, significant figures and uncertainty rather than for the final number, and who insists a principle is stated before any algebra. Higher Level supply is thin; Standard Level is manageable within Abu Dhabi.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The best-supplied Diploma science in the emirate. Command-term work and data-based question technique do most of the grade movement here, and both are widely taught, so a local match is realistic if that is what a family wants.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Needs diagram discipline — labelled, titled, referred to in the prose — plus evaluation technique and, at Higher Level, quantitative handling. Supply is good on the island and thinner in the mainland communities, which is a district-level gap rather than a national one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Needs case-study application rather than definitions, and drilling on the quantitative content: ratios, break-even and cash-flow forecasting. Reasonably supplied across Abu Dhabi, including the Khalifa City corridor.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Needs unseen analysis technique and Individual Oral preparation, where a precisely stated global issue has to be traced through both an extract and a literary work. Well supplied in this emirate at both levels.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The thinnest supply of any Diploma subject in the UAE. Needs pseudocode convention work, documented testing in the solution development stage, and a Higher Level case study read months ahead. Searching by distance for this subject returns essentially nothing useful.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Needs calculator-evidence discipline and statistical interpretation in context, since an unexplained output earns the calculation mark and nothing more. Supply sits between Analysis and Approaches and the sciences.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandated alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools and ignored by almost every tutoring site in this market. Local supply is the strongest of any subject here, which makes it the one case where a near-me search genuinely works.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same scarcity question at IGCSE level, where supply is generally better and the gaps are narrower but still real.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The deepest supply in the emirate; a local match is entirely realistic. What a tutor must know is which code and which tier, because the grade ceilings differ and the 2025 Cambridge revision added a non-calculator paper that caught out a cohort.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Reasonable supply for Core, thinner for Extended at the top of the range. The tutor needs to know whether the student sits Cambridge's separate practical component or Pearson's papers, which examine practical skills internally with no separate component.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Similar to Physics. The qualitative-analysis tables and the alternative-to-practical paper are the coachable parts and the parts most commonly taught badly, so ask a prospective tutor to describe how they teach them.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Good supply across Abu Dhabi. Extended physiology answers need sequence and named structures, and magnification and surface-area calculations appear almost every series while being routinely skipped in revision.

igcseSubjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Good supply. The constraint is marking capacity rather than availability — this subject generates the heaviest marking load at IGCSE, so confirm whether marking between sessions is inside the rate.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Adequate supply on the island and thin in Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha. Short engagements work here: diagram labelling and evaluation technique recover marks faster than content coverage does.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Adequate supply emirate-wide. The calculation questions are the fastest marks to recover and the ones most often left blank, which makes the first three sessions the most productive of any engagement.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Thin supply at IGCSE as well as Diploma. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are quick wins; the programming component justifies a longer engagement. Distance-based searching for this subject in Abu Dhabi returns little.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: The emirate mapped: commute, cluster and workable session time
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: This is the detail a near-me search is actually reaching for. Each district is set against the school run it imposes, the schools it feeds, and the earliest hour a session can realistically begin.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah, Al Bateen and Al Manaseer
regions.note: Central island addresses with the shortest school runs in the emirate. A 16:30 or 17:00 start genuinely works here, and those are the easiest slots to book because fewer families compete for them. Local tutor supply is the densest in Abu Dhabi for Maths and English.

regions.name: Al Mushrif, Al Rawdah and Al Karamah
regions.note: Established island villa districts with long-standing school allegiances and predictable finish times. In-home tutoring is most entrenched here, and the constraint reported by families is sessions running short because the tutor's previous appointment overran.

regions.name: Al Reem Island, Al Maryah and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: High-rise living with short runs and a high rate of mid-cycle curriculum changes. Families here frequently arrive mid-year from another system, so the first session is usually a syllabus audit against the new specification rather than teaching.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Al Bandar
regions.note: Newer international enrolment weighted heavily towards the Diploma. Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision dominates the requests, and those are usually booked as weekend daytime blocks rather than weekday evening slots.

regions.name: Khalifa City, Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: The corridor carrying a large share of the emirate's British and IB enrolment. Bus routes are long enough that nothing before 17:30 is realistic and 18:30 is the slot that actually gets kept. Specialist supply within driving distance is noticeably thinner than on the island.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha
regions.note: The longest bus runs in Abu Dhabi, with a working window from 18:30 to 20:00. In-home specialist supply here is close to nonexistent for Higher Level sciences and Computer Science, which makes this the catchment where removing distance from the equation changes the most.

regions.name: Yas Island and Hudayriyat
regions.note: Spread-out catchments where the nearest tutor and the nearest subject specialist are rarely the same person. Demand skews to Diploma sciences and Maths, with a steady stream of Internal Assessment supervision requests.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Shakhbout City and Baniyas
regions.note: Mainland communities with mixed curriculum intake and the strongest demand in the emirate for Arabic alongside the school's licensed curriculum. A share of students here work towards a November series rather than May, which shifts their pressure window to August and September.

schoolClusters.city: Island cluster — Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and Al Khalidiyah
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi's longest-established British and American schools, with the shortest commutes and the earliest workable session times. This is the only part of the emirate where a genuinely local specialist match is realistic for most subjects.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef cluster
schoolClusters.note: Large British and IB enrolment with the emirate's hardest commute constraint. Families here are the main reason the regions table on this page exists: the gap between the slot people book and the slot their child can actually attend is widest in this corridor.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and newer mainland cluster
schoolClusters.note: Newer campuses with high Diploma intake and frequent mid-cycle arrivals from other systems. Requests lean to Internal Assessment supervision, Extended Essay process coaching and curriculum-transition work rather than single-subject repair.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Three ways families use this, all one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. None involves a tutor travelling to an Abu Dhabi address.

modes.title: A single subject specialist, weekly
modes.description: The most common arrangement and the one a near-me search was trying to produce. One subject, one tutor who teaches the failing component, one fixed evening slot held across the year. The slot is chosen from the commute reality of your district rather than from an ideal timetable, which is why the regions table above exists.

modes.title: Two or three Diploma specialists in parallel
modes.description: What a Higher Level student frequently actually needs, and what no local search can assemble. Different tutors for Higher Level Maths, a Higher Level science and Internal Assessment supervision, each in their own slot. The coordination is the family's and the schedule has to be built around one student's capacity rather than three tutors' convenience.
bullets: Each subject matched independently to a component specialist
Slots spread across the week rather than stacked on one evening

modes.title: A short diagnostic block before committing
modes.description: Four to six sessions bought as a diagnosis rather than a treatment, ending in a written list of recurring error types. Useful where the school report says 'needs to work harder' and nobody knows which component is actually losing the marks. There is no obligation to continue and no package discount dangled to discourage stopping.
