sections.heading: What an IB IGCSE tutor near me search returns in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The results page for this search is not a list of tutors. It is a mixture of five different things wearing the same clothes, and separating them is the first useful step a parent can take. Directory listings rank on how much a provider paid the directory. Tuition centre pages rank on having a verified map pin, which tells you about premises rather than about teaching. Agency landing pages rank on mentioning the district by name, often with no tutor in it. Classified adverts rank on recency. Blog posts with a district in the title rank on domain authority and frequently exist only to collect enquiries and sell them on.

None of those five is sorted by anything that predicts a grade. The research behind this project fetched and dissected sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026, and the pattern was consistent: three of six commercial pages published no price at all, five of six carried no data table, one page's structured data was unparseable by Google, and one listed a school that appears not to exist. The best page in the set was 2,294 words and still refused to answer its own question about cost.

The honest reframing is to search for the component rather than the place. A parent whose child is losing marks on Cambridge 0620 mole calculations wants someone who teaches Cambridge 0620. A parent whose Year 12 child is stuck on a Higher Level Maths Exploration wants someone who has supervised Explorations against the published criteria. Those are findable. 'A good tutor nearby' is not a specification and cannot be matched against.
The table below sorts what the results page actually contains, with what each type is optimised for and the question that exposes it.

sections.heading: The commute, not the bell, decides when a session starts
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families book sessions at times their children cannot attend, and the cause is arithmetic rather than optimism. A school finishing at 15:00 on the island releases a student who lives in Al Reef into a bus route that can run an hour and a quarter in evening traffic. Add food and the change of clothes and the earliest honest start is 17:30, often 18:30. A 16:00 slot booked in September becomes a 16:25 start by October and a cancelled session by November.

The consequence is worse than a late start. A tutor holding a 16:00 slot that consistently begins at 16:25 either runs over into the next student's time or delivers thirty-five minutes for a sixty-minute fee, and the second is what usually happens. Across a term that is several hours of paid teaching that did not occur, and the family concludes that tutoring does not work. The fix is to book the slot the child can actually reach.

The second scheduling reality is capacity rather than time. A Year 11 student with three subjects under support cannot absorb three sessions stacked on a Tuesday, and a Diploma student cannot absorb two hours of Higher Level Maths after a full school day plus a bus. Spreading sessions across the week and keeping each one short enough to finish well is a better plan than maximising contact hours, and the family is better placed to judge that than any provider.

sections.heading: Where the specialists are not: subject coverage across the emirate
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market implies it covers everything. None of the sixty-odd competitor pages researched for this project discloses a single coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an Indian telephone number rather than stating where the tutor sits. That is the gap this section fills, because a disclosed limit is more useful to a family than an undisclosed promise.

The pattern is consistent and not specific to Abu Dhabi. Maths and English at IGCSE are deeply supplied everywhere. Biology and the commercial subjects are adequately supplied. Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches, and Computer Science at any level are thin across the whole country, and within Abu Dhabi they are concentrated on the island. Arabic is the exception that runs the other way — local supply is excellent and almost no tutoring site in this market treats it as a subject at all.

What a family should do with that depends on the subject. Where coverage is deep, a local in-person arrangement is a genuine option and we will say so rather than arguing against it. Where coverage is thin, the realistic choice is a specialist outside your district or outside the UAE, delivered over live video, with the location stated. Where nothing fits the slot you have, the answer should be that nothing fits — not a general science teacher booked against a Higher Level Paper 3 problem.
The table states the position subject by subject. It is a coverage statement, not a sales argument, and the fallback column is the part most providers would prefer not to publish.

sections.heading: Who regulates what: ADEK, and the other four
paragraphs: Parents in this emirate are told a great deal about regulators that is not accurate, and the research behind this project found ADEK named by none of the competitor pages fetched. The position is straightforward and comes from the UAE government's own private-schools page. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge 'supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate'. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education'. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority 'regulates private education in the emirate', as does the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the Ministry of Education 'plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools'.

What that means practically: the regulator decides whether a school may operate, which curricula it may offer, how it is inspected and what rating it publishes. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities also 'approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods', so curriculum approval sits with the emirate rather than only inspection. What the regulator does not do is set your child's grades. Cambridge Assessment International Education, Pearson Edexcel and the International Baccalaureate write the papers, publish the mark schemes and set the boundaries. A regulator rating tells you about a school; it tells you nothing about a syllabus.

Two claims to treat as warnings. First, no tutoring provider should describe itself as approved, accredited or endorsed by ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless it can produce the permit number, and the research for this project found claims of that kind circulating in this market with nothing at all behind them. IB Gram holds no such status and claims none. Second, a tuition business with premises and staff is licensed differently from an individual tutor — in Dubai that is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute — so a centre asserting approval can be asked for the number.

IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. It is a matching platform delivering one-to-one lessons over live video, and the regulators are described on this page as context for how Abu Dhabi schooling works rather than as any kind of endorsement.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside an international curriculum
paragraphs: Families searching for an IGCSE or IB tutor in Abu Dhabi usually arrive with an international subject in mind and then discover, often in Year 10, that their child also carries UAE-mandated subjects that will not go away. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Across the border in Dubai, KHDA's published guidelines make the operational detail explicit, and while they are Dubai's rules rather than Abu Dhabi's, they show what the federal baseline looks like in practice. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies — combined classes for both groups are, in KHDA's words, 'strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction'. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

Two further points from the same source matter for anyone tutoring these subjects. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools must hold the relevant KHDA approval to teach them, which is a credential question a parent can ask about. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, 'the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited' — which constrains what tutoring material in these subjects may be. A tutor offering an alternative curriculum for Islamic Education is offering something the rules do not permit.

For an Abu Dhabi family the practical consequences are three. These subjects consume timetable hours that the international subjects do not get. A student weak in Arabic as an additional language carries that into a report regardless of their IGCSE grades. And, as the equivalency section below sets out, Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside the five subjects the Ministry of Education counts, which changes how a family should think about subject choice.
bullets: Private schools must cover Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum
Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required in Arabic first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies
Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit
Additional or alternative content for these subjects requires prior Ministry permission

sections.heading: UAE equivalency: the five subjects that actually have to count
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that makes a foreign school certificate usable in the UAE, and it is one of the eighteen gaps the research for this project found competitors leaving entirely empty. It matters to a near-me search because it changes subject choice, and subject choice is settled in Year 10 — long before anybody is looking for a tutor.

On the British track, as reported when the UAE clarified its requirements, students must pass 'five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3', and must additionally submit proof of 'one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E' or 'two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade'. The detail families miss is that Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. One site ranking in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong — publishing the correct rule is a straightforward accuracy win over a page currently outranking us.

On the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at 'a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test', '61 in the TOEFL iBT test', or '450 in the reading and writing section in the SAT test', with mathematics requiring 'at least 450 in the SAT Math test' before applying. For the IB there is no figure here to publish. The article states no IB points threshold, and ibo.org blocks automated fetching, so any IB equivalency number has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the emirate's attestation authority before it is relied on. We would rather print that gap than fill it with a number we cannot stand behind.

Three cautions. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry of Education, not something a tutoring provider performs, arranges or guarantees — descriptions of it belong on a page like this, applications belong on the official channel. Tutoring is not required for equivalency and nobody should tell you it is. And the rule as set out here was reported in July 2026, so verify the current version before making a subject decision on it.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is who the listing says they are
paragraphs: A distance-sorted list carries no verification at all, so the checking falls to the family. Four questions do most of the work, and a tutor who cannot answer them in writing has told you something useful.

Ask for the permit. A tutor based in the UAE providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing' service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, there is no cost excuse for not holding one. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount quoted at you.

Ask about the school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is understood to bar the same. That reporting is press-sourced rather than read here from the current ADEK policy document, so verify it with ADEK directly — but treat 'your child's own class teacher, privately' as the arrangement to avoid regardless.

Ask about the syllabus and ask about examiner claims. A tutor should be able to name the code they teach, describe how the components are weighted, and say where students lose marks on it; vagueness there is the only credential test that matters. On examiner status, be sceptical: nobody should be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner without current evidence, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Finally, ask what happens to prepaid hours if the match changes, and ask for the cancellation terms in writing before any payment — Abu Dhabi school calendars generate clashes constantly and a loose policy becomes an argument in month two.
bullets: Ask for MoHRE permit confirmation; the permit is free and takes two working days
Avoid any arrangement involving your child's own class teacher at their own school
Ask the tutor to name the syllabus code and describe where marks are lost on it
Get cancellation terms and prepaid-hour protection in writing before paying

process.title: Replace the place with the component
process.description: Instead of a district, send the board, syllabus code, tier and the component going wrong — Cambridge 0620 Paper 4, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, or a Higher Level Maths Exploration stuck on Criterion E. That is a specification a match can be made against. 'A good tutor nearby' cannot be matched at all.

process.title: Send the window your child can actually attend
process.description: Take the earliest honest start from the regions table for your district rather than the school finish time. A 16:00 slot in Al Reef becomes a 16:25 start and then a cancellation, and the sessions lost that way are usually blamed on tutoring rather than on scheduling.

process.title: Hear the coverage answer before paying
process.description: For Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics or Computer Science, ask directly whether a specialist is free in your slot and where they are based. If the answer is nobody, that is the answer. Matching a general science teacher to a Higher Level Paper 3 problem wastes a term.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per student, no payment, no card, no commitment. It runs as a working session: the student writes something under time and the tutor marks it against the published scheme. For a primary-age child it also answers whether the format works for them at all, before any money moves.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep it through the crunch
process.description: Demand concentrates between January and April for the May and June series. A recurring slot booked in the autumn survives that; week-by-week arrangements do not, and the tutor still free in March is rarely the specialist you wanted in October.

process.title: Review against the marked evidence
process.description: Every half-term, look at the annotated scripts: which error types stopped recurring and which did not. If the marks have not moved, change the plan or end the engagement. A quiet renewal with no evidence behind it is how a year of tutoring produces nothing.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the kilometre
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the syllabus code and the failing component. A distance-sorted list optimises for the one variable that has no bearing on a grade, and in an emirate running from the island to Al Shamkha it actively narrows the pool to whoever can drive to you.

whyPoints.title: Commute reality built into the slot
whyPoints.description: The session time is set from the bus route rather than the school bell, because an Al Reef student does not reach a desk at 16:00 no matter what the timetable says. Booking the slot a child can actually attend is the difference between sixty minutes and thirty-five.

whyPoints.title: Coverage gaps published
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics and Computer Science are thinly supplied across the UAE, and that is written on the page. None of the sixty-odd competitor pages researched discloses a single coverage limit, and several hide non-UAE delivery behind a foreign telephone number.

whyPoints.title: ADEK explained, not invoked
whyPoints.description: The regulator table cites the UAE government's own private-schools page and separates what a regulator governs from what an awarding body decides. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or endorsement from ADEK or anyone else, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch.

whyPoints.title: The equivalency rule stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five. A site currently ranking in this market publishes six, which is wrong, and no IB points figure appears here because none could be read from an official source.

whyPoints.title: Verification questions handed to you
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE permit, the rule against tutoring a teacher's own students, naming the syllabus code, and written cancellation terms. Four questions, all answerable in writing, and a provider's reluctance to answer any of them is itself the result you were looking for.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi return so few real options?
faqs.answer: Because the results are sorted by distance and most of them are not tutors. The page mixes paid directory listings, tuition centres ranking on a map pin, agency pages naming your district without staffing it, classified adverts and blog posts that exist to collect and resell enquiries. None of those columns predicts a grade. The variables that do — board, syllabus code, the specific failing component, and whether a recurring evening slot can be held — are invisible in a distance ranking. Searching for the component instead of the place produces a specification that can actually be matched.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi districts have the thinnest IGCSE subject coverage?
faqs.answer: Al Reef, Al Samha, Al Shamkha and the outer parts of the Khalifa City corridor, measured by how many subject specialists live within an evening's drive. Maths and English are fine almost everywhere in the emirate. Physics and Chemistry Extended thin out noticeably off the island, and Computer Science 0478 is close to unavailable locally in those districts. The island — Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif — is the only part of Abu Dhabi where a genuinely local specialist match is realistic across most subjects, and that is the honest version of the coverage picture.

faqs.question: Does living on Saadiyat Island or in Al Reef change which tutors we can reach?
faqs.answer: For an in-home arrangement, enormously. Saadiyat has campus-based schools and moderate runs; Al Reef has the longest bus routes in the emirate and almost no local specialist supply for Higher Level sciences. For a live video session, the district changes nothing about which tutor is available — only the slot time differs, because an Al Reef student realistically starts at 18:30 while a Saadiyat student can start at 17:00. That difference between the two answers is the clearest practical argument on this page for ignoring distance in the search.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after an Abu Dhabi school run?
faqs.answer: It depends on the district rather than on the school bell. On the island, in Al Khalidiyah or Al Bateen, 16:30 genuinely works. In the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor the earliest honest start is 17:30 and the slot that actually gets kept is 18:30. In Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha the working window is 18:30 to 20:00. Booking a 16:00 session for a child who arrives home at 16:20 produces a thirty-five-minute lesson at a sixty-minute price, every week, and the family usually blames the tutoring rather than the timetable.

faqs.question: My child's school teaches MYP rather than IGCSE. Does this page apply to us?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the difference matters enough to flag. Several Abu Dhabi schools run the IB Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then move students straight into the Diploma, so those students never sit an IGCSE paper and searching for an IGCSE tutor produces the wrong match. MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, usually with no external paper. What that cohort needs most is exam-condition practice before Year 12 begins, because their first external timed paper will otherwise be a Diploma one in Year 13.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE and DP subjects are hardest to staff locally in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Computer Science at either level is the thinnest, followed by Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics, then Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches. Those gaps are national rather than specific to this emirate, and within Abu Dhabi the available specialists are concentrated on the island. Running the other way, Arabic as a first or additional language has the strongest local supply of any subject here and is treated as a subject by almost no tutoring site in this market. Where coverage is thin, the realistic answer is a specialist outside your district with their location stated.

faqs.question: Is a tutor fifteen minutes away better than a specialist in a different time zone?
faqs.answer: For a primary-age child, usually yes — a young student often needs an adult physically in the room, and no screen substitutes for that. For a Year 11 student losing four marks a paper on Cambridge 0620 mole calculations, no. The nearby generalist will re-teach moles pleasantly; the specialist will mark the student's own script against the published scheme and show them the line where the marks were available. A UK-based tutor finds an Abu Dhabi 18:30 a convenient mid-afternoon, so the time zone is frequently less of an obstacle than the drive.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in another emirate teach my child in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, over live video, and it is common for the scarcer subjects. The permit position is the same wherever in the UAE the tutor sits: the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 applies nationally and is granted free of charge for two years. What differs between emirates is school regulation — ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah — and that governs schools rather than tutors. A tutor in Dubai teaching an Abu Dhabi student needs the same permit as one in Al Mushrif.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor really knows my child's exam board?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the syllabus code and describe its components. Someone who teaches Cambridge 0625 will tell you there is a separate practical component worth a fifth of the grade and that it can be sat as the alternative-to-practical paper; someone who teaches Pearson 4PH1 will tell you practical skills are examined inside the written papers with no separate component. Then ask where students lose marks on that paper. Specific answers to both questions are the only credential test that matters, and vagueness on either is decisive.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi school teachers tutor their own students privately?
faqs.answer: They should not, and this is the one rule parents here most often try to work around. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct is understood to bar the same arrangement. That reporting is press-sourced rather than read here from the current ADEK document, so verify it with ADEK before relying on the exact wording. Either way, treat an offer of your child's own class teacher privately as a reason to decline.

faqs.question: What does ADEK actually do, and does it regulate private tutors?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, in the UAE government's own words. It decides whether a school may operate, which curricula it offers, how it is inspected and what rating it publishes. It does not set your child's grades — Cambridge, Pearson and the IB do that — and it does not license individual private tutors. Tutors sit under the MoHRE permit regime instead. No tutoring provider should describe itself as approved or accredited by ADEK; IB Gram holds no such status and claims none.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not towards the five subjects on the British track. When the UAE clarified its equivalency requirements, the rule was that students must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. Those subjects remain compulsory in UAE private schools regardless, because the federal rule requires Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum. They simply sit outside the equivalency count, which is worth knowing before Year 10 subject choices are made.

faqs.question: How does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency work for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or grade 3 or better, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, and must additionally show one A Level at no less than grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One site ranking in this market tells UAE families they need six IGCSE subjects, which is incorrect. For the IB there is no points figure we can publish, because the source we read states none — check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: How long does matching a subject specialist take once we ask?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot rather than on paperwork. A Maths or English request in a 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time window is usually quick, because supply is deep. A Higher Level Chemistry or Computer Science request pinned to one weekday at 18:30 in March can take considerably longer, and in that case you hear it before paying rather than being matched with the nearest approximation. The free trial lesson comes first regardless, so the first contact is a working session rather than a commitment.

faqs.question: Does my child need Arabic alongside IGCSE in an Abu Dhabi private school?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, and every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement follows from that. The subject consumes timetable hours the international subjects do not get, and a weakness there appears on a report regardless of IGCSE grades. Local tutoring supply for Arabic is the strongest of any subject in this emirate, which makes it one case where searching near you genuinely works.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Search for the component, send the real slot
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi, swap the two inputs. Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component that keeps losing marks, and send the evening window your child can genuinely sit a session in once the bus has arrived. Those two pieces of information produce a match that distance never could. The free trial lesson follows — one per student, no payment, no card, no commitment — and it runs as a working session: the student writes under time, the tutor marks against the published scheme, and you get the breakdown. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and no tutor travels to a UAE address.

abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma mathematics courses as separate subjects, because they are. A specialist who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level daily is not automatically the right person for an Applications and Interpretation Standard Level student sitting a modelling paper, and we do not pretend otherwise.

intro.heading: The form asks for a box. The decision is about which paper your child will sit for two years.
paragraphs: There are four mathematics courses in the IB Diploma, not two: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. Most Abu Dhabi schools present them on a single option sheet in the spring term of Year 11 or MYP 5, with a short return deadline and a line of explanation each. Families then choose on reputation and rumour, because almost nothing published about the two courses describes what sitting them is like.

The difference is not difficulty. Analysis and Approaches keeps algebraic manipulation, exact values, formal calculus and proof, and it tests a chunk of that with the calculator put away in Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation allows a graphic display calculator in every paper, and spends its time on data, statistics, modelling and the interpretation of results in context. A student can struggle badly in either one. They struggle in different ways, and the fix for each is a different kind of session.

The second thing the option sheet does not say is that the choice is also a timetable constraint. Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, and a school with twenty-two Diploma students may run Analysis and Approaches at both levels and Applications and Interpretation only at Standard Level, or it may combine two sets into one teaching group. ADEK licenses and inspects the school, and publishes an inspection rating, but it does not publish which mathematics sets will run in September. Only your school's DP coordinator knows, and the honest answer in March is often that numbers decide it.

The third thing nobody mentions is that the route decision is reversible for roughly one term, and expensive after that. Each school sets its own internal cut-off for a change, usually inside the first term of DP1. Past that point, moving from Applications and Interpretation to Analysis and Approaches means closing an algebra and calculus gap that the new course assumed was already there, on top of five other subjects, the exploration, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. That is the week that families start searching for IB math AA vs AI guidance in Abu Dhabi, and by then the useful question has changed.

So this page is built in the order the decision is actually made. What the two courses assess. Where marks go missing, paper by paper. How the mathematics exploration criteria are scored, by letter and by mark. What the Abu Dhabi school calendar does to the timing. What a route change costs in hours and in AED at published market rates. And what a tutor may and may not do with an exploration, which is a boundary worth being clear about before anyone starts work.

Standard Level in both routes: Paper 1 40%, Paper 2 40%, exploration 20%

Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and is two extended investigations

abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.programmesIntro: The route question does not begin in DP1. What a student can realistically take in the Diploma is shaped by the programme they are finishing now, and by how that programme handled algebra and data. Here is how each feeder looks from the mathematics side.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria and reported on a 1-8 scale, with extended and standard routes in the final years. It builds investigation and communication habits that transfer directly to the exploration, and it is deliberately lighter on drilled algebraic fluency than an IGCSE course. An MYP 5 student arriving in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level often has the reasoning and not the manipulation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a cluster of through-schools running MYP into the Diploma on one campus, which means the maths department usually knows exactly which MYP 5 students it expects to cope with Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Ask for that view in writing before the option form is returned, and ask specifically about extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics is compulsory, so every Diploma student in Abu Dhabi sits one of the four courses. The route sits in Group 5 and cannot be dropped, which is why a wrong choice is felt in every term rather than survived for one year.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma schools licensed in the emirate are concentrated on Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas and along the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. Cohort size drives which sets run, so two schools eight minutes apart can offer genuinely different mathematics options in the same September.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills component. A CP student may take one Diploma mathematics course alongside their career-related study, usually Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, because the modelling and data content maps onto applied study more directly than formal calculus does.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is worth asking about in Abu Dhabi if a student is strong in applied work and would be set back two years by a compulsory Higher Level. Check the IB programme listing for the school rather than assuming from the website.

programmes.name: IGCSE and O Level as the feeder
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum students in Abu Dhabi arrive in the Diploma from Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, International Mathematics 0607, Additional Mathematics 0606 or a Pearson equivalent. The syllabus a student sat matters more than the grade. A 0607 or 0606 student has met functions and early calculus language; a 0580 Extended student has met neither in that form.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools enter students for 0580 Extended only, then feed them into Analysis and Approaches. That combination is workable with a bridging block over the summer and difficult without one, and it is the single most common reason an Abu Dhabi DP1 student asks for mathematics help in October.

abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on the form and four courses in practice, and the route a student picks changes the shape of three other subjects on their timetable. These are the courses and the neighbours that feel the decision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most demanding Group 5 route. Proof, complex numbers, vectors, extended calculus including integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. Paper 3 adds two extended investigations. Students lose marks on by-hand manipulation under time pressure, and on the exact-value work that the non-calculator Paper 1 is built around.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, probability and an introduction to calculus, with a non-calculator Paper 1 and a calculator Paper 2 at 40% each. It is the common default for students heading towards economics, business and the social sciences who still want an algebraic course. Marks go missing in logarithms, sequences and the chain rule.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, probability distributions, matrices, graph theory, complex numbers in modelling form and substantial technology use. Paper 3 is two extended data and modelling investigations. The common misreading is that a calculator in every paper makes it light; the demand moves to choosing the right statistical test and justifying it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, descriptive and inferential statistics, financial mathematics and applied geometry, with a calculator allowed throughout. It suits students who read context well and dislike abstraction. Marks are lost on interpretation rather than calculation: a correct chi-squared value with the wrong conclusion earns very little.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics Higher Level assumes the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches trains. Students on Applications and Interpretation Standard Level taking Physics Higher Level usually need separate algebra support, because the physics teacher will not have time to teach rearrangement and exponentials from scratch.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Less algebra than Physics, more proportional reasoning, logarithms in pH work and careful unit handling. Either mathematics route supports Chemistry, but the data-processing criterion in the Chemistry internal assessment rewards the statistical habits that Applications and Interpretation drills.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics includes quantitative questions on elasticity, market calculations and national income data. Both mathematics routes cover enough. University economics is the issue: some faculties name a specific mathematics route in their published entry requirements, which is a question for the admissions page, not for the school.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic, number bases, recursion and complexity. Applications and Interpretation covers matrices and graph theory that map onto parts of the course, while Analysis and Approaches builds the proof habits that recursion arguments reward. Neither route is a prerequisite; both help in different places.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Finance, investment appraisal and quantitative tools. Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is a natural pairing and covers the financial mathematics directly. Students regularly find the business calculations easier than the written analysis, which is the opposite of what they expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics exploration
subjects.description: The internally assessed component, worth 20% of the mathematics grade and marked out of 20 across five criteria. It is a piece of the student's own mathematical writing, and the criteria reward personal engagement and reflection as heavily as correctness. It is also where honest tutoring boundaries matter most.

abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes which schools are realistic, and therefore which mathematics sets are on the table. These notes are about option availability and session timing, not travel: lessons are online.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Dense in Diploma provision, with several schools running the full programme on one campus. Families here most often ask about Analysis and Approaches Higher Level because the cohorts are large enough that the set reliably runs. Sessions start comfortably at 16:30 Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A high-rise community with school runs crossing to the island and the mainland. Students here often arrive home late, so 18:00 and 19:00 slots are the realistic ones, and a 45-minute focused session beats a 90-minute one at 17:00 that nobody is awake for.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest single source of British-curriculum students moving from 0580 Extended into Analysis and Approaches. Khalifa City IB maths tutor requests peak in September and October, which is exactly when the DP1 route-change window is still open.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A corridor of villa communities feeding a mix of British and IB schools. Families here frequently have one child on an IGCSE timetable and another in DP1, and ask for the same tutor across both, which works for algebra and rarely for the exploration.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer provision with growing Diploma cohorts, which means set availability genuinely changes year to year. Worth asking the coordinator whether Applications and Interpretation Higher Level will run before naming it on the form.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods with long-standing British-curriculum schools and a smaller IB presence. Students here more often move to a Diploma school for Years 12 and 13, which puts the route decision and a school change in the same term.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller Diploma cohort and fewer set options. Online one-to-one maths tuition in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain removes the geography problem entirely: the constraint becomes the subject specialist's calendar, not the drive to the campus.

schoolClusters.note: These campuses carry the emirate's largest Diploma cohorts, which is why they are the ones most likely to run all four mathematics courses in a given year. Students we support sit Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels across this cluster.

sections.heading: What the two courses actually assess, in the words the papers use
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches is the route that keeps formal mathematics. Its content is organised around number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, and it treats the last of those seriously: at Higher Level that means integration by substitution and by parts, differential equations, Maclaurin series and vector geometry. Proof runs through the course, including proof by induction and by contradiction at Higher Level. The command terms that dominate are show that, hence, prove and find the exact value.

Applications and Interpretation covers the same five topic headings and weights them differently. Statistics and probability is much larger, and it is inferential rather than descriptive: hypothesis testing, chi-squared, correlation and regression, and at Higher Level probability distributions and non-linear regression. Modelling is the organising idea. Matrices, graph theory and voronoi diagrams appear here and not in the other route. The command terms are describe, interpret, comment on, justify and suggest, and the marks sit on the justification.

Read those two paragraphs again and the real difference appears. Analysis and Approaches asks a student to do mathematics correctly. Applications and Interpretation asks a student to choose mathematics, apply it to someone else's messy context and say what the answer means. A student who writes fluently and reasons about context will find the second easier. A student who manipulates symbols confidently and dislikes writing will find the first easier. Neither description is about ability, which is why the usual staffroom shorthand of harder and easier is close to useless on an option form.
bullets: Analysis and Approaches: proof, exact values, extended calculus, vectors at Higher Level
Applications and Interpretation: hypothesis testing, regression, matrices, graph theory, voronoi diagrams
Command terms differ: show that and prove against interpret and justify
Technology is assumed throughout Applications and Interpretation and withheld in Paper 1 of the other

sections.heading: Where the marks go, paper by paper, in both routes
paragraphs: Weightings are identical across the routes, which surprises most families. At Standard Level, Paper 1 is 40%, Paper 2 is 40% and the exploration is 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 are 30% each, Paper 3 is 20% and the exploration is 20%. The arithmetic there is worth pausing on: at Higher Level, 40% of the grade sits outside the two conventional papers, in an extended investigation paper and a piece of coursework. Most revision plans spend about a fortnight on that 40%.

The non-calculator Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is the single most distinctive feature of the route, and the most common place a misplaced student comes apart. It is not harder mathematics; it is the same mathematics with no safety net. A student who has always checked a factorisation on a graph, or evaluated a logarithm numerically, has no route to a mark. This is checkable in advance in about forty minutes, which is exactly what a route diagnostic does.

In Applications and Interpretation the loss pattern is different and less visible. Students reach a correct statistic and then stop, or write a conclusion that the statistic does not support. A chi-squared test completed correctly and concluded wrongly scores a fraction of the marks available. Paper 3 at Higher Level compounds it: both routes sit two extended investigations, and the later parts reward generalisation and clear reasoning that nobody practises unless a teacher or tutor builds it in from early DP2.

sections.heading: The option form arrives before the results do, and the Abu Dhabi calendar makes that worse
paragraphs: The sequence matters. Abu Dhabi schools issue Diploma option forms in the spring term of Year 11 or MYP 5, which is before IGCSE or MYP final results exist. Families are therefore choosing a two-year mathematics route on the basis of mock grades and a teacher's prediction. That is not a criticism of the school; timetabling a Diploma cohort requires numbers months ahead. It does mean the evidence available in March is thinner than the decision deserves.

What follows is a set of dates nobody writes down together. Sets are confirmed late in the summer term once the school knows how many students picked each course. DP1 starts in the first term of the new academic year. Each school then operates its own internal window for a route or level change, typically closing inside that first term, and after it the move stops being administrative and becomes a catch-up project. The May examination session is registered by the school as the IB registering centre, months before the papers themselves.

A specific warning on the IB side. Session and results dates for the Diploma are published by the IB and by your school's coordinator, and this page deliberately does not restate them: they are revised, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with your DP coordinator or on ibo.org. The Cambridge and Pearson dates further down are different, because both boards publish them in documents we can cite.

sections.heading: The exploration is 20% of the grade and is marked out of 20 across five letters
paragraphs: Every Diploma mathematics student, in either route and at either level, produces one internally assessed exploration. It is marked against five criteria, A to E, for a total of 20 marks, and it carries 20% of the final subject grade. Almost nothing published for parents in this market names those criteria or their mark allocations, which is unfortunate, because the allocation is the single most useful thing a family can know about the component.

Criterion A, presentation, carries 4 marks and rewards a piece that is coherent, organised and concise. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries 4 and rewards correct notation, defined variables and labelled graphs. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries 3 and rewards evidence of the student's own thinking rather than a topic lifted from a list. Criterion D, reflection, carries 3 and rewards critical discussion of results and limitations. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6 and is the largest single block.

The pattern of lost marks is consistent. Students assemble the piece in the order they did the work, which costs them on A. They paste calculator output onto the page, which costs them on B. They pick a topic from a handout, which costs them all three marks on C. They summarise instead of evaluating, which costs them on D. And at Higher Level they use mathematics that would have been fine in a Standard Level piece, which costs them on E, where the marks are heaviest. Those are five separate, fixable problems, and none of them requires anyone to write any part of the work for the student.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE, MYP or CBSE background actually predicts
paragraphs: Prior attainment predicts the route better than it predicts the level, and the syllabus predicts better than the grade. A Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 student has met function notation, transformations of graphs and the language of gradients as rates of change. A Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 student has met early calculus outright. A student who sat 0580 Extended, however well, has met neither in that form, because the syllabus does not contain them.

This matters in Abu Dhabi specifically because several British-curriculum schools in the emirate enter their cohort for 0580 Extended only, then feed students into Analysis and Approaches at a Diploma school. That is a workable path with a bridging block over the summer and a hard one without. The student is not behind in ability; they are behind in content that the new course assumes on day one, and the DP1 teacher has a scheme of work to get through.

MYP 5 students arrive with the opposite profile: strong investigation and communication habits that pay off immediately in the exploration, and lighter drilled fluency in manipulation. CBSE Class 10 students usually arrive with the manipulation and without the interpretation, which makes Analysis and Approaches feel familiar and Applications and Interpretation feel oddly hard. In each case the gap is specific, nameable and about six to eight weeks of focused work, which is a far better conversation than a general worry about whether a student is a maths person.

sections.heading: Where the route is named in university entry requirements, and who to ask
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi ask this question earlier than families elsewhere, because the city's own universities sit next to the schools. Khalifa University, NYU Abu Dhabi, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi, Zayed University, Abu Dhabi University and United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain all publish their own admission requirements, and those requirements change. This page will not restate them, because an entry requirement reproduced on a tutoring page and then revised is a trap for the family that trusted it.

What can be said safely is the shape of the pattern. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and some economics programmes commonly name an algebraic mathematics route, and frequently a Higher Level one. Life sciences, business, social sciences, design and humanities programmes commonly accept either route. Medicine varies by country and by school more than any other destination. Where a programme names a route, it is almost always in a published table on the programme's own admissions page, and that is the only version worth acting on. A dated screenshot of the page is worth keeping in the family file.

The practical advice is sequencing. Write down the three or four degree families your child is actually considering, open each institution's current admissions page, and read the mathematics line. Do that before the option form is returned, not in DP2. And ask the school's university guidance counsellor to confirm what they have seen accepted from your school's own leavers, which is information no website holds and the counsellor usually does. Counsellors in Abu Dhabi schools track their own cohort's offers year by year, and that record is the closest thing to a locally reliable answer.

Moving from Applications and Interpretation Standard Level to Analysis and Approaches Standard Level in the first term of DP1 means acquiring non-calculator fluency, exact-value trigonometry, logarithm laws and early differentiation, while keeping up with six subjects. Realistically that is one or two sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks, plus written work between them. Moving up a level as well roughly doubles it.

The comparison with in-home delivery is worth making plainly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an exploration, and what nobody may do
paragraphs: This boundary is worth stating before any work starts, because the Abu Dhabi search results for mathematics help include operations that sell completed internal assessments. Under IB academic honesty rules the exploration must be the student's own work. A piece produced by someone else is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. That is not a technicality; it reaches the award of the Diploma.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the mathematics the student wants to use. They can discuss whether a proposed topic will generate enough mathematics to reach the top band of criterion E. They can read a draft the student has written and give feedback against the criteria by letter. They can point out that variables are undefined, that a graph is unlabelled, that the reflection summarises rather than evaluates. They can teach the student to check their own work, and show them how an examiner reads the five criteria in order.

What a tutor cannot do is produce any part of the piece, rewrite a paragraph into better English, or supply the mathematics for the student to copy. Nor should anyone supply reproduced IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those are the board's copyright and should be reached through the school or the official site. If a provider in this market offers a finished exploration, that offer is the clearest possible signal to walk away. The price is irrelevant next to what it risks, and the student carries that risk alone.

sections.heading: ADEK, the cohort and what to ask your DP coordinator this week
paragraphs: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection ratings for them. That is the regulator's role, and it is worth understanding what it does not cover: ADEK does not publish which mathematics sets a given school will run next September, and no tutoring company holds any ADEK approval that would let it tell you. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation, and any provider claiming one should be asked to show the permit number.

The information you need is held by one person, and it is a short list of questions. Will Analysis and Approaches run at both levels next year, and Applications and Interpretation at both. What is the minimum group size before a set is withdrawn. What is this school's internal deadline for a route or level change in DP1. Which IGCSE or MYP syllabus does the school feed from, and does the maths department expect a bridging gap. Who teaches each set.

Separately, one UAE rule is worth knowing before you arrange anything privately. Private tutoring here runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service. Press reporting also indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so your child's own teacher is not the person to ask. Verify both with ADEK and MoHRE directly before acting.

faqs.question: Our Abu Dhabi school's option form is due before the DP coordinator meeting. What should we ask for first?
faqs.answer: Ask for two things in writing. First, which mathematics sets the school expects to run next September, at which levels, and the minimum group size before a set is withdrawn. Second, the maths department's view of your child specifically against Analysis and Approaches, based on their current work rather than their effort grade. Alongside that, get a marked diagnostic of by-hand algebra, exact-value trigonometry and one modelling task, because that is the evidence the form is really asking about and nobody has it in March. With the school's answer and a marked diagnostic you are choosing on information rather than on reputation.

faqs.question: Does ADEK publish which Abu Dhabi schools run Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection ratings, but set availability is a school-level timetabling decision taken once option numbers are known, usually late in the summer term. The IB publishes which programmes a school is authorised to offer, not which courses within them will run in a given year. The only reliable source is your school's DP coordinator. Treat any tutoring company that claims to know, or that claims ADEK approval of its own, with caution: IB Gram holds no ADEK or IB accreditation and says so.

faqs.question: How are the marks split between the papers in IB mathematics?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, in both routes, Paper 1 is 40% of the grade, Paper 2 is 40% and the exploration is 20%. At Higher Level, in both routes, Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 is 30%, Paper 3 is 20% and the exploration is 20%. The weightings are the same whichever route a student takes, which catches families out, because the usual assumption is that one course is assessed more gently. The useful consequence is that at Higher Level, 40% of the grade sits outside the two conventional papers, in an investigation paper and a piece of coursework that most revision plans barely touch.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and does it exist in both mathematics routes?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level, and it exists in both routes. It is two extended response questions, each building through several parts from an accessible opening to a demanding generalisation, and it carries 20% of the Higher Level grade. In Analysis and Approaches the investigations are problem-solving in character; in Applications and Interpretation they are framed around data and modelling. The common failure is the same in both: students run out of time around part (c) and never attempt the later parts where the reasoning marks are. Practising whole Paper 3 questions under timing from early DP2 is the fix, and it has to be scheduled.

faqs.question: How many marks is the mathematics exploration worth, and how is it broken down?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of 20 and carries 20% of the final mathematics grade, at both levels and in both routes. The five criteria are A presentation, worth 4 marks; B mathematical communication, worth 4; C personal engagement, worth 3; D reflection, worth 3; and E use of mathematics, worth 6. Criterion E is the largest single block and is where a Higher Level student most often loses marks by using mathematics that would have been fine in a Standard Level piece. Knowing the allocation changes how a student spends their time, which is why it is worth having before the first draft rather than after it.

faqs.question: My daughter is at a British-curriculum school in Khalifa City. Which route fits an IGCSE 0580 background?
faqs.answer: Either route is possible, but 0580 Extended does not contain function notation in the Diploma's sense, exact trigonometric values or differentiation, so Analysis and Approaches assumes content she has not met. That is a content gap of roughly six to eight weeks, not an ability judgement, and it is much cheaper to close over the summer than in October of DP1. Students who sat 0607 International Mathematics or 0606 Additional Mathematics arrive with more of that language already in place. The practical test is a short non-calculator diagnostic: if exact values and index laws are secure, Analysis and Approaches is a reasonable choice with bridging.

faqs.question: What happens if our school will not run the Standard Level set my son needs?
faqs.answer: It happens, particularly in Abu Dhabi where Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, and it is a conversation to have in March rather than August. A school may withdraw a set below a minimum group size, combine two sets into one teaching group, or ask a student to take the level that runs. Ask the coordinator what the minimum is and what the fallback would be. If the outcome is that your child takes a route the school can staff rather than the one that suits them, independent weekly support becomes the way the gap is managed, and the plan should be written down before DP1 starts.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi universities publish which mathematics route they require?
faqs.answer: Each institution publishes its own admission requirements on its own site, and those requirements are revised, so the only version worth acting on is the current page for the specific programme. Khalifa University, NYU Abu Dhabi, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi, Zayed University, Abu Dhabi University and United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain all have their own tables. The broad pattern is that engineering, physics, mathematics and computer science programmes commonly name an algebraic route and often a Higher Level one, while many business, life science and humanities programmes accept either. Read the programme page, and ask your school's university counsellor what their own leavers have had accepted.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move from Applications to Analysis in DP1?
faqs.answer: If the school's internal window is still open, the administrative move is quick and the content work is the real cost. Expect one or two sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks to acquire non-calculator fluency, exact-value trigonometry, logarithm laws and early differentiation, while keeping up with the new course and five other subjects. Moving up a level at the same time roughly doubles that. The honest version is that a change made in the first weeks of DP1 is manageable and one attempted in DP2 usually is not, which is why the school's deadline is the date to find out first.

faqs.question: Which topics in Analysis and Approaches cause the most lost marks in the first DP1 mocks?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Logarithm and index laws, where students who have always evaluated numerically cannot manipulate symbolically. Exact trigonometric values and radian work, which the non-calculator Paper 1 depends on completely. Function transformations and composite functions, where notation defeats students who understand the idea. And the chain rule applied inside a product or quotient, which is the first place calculus stops being a procedure. None of those is conceptually hard. All four reward about three weeks of deliberate practice, and all four are visible in a single marked diagnostic rather than needing a term of observation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor sit with my child during the exploration, or is that against IB rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the mathematics the student plans to use, discuss whether a topic will generate enough mathematics for the top band of criterion E, and give feedback on a draft the student has written, criterion by criterion. What nobody may do is produce any part of the piece, rewrite passages into better English, or supply mathematics for the student to copy. The exploration must be the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student and can reach the award of the Diploma. Any provider offering a finished internal assessment is offering a disciplinary case.

faqs.question: Does the graphic display calculator matter more in one route than the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, in opposite directions. Applications and Interpretation assumes a graphic display calculator in every paper, and marks depend on using it fluently for regression, distributions and statistical tests, so a student who navigates menus slowly loses time everywhere. Analysis and Approaches withholds it entirely in Paper 1, so the same student loses marks for the opposite reason. Schools specify which models are permitted and set them up with exam-compliant firmware; ask your school rather than buying from a general recommendation. In both routes, calculator work should be practised on the exact model the student will take into the examination room.

faqs.question: What do mathematics sessions cost in the Abu Dhabi market at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates in October 2026 run roughly as follows. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors sit around AED 150-300 online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist exam-year support runs AED 200-450 and above, and a premium named tier reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. In-home visits carry a travel premium, at AED 180-500. Those are market figures from each provider, not an IB Gram price list; ask us for a written plan after the free trial.

faqs.question: How do mathematics sessions work around Ramadan and the Abu Dhabi school calendar?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten during Ramadan and household routines move late, so sessions move with them: post-Iftar slots work well, and shorter, more frequent sessions hold attention better than a long one in the afternoon. The wider calendar matters too. Diploma internal deadlines for the exploration cluster in late DP1 and early DP2, mock weeks arrive before the long winter break, and the May session preparation runs through the hottest part of the spring term. Planning the year around those dates, rather than booking a fixed weekly slot and hoping, is what makes a weekly hour actually land.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 5 at a school on Al Reem Island. When should the route conversation happen?
faqs.answer: Before the option form is returned, which in practice means early in the spring term of MYP 5. MYP students usually arrive in the Diploma strong on investigation and communication, which pays off in the exploration, and lighter on drilled algebraic fluency, which is what Analysis and Approaches tests hardest in Paper 1. A diagnostic at that point tells you whether the manipulation is secure enough, and leaves the summer available for bridging if it is not. Ask the MYP maths teacher directly whether they would place him in extended mathematics and why; their answer is usually specific and useful.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Mathematics support for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on and the tutor marks as they go. For a route question that is genuinely better rather than a compromise, because the scarce thing is a specialist in your child's exact course and level, not someone who can reach Khalifa City by 17:00. A family in Al Ain and a family on Saadiyat Island reach the same tutor in the same evening slot.

abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.closingHeading: Get the route decided on evidence, not on a prediction
abu-dhabi/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.closingBody: If the option form is due, book the free trial lesson and treat it as a diagnostic: forty minutes of marked by-hand algebra and one modelling task will tell you more than any amount of discussion about which child is a maths person. You keep the written diagnosis whether or not you continue, and it is written to be taken into a meeting with your DP coordinator. If DP1 has already started and the first assessed test came back lower than expected, find your school's internal deadline for a route change this week, then call us. Sessions are one-to-one, online, and timed to the Abu Dhabi evening.

intro.heading: Arabic is the one MYP subject an Abu Dhabi family cannot opt out of, which is why the price matters
paragraphs: Arabic sits in a different category from every other language on an Abu Dhabi school timetable. Federal rules state that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. A family choosing between Spanish and French is choosing an option. A family dealing with Arabic is dealing with a requirement that runs alongside whichever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and that changes the economics of tutoring it.

The practical consequence is that demand for Arabic support in Abu Dhabi is both steady and badly matched. Almost every student in an IB World School in the emirate carries Arabic on the timetable. Comparatively few private tutors are equipped to teach it to the MYP language acquisition criteria rather than as conversation practice, and the ones who are tend to be in school classrooms during the hours a parent wants a session. Scarcity of that specific skill, not fuel or villa size, is what sets the top of the Abu Dhabi rate band.

What follows is a price page rather than a brochure. It sets out the published market bands in AED, names what each band actually buys, lists the six things that move a quote up or down in this emirate, and then costs out a full MYP 1 to MYP 5 run so you can see the whole number rather than an hourly one. Every figure is somebody's published rate, attributed where it came from, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price list.

Two structural facts about Abu Dhabi shape the supply side, and both are worth understanding before you compare quotes. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Separately, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a bar on private and charter school staff providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but the direction is clear: the obvious cheap option, your child's own Arabic teacher, is not an option at all.

IB Gram delivers Arabic as one-to-one tuition over live video to families across Abu Dhabi. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; tutors travelling to an address is an India-only service. On the page below, the in-home column exists because it is what the local market charges, not because we sell it. Read it as the comparison it is: a Khalifa City family pays a travel premium to reach whoever lives nearby, or pays for an Arabic specialist who is free at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time and appears on screen.
