abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.programmesIntro: Biology shows up differently in each part of the IB continuum, and so does the evidence it produces. The record you can build in the MYP is better than most families realise and worse than the external record the Diploma generates, which is why what you do with it matters.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Biology is one strand of the Sciences subject group. MYP 1 to 3 is typically integrated, with cells, nutrition and ecology units alongside chemistry and physics. MYP 4 and 5 may split into discrete biology. All work is marked internally against criteria A to D, each out of eight, on tasks the school writes. That internal model is what makes a private baseline worth keeping.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the schools licensed by ADEK report criterion levels directly, so the raw material for an evidence ledger is already in your household. ADEK also inspects these schools and publishes ratings, which gives a second reference point: a department rated well where your child is scoring poorly points towards a student-specific gap rather than a teaching one. That distinction decides whether tutoring is the right purchase at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology becomes a named Standard or Higher Level course with external papers and an Internal Assessment. The evidence changes character completely: marks come from outside the school, past papers exist, and progress can be measured against published assessment criteria on work that an examiner will eventually see.
programmes.countryNote: What an Abu Dhabi family keeps from the MYP is a record of which criteria were weak, and that predicts Diploma difficulty better than the MYP grade does. A student who left MYP 5 with a solid criterion A and a persistent criterion C problem will struggle with the Internal Assessment two years later, because the Internal Assessment is criterion C with the scaffolding removed. Families who kept the ledger know to spend DP 1 money on data handling rather than on content revision.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led science with no criterion grading. Children observe living things, record what they see and describe change. There is no biology mark, no rubric and therefore no evidence to baseline, which is the honest reason paid biology tutoring has nothing to work with at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: In continuum schools in this emirate a child moves from PYP 5 straight into MYP 1 and meets criterion marking for the first time. The transferable habit is recording: a child who writes down what they observed, with a unit and a date, arrives in MYP 1 already doing the thing criterion C will reward. That costs nothing and we would rather recommend it than sell a biology course to a ten-year-old.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.subjectsIntro: A biology request usually arrives attached to something else, because the Sciences criteria are shared and the skills travel. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families most often combine with biology, and what evidence each one generates.

subjects.name: Sciences: the biology strand
subjects.description: Cells and microscopy, transport across membranes, nutrition and digestion, gas exchange, homeostasis, inheritance, evolution and ecology. The clearest evidence of progress here is a labelled diagram and an ecology sampling write-up, both of which show criterion C work plainly.

subjects.name: Sciences: the chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, reactions and quantitative work. Shares criteria C and D with biology, so a data-processing fix made in biology is visible in the next chemistry write-up without being taught twice.

subjects.name: Sciences: the physics strand
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves and electricity. Its graph work is the most demanding of the three strands, which makes it a useful place to practise a criterion C skill that biology will then reuse on a growth curve or a transect.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: One grade covering all three strands, which averages away exactly the signal a parent needs. Ask for criterion levels per unit instead; a biology unit at 6, 3, 4, 5 next to a physics unit at 5, 5, 5, 5 tells you something the overall grade hides.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard)
subjects.description: Scale, ratio, percentages and simple statistics. Biology is quietly numerical: magnification calculations, rates of reaction in enzyme work, percentage change in growth data and means from sampling all sit inside criterion C levels.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Produces a process journal, which is the closest thing in the MYP to the fortnightly record this page argues for, and students who keep one well transfer the habit to Sciences.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation, source handling and critical thinking. Directly useful for criterion D in biology, where implications of applying science must be discussed with specific consequences rather than general concern about the environment.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis, organisation, text production and language use. Biology write-ups are extended prose, and a student who cannot structure a paragraph will lose Sciences levels for reasons a biology tutor alone cannot fix.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with its own homework load. It is the main reason an Abu Dhabi biology plan has fewer workable evenings than a plan written for a student elsewhere.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed units pairing Sciences with another subject group. Ecology and sustainability pairings are common in this emirate, and they carry their own criteria and their own grade, which parents often discover only when the report arrives.

modes.title: Baselined weekly term
modes.description: The arrangement this page is built around. A recorded baseline, one session a week for a term, a marked practice task every fortnight and a six-week comparison against the baseline on the same criterion. It is the only arrangement in which a claim about progress can be checked rather than believed.

sections.heading: The baseline: what gets written down before the first paid session
paragraphs: A baseline in MYP biology takes one marked task, the current criterion levels and about twenty minutes of a specialist's reading. What comes out of it is a short document naming four things: where each criterion currently sits, which strand inside the weakest criterion lost the level, what the task's command terms asked for, and which single criterion the term will target. That document is sent to you before anything is paid for, and every later claim about progress is measured against it.

Specificity is what makes it useful. 'Criterion C is weak' is not a baseline. 'Criterion C sits at 3; the data table had units in the cells rather than the headings, no mean was calculated from the three repeats, the graph used a line where the variable was categoric, and the evaluation named no limitation of the method' is a baseline, because each of those four statements can be checked against the same student's work six weeks later. It also tells you what the sessions are supposed to be doing, which means you can tell when they are not doing it.

Parents sometimes ask why a report card is not enough. Because a report gives you an average of tasks of different difficulty, written by different teachers, at different points in a unit. It tells you roughly where a student stands and almost nothing about why. A marked task tells you why, and the why is the only thing a tutor can act on. If the school has not sent marked work home this term, ask for it; schools in this emirate are generally willing, and the request itself tends to produce a useful conversation with the subject teacher.

sections.heading: Reading a marked biology task when you are not a biologist
paragraphs: A parent with no biology background can extract a surprising amount from a marked task in ten minutes, and the method does not require knowing the answers. Start with the command terms. Find each one in the question and read whether the answer did what it asked. If a question says 'explain' and the answer contains no 'because' and no mechanism, that is a lost mark you can see without understanding the biology at all.

Next, look at the diagrams. MYP biology rewards accurate labelled diagrams, and they fail in predictable ways: labels with lines that touch nothing in particular, structures drawn freehand where the shape carries meaning, no title, no magnification stated where a microscope was used. All of that is visible to anyone. A student who draws well and labels carelessly is losing criterion A marks for reasons that take one session to fix.

Then look at the data. In any biology write-up, check whether the table has units in the headings, whether repeats appear, whether a mean was calculated, and whether the graph type matches the kind of variable. A bar chart for a continuous variable or a line joining the dots instead of a line of best fit are the two errors that recur most, and both are mechanical. Finally, read the last paragraph. If it says 'there may have been human error' and stops, criterion C's evaluation strand has been left on the table, and that is worth one or two levels in itself.

What you cannot assess yourself is whether the biology content is right, and that is fine, because it is usually not the problem. Across requests from this emirate, content-only failures are the minority. The majority are command terms, diagram discipline, data presentation and evaluation, all of which a parent can audit directly. Doing that audit before buying tutoring often reveals that one focused term, not an open-ended arrangement, is what is actually needed.

sections.heading: What moves a biology criterion level, and how long each takes
paragraphs: Criterion levels do not move at the same speed, and knowing the rates stops families from abandoning an arrangement that is working or continuing one that is not. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the quickest: two to four sessions of focused work on explanation rather than description will usually move it a level, because the underlying knowledge is often already there and being presented wrongly.

Criterion B, inquiring and designing, is the slowest. A student has to produce a testable research question, identify and control variables, justify a method and plan something that would actually work. Four to eight sessions is a realistic expectation for one level, and the work is largely transferable: a student who can plan an osmosis investigation can plan an enzyme one. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, sits in similar territory, although the presentation half of it can move fast while the evaluation half takes longer.

Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, is the one where a specific local context produces the fastest movement. Students write generically about environmental harm and score in the middle. Given a real habitat, a real trade-off and a citable source, the same student writes something specific and moves two levels. That is why the Abu Dhabi ecology context is treated as a tool on this page rather than as decoration. The table sets out each criterion with the strand that most often costs the level and a realistic number of sessions.

sections.heading: Diagrams, systems and the biology that produces checkable evidence
paragraphs: Biology content divides into parts that generate good evidence quickly and parts that do not. Cells and microscopy generate it immediately: a labelled diagram with a stated magnification is either accurate or it is not, and a student's second attempt sits next to their first. Transport across membranes is similarly legible, because osmosis and diffusion investigations produce numbers, and numbers produce the tables and graphs that criterion C is marked on.

Systems content, meaning digestion, circulation, gas exchange and homeostasis, generates evidence through explanation. These topics are where the gap between describing and explaining is widest: a student can list the parts of the digestive system and still be unable to explain why surface area matters to absorption. A tutor's intervention here is to keep asking why until structure and function are linked, and the evidence is a cold answer to a question the student has not seen, before and after.

Inheritance produces the cleanest evidence of all, because it is partly procedural. A student either sets out a genetic cross correctly, with parental genotypes, gametes, offspring genotypes and the phenotype ratio, or they do not. That is checkable by a parent in thirty seconds and improves in two or three sessions. Evolution and natural selection are the opposite: they reward precise reasoning about variation, selection and inheritance over generations, and loose phrasing about animals adapting because they needed to is penalised heavily. Ecology sits between the two, generating sampling data and the opportunity for a genuinely local criterion D discussion.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi habitat on your doorstep, used as criterion D evidence
paragraphs: Criterion D asks a student to apply science to address a problem and to discuss the implications of doing so. Most students answer it with generalities about pollution, and most scripts look identical as a result. Abu Dhabi students have access to specific local material that almost none of them use, and specificity is exactly what separates a middling level from a strong one.

The mangrove stands along the eastern edge of the island are a working example. They are a real habitat with a named dominant species, a measurable role in sediment stabilisation and carbon storage, a nursery function for fish, and a direct conflict with coastal development. A student can visit, photograph a transect, note the zonation from the water's edge inland, and write about a trade-off that exists rather than one imagined. The Environment Agency for the emirate publishes material on coastal and marine habitats that can be cited properly, which turns an assertion into a referenced claim.

Other contexts work the same way. Desert ecology supports a discussion of water conservation and grazing pressure. Species reintroduction programmes in this emirate raise questions about captive breeding, genetic diversity and the cost of conservation in money terms. Wetland reserves inland support a discussion of migratory birds and habitat protection against land use. Each of those has published local material behind it, which is the difference between a criterion D paragraph that could have been written anywhere and one that could only have been written here. The second scores better and takes no longer to write.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line, and why the evidence depends on it
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement only works if the evidence is the student's. The IB's position is unambiguous: submitted work must be the student's own, and a tutor who supplies text has destroyed both the student's position and the only record worth keeping. A tutor may teach biology, question reasoning, mark practice work, name an unaddressed strand of the rubric and explain in general terms what a limitation or an implication is. A tutor may not provide sentences for a submission, correct a draft into a finished state, or supply answers to the task being assessed.

The question-led method is what makes this practical rather than merely principled. A tutor who annotates a draft with 'what was the smallest division on the instrument you used, and could you see the difference you are claiming?' has taught the evaluation strand without writing a word of it. The student answers in their own language, and the answer survives a teacher asking about it later. A tutor who writes 'the thermometer's precision limited the result' has handed over a sentence that the student cannot defend and that has taught nothing.

This matters commercially as well, because the same search results that brought you here contain providers selling completed assessed work. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the student bears the consequence. It is also why the annotated draft and its rewrite are both kept in this arrangement: two versions in the student's own voice, with the tutor's questions visible between them, are evidence of teaching. A single polished document with no history behind it is evidence of nothing, and in a dispute it is worse than nothing.

sections.heading: When the record says stop, and what to do about it
paragraphs: A six-week review has three honest outcomes, and two of them are not 'continue'. If the targeted criterion moved and the artefacts are in place, continuing is straightforward. If nothing moved, the question is why, and there are only a few real answers. The diagnosis may have been wrong, in which case the baseline gets rewritten and the target changes. The tutor may be the wrong match, in which case changing tutor rather than stopping is usually right. Or the obstacle may sit outside biology entirely.

That third case is more common than families expect. A student whose criterion C problem is really a mathematics problem will not improve with biology sessions, however good they are, because every data-processing task will keep failing at the same arithmetic step. A student whose write-ups fail on structure needs writing support, not biology support. A student whose sessions keep landing at half past seven after a long bus journey and two other homework subjects is not failing to learn; they are too tired to. The record usually shows which of these it is, because session notes that say 'ran out of time again' six weeks in a row are telling you something about the timetable rather than about the biology.

The fourth possibility is that tutoring is not needed. If the evidence shows a student at 6 or 7 across the criteria who is anxious rather than behind, more sessions will not help and may make it worse. We would rather say that at the six-week review and stop than keep selling hours into a problem that is not academic. Saying it is only possible because the baseline exists; without a record, every arrangement defaults to continuing indefinitely, which is precisely why so many of them do.

sections.heading: What the MYP biology record predicts about the Diploma
paragraphs: The most valuable thing a family takes out of MYP biology is not the grade. It is knowing which criteria were weak, because the Diploma reuses them with the scaffolding removed. The Internal Assessment in Diploma biology is essentially criteria B and C combined and extended: a student designs an investigation, collects and processes data, and evaluates the method, largely unaided. A student who left MYP 5 with a persistent criterion C weakness will meet that weakness again two years later with far higher stakes.

Criterion A translates less directly, because Diploma content is far broader and recall demands are higher. What does translate is the explanation habit. Students who learned in MYP 4 to answer 'explain' with a mechanism rather than a description arrive able to write Diploma answers that earn marks, and students who never learned it spend DP 1 being told the same thing their MYP teacher told them. Criterion D has the loosest mapping of the four, although the discipline of citing a source and naming a specific consequence is exactly what Diploma extended responses reward.

For an Abu Dhabi family choosing whether to spend in MYP 5, that is the practical frame. You are not buying a middle-years number that no university will ever see. You are buying the criterion B and C skills that the Internal Assessment will assume are already in place, at a market rate well below what Diploma support costs, in a year when the student has more time than they will have in DP 1. The record from MYP 5 then tells your DP 1 tutor exactly where to start, which is itself worth several sessions.

process.title: Send one marked biology task
process.description: With the teacher's comments on it, plus the current report showing criterion levels. These two documents support a real diagnosis; a phone conversation about how biology is going does not, because students and parents are usually wrong about which criterion is the problem.

process.title: Receive the written baseline
process.description: Before any payment, you get a short document naming where each criterion sits, which strand lost the level, what the command terms asked, and the single criterion a term would target. It is written so that it can be proved wrong later, which is the point of it.

process.title: One session at no charge on the same work
process.description: A fifty-minute session with an MYP Sciences specialist at no charge, one per family, no card details taken. It tests the baseline's diagnosis against the student cold. Occasionally it disproves the diagnosis, which is more useful than confirming it.

process.title: Agree target, count and terms in writing
process.description: One criterion, a number of sessions, the rate in AED, whether preparation time is charged, and the reschedule window. Chasing all four criteria at once produces a busy term with nothing to show at the end of it.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the baseline
process.description: Second marked task next to the first, same criterion, read strand by strand. Continue, change tutor, change target, or stop. All four are real outcomes, and the review is where we say which one the evidence supports rather than which one sells more hours.

whyPoints.title: A baseline you can hold us to
whyPoints.description: The target criterion and the failing strand are written down and sent to you before the first paid session. That document is specific enough to be proved wrong, which is the only kind of promise worth making about tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not impressions
whyPoints.description: A marked practice task every fortnight, an annotated draft with the student's rewrite beside it, and a comparable second task at six weeks. Each is a thing you can look at. None of them is a score we invented or a dashboard built to look like progress.

whyPoints.title: Honest reading of a grade
whyPoints.description: A grade that rises may reflect an easier task rather than a better student, and we will say so when that is the likelier explanation. A criterion level on comparable work is the stronger signal, and treating the two as equivalent is how families get told good news that is not true.

whyPoints.title: Questions instead of answers
whyPoints.description: Drafts are annotated with questions. The student answers them and rewrites in their own language, which is both the honest route and the one that produces defensible work. No sentence for a submission is ever supplied by a tutor here.

whyPoints.title: Local context used properly
whyPoints.description: Criterion D rewards specificity, and this emirate has mangrove stands, desert ecology, reintroduction programmes and wetland reserves with published material behind them. A referenced paragraph about a habitat your child can visit outscores a general one about the environment.

whyPoints.title: A review that can say stop
whyPoints.description: At six weeks the evidence decides, and sometimes it decides against continuing. If the obstacle is mathematics, writing or an exhausted eight o'clock session, we will say that rather than sell another term into a problem biology tutoring cannot reach.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's biology tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By comparing a marked task from week one with a comparable one from week six, on the same criterion, strand by strand. That is the only comparison that means anything, because MYP tasks vary in difficulty and an overall grade averages them. Alongside it you should have a marked practice task every fortnight, an annotated draft with the student's rewrite beside it, and a short written note after each session. If those artefacts do not exist after six weeks, you have no evidence of progress regardless of how the sessions felt, and you are entitled to say so.

faqs.question: How can I check a marked biology task if I have no biology background?
faqs.answer: Four checks, none of which need subject knowledge. Find each command term and read whether the answer did what it asked, so an 'explain' question with no 'because' in the answer is a visible lost mark. Look at the diagrams for labels that point at nothing, missing titles and absent magnification. Check the data table for units in the headings, repeats and a mean. Read the final paragraph: if it says there may have been human error and stops, the evaluation strand has been left unwritten. Those four cover most lost marks in this emirate.

faqs.question: My daughter's biology criterion levels are 6, 3, 4, 5. What does that tell us?
faqs.answer: That the biology knowledge is in good shape and the investigation work is not. A 6 on criterion A means she can explain and apply content. A 3 on criterion B means inquiring and designing is the problem: the research question, the variables, the justification of the method. The 4 on criterion C says data processing and evaluation are mediocre, which usually travels with a weak B. A term aimed squarely at B, with C following, is the right purchase. A term of content revision would raise the 6 slightly and change nothing else.

faqs.question: How long does it take for a biology criterion level to move?
faqs.answer: It depends on which one. Criterion A usually moves in two to four focused sessions, because the knowledge is often present and being presented wrongly. Criterion B takes four to eight, as designing a controlled investigation is a composite skill that has to be built. Criterion C is similar, with presentation improving faster than evaluation. Criterion D can move in two to five sessions if the student is given a specific local context and a citable source instead of writing generally about the environment. Anyone promising a level in a fortnight is describing a sale.

faqs.question: Can we see evidence of the approach before committing to a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the sequence we prefer. Send one marked task and the current criterion levels, and you receive a written baseline naming where each criterion sits and which strand lost the level, before any payment. Then one fifty-minute session at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken, which tests that diagnosis against your child cold. You keep the baseline document either way. If the session disproves the diagnosis, that is a useful outcome rather than an embarrassing one, and it changes what gets bought.

faqs.question: What should exist after four weeks of biology sessions?
faqs.answer: Three things. A marked practice task from around week two, scored against the published criterion rubric rather than given a percentage. An annotated draft of a biology write-up, with the tutor's marks appearing as questions rather than as corrections, plus the student's own rewrite of it so the change is visible side by side. And four short session notes, one paragraph each, naming which criterion strand was worked on and what to practise. If any of those is missing at four weeks, ask why before week six.

faqs.question: Is a rising biology grade proof that the tutoring worked?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. MYP grades come from tasks of varying difficulty, written and marked by your child's own school, so a move from 4 to 5 could reflect a kinder task rather than a better student. The stronger signal is a criterion level on comparable work, which is why the baseline records the strand rather than the grade. We will tell you when we think a rise is task difficulty rather than progress. A provider that treats every improvement as proof of its own value is not measuring anything.

faqs.question: How do we evidence criterion B when the practical happens at school?
faqs.answer: By working on the plan rather than the apparatus. Criterion B is assessed on the research question, the variables identified and controlled, the justification of the method and the plan's workability, all of which are written documents. A tutor can set an investigation planning task on a biology topic the school is not currently assessing, mark it against the rubric, and repeat it a fortnight later on a different topic. Two plans, two marked levels, same criterion. That is clean evidence, and it does not touch the work being submitted at school.

faqs.question: What counts as strong evidence for criterion D in biology?
faqs.answer: A paragraph that names a specific application, a specific consequence and a source. Writing that pollution harms ecosystems earns a middling level because it is true of everywhere. Writing about the mangrove stands at the eastern edge of Abu Dhabi, their role in stabilising sediment and sheltering juvenile fish, and the direct conflict with coastal development, with an emirate environment-agency publication cited, earns considerably more. The evidence of progress here is simple: the earlier paragraph next to the later one, with the citation and the named trade-off present in the second.

faqs.question: Does my child have to do fieldwork for MYP biology?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, as it depends entirely on what your school's units require, and the IB prescribes concepts and criteria for Sciences rather than a content list. Where ecology appears, fieldwork is common because sampling produces data a student can process. Even where the school does not run a trip, a student can practise the whole cycle informally: a transect along a public shoreline or a quadrat on a patch of ground generates real numbers to tabulate, mean and plot. The marks live in the processing and evaluation, not in the location.

faqs.question: Can we use the Abu Dhabi mangroves in a biology investigation write-up?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better options available in this emirate. The stands along the eastern coast have a named dominant species, visible zonation from the water inland, and a documented role in sediment stabilisation and as a fish nursery. A student can photograph a transect, record zonation, and build a criterion D discussion about coastal development trade-offs with an emirate environment-agency publication as the source. Two cautions: check access rules for the specific site, and keep the write-up entirely in the student's own words.

faqs.question: What should we do if six weeks of sessions show no movement?
faqs.answer: Work through four explanations in order. The diagnosis may have been wrong, so rewrite the baseline and change the target. The tutor may be a poor match, in which case change tutor rather than stopping. The obstacle may sit outside biology: a criterion C problem that is really a ratio problem, or write-ups failing on paragraph structure. Or the schedule may be the issue, which session notes repeatedly mentioning lost time will reveal. If none of those applies and the student is already at 6 or 7, the honest answer may be that tutoring is not the right purchase.

faqs.question: Do labelled diagrams really earn marks in MYP biology?
faqs.answer: They do, and they are the most frequently wasted marks we see. Criterion A rewards accurate representation of biological knowledge, and diagrams fail predictably: label lines that end near a structure rather than on it, freehand shapes where proportion carries meaning, no title, and no magnification stated where a microscope was used. None of that is a biology failure, which is why it is fixable in one or two sessions. It is also the easiest thing for a parent to audit in a marked task without knowing any biology at all.

faqs.question: How well does an MYP biology record predict Diploma biology?
faqs.answer: Better than the grade does. The Diploma Internal Assessment is largely criteria B and C extended with the scaffolding removed: the student designs an investigation, processes the data and evaluates the method with far less support. A persistent criterion C weakness in MYP 5 reappears there with much higher stakes. Criterion A translates as the habit of explaining rather than describing, which earns Diploma marks immediately. Keeping the MYP record means a DP 1 tutor can start where the gap actually is instead of spending three sessions finding it.

faqs.question: Will a biology tutor come to our address in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service we provide only in India. UAE lessons are one to one, live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For an evidence-led arrangement that is an advantage: annotated drafts, marked practice tasks and session notes are files in a shared place rather than paper in a school bag, so a six-week comparison is actually possible. The tutor is also chosen for how well they mark MYP Sciences criteria rather than for where they live.

faqs.question: Should we record the biology sessions to keep our own record?
faqs.answer: The session notes and marked artefacts are the record that matters, and they are easier to use than video. A one-paragraph note naming the criterion strand worked on, plus a marked task every fortnight, can be read in two minutes at the six-week review. An hour of video cannot. If you do want recordings, agree it in writing with the tutor in advance, keep them private to the household, and remember that recordings of a minor are personal data under the UAE's data-protection law and should be stored and deleted accordingly.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a baseline, not with a booking
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step costs nothing and takes a day. Send one marked biology task with the teacher's comments and the report showing criterion levels. You will get back a written baseline naming where each criterion sits, which strand is costing the level and what a term would target, followed by one fifty-minute session at no charge that tests that reading against your child cold. From there you can decide with a document in front of you rather than a feeling, and six weeks later you can check whether the document turned out to be true.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach the chemistry strand of MYP Sciences: integrated units in MYP 1 to 3 and discrete chemistry where an Abu Dhabi school offers it in MYP 4 and 5. Each works from your school's unit planner and marks practice tasks against the published criterion rubric rather than against a general impression.

intro.heading: What MYP chemistry is actually marked on, and why that answer matters
paragraphs: A parent in Abu Dhabi looking at an MYP report sees four numbers against Sciences and no percentage. Those numbers are criterion levels. Criterion A is knowing and understanding. Criterion B is inquiring and designing. Criterion C is processing and evaluating. Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked out of eight by your child's own subject teacher, against rubrics the IB publishes in the Sciences guide, and the four are then combined into the single grade from 1 to 7 that appears on the report. Ask your MYP coordinator for the boundary table your school applies; it belongs to the school, not to a tutoring page.

This matters because the question 'how is my child doing in chemistry' has four different answers, and they usually disagree with each other. The most common Abu Dhabi profile we see is a student with a 6 on criterion A and a 3 on criterion C: the chemistry is understood, and the data from the practical was processed into an unreadable table and a graph with no units. The overall grade comes out as a 4 or a 5, the parent concludes that chemistry is a problem, and the real problem is that nobody has ever taught the student how to process a result.

The content side of MYP chemistry is not fixed. The IB's Sciences guide sets out key concepts, related concepts and global contexts; it does not prescribe a topic list. Your school writes the units. In practice almost every Abu Dhabi MYP chemistry sequence passes through states of matter and the particle model, atomic structure and the periodic table, ionic and covalent bonding, word and symbol equations, conservation of mass and balancing, acids, bases and pH, rates of reaction, and separation techniques. Quantitative work using amount of substance appears in MYP 4 or 5 at some schools and not at all at others, which is why a tutor needs the planner rather than a textbook.

What a session fixes depends on which of those things is actually broken, and the answer is rarely the one a student volunteers. Students report that they find chemistry hard. Marked tasks report something far more specific: that symbol equations are being written without checking the mass balance, that 'explain' is being answered as though it said 'describe', that the evaluation paragraph apologises for human error instead of naming a limitation of the method. Each of those is a thirty-minute fix repeated until it holds, and none of them requires more chemistry knowledge.

Lessons are delivered one to one, live over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; that is a service we run only in India. For chemistry the online format is a practical advantage, because the artefacts are documents: a photographed practical write-up can be annotated line by line on a shared screen, a results table can be rebuilt in a spreadsheet while the student watches, and a balanced equation can be corrected in the same pen stroke the student used to get it wrong.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.programmesIntro: Chemistry appears in three different shapes across the IB continuum, and the tutoring problem is different in each. Abu Dhabi families most often need the middle one, but the reason they need it usually starts earlier and the consequence usually lands later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry is a strand inside the Sciences subject group rather than a standalone subject. MYP 1 to 3 is usually integrated, with chemistry units on particles, mixtures and reactions sitting between physics and biology units. MYP 4 and 5 may split into discrete chemistry at the school's discretion. All of it is assessed on criteria A to D through tasks the school writes and marks.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools licensed by ADEK report these criterion levels directly to parents, and the four-number format is new to most families arriving from a percentage-based system. ADEK inspects these schools and publishes ratings, so the quality of a Sciences department is often visible in an inspection report before it is visible in a grade. A tutor here starts by translating the report, because a parent who can read criterion levels stops buying the wrong help.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry becomes a named Standard or Higher Level course with external papers and an Internal Assessment. The quantitative demand rises sharply: amount of substance, concentration, limiting reagents and energetics all assume arithmetic fluency. Students who reached MYP 5 with weak symbol equations spend the first DP term repairing that rather than learning new chemistry.
programmes.countryNote: This is the argument for taking MYP chemistry seriously in an emirate where many students continue into the Diploma at the same school. Nothing in MYP 1 to 4 is externally examined, so a thin middle-years chemistry record leaves no mark on a transcript and a real gap in DP 1. The students who cope best with DP chemistry are not the ones who memorised more; they are the ones who can balance an equation and process a data set without thinking about it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based science with no criterion grading and no chemistry as such. Children meet materials, changes of state and simple mixtures through units of inquiry. There is no mark to compare and no chemistry gap to diagnose, so paid chemistry support at this stage has nothing to act on.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi campuses run the full continuum, and parents of PYP children sometimes ask about getting ahead in science. The honest answer is that the useful preparation is measurement and recording, not chemistry: a child who can read a scale, record a value with its unit and describe what changed is already doing what criterion C will later reward. We would rather say that than sell a chemistry course to a nine-year-old.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.subjectsIntro: Chemistry rarely arrives on its own. It shares criteria with the other two science strands, depends on arithmetic that sits in mathematics, and reappears inside interdisciplinary units with a different mark attached. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families book around a chemistry request.

subjects.name: Sciences: the chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particle model, atomic structure, the periodic table, bonding, equations and balancing, acids and bases, rates of reaction, separation techniques. Levels are lost most often on symbol equations that do not balance and on data tables that cannot be read.

subjects.name: Sciences: the physics strand
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves and electricity. Shares criteria C and D with chemistry exactly, so graph work taught in one shows up immediately in the other. A student whose chemistry graphs are poor almost always has the same problem in physics.

subjects.name: Sciences: the biology strand
subjects.description: Cells, systems, genetics, ecology. Its investigations are the easiest place to practise variable control, which is why biology tasks are sometimes the better vehicle for teaching a criterion B skill that will then be used in chemistry.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: One course, one teacher, one grade, with chemistry units distributed through it. Diagnosing a chemistry problem here means asking for unit-by-unit criterion levels rather than the overall Sciences grade, which averages away the signal you need.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard)
subjects.description: Ratio, proportion, percentages, indices and standard form. Every quantitative chemistry failure we see traces back to one of those five. A student who cannot handle ratio will not balance equations reliably or calculate a percentage yield, whatever they know about reactions.

subjects.name: Extended Mathematics
subjects.description: Deeper algebra and functions for students heading towards Analysis and Approaches. Relevant to chemistry because rearranging a relationship and working confidently in standard form removes most of the arithmetic risk from DP-level quantitative work.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The planning discipline is close enough to a chemistry investigation that students who can write a Design specification can usually write a method once the vocabulary changes.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation, source evaluation and critical thinking. Directly useful for criterion D in chemistry, where a student has to discuss the consequences of applying science and cite where a claim came from rather than asserting it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools. It occupies real timetable space and real homework time, which is the practical reason an Abu Dhabi chemistry plan has fewer free evenings than a plan written for a student elsewhere.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed units pairing Sciences with another subject group, frequently Individuals and Societies in this emirate. They carry their own criteria and their own grade, and chemistry content often appears inside them with no chemistry lesson attached.

They describe what families in each community actually ask for, which differs more than you would expect across a single emirate, and when in the week a chemistry session can hold a student's attention.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Long-established island community feeding several older private schools. Chemistry requests here arrive after a specific marked task rather than after a report, and are usually about criterion A explanation rather than practical work.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Early bus returns make four o'clock sessions workable. Al Reem families often ask for help with symbol equations and balancing specifically, which is the one chemistry topic parents can recognise as broken without reading a rubric.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Later bus arrivals push sessions to five or six o'clock. The most common request from this corridor is criterion C: a practical write-up has come back with a low level and nobody at home can tell why the table was the problem.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Apartment living and short commutes, with a mix of continuum and British-curriculum schools nearby. Requests often cover two children at once, with the chemistry hour given to the older MYP 4 or 5 student.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Larger year groups and longer journeys home. Weekend morning sessions work better here than weekday evenings for anything involving a full investigation write-up rather than a single calculation.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Villa community with established school routines. Chemistry enquiries from Al Mushrif skew towards MYP 5, triggered by the subject-choice conversation about whether to continue to Diploma chemistry.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: The one community where criterion D arrives as the stated request rather than as an afterthought. Families here want the impacts discussion done properly, often on energy, water or emissions, because that is the conversation at their dinner table anyway.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Newer mainland communities with growing cohorts. First-time MYP parents are common, and the opening session is frequently spent reading the report card together before any chemistry is taught.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.modesIntro: Chemistry support divides naturally into three jobs, and they are not interchangeable. Each is delivered one to one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked work as the material.

modes.title: Criterion-targeted weekly sessions
modes.description: One session a week aimed at a single named criterion for a whole term, chosen from the evidence in a marked task rather than from a conversation. Criterion C work looks completely different from criterion A work, and a term spent on the wrong one moves nothing. Twelve sessions is a realistic term.

modes.title: Equation and calculation drill
modes.description: Short, repetitive sessions on the mechanical chemistry that tasks assume: writing formulae, balancing symbol equations, conservation of mass, ratio and proportion, percentages, standard form. Unfashionable and the highest-yield purchase available in MYP 4 chemistry, because it removes a whole category of lost marks without teaching new content.

modes.title: Write-up review clinic
modes.description: Sessions built around a practical the student has already carried out at school. The tutor reads the draft, asks questions about the data and the method, and the student rewrites it. The tutor does not supply sentences, and that line is explained to the student in the first session so there is no confusion later.

sections.heading: The particle model: the one idea that sets criterion A levels
paragraphs: Almost every criterion A failure in MYP chemistry traces back to the same place. A student who cannot picture particles cannot explain anything, and so answers every question descriptively. Asked why a gas fills its container, they say that gases spread out. Asked why a solid has a fixed shape, they say that solids are hard. Both statements are true and neither explains, so both sit at a level 3 or 4 no matter how neatly they are written.

The repair is specific and quick. It takes a handful of sessions to build the habit of answering chemistry questions in terms of particles, their arrangement, their movement and the forces between them, and then applying that picture to whatever the question is about. Once a student automatically asks themselves where the particles are and what they are doing, dissolving, diffusion, changes of state, pressure, conduction and the difference between a mixture and a compound all stop being separate facts to remember and become one model applied repeatedly.

The same gap explains why students find bonding hard later. Ionic and covalent bonding are not two lists of properties to memorise; they are two consequences of what electrons do. A student who learned the properties as a list will be able to recite that ionic compounds have high melting points and will not be able to explain it, which is precisely the difference criterion A is measuring between a level 4 and a level 7. In marked work this shows up as answers that stop one sentence before the explanation starts, and a tutor's most useful intervention is to keep asking why until the student has nowhere left to go but the particles.

sections.heading: Balancing, formulae and the arithmetic that quietly eats marks
paragraphs: The second recurring failure is mechanical. MYP chemistry tasks assume that a student can write a formula, balance a symbol equation and handle ratio, and they assume it without ever assessing it directly. So a student loses criterion A marks on a question about reactions because the equation underneath was wrong, and the feedback says 'check your equation' rather than 'you cannot balance equations', which is what is actually true.

Balancing is a counting discipline, not an insight. The students who find it hard are almost always the ones who try to do it in their heads, and the fix is to write the tally of each element on both sides, every time, until the tally becomes unnecessary. Twenty minutes a session for three weeks moves nearly everyone. Formulae of common ions are the same kind of problem: learned from a list they evaporate, learned by writing twenty compound formulae a week they stay.

Then there is the arithmetic. Conservation of mass questions, percentage composition, concentration and, in schools that introduce amount of substance in MYP 4 or 5, mole calculations all rest on ratio, proportion, percentages and standard form. Those are mathematics skills being marked inside a chemistry grade. It is worth checking your child's mathematics criterion levels alongside the Sciences ones before concluding that chemistry is the problem, because quite often the chemistry is fine and the ratio work is not. The table below lists the calculations that recur in Abu Dhabi MYP chemistry tasks, what each task is really testing, and the error we see most.

sections.heading: Criterion C in chemistry: the table, the anomaly and the word evaluate
paragraphs: Criterion C, processing and evaluating, is where Abu Dhabi chemistry students lose the most ground and where the fewest hours are usually spent. It asks the student to process their raw data, present it correctly, interpret it against the hypothesis and evaluate the method. Four separate skills, one level out of eight, and students frequently do the first and skip the fourth.

Presentation is where it starts going wrong. A chemistry results table needs the independent variable in the first column, the dependent variable in the next, units in the headings rather than scattered through the cells, repeats shown and a mean calculated where repeats exist. Tables that break those conventions are not penalised for untidiness; they are penalised because they cannot be interpreted, and interpretation is the next strand of the same criterion. Graphs follow the same logic: an axis scaled to use the paper, points plotted accurately, a line of best fit where the relationship is continuous and a bar chart where the variable is categoric.

The anomaly is the moment that separates levels. A student who deletes an odd result has lost marks. A student who keeps it, marks it as anomalous, excludes it from the mean and says why they think it happened has gained them. Teaching that takes one session and one real data set with a genuinely odd point in it, and it is one of the few interventions that reliably moves a level immediately.

Evaluation is the strand that students write worst, because nobody has told them what it means. 'Evaluate' asks for a judgement about the method's reliability with reasons, not an apology. The sentence 'there may have been human error' earns nothing. The sentence 'the thermometer was read to the nearest degree, which is a significant fraction of the temperature change measured, so small differences between runs cannot be distinguished' earns a great deal. Getting a thirteen-year-old from the first to the second is a question-led process: what did you measure, how precisely, and was that precise enough to answer the question you asked?

sections.heading: Criterion D and the UAE context most schools leave on the table
paragraphs: Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, asks the student to apply science to address a specific problem, discuss the implications of using science to solve it, and use scientific language accurately. It is a writing task inside a science grade, and it is the criterion most often left half-finished by students who are perfectly good at chemistry.

The usual failure is abstraction. A student asked about the implications of a chemical process writes two sentences about pollution being bad. A level 7 response names a specific application, names a specific consequence, and distinguishes between the moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural and environmental factors involved rather than blending them into one word. The difference is not opinion quality. It is specificity, and specificity is teachable in a few sessions if the student has a real context to work in.

Abu Dhabi students have better contexts available to them than almost anyone writing this criterion, and most never use them. Water in this emirate is largely desalinated, which is a chemistry problem with an energy cost, a brine disposal question and a direct economic dimension. Carbon capture has been operating industrially in the UAE. The petrochemical sector is local rather than theoretical. Plastics, recycling and air quality are all documentable here with real local figures rather than general claims. A student who writes criterion D about desalination near the Corniche, with a cited source and a named trade-off, is writing something an examiner has not read forty times that week. sections.heading: Command terms: the reason a correct answer scores four
paragraphs: A great many lost chemistry marks are not chemistry mistakes at all. They are answers to a different question from the one asked. MYP tasks use command terms deliberately, and each one sets the depth of response required. A student who answers 'explain' with a description has written something true that cannot be awarded the level, because the rubric is looking for reasons and has been given facts.

The fix is mechanical and fast. Read the command term first, underline it, and decide the shape of the answer before writing a word. 'State' wants one line with no justification. 'Describe' wants the features in order. 'Explain' wants because. 'Analyse' wants the thing broken into parts with the relationships between them made clear. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement with reasons on both sides. 'Discuss' wants a balanced review before a conclusion. 'Justify' wants the reasoning for a choice already made. Five sessions of marking a student's own answers against the command term they were given will usually change their marks more than five sessions of new content.

This is also the single easiest thing for a parent to check without knowing any chemistry. Take a marked task, find the command term in each question, and read whether the answer did what the term asked. If a 'describe' question is answered in one word and an 'explain' question has no 'because' in it anywhere, you have found the problem, and it is not a chemistry problem. sections.heading: What a single fifty-minute chemistry session can honestly fix
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what they get for one hour. Here is an honest inventory. In one fifty-minute session a tutor can diagnose from a marked task which criterion strand is costing levels, and that diagnosis alone is often worth the session, because it stops a family spending a term on the wrong thing. A session can also teach balancing to the point where the student is slow but correct, repair a results table and have the student rebuild it, or get a first evaluation paragraph written that names one real limitation instead of blaming human error.

What one session cannot do is build the particle model, make criterion B planning secure or change a grade. Those take four to eight sessions each, and anyone saying otherwise is describing a transaction rather than teaching. The mismatch between what an hour can do and what families hope an hour will do is the most common source of disappointment in this market, which is why it is written down here before any money changes hands.

A productive single session has a shape. Ten minutes reading the marked work and asking the student what they thought the question wanted. Fifteen minutes on the specific mechanical failure, done by the student with the tutor prompting rather than demonstrating. Fifteen minutes applying it to a fresh question, cold. Five minutes agreeing what gets practised before next time, written down. Five minutes writing the note that goes to the parent. That last five minutes is what turns a session into evidence, and it is the part most providers skip.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in chemistry, stated plainly
paragraphs: The boundary between tutoring and malpractice is not vague in the IB, and in this market it needs saying out loud because some providers in the same search results sell completed coursework. The rule a tutor works to is simple: the student's submitted work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the chemistry, question the reasoning, point at a strand of the rubric and say that it has not been addressed, mark practice work, and discuss what a limitation means in general. A tutor may not supply text for a submission, dictate an evaluation, correct a draft into a finished state, or hand over worked answers to the task being assessed.

In practice that distinction is easiest to hold with questions. Instead of telling a student that their thermometer precision was the limitation, a tutor asks what they measured, how precisely they could read the instrument, and whether that was good enough for the differences they were trying to detect. The student arrives at the limitation themselves, writes it in their own words, and owns it in a viva or a follow-up question from their teacher. That is both the honest route and the one that produces a better level, because rubrics reward reasoning the student can defend.

The same applies to the MYP 5 Personal Project where it touches chemistry. A tutor can discuss the inquiry cycle, ask about the process journal and explain what the criteria reward. The report must be written by the student alone, and a supervisor at the school signs off on authenticity. Students should also know that their own teacher may ask them to explain any part of their submitted work on the spot. Work the student genuinely produced survives that conversation; work produced for them does not, and the consequences fall on the student rather than on whoever supplied it.

sections.heading: Where chemistry breaks between MYP 5 and the Diploma
paragraphs: The transition out of MYP chemistry is the point at which earlier gaps become expensive. Diploma chemistry assumes quantitative fluency that the MYP introduces unevenly: amount of substance, concentration, limiting reagents, energetics and equilibrium all require a student to move between units, ratios and standard form without stopping to think. A student who left MYP 5 balancing equations slowly will be doing DP 1 arithmetic repairs instead of DP 1 chemistry.

The second break is in writing. MYP criterion D rewards a discussion of impacts; DP chemistry rewards precision about mechanism and evidence. Students who were praised in the MYP for an enthusiastic criterion D paragraph are sometimes surprised to find the same register marked down later. The bridge is specificity: naming the chemical species, the condition and the consequence rather than writing about chemistry in general. That habit is best built in MYP 5, where the stakes are lower and the feedback loop is a teacher rather than an examiner.

The third is independence in practical work. MYP investigations are scaffolded to varying degrees by the school; Diploma work expects a student to design, justify and evaluate with far less support. Any criterion B weakness that was survivable at fifteen becomes a visible problem at seventeen. For an Abu Dhabi family deciding whether to buy chemistry support in MYP 5, that is the most useful frame available: you are not buying a middle-years grade, you are buying the skills that the next two years will assume are already there.

process.title: Send one marked chemistry task
process.description: Not a description of the problem, and not a report card on its own: one marked piece of chemistry with the teacher's comments on it. From that a tutor can usually name the failing strand within ten minutes, and the diagnosis will frequently contradict what the student believes is wrong.

process.title: Add the unit planner and the rubric
process.description: The MYP prescribes no chemistry content, so the planner tells a tutor what your school is assessing this term and the rubric tells them what separates a level 5 from a level 7 on it. Without both, sessions default to generic chemistry and the criterion levels do not move.

process.title: One session at no charge, on real work
process.description: A fifty-minute session with an MYP Sciences specialist at no charge, one per family, no card details taken. It runs on your child's actual task rather than a demonstration topic, and it ends with a written note naming the strand to target and what to practise first.

process.title: Pick one criterion and commit to a term
process.description: Agree in writing which criterion the term is aimed at, how many sessions, the rate in AED, whether preparation is charged and the reschedule terms. Chasing all four criteria at once is how a term produces activity and no level movement.

process.title: Review at six weeks on marked evidence
process.description: Put the week-one task next to a week-six task and compare the targeted strand. If it moved, continue. If it did not, we say so and examine why, which is sometimes the tutor, sometimes the schedule, and sometimes a mathematics problem wearing a chemistry costume.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before purchase
whyPoints.description: The first useful act is reading a marked task, not selling a package. Strong criterion A with weak criterion C needs a completely different term from the reverse, and most families arrive believing the opposite of what their evidence says. That read costs nothing and changes what gets bought.

whyPoints.title: Taught from your school's planner
whyPoints.description: Because the IB prescribes concepts rather than chemistry content, two Abu Dhabi schools can assess different chemistry in the same term. Tutors here work from your unit planner, task sheet and rubric, so the sessions follow what your child's teacher is actually marking.

whyPoints.title: The mechanical skills nobody sells
whyPoints.description: Balancing, formulae, ratio, units and standard form are unglamorous and they are where most chemistry marks go missing. We will sell you a drill block on those in preference to a tour of the periodic table, because it returns more levels per hour and the effect does not fade.

whyPoints.title: A stated academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark practice work and give feedback. They do not supply submissions or rewrite drafts into finished text, and the student is told where the line sits in the first session. In a search result that contains vendors of completed coursework, that difference is worth stating.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a non-chemist can read
whyPoints.description: A short written note after every session, practice work marked against the published rubric, and a six-week comparison on the strand being targeted. No invented scores and no dashboards. A parent can see which strand moved without knowing any chemistry.

whyPoints.title: Online by design, not as a compromise
whyPoints.description: Chemistry tutoring is document work: annotating a write-up, rebuilding a table, correcting an equation in the student's own handwriting. Doing that on a shared screen is clearer than doing it over a shoulder, and it removes travel from the hour entirely.

faqs.question: What exactly is my child's MYP chemistry work marked against?
faqs.answer: Four criteria, each out of eight, applied by your child's own school. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is inquiring and designing, criterion C is processing and evaluating, and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. The four levels are combined into the single 1-7 grade on the report using a boundary table the IB publishes in its programme documentation; your MYP coordinator can tell you which version the school applies. There is no external chemistry examination in MYP 1 to 4, so every chemistry mark your child has received was awarded inside the school.

faqs.question: Why does my son understand chemistry and still come home with a 4?
faqs.answer: Usually because his understanding is being measured by criterion A and the 4 is being dragged down by criterion C. The most common profile we see in Abu Dhabi is a student who can explain the chemistry well and who presents data in a table that cannot be read, plots a graph without units, and writes an evaluation that blames human error. The grade averages the four criteria, so strong knowledge and weak data handling produce a middling number. Ask for the criterion levels separately rather than the overall grade and the pattern usually becomes obvious immediately.

faqs.question: Is the particle model really worth spending sessions on?
faqs.answer: It is the highest-yield content purchase in MYP chemistry. Almost every criterion A answer that stops short of an explanation stops because the student has no mental picture of particles to reason from, so they describe instead. Once a student automatically asks where the particles are, how they are arranged, how they move and what holds them together, dissolving, diffusion, changes of state, pressure and bonding properties stop being separate facts and become one model used repeatedly. That shift takes a handful of sessions and changes answers across every subsequent unit.

faqs.question: At what point do MYP students start doing mole calculations?
faqs.answer: It varies by school, which is the honest answer. The IB prescribes concepts and criteria for Sciences rather than a content list, so some Abu Dhabi schools introduce amount of substance in MYP 4, some in MYP 5 and some leave it for the Diploma. Check the unit planner rather than a textbook. Where it does appear, the difficulty is almost never conceptual: it is proportional reasoning and standard form, which are mathematics skills being assessed inside a chemistry grade. Students who struggle with it usually need ratio practice, not more chemistry.

faqs.question: What should my daughter do with an anomalous result in a chemistry practical?
faqs.answer: Keep it, label it, exclude it from the mean and say what she thinks caused it. Deleting an odd value loses marks under criterion C; identifying it and reasoning about it gains them. The strand rewards interpretation and evaluation, and an anomaly is the clearest opportunity in the whole write-up to show both. This is one of the few things a tutor can teach in a single session using one real data set with a genuinely odd point in it, and it frequently moves a level straight away.

faqs.question: What does the command term evaluate actually require in a chemistry task?
faqs.answer: A judgement with reasons, not an apology. 'There may have been human error' earns nothing because it names no mechanism and no consequence. A response that says the thermometer could only be read to the nearest degree, which is a large fraction of the temperature change being measured, so differences between runs cannot be distinguished reliably, is doing what the term asks. Getting there is a question-led process: what was measured, how precisely, and was that precise enough for the question asked? Three or four sessions usually makes it a habit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry inside an interdisciplinary unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one caution. Interdisciplinary units are separately assessed against their own criteria, and the chemistry inside them is often not taught in a chemistry lesson, which is exactly why they catch students out. A tutor can teach the chemistry content, explain how the interdisciplinary criteria differ from the Sciences ones, and mark practice work. What a tutor cannot do is contribute to the submitted product, which must be the student's own. Send the task sheet and the criteria, because these units vary more between Abu Dhabi schools than any other assessment.

faqs.question: Does my child need practical equipment at home for chemistry sessions?
faqs.answer: No, and we would discourage buying any. The assessed practical work happens in your school's laboratory with the subject teacher supervising. What a tutor works on is everything around the bench: the research question, the variables, the method, the results table, the graph, the interpretation and the evaluation. All of that is paper and screen work. Where a demonstration genuinely helps, dissolving, diffusion in water and separation of a mixture can be shown with kitchen materials, but the marks live in the write-up rather than in the apparatus.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics cause the most trouble in MYP 4 and 5?
faqs.answer: In order of how often they appear in requests from this emirate: symbol equations and balancing, bonding explained rather than listed, rates of reaction where students describe the graph instead of the collisions, acids and bases where pH is memorised without the particle picture, and any quantitative work involving ratio or standard form. Notice that only two of those five are really chemistry content problems. The rest are mechanical or mathematical, which is why the fastest improvements usually come from drill rather than from revisiting a topic.

faqs.question: How is MYP chemistry different from IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: IGCSE chemistry has a published syllabus with topic codes, a defined content list and an external examination at the end. MYP chemistry has none of those: the IB sets concepts, contexts and four assessment criteria, and your school writes the units and marks the work. So an IGCSE student can be given a past paper and a syllabus checklist, while an MYP student needs their own school's unit planner. The skills overlap heavily, but a tutor who treats an MYP 5 student as an IGCSE candidate will teach content the school is not assessing.

faqs.question: What can one fifty-minute chemistry session realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: A great deal of diagnosis and one mechanical repair. In one session a tutor can read a marked task, name which criterion strand is costing levels, and teach balancing to the point of slow accuracy, or rebuild a results table with the student, or get a first real evaluation paragraph written. What one session cannot do is build the particle model, secure criterion B planning or move a grade. Those take four to eight sessions each. Saying so before payment prevents the most common disappointment in this market.

faqs.question: How much chemistry support does an MYP 5 student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: If the target is one criterion level on a specific strand, plan for four to eight sessions and a term rather than a fortnight. MYP 5 is also the most congested year in this emirate, with the Personal Project, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education, and in some schools on-screen components all competing for the same evenings, so a realistic plan is one fixed weekly session rather than two that keep getting cancelled. Families with only one term of budget get more from starting early in the term than from an intensive block before a task.

faqs.question: Is organic chemistry taught in the MYP?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, lightly, and entirely at the school's discretion. Because there is no prescribed content list, some Abu Dhabi schools introduce hydrocarbons, combustion and polymers in MYP 4 or 5 as part of a unit on fuels or materials, and others do not touch organic chemistry until the Diploma. If your child has come home with an organic topic, the planner will say how deep the school intends to go. A tutor should match that depth rather than teaching Diploma-level mechanisms to a fifteen-year-old who needs the criterion C work instead.

faqs.question: Do MYP students in Abu Dhabi study Arabic alongside chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai the KHDA guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students with specified languages of instruction. The federal rule behind this is that private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their chosen curriculum. The practical consequence for a chemistry plan is timetable pressure: those lessons and their homework occupy real evenings, so one protected weekly chemistry slot outperforms an ambitious schedule that collapses.

faqs.question: Who marks MYP chemistry, the school or the IB?
faqs.answer: Your child's school, in MYP 1 to 4 and for most of MYP 5. Teachers apply the published criterion rubrics to tasks they have written themselves, and schools run internal standardisation to keep that marking consistent. Some Abu Dhabi schools additionally enter MYP 5 candidates for the IB's on-screen components, which are externally marked, but that is a school decision rather than a requirement. This is why a tutor's job includes teaching a student to read the rubric: the person awarding the level is the person who wrote the task.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to homes in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are one to one, live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For chemistry that format is genuinely better suited to the work: a photographed write-up is annotated line by line on a shared screen, a results table is rebuilt in a spreadsheet while the student watches, and the match is made on who teaches MYP Sciences criteria well rather than on who happens to live nearby.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.closingHeading: Send one marked task and the diagnosis takes ten minutes
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to find out what your child's chemistry actually needs is to stop describing it and start showing it. Send one marked chemistry task with the teacher's comments, the current unit planner and the criterion rubric. A Sciences specialist will read all three, tell you which strand is costing levels and which is not, and run one fifty-minute session at no charge on that exact piece of work. You will finish with a written note, a named target criterion and an honest estimate of how many sessions it takes, which is usually more than a fortnight and less than a year.
