abu-dhabi/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-tu.regionsIntro: What changes between communities for an extended student is the shape of the week: how late school transport runs, how heavy the co-curricular commitment is, and whether the school's extended class is large enough to offer a second explanation.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Large schools with extended classes big enough to have more than one teacher who can cover them. The binding constraint here is co-curricular load, which routinely leaves a strong mathematician with one genuinely free evening a week. Depth work has to fit that single slot rather than being spread thinly.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment households where a student doing dense algebraic writing needs a surface and quiet more than anything else. Families here often find a Saturday morning works far better than a weekday evening, because extended work requires attention rather than time.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Buses from island schools arriving after half past four leave a tired student facing the hardest subject on their timetable. The practical answer for extended work is a later start and a shorter session, because ninety minutes of quadratics at five o'clock produces less than fifty minutes at seven.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A dense IB population where extended cohorts are sizeable and competitive. Students here compare levels with each other constantly, which can be useful pressure and can also convince a perfectly strong student that a 5 in criterion B means they do not belong on the route.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established schools with experienced mathematics departments, and mixed-curriculum streets where extended students sit alongside IGCSE Higher tier friends. Explaining why an IGCSE-style answer scores badly against criterion B is often the most useful first conversation here.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer cohorts where the extended class may be small and taught by one specialist. That is excellent for a student who follows that teacher's approach and difficult for one who does not, because there is no alternative explanation available inside the school.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland households with long commutes and several children. An extended student here is often doing their hardest thinking at the end of the longest day, which argues for fewer, better-protected sessions rather than a weekly hour squeezed between school runs.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: The local supply of tutors who have taught both extended mathematics and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is thin, and a driving radius would exclude most of the people who have. Matching online is what makes the right specialist available at all out here.

modes.title: Depth on one of the four extended topics
modes.description: A bounded block on quadratics, non-right-angled trigonometry, transformations or conditional probability, taught until the student can choose a method and justify the choice. modes.description: The slowest and highest-value work on the route. Sessions take an extended pattern task, require a general rule, and then refuse to accept it until the student has written an argument for why it holds. Six to eight sessions, with the student attempting a fresh task between each one.

sections.heading: What changes at the start of extended mathematics
paragraphs: The honest answer to why extended is harder is that it asks for a different intellectual act. Standard mathematics, at its top band, rewards selecting a correct procedure and executing it accurately in an unfamiliar context. Extended keeps that and adds judgement: rearranging to reveal something hidden, choosing between two valid methods and defending the choice, noticing that a solution set has two members and that one of them is nonsense in context.

Fluency does not produce judgement. This is the reason a student with straight 7s in MYP 3 can drop two criterion levels in a term without becoming worse at mathematics. Everything they were rewarded for previously still works and is no longer sufficient. Nobody tells them that, because from inside a classroom it looks like the same subject with harder numbers, and so the student concludes they have become less capable. That conclusion does more damage in Abu Dhabi's comparison-heavy school communities than the mathematics itself.

The practical consequence for teaching is that the first intervention is rarely content. It is making the new demand explicit: here is what the top band is asking for, here is what you are currently doing, and these are not the same move. Students respond to that well, because it reframes the drop as a change in the rules rather than a verdict on them. A session that achieves nothing except that reframing is frequently the most valuable one in a block.
bullets: Extended adds judgement to fluency rather than adding difficulty to it
A levels drop in MYP 4 usually signals a change of demand, not a loss of ability
The first useful intervention is naming the new demand explicitly
More practice on familiar exercises does not move an extended level

sections.heading: The four extended topics where levels actually go
paragraphs: Four content areas separate extended from standard, and in practice almost every lost criterion A level on this route traces back to one of them being held shallowly. Shallow here has a precise meaning: the student can execute the method when told which method to use, and cannot select it or adapt it.

Quadratics is the largest. A student who has learned completing the square as a sequence of steps cannot use it to locate a vertex or to show that an expression is always positive, which is what it is for. The sine and cosine rules are second, and the specific failure is the ambiguous case: a sine rule calculation returning one angle when two are geometrically possible. A student who never checks for the second solution will lose that mark every time it appears, and it appears regularly.

Transformations are third, and the failure is order of application rather than the transformations themselves. Students apply them in the order they are written rather than the order in which they act, and produce a confident, wrong graph. Conditional probability is fourth and the arithmetic is usually fine; the losses are in interpretation, where a correctly computed conditional probability is then described as something it is not. Each of these is a four-to-six session block and each one, once properly held, stops costing marks for the rest of the student's school career.

Worth saying what shallow is not: it is not carelessness, and telling a student to be more careful will not touch it. A student who executes completing the square flawlessly when instructed to and never reaches for it unprompted has a representation problem, not an attention problem. The teaching that fixes it uses the technique for something — a vertex, a positivity argument, an optimisation — until the method and its purpose are stored together rather than separately.

sections.heading: Criterion B on extended: what an argument looks like
paragraphs: Criterion B asks a student to investigate a pattern, express a general rule, verify it and justify why it holds. On the extended route the expectation for that last step rises to something close to a short proof. This is the single largest gap between what extended students know and what they are awarded, and it is almost never about content.

What a justification is not: a table of three cases that the rule fits. That is verification, which is a lower band, and students produce it because it feels like evidence. What a justification is: an explanation grounded in the structure of the situation. If the number of diagonals in a polygon is given by a certain expression, the argument explains why each vertex connects to a certain number of others and why the result must be halved. That reasoning is available to any extended student. It is simply not what they have been asked for before.

Teaching it is slow because it cannot be demonstrated into someone. The method is to require the argument in the student's own words, refuse the first three attempts because they describe rather than explain, and keep asking why until the structural reason surfaces. Students find this frustrating for two sessions and then it clicks, usually visibly. Six to eight sessions is a realistic block, and the level movement that follows is often two bands rather than one, because the student has acquired a move rather than a fact.

sections.heading: Criterion A under unfamiliarity, which is the extended trap
paragraphs: Criterion A rewards applying mathematics accurately in familiar and unfamiliar situations, and on the extended route the unfamiliar half carries most of the weight. That has a consequence families rarely anticipate: a student can complete every exercise in the textbook correctly and still sit in the middle bands, because the tasks they practised were all familiar.

Unfamiliar in practice means multi-step, differently framed, or requiring a tool from one topic to be used inside another. A question that asks for the maximum area of a rectangle with a fixed perimeter is a quadratics question wearing a geometry coat. A student who has studied quadratics in a quadratics chapter will not recognise it. Nothing about that is a knowledge gap, and nothing about it is fixed by more quadratics exercises.

What fixes it is practice on altered question stems: the same mathematics approached from a direction the student has not seen, with the recognition step left to them. This is a specific kind of material and it is why past papers are a blunt instrument for this problem — a paper gives a student the usual framings, in the usual proportions, and the recognition work happens only by accident. A tutor's useful contribution is deliberately selecting or constructing questions that hide the topic, and then marking the recognition rather than the arithmetic.

There is one more reason this matters in an Abu Dhabi context specifically. Several schools here run small extended classes taught by one senior mathematician, and a single teacher inevitably has characteristic framings. A student who meets a topic only in that teacher's preferred presentation has a narrower sense of what the topic looks like than a student in a four-teacher department, through nobody's fault. Deliberately varied framings from outside the school are therefore worth more here than they would be elsewhere.

sections.heading: Telling 'behind' apart from 'wrong route'
paragraphs: Two very different students arrive at the same symptom, which is falling criterion levels on extended in MYP 4. One is behind: the content is insecure, usually in one of the four extended areas, and a bounded block repairs it. The other was placed on the basis of fluency, has no particular appetite for algebraic argument, and would be reaching the top bands on standard. Treating the second as the first produces a year of expensive, unhappy sessions.

The distinction is diagnosable from one carefully chosen task plus a conversation, and the table below sets out the evidence. The central question is not whether the student can do the mathematics but what happens when they meet something they cannot immediately do. A student who is behind but belongs on the route will engage with the obstacle, try something, and be interested when the structure is explained. A student on the wrong route will wait to be told the method, because that is what mathematics has always been for them, and will be untroubled rather than curious when the reasoning is shown.

Neither answer is a verdict on the child. Thriving on standard and reaching a 7 there is a better outcome in every respect than a 4 on extended, including for Diploma purposes, since a strong standard profile supports Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level perfectly well. The school makes the decision, not a tutor, but a written criterion-by-criterion read is exactly the evidence a head of mathematics will want to see, and families who bring it get a better conversation than families who bring a worry.

sections.heading: What extended mathematics is preparing for, concretely
paragraphs: Extended exists to make Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level possible without heroics two years later, and the mapping between the two is tighter than most students realise. Knowing it changes how extended work gets prioritised, because some extended topics are load-bearing for the Diploma and others are not.

Algebraic rearrangement is the most load-bearing of all. Higher Level work in calculus, in sequences and in functions assumes that manipulating an expression is free, in the sense of costing no attention. A student for whom rearrangement is effortful will spend their attention there and have none left for the actual idea. The same is true of function behaviour: Higher Level asks what happens to a graph under a transformation almost as an aside, and a student who has to reconstruct the rules each time is at a permanent disadvantage.

The table sets out which Diploma topics rest on which extended foundations and what the symptom is when the foundation was shallow. The practical use of it in MYP 5 is prioritisation: if a student has a limited number of sessions available, spending them on rearrangement and function behaviour buys more Diploma readiness than spending them on, say, cumulative frequency. The exploration is worth a mention here too, because the judgement criterion B is building is precisely what the exploration's personal engagement and use-of-mathematics criteria reward.

The exploration point deserves one more line, because it is where extended work pays off most visibly. A student who has spent MYP 5 being made to justify general rules arrives at the Diploma exploration already able to say why their mathematics is appropriate to their question, which is precisely what the personal engagement and use-of-mathematics criteria reward. A student who has only ever executed methods arrives with a technically clean piece of work that sits in the middle bands.

sections.heading: What an extended student should stop doing
paragraphs: A page about tutoring usually lists things to start. On this route the things to stop matter more, because an extended student in MYP 5 has very little spare time and most of what they currently do with it is low-yield.

Stop working through past papers as a default activity. Papers are a diagnostic instrument and a timing instrument, and they are poor teaching material, because they present topics in their usual framings and reward recognition the student already has. Two papers marked properly against the criteria are worth more than ten papers completed and self-checked against an answer key. Stop, also, racing ahead into Diploma content. A student who has read about differentiation but cannot rearrange an expression fluently has bought nothing, and the appearance of being ahead discourages the depth work that would actually help.

Stop doing more of what already works. The instinct, in a student and in a parent, is to practise the topic that feels productive, which is by definition the secure one. And stop treating length of study as a measure of effort: ninety minutes of exercises at the end of a long school day in Khalifa City produces less than fifty focused minutes at seven o'clock. What to start instead is short and specific: disguised questions, written arguments, and one extended topic taken to real depth at a time.

One caveat so this does not read as an argument for doing less. The point is not reduced effort; it is redirected effort. A student who stops doing three past papers a week and starts writing two structural arguments and six disguised questions is working just as hard and getting a different result. Families sometimes hear stop as permission to relax, and extended mathematics in MYP 5 is not a place where relaxing produces anything useful.

sections.heading: Building a sustainable week around the hardest subject on the timetable
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is usually the most cognitively expensive subject an MYP 4 or 5 student takes, and it sits in a week that in Abu Dhabi is often extremely full: long bus journeys, competitive sport, music, service commitments, and mandatory UAE subjects alongside the international curriculum. Planning the week badly is the commonest reason good intentions produce no movement.

Three rules hold up in practice. Put extended mathematics where the attention is, not where the gap in the diary is: a protected slot at seven in the evening beats an unprotected one at half past four. Keep sessions shorter and more frequent during a heavy term rather than longer and weekly, because depth work degrades badly with fatigue. And protect the work between sessions, which is where the learning actually consolidates; a student who does nothing between sessions is buying a weekly demonstration.

Ramadan deserves specific planning rather than improvisation. Lessons shift comfortably to after Iftar, which online delivery makes straightforward because nobody is driving across the emirate after a long fast. Many families find the month suits depth work well, since the late evening is quiet and uninterrupted. Tell us before the month begins rather than during it so the slot is rebooked rather than cancelled, and expect the fortnight either side to be lighter rather than pretending otherwise.

The mandatory UAE subjects are part of this arithmetic rather than a footnote to it. The federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, so those lessons occupy timetable hours and sometimes homework hours too. A week planned as though extended mathematics were the only demanding thing in it will not survive contact with a real Abu Dhabi term.

sections.heading: Honesty, the regulator and who you should not pay
paragraphs: Three checkable things, because an extended student's work is exactly the kind that someone will offer to do for them. MYP tasks and the Personal Project have to be the student's own. A tutor's role is to teach, question and give feedback on work the student has produced, and criterion B in particular is worthless if the argument is not in the student's words, because the whole point of it is that the student can reason. Anyone offering to supply the reasoning is selling a problem.

On the regulator: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government's portal describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes an inspection record per school. Separately, press reporting describes ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE private tuition permit carrying a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Verify that wording against ADEK's current policy document. The implication for extended mathematics is practical: in a school with one extended teacher, that teacher is the person you most want and the person you should not pay.

On the permit: private tutoring in the UAE is governed by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The government portal records the permit as granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted. IB Gram holds no accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and runs no premises in the UAE.

process.title: Send a marked piece of work, not a description
process.description: One marked extended task tells a tutor more than a term of verbal updates. Add the four criterion levels and the MYP year. From that it is usually possible to say which of the four extended topics is shallow and whether the problem is content or judgement, before any teaching happens.

process.title: A free first lesson built around an unfamiliar question
process.description: The diagnostic is deliberately a question your child has not seen framed that way. What matters is not whether they solve it but what they do when they cannot start. That reaction is the most reliable signal available about whether the route fits and where the gap sits.

process.title: One extended topic at a time, to real depth
process.description: Blocks are built around a single topic taken until the student can select the method and defend the selection. Covering four topics shallowly in six sessions is the standard mistake; it feels thorough and changes nothing. The block ends when the topic survives being asked backwards.

process.title: Re-mark the same criterion after four sessions
process.description: A fresh task of the same style, marked against the same descriptor, is the measurement. On criterion B expect movement after four sessions and two frustrating ones before that. A level that has not moved means the diagnosis was wrong, which is useful information rather than a reason to buy more hours.

process.title: Say so if the route is the problem
process.description: Where the evidence points to a student who would reach the top bands on standard rather than the middle on extended, we will write that down and you can take it to the head of mathematics. The school decides. A tutor who never reaches that conclusion for any student is not reading the evidence.

whyPoints.title: The four extended topics are named and diagnosed
whyPoints.description: Quadratics held as a ritual, the unchecked ambiguous case, transformations applied in the wrong order, conditional probability computed and then misdescribed. Almost every lost criterion A level on this route is one of those four, and knowing which saves a term of general revision.

whyPoints.title: Criterion B taught as argument, not as practice
whyPoints.description: The gap between what extended students know and what they are awarded sits in justification. Sessions require the argument in the student's own words and refuse descriptions, which is slow, unpopular for a fortnight, and the only thing that moves the level.

whyPoints.title: A written test for the route question
whyPoints.description: Falling levels on extended can mean insecure content or an ill-fitting route, and the two need opposite responses. We diagnose which, in writing, and will recommend a move back to standard where the evidence supports it rather than selling a year of sessions into the wrong problem.

whyPoints.title: Prioritised by what the Diploma actually needs
whyPoints.description: Algebraic rearrangement and function behaviour are load-bearing for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; some other extended topics are not. With a limited number of sessions, that ordering is worth more than coverage.

whyPoints.title: We tell students what to stop doing
whyPoints.description: Past papers as a default activity, reading ahead into Diploma content, and practising the secure topic all feel productive and move nothing. An extended student in MYP 5 has very little spare time and most advice they receive spends it badly.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: One-to-one lessons online on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around a full week and shifted after Iftar during Ramadan. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and the pool of tutors who have taught both extended mathematics and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is too small to filter by driving distance.

faqs.question: My son was placed on extended and his criterion levels have fallen. Should he move back?
faqs.answer: Not on that evidence alone, because two very different situations produce the same symptom. He may be behind on one of the four extended content areas, which a bounded block repairs. Or he may have been placed on fluency and lack appetite for algebraic argument, in which case he would reach the top bands on standard. The distinguishing signal is what he does when he meets a problem he cannot start: trying something and asking about structure points one way, waiting to be told the method points the other. Get a written criterion-by-criterion read before anyone decides.

faqs.question: What exactly makes extended mathematics harder than standard?
faqs.answer: It asks for a different act rather than a harder version of the same one. Standard, at its top band, rewards selecting a correct procedure and executing it accurately in an unfamiliar context. Extended keeps that and adds judgement: rearranging an expression to reveal information, choosing between two valid methods and defending the choice, noticing that an equation has two solutions and that one does not fit the situation. Fluency does not produce judgement, which is why a student with straight 7s in MYP 3 can lose two levels in a term without having become worse at mathematics.

faqs.question: Which extended topic causes the most lost levels?
faqs.answer: Quadratics, by a clear margin, and specifically completing the square. Students learn it as a sequence of steps and then cannot use the completed form to locate a vertex or show that an expression is always positive, which is what the technique exists for. The sine and cosine rules come second, almost entirely because of the ambiguous case. Transformations are third, where the error is applying them in the order written rather than the order they act. Conditional probability is fourth, and there the arithmetic is usually right and the interpreting sentence wrong.

faqs.question: Is the ambiguous case of the sine rule really examined at this level?
faqs.answer: It appears often enough that not checking for it is a recurring, silent loss of criterion A marks. The situation is a sine rule calculation where the angle returned by a calculator is one of two geometrically possible answers, and the question's context determines which. Students who have been taught the rule as a formula will take the first answer and move on. The fix is a habit rather than knowledge: after any sine rule angle, ask whether a second solution exists and whether the triangle permits it. That takes one session to install and pays for several years.

faqs.question: Does the extended route lead automatically to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No. It is the route built to make that course comfortable, which is a different claim. What determines whether Higher Level is sensible is how securely the extended content is held, particularly algebraic rearrangement and function behaviour, plus the school's own entry criteria and the student's appetite. A student who has covered extended but holds rearrangement effortfully will spend their attention on algebra in a calculus lesson and have none left for the calculus. Schools also set their own thresholds, so the Diploma coordinator is the person to ask about requirements rather than any provider.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my daughter is behind or simply misplaced on this route?
faqs.answer: Watch two things rather than her marks. First, what she does with a problem she cannot start: engagement with the structure, even irritated engagement, points to a student who belongs on the route and needs content repair. Waiting to be told the method points the other way. Second, her reaction to a structural explanation: visible interest and a wish to test it is appetite, and appetite is what extended requires. A high criterion A with a persistently low criterion B across several tasks is the clearest profile suggesting standard would suit her better.

faqs.question: He scores 7s on criterion A and 4s on criterion B. What is going on?
faqs.answer: He has excellent procedural command and has never been asked to justify anything, which is an extremely common extended profile and a very fixable one. Criterion B wants a general rule and then an argument for why it must hold; he is almost certainly producing the rule and verifying it on a few cases, which is a middle band by design. The work is six to eight sessions of being required to write the structural reason in his own words, with the first three attempts refused because they describe rather than explain. Expect two frustrating sessions, then visible movement.

faqs.question: Should an extended student be working through past papers?
faqs.answer: Sparingly, and for the right purpose. Papers are good diagnostic and timing instruments and poor teaching material, because they present topics in their usual framings and so test recognition the student already has. Two papers marked properly against the four criteria, with the marks attributed to a criterion rather than to a question number, are worth more than ten papers self-checked against an answer key. The material that actually moves extended criterion A is deliberately disguised questions, where a quadratics problem arrives wearing a geometry coat and the recognition work is left to the student.

faqs.question: Is it better to cover everything or go deep on fewer topics?
faqs.answer: Deep, almost always, and the choice is not close on this route. Covering four extended topics shallowly in six sessions feels thorough and changes nothing, because shallow means the student can execute a method when told which to use and cannot select it. One topic taken until it survives being asked backwards stops costing marks permanently. With a limited number of sessions, the ordering that buys most is algebraic rearrangement first, then function behaviour, because those two are load-bearing for everything in the Diploma that follows.

faqs.question: How much mathematics should an extended MYP 5 student be doing each week?
faqs.answer: Less than most are doing, and better. Extended mathematics is usually the most cognitively expensive subject on the timetable, and an Abu Dhabi week is often already full of long bus journeys, sport, music and mandatory UAE subjects. Fifty focused minutes at seven in the evening produces more than ninety tired ones straight off a bus at half past four. Shorter and more frequent beats longer and weekly during a heavy term. The non-negotiable part is work between sessions, because that is where consolidation happens rather than in the session itself.

faqs.question: What does proof mean at MYP level?
faqs.answer: Something more modest than a university proof and considerably more than a demonstration. It means an explanation grounded in the structure of the situation rather than in examples. If a general rule describes the number of connections between points, the argument says why each point connects to a particular number of others and why the total must then be halved. No formal notation is required. What is required is that the reasoning explains rather than illustrates, and that it is written in the student's own words, since the entire purpose of criterion B is to evidence that the student can reason.

faqs.question: She understands it in the session and cannot do it alone the next day. Why?
faqs.answer: Because following an explanation and generating one are different skills, and a session that consists of watching good mathematics being done trains the first. The remedy is structural: the student should hold the pen for most of the session, attempt before being shown, and be asked to explain the step back. It also matters that something is attempted alone within a day, while the structure is still fresh, rather than at the weekend. If a session is largely the tutor talking and the student nodding, this symptom is guaranteed and it is the tutor's problem rather than hers.

faqs.question: Does extended mathematics help with Physics and Chemistry as well?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it is an underrated argument for taking the depth seriously. Rearranging a formula, handling indices, reading a gradient as a rate of change and interpreting a non-linear graph are all extended skills that appear constantly in MYP and Diploma sciences. Students who find Physics hard frequently have a mathematics problem wearing a Physics label: the concept is understood and the algebra consumes the attention. Fixing rearrangement properly in MYP 4 tends to show up in science grades within a term, which families notice before they notice it in mathematics.

faqs.question: Can a student move onto extended at the start of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the school's timetable as much as on the student. Larger Abu Dhabi departments with full classes on both routes often review at the end of MYP 4; smaller ones may not be able to move anyone. Ask the head of mathematics what the review process is and what evidence it requires. The realistic catch-up is concentrated on the four extended areas and amounts to a bounded block rather than a year. Bring a written criterion-by-criterion read to that conversation, because evidence gets a better hearing than a request.

faqs.question: How do extended sessions work during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move, usually to after Iftar, and the month often suits depth work well because the late evening is quiet and uninterrupted. Online delivery is what makes the shift painless: nobody is driving across the emirate after a long fast, so a nine or ten o'clock slot costs no more than an afternoon one. Plan it before the month starts rather than during it, so the slot is rebooked rather than cancelled, and expect the few days either side to be lighter. Families who schedule the month deliberately tend to lose nothing from it at all.

faqs.question: Who at the school should we ask about the extended route, and who should we not pay?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of mathematics about the route and the review process, and the Diploma coordinator about entry requirements for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Do not pay your child's own mathematics teacher. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on private and charter school staff providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Verify that against ADEK's current policy. In a school with one extended teacher, that is the person you most want and must not pay.

It ends in a written read: which extended topic is shallow, whether the problem is content or judgement, and whether the route fits. Lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time, for families from Saadiyat Island and Al Reem to Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas Island and the mainland.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-french-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are tutors who teach MYP French as Language Acquisition rather than conversational French. Each one works to the four published criteria, marks written and spoken tasks the way a school department does, and can tell you after one lesson which phase your child is realistically working in.

intro.heading: What an hour of MYP French costs in Abu Dhabi, and why the quotes differ so much
paragraphs: Ask three providers in Abu Dhabi what MYP French costs and you will get three numbers between AED 50 and AED 650 an hour. Nothing about the subject explains that spread. The spread exists because the word tutor covers a university student revising vocabulary lists, a qualified languages teacher who marks to the MYP criteria, and an agency charging a premium for a named specialist. Parents are quoted a price before anyone has established which of those three the child actually needs, which is why the number feels arbitrary.

The deciding variable is phase. MYP Language Acquisition runs across six phases, and a French learner in Phase 1 and a French learner in Phase 5 are doing different subjects wearing the same name. Phase 1 work is about recognising and producing short, familiar language with heavy support. Phase 5 work asks a student to interpret unfamiliar text, infer meaning, and write at length for a defined audience and purpose. The first can be taught well by a strong generalist. The second needs someone who has marked the criteria and knows where a level 6 answer stops short of a level 7.

Published rates in this market cluster into recognisable bands. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both online and both at the entry end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market figures from the providers themselves, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Abu Dhabi adds its own arithmetic. The emirate's private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and enrolment is spread between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and newer mainland communities such as Al Shamkha and Al Falah. A tutor driving from Al Reem Island to Khalifa City in the 4pm window is committing closer to ninety minutes than sixty, and someone pays for that time. Online delivery removes the drive from the invoice, which is the single largest controllable line in an in-home quote.

What follows is the honest version. A rate table with sources. The five variables that move your quote up or down. What marking a written task against criterion C actually involves, so you can judge whether the hour is worth the money. The MYP five-year budget counted backwards from the final year rather than forwards from today. And a plain statement of how IB Gram delivers: one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, with one free trial lesson before anything is paid and no card details taken to book it.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-french-tutor.programmesIntro: French appears in three IB programmes and each one prices support differently, because each one assesses something different. A parent looking for MYP help is usually one or two years away from the Diploma decision, so the programme map below is worth reading as a budget sequence rather than a brochure.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: French in the PYP is an additional language taught through inquiry units rather than a graded subject with external criteria. There is no phase label and no criterion marking, so support here is about building listening confidence and a working vocabulary. Sessions are short, oral-heavy and cheap by comparison, because the tutor is not marking anything. Families who start French support in Year 5 or 6 generally pay the lowest hourly rate they will ever pay for the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a large French-speaking expatriate community served by French-curriculum schools such as Lycee Louis Massignon alongside the IB and British sector. Children arriving into an Abu Dhabi IB school from a French-medium background often need the opposite of tutoring in French - they need English support - and a good first lesson establishes which of the two is actually the problem.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: This is the programme in the URL. French sits inside Language Acquisition, assessed against four criteria worth 8 marks each: comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating in response to text, and using language in spoken and written form. Each criterion is marked on a published descriptor band and converted to a 1-7 subject grade by the school. Pricing rises with phase because criterion D at Phase 5 demands accuracy a generalist tutor cannot reliably assess.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP schools place students into phases on arrival, and a mid-year transfer from a British or Indian curriculum school often lands in a phase that flatters or punishes them. Families in the Khalifa City and Raha corridor move schools more often than island families do, so phase misplacement is a recurring reason Abu Dhabi parents book French support in the first term rather than the third.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: French in the Diploma is taken as Language B at SL or HL, or as Language ab initio at SL for near-beginners. The phase a student leaves MYP in effectively decides which of those three doors is open, and ab initio is closed to anyone with meaningful prior study. Diploma-level French support costs more per hour than MYP support in every published rate table, which is the practical argument for spending money in MYP 4 and 5 rather than DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are small, and a school may run French B SL in a class of six or not at all in a given year. When a school cannot timetable the level a student needs, families either change the subject choice or arrange outside support - and the cost of that decision is set two years earlier, by the phase the student reached in MYP.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a language development component. French can sit inside that language development strand, which is assessed through a portfolio rather than an examination. Support is cheaper per hour than Diploma Language B because the evidence requirement is lighter, but it still needs a tutor who understands portfolio evidence rather than one who teaches conversation.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Abu Dhabi schools run the Career-related Programme, so most families reading this page will not need it. It is included because parents comparing quotes are sometimes offered a CP language rate by a provider that has not checked which programme the child is in, and the difference is large enough to notice.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-french-tutor.subjectsIntro: A French booking rarely stays a French booking. Families in Abu Dhabi commonly add a second subject within a term, and the rate you are quoted for French tells you very little about what the second subject will cost. The grid below sets out the MYP subjects most often paired with French and what each one is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: French - Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four criteria at 8 marks each. Phases 1-2 reward recognition and short production; Phases 4-6 demand inference from unfamiliar text and sustained writing for a stated audience. The commonest hidden problem is a student placed a phase above their real level, scoring 3s on criterion D and losing confidence.

subjects.name: Spanish - Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Same four criteria, same phase structure, different interference patterns. Students who take French and Spanish together confuse verb endings before they confuse vocabulary, and a tutor who teaches both can separate the two faster than two tutors working independently.

subjects.name: English - Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed on analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Marks are lost on criterion A when a student retells a text instead of analysing how it works. A French learner with weak English analysis usually has one writing problem, not two language problems.

subjects.name: Arabic - Language Acquisition or first language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. Families budgeting for French often forget Arabic is also being graded, and the two together are the most common double booking in Abu Dhabi.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The written tasks look like history essays but are marked on process evidence as much as content, which catches out students who write well and plan nothing.

subjects.name: Mathematics - Standard and Extended
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, applying maths in real-life contexts. The investigating patterns criterion is where marks go missing, because students find the pattern and never justify the general rule.

subjects.name: Sciences - Biology, Chemistry, Physics
subjects.description: Four criteria including inquiring and designing, and processing and evaluating. Lab reports lose marks on the evaluation strand far more often than on the practical work itself, which is the opposite of what most students assume.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. A design cycle folder is the assessment, and students who build a strong product and document it thinly score lower than students who do the reverse.

subjects.name: Arts - visual and performing
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. The process journal carries the marks, and a French student doing a francophone arts unit can reuse research across both subjects if the referencing is handled properly.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Investigating, planning, taking action, reflecting, evidenced through a process journal and a report. It runs in the same year as the heaviest French assessment for most Abu Dhabi students, which is why MYP 5 is the year families most often need two bookings at once.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-french-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live in Abu Dhabi changes an in-home quote and changes nothing about an online one. That difference is worth a few hundred dirhams a month in the 4pm to 6pm window, so the notes below are written around travel and timetable rather than scenery.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense towers, a short bridge to the island and a long queue onto it at 4pm. In-home tutors quote Al Reem at the higher end of their band because one session can swallow an afternoon. Online slots here fill earliest at 4.30pm.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding Raha International School and the Al Yasmina and Yasmina cluster. Families here are the most frequent movers between schools in the emirate, which makes first-term phase checks more common than elsewhere.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A compact corridor with a predictable school run, so in-home rates are nearer the middle of the band. A 5pm start is realistic here, where it is optimistic on the island.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Low-density housing and a long single approach road. Travel time is the whole premium in an in-home quote here, and it does not buy any additional teaching.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods close to several long-standing private schools. Tutor supply is better here than anywhere else in the emirate, which pushes in-home rates down and makes evening slots easier to find.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer family housing with a growing school cluster. Session timing is dictated by the bridge rather than by distance, and families often prefer a 6.30pm start after traffic has cleared.

regions.note: Mainland communities with longer commutes to island schools. In-home coverage thins out markedly here, and this is where the gap between an advertised rate and an achievable one is widest.

sections.heading: The five variables that move your quote
paragraphs: Two Abu Dhabi families can be quoted AED 180 and AED 420 for what sounds like the same hour of MYP French. The difference is almost never negotiation. It is five identifiable variables, and four of them are inside your control.

Phase is the largest. A Phase 1 or 2 learner needs vocabulary building, sentence patterns and oral confidence, which a strong generalist languages teacher delivers well. A Phase 5 or 6 learner needs someone who can read a criterion C descriptor and say precisely why a piece of writing sits at level 5 rather than level 7. That second skill is scarcer and priced accordingly. Paying specialist rates for Phase 2 work buys nothing; paying generalist rates for Phase 5 work buys a pleasant hour and no grade movement.

Session length is the variable families get wrong most often. A 90-minute session sold as better value is worse value for a twelve-year-old in Phase 2, whose useful attention on unfamiliar French runs out well before the end. Timing in the year matters too: demand concentrates in the three weeks before a reporting window, and that is when availability tightens and premium tiers get booked. Format is the last lever - two siblings in adjacent phases sharing a tutor, or French and Spanish with one person, cuts the total without cutting the teaching.

The fifth variable is the one nobody mentions in a quote: travel. An in-home tutor crossing from Al Bateen to Al Shamkha at 4pm is paid for the drive whether the invoice itemises it or not. Removing that line is why online delivery sits lower in every published rate table in this market, and it is the reason an Abu Dhabi family can reach a specialist tier at a generalist price.

sections.heading: The four criteria your money is actually buying time against
paragraphs: MYP Language Acquisition is marked against four criteria, each out of 8, and the school converts the profile into a 1-7 subject grade using published boundaries. Criterion A covers comprehending spoken and visual text. Criterion B covers comprehending written and visual text. Criterion C covers communicating in response to spoken, written and visual text. Criterion D covers using language in spoken and written form. A parent who knows which of those four is weak can buy ten hours of useful support. A parent who does not buys ten hours of general French.

In practice, Abu Dhabi MYP reports cluster failure in two places. Criterion B marks drop when a student can decode every word in a text and still cannot infer what the writer wants the reader to conclude - a reading-strategy problem dressed as a vocabulary problem. Criterion D marks drop when a student has the ideas and loses them to tense agreement, gender and register, which is an accuracy problem that responds to drilling rather than discussion.

That distinction decides the shape of a session and therefore the cost of a term. A criterion B weakness is fixed with short unfamiliar texts and a repeated inference routine, which works at 45 minutes a week over a term. A criterion D weakness needs frequent, small, corrected production - more like three short pieces a week marked in detail than one long conversation. The second is more tutor hours of marking and less tutor hours of talking, and a provider who prices only talking time will quietly do less of it.

Ask any prospective tutor one question before you pay: which criterion are we working on first, and what will the evidence of movement be? A tutor who answers with a criterion letter and a named task is worth the upper band. A tutor who answers that they will build confidence is worth the lower one.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home French tutor in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Parents searching for a French tutor in Abu Dhabi usually start by looking for someone to come to the villa, and that is a reasonable instinct. It is worth pricing honestly. An in-home one-to-one visit in this market runs AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on tier, against AED 150 to 300 for the equivalent online, and monthly in-home packages advertised in the Dubai market reach AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against about AED 799 for eight online sessions.

The gap is travel, and travel is worse in Abu Dhabi than the map suggests. The 4pm to 6pm window is when every school run in the emirate happens at once, and the bridges onto Al Reem, Saadiyat and Yas are the choke points. A tutor who lives on the island and teaches in Al Shamkha can reasonably take an hour each way. Either the family pays for that time, or the tutor declines the booking - which is why in-home coverage thins out sharply in the mainland communities where new family housing has grown fastest.

There is a second cost that does not show on an invoice. In-home tutoring restricts you to whoever is willing to drive to your address at the hour your child is free. For a Phase 2 French learner that pool is adequate. For a Phase 5 student who needs criterion-level marking, the pool in a given neighbourhood may be one person, or nobody. Online removes the geography from the selection and leaves only the match.

IB Gram delivers to Abu Dhabi families as one-to-one tuition over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is stated plainly here because the alternative - implying a visit and then explaining the truth after a deposit - is how this market loses parents' trust.

sections.heading: Counting the MYP five-year budget backwards
paragraphs: Most families start French support in the year the report card gets uncomfortable, which is usually MYP 4. The cheaper sequence runs the other way. Phase progression in Language Acquisition is cumulative: a student who finishes MYP 3 solidly inside Phase 3 reaches MYP 5 with a realistic route to a Diploma Language B course. A student who arrives in MYP 5 still working at Phase 2 is choosing between ab initio and dropping the language, and both of those decisions cost more than two years of weekly support would have.

Counted backwards from the end of MYP 5, the honest plan looks like this. MYP 5 is the heaviest year and the worst year to start, because the Personal Project is running at the same time and the student has no spare evenings. MYP 4 is when most of the gap can still be closed, and it is the year where a term of focused criterion D work pays for itself. MYP 3 is where cheap preventive support works - a 45-minute weekly slot at the lower market band, aimed at reading strategy before the texts get unfamiliar. MYP 1 and 2 rarely need paid support at all unless the child has arrived from a non-French school mid-phase.

This sequence also decides whether you ever need the premium tier. Criterion-level marking is the expensive skill, and it is only genuinely necessary from Phase 4 upwards. A family that keeps a student on track through MYP 3 with lower-band support may never need to buy the top band at all, which over five years is the difference between a few thousand dirhams and a great many.

Build the plan around your school's own reporting dates rather than the exam calendar. ADEK schools in Abu Dhabi set their own internal assessment windows, and the dates that actually matter to an MYP student are the ones in the school's calendar, not a national one. Ask the MYP coordinator for the Language Acquisition assessment schedule for the year and work backwards from it.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and what a parent can actually check
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and accredited by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by effectively none of the competing tutoring pages in this market, which is odd, because it is the body whose inspection reports tell an Abu Dhabi parent what the school is actually delivering. ADEK does not set, cap or approve private tutoring rates, and no tutoring provider is licensed by ADEK unless it operates premises under a separate permit.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated separately, by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, and gives a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. There is a further point specific to this emirate: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

What this means for a quote is simple. A permit costs the tutor nothing, so a provider adding a licensing surcharge to your invoice is charging you for a free document. And a tutor who cannot tell you their permit position is a risk you are paying for. IB Gram holds no ADEK, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and does not claim any; what we do is deliver one-to-one online teaching and tell you plainly where the regulatory lines sit.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the real cost of a UAE timetable
paragraphs: A French budget drawn up in isolation is usually wrong, because French is not the only language being graded. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a child in an Abu Dhabi IB school carries Arabic and, where applicable, Islamic Education alongside MYP French.

The operational detail is published most clearly in Dubai's guidance, and the principles are instructive across the country. KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements set out that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. The instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

For families, the consequence is arithmetic. A student carrying Arabic, French and English in the same week has three languages under assessment, and a tutoring plan that treats French as the only problem will run into a timetable that has no room for it. The practical answer is sequencing rather than volume: one language supported properly at a time, in the term where its assessment actually falls, rather than three thin bookings at once.

There is one constraint worth knowing before anyone offers you Arabic material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic works with the school's own set material, not with an imported scheme - and a provider promising their own Arabic curriculum has not read the rule.

sections.heading: What an hour looks like, and what the trial establishes
paragraphs: A first session for MYP French in Abu Dhabi is a diagnosis, not a lesson, and it is free. One trial lesson per student, booked without card details and with nothing payable before or after it. The condition is simply that it is one lesson for one student - there is no obligation to continue and no charge if you do not.

In that lesson the tutor establishes three things. Which phase the child is genuinely working in, which is not always the phase the school has recorded. Which of the four criteria is dragging the grade, established by looking at a recent marked task rather than by asking. And what the realistic weekly commitment is, given a school timetable that already carries Arabic and English under assessment.

After the trial you get a written note with a phase judgement, a named criterion to work on first, and a recommended session length and frequency - with the tier that implies, so you can compare the number against the market bands published higher up this page. If the honest answer is that your child needs forty-five minutes a week at the lower band rather than a specialist block, that is what the note says.

Where no suitable MYP French specialist is free for the slot a family needs, we say so rather than substituting a generalist at a specialist price. In that case the options offered are a different slot with the right tutor, a temporary tutor at the lower band with the limitation stated, or a referral back when availability opens. Disclosing a coverage limit is not a weakness in this market; concealing one behind a premium rate is.

faqs.question: What does an MYP French tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with entry-level online tuition advertised from AED 33 to 65 by Tutopiya and EdFlik, around AED 270 by TutorChase, and AED 650 at BartyED's premium tier. In-home one-to-one in the UAE runs AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the fee. Those are the providers' own published figures, not an IB Gram price list. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson, once a tutor has established which phase your child is working in and therefore which tier is actually needed.

faqs.question: Why is Phase 5 French priced above Phase 1 in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Because they are different teaching jobs. Phase 1 and 2 work is vocabulary, sentence patterns and oral confidence, which a strong generalist languages teacher delivers well at the lower market band. Phase 5 and 6 work asks a tutor to read a criterion descriptor and explain exactly why a piece of writing sits at level 5 rather than level 7, and to mark unfamiliar text comprehension accurately. That judgement is a scarcer skill, so it costs more. Paying specialist rates for Phase 2 content buys nothing useful, and paying generalist rates for Phase 5 content buys a pleasant hour with no grade movement.

faqs.question: Is a French tutor cheaper for us in Khalifa City than on Abu Dhabi island?
faqs.answer: For in-home tutoring, yes and no - the island has the deepest tutor supply in the emirate, which pushes rates down there, while mainland communities like Al Shamkha and Al Falah see both higher quotes and thinner coverage because of the drive. Al Raha and Khalifa City sit in the middle, with a more predictable school run. For online tutoring your postcode changes nothing at all: the rate, the tutor pool and the available slots are identical across the emirate, which is the main reason families in the outer communities end up online.

faqs.question: How many hours of MYP French support does an Abu Dhabi family usually buy in a term?
faqs.answer: The common pattern is one 45- or 60-minute session a week across a school term, so roughly ten to twelve hours, with written tasks marked in between. Phase 1 and 2 learners do better on 45 minutes; from Phase 4 upwards a 60-minute session earns its length. Families working to a specific reporting window instead buy a block of four to eight sessions and then stop. Buying a large bundle up front is rarely good value before anyone has established the phase, because the phase decides both the tier and the session length you actually need.

faqs.question: Does the MYP eAssessment option change what French support costs?
faqs.answer: It changes the shape of the work rather than the hourly rate. Where a school registers Language Acquisition for MYP eAssessment, the evidence is portfolio-based rather than a sat paper, so support shifts towards building and refining pieces of the student's own work over months instead of exam technique in a final block. That spreads cost across the year rather than concentrating it. Not every Abu Dhabi school takes the eAssessment route, and the components a school enters vary, so confirm with your MYP coordinator which route your child is on before you plan a budget around it.

faqs.question: Do we pay more for a native French speaker?
faqs.answer: Native fluency on its own does not command a premium in this market, and it is not the variable that moves an MYP grade. What is priced is criterion judgement - whether the tutor has marked MYP Language Acquisition tasks and can say why a piece of writing scored what it scored. A native speaker without that experience sits in the lower band; a non-native teacher with it sits in the upper band. For Phase 1 and 2 oral confidence, native fluency genuinely helps. For criterion B inference and criterion D accuracy at Phase 5, marking experience helps far more.

faqs.question: Is marking written French between sessions included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: With IB Gram it is part of the weekly arrangement rather than a separate line - written tasks are submitted between sessions and returned with comments against the specific criterion. Elsewhere in this market it varies, and it is worth asking directly, because marking is where criterion D accuracy actually improves. A provider charging only for contact time has a financial reason to do less marking. When comparing quotes, ask how many pieces of written work will be marked per month and what the feedback looks like, then compare the real cost per marked task.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover French and Arabic to reduce what we spend?
faqs.answer: One tutor covering two languages is possible where the phases are adjacent and the tutor genuinely teaches both, and it does cut total cost by removing a duplicated diagnosis. It is more common to pair French with Spanish, because the interference patterns overlap and one person can separate them faster than two. Arabic is a different case: it is a mandatory subject with set school material, and the Ministry prohibits using different or additional content without prior permission, so an Arabic tutor works from the school's own scheme rather than their own.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise before an MYP reporting window?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates do not usually change, but what you can actually book does. Demand concentrates in the two or three weeks before a school's reporting or portfolio deadline, and the first thing to disappear is availability in the 4.30pm to 6pm slots at the specialist tier. Families who leave it until that point often end up paying an upper-band rate for a tutor who was their third choice. Booking from the start of a term, or at least a month before a known deadline, is the cheapest scheduling decision available in this market.

faqs.question: Does ADEK set or cap what a private French tutor may charge?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate of Abu Dhabi and publishes school inspection outcomes. It does not regulate private tutoring rates, and no tutoring provider is licensed by ADEK unless it operates premises under a separate permit. Private tutoring is regulated through a different route: the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. IB Gram holds no ADEK accreditation and claims none - we name the regulator because its school reports are useful to parents.

faqs.question: Does our tutor need a MoHRE permit, and does that cost us anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing. The UAE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A provider adding a licensing charge to your invoice is billing you for a free document.

faqs.question: Can we buy French support in MYP 5 only and skip the earlier years?
faqs.answer: You can, and it is the most expensive version of the plan. Phase progression in Language Acquisition is cumulative, so a student who reaches MYP 5 still working at Phase 2 is choosing between Diploma ab initio and dropping French, and both decisions carry a cost. MYP 5 is also the year the Personal Project runs, so the student has fewer free evenings exactly when the French workload peaks. A term of lower-band support in MYP 3, aimed at reading strategy before the texts turn unfamiliar, is the cheapest intervention available in the whole five years.

faqs.question: How do we keep MYP French costs down across the five MYP years?
faqs.answer: Four decisions do most of the work. Start early and low: 45 minutes a week at the lower band in MYP 3 beats a specialist block in MYP 5. Match the tier to the phase rather than to anxiety. Sequence languages instead of stacking them, supporting one properly in the term its assessment falls. And keep delivery online, because travel is the largest controllable line in any UAE quote - AED 50 to 150 an hour that buys no teaching. Stopping a block when it has done its job is the fifth, and the one families forget.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change the price or only the timing of French lessons in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The rate does not change; the schedule does. School days shorten during Ramadan and family routines move later, so sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot and the usual 4.30pm to 6pm block empties out. Because online delivery is not constrained by a tutor's driving schedule, moving a weekly slot later is straightforward, which is not always true of an in-home arrangement. Plan around it rather than pausing: the weeks after Ramadan often sit close to a school reporting window, and that is the worst possible time to be restarting from a standstill.

faqs.question: What happens if no MYP French specialist is free for the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not the market norm. The options are a different slot with the right tutor, a tutor at the lower band with the limitation stated plainly so you are not paying a specialist rate for generalist teaching, or a referral back when availability opens. No competitor page reviewed in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number. A disclosed gap is cheaper for a family than a concealed one, because it does not waste a term.

intro.heading: The search is for a home tutor; the problem is usually the evening
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry that starts with a search for an IB MYP home tutor in Abu Dhabi is really two problems bundled together. One is academic: a report card with criterion levels that are not moving, or a subject that has started to slide since Year 8. The other is operational: the school day finishes, the bus or the car gets home somewhere between 15:30 and 16:45 depending on which side of the city you live, there are activities on two or three evenings, and the window in which a tired twelve-year-old can learn anything is narrow and movable. A home tutor looks like the answer to both because it removes a journey.

It is worth being precise about what the visiting option actually buys and costs, because almost nobody publishes those numbers. Bestimate's 2026 survey of tutoring costs puts in-home one-to-one sessions at AED 180 to 350 per hour, with home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500. Monthly in-home packages in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Comparable online one-to-one rates sit lower: Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, and budget providers such as EdFlik and Tutopiya publish online hours from AED 45 to 65 and AED 33 to 52 respectively. Those were the published positions in October 2026 and providers revise them.

The difference between those bands is not mostly teaching quality. It is the unbilled forty minutes at each end of a visit, the smaller pool of people willing to make the drive, and the loss of flexibility once a tutor's week is built around travel. For Middle Years work that last point matters more than it does for an older student, because the useful hour for an eleven to fourteen-year-old moves around with the week, and a visiting schedule cannot move with it.

So the honest statement up front: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Middle Years sessions for Abu Dhabi families are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The case for that is not that it is cheaper, though it generally is. It is that the match is made on who has actually taught that subject group in the Middle Years Programme, and that an online slot can be moved by twenty minutes on a Tuesday without anybody renegotiating a drive across the emirate.

The rest of this page is written for the parent rather than the student, because at these ages the parent is still the operating system. It covers what a household actually needs in place, what you can observe from the next room without understanding the subject, how to divide a single tutoring budget between two children in different MYP years, where the line sits when an adult is sitting beside a sixteen-year-old's Personal Project, and how to check that the person you are paying holds the permit UAE private tutoring now requires.
