intro.heading: What an MYP physics tutor in Abu Dhabi costs, and what sets the number
paragraphs: Start with the only honest answer: the published range for private tutoring in the UAE runs from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor, and MYP physics sits in the lower middle of that spread. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB tutoring from AED 200. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and exam-year specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. BartyED quotes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures, read in October 2026, not ours.

MYP physics is cheaper per hour than Diploma physics for a structural reason, not a marketing one. There is no external examination hanging over MYP 1 to 4, no Internal Assessment to supervise, and the assessment is criterion-referenced coursework set by your child's own school. A tutor working in MYP 4 is not preparing a candidate for a terminal paper; they are moving criterion levels on tasks the subject teacher has written. That is skilled work, and it is less specialised work than coaching a Paper 3 option at Higher Level, so the market prices it lower.

What pushes an Abu Dhabi quote up is not the emirate's cost of living. It is three things. First, discrete versus integrated: a tutor asked to cover physics as a separate MYP 5 course is being asked for subject depth, and depth costs more than general science coverage. Second, criterion B and C work: designing a controlled investigation and processing data properly takes longer to teach than recalling definitions, so a term aimed at those criteria needs more hours than a term aimed at criterion A. Third, timing. A request that lands two weeks before an end-of-unit task competes with every other family in the same school for the same evening slot, and scarce evening slots are the only part of this market that behaves like a commodity.

The second cost nobody quotes you is unseen preparation. The MYP does not publish a content syllabus for physics. The IB Sciences guide sets out key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria; your child's school then writes its own units and its own tasks. So before lesson one a tutor has to read the unit planner, the task sheet, the criterion rubric and the last marked piece of work. Providers handle that differently: some absorb it, some bill it, some skip it and then teach the wrong thing for a fortnight. Ask which, in writing, before you pay anything.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered live online, one to one, over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a physics family that is the cheaper and the better arrangement at the same time, because the screen is where the work already lives. Graphs get drawn on a shared whiteboard, a photographed lab book is annotated in real time, and a logger-recorded data set can be opened and reprocessed in front of the student instead of being described from memory.

A two-year MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023
Delivery is live online on Gulf Standard Time, which removes travel cost from the hourly rate entirely

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families usually arrive on this page in MYP 3 or MYP 4, when Sciences splits into recognisable physics content and the report card suddenly reads 4, 5, 3, 5 instead of a percentage. Here is where the Middle Years Programme sits either side of that moment, and what the physics workload looks like in each phase.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years in which Sciences is one subject group rather than three subjects. In MYP 1 to 3 most Abu Dhabi schools teach integrated Sciences, so physics appears as units on forces, energy and waves alongside chemistry and biology content. In MYP 4 and 5 many schools let students take discrete physics. Assessment is against four criteria, each marked out of eight, set and marked internally by the school.
programmes.countryNote: In this emirate the schools licensed by ADEK publish criterion levels on their reports, and parents routinely see four numbers with no percentage anywhere. ADEK also inspects these schools and publishes ratings, so a weak Sciences department usually appears in the inspection narrative before it appears in your child's grade. A physics tutor here reads the school's own unit planner, because no two Abu Dhabi MYP schools teach the same physics in the same term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two years after MYP 5, where physics becomes Standard or Higher Level with external papers and an Internal Assessment. The jump that catches students is quantitative: DP physics assumes fluent algebra, confident unit work and uncertainty handling that the MYP introduces but does not drill. Hourly rates for Diploma physics support run visibly higher than MYP rates in every published UAE price list.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students choosing physics at Higher Level after MYP 5 are the ones who benefit most from MYP money spent early. Nothing about MYP physics is externally examined, so a thin MYP 4 and 5 leaves no trace on a transcript and a large hole in DP 1. Families who spend on criterion B and C skills in MYP 4 typically buy fewer catch-up hours in DP 1, which is the clearest return-on-cost argument this page can make.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme that feeds the MYP in continuum schools. Science in the PYP is inquiry-led and not graded on criteria, so there is no physics mark to compare. What carries forward is measurement, recording and the habit of explaining a result rather than stating it, all of which reappear in MYP criterion C.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the full IB continuum, which means a child can move from PYP 5 into MYP 1 without changing campus. Parents of those children rarely need paid physics support, and we say so plainly rather than selling it. The sensible spend at this stage, if any, is on number fluency, because unit conversion and rearranging a formula are where MYP 3 physics first goes wrong.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.subjectsIntro: A physics request in the MYP is almost never only physics. Sciences is a single subject group, maths sits underneath every calculation, and the criteria are shared across the group. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families most often book alongside or instead of physics, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Sciences: the physics strand
subjects.description: Forces and motion, energy transfer, waves, electricity and magnetism, taught through the school's own units. Marks are lost less on recall than on rearranging a relationship, converting a unit and reading a gradient off a graph with its units attached.

subjects.name: Sciences: the chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particle model, bonding, reactions and quantitative work. Shares criteria C and D with physics, so a student who processes data badly in chemistry is almost always processing it badly in physics, and one set of sessions can fix both.

subjects.name: Sciences: the biology strand
subjects.description: Cells, systems, genetics and ecology. Criterion B investigation design is identical in structure to physics, which is why a tutor who teaches variables and controls well in biology transfers straight into a physics practical.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: The single course most Abu Dhabi MYP schools run for the first three years. One teacher, one grade, three sciences inside it. A physics problem at this stage usually shows up as a low criterion A on one unit and a solid level on the next.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard)
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry and statistics. Rearranging a formula, handling indices and plotting a line of best fit are maths skills marked inside physics, so weak standard maths caps a physics level regardless of how well the concept is understood.

subjects.name: Extended Mathematics
subjects.description: The faster route for students heading to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Covers algebraic manipulation and functions at a depth that makes DP physics readable. Often the better purchase for a student whose physics problem is arithmetic, not physics.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The criteria mirror the Sciences investigation cycle closely enough that a student who can plan a Design project can usually plan a physics investigation once the vocabulary is swapped.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation, source handling and critical thinking. Shares criterion D ground with Sciences, where students must discuss the impacts of science on people and the environment, and that is the criterion Abu Dhabi students most often leave half-written.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis, organisation, text production and language use. Relevant to physics because criterion D asks for a written discussion, and a student who cannot structure a paragraph loses science levels for writing reasons.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed units combining two subject groups, often Sciences with Individuals and Societies in Abu Dhabi schools. They carry their own criteria and their own grade, and parents are frequently surprised to find a second mark on the report with no obvious lesson behind it.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Abu Dhabi MYP physics families sit, and what that does to a session time
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so none of these notes are about travel distance for a tutor. They are about the clock in your household: when school ends, when the driver gets home, and when a fifty-minute physics session can realistically start without the student arriving at it exhausted.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Island-side bus runs land many MYP students home by half past three. Al Reem families book the earliest slots on this page, which are also the easiest to get at short notice before an end-of-unit task.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Buses to the island and back make four o'clock unreliable for Khalifa City MYP 4 students. A five o'clock physics session with the lab book open, scanned before the lesson, works better than a rushed four o'clock.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: Families here often have a parent working in energy or engineering, and the physics requests we get from Masdar City lean towards extension rather than remediation: a level 6 student who wants level 7 criterion D writing on energy.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Short school runs and a cluster of long-established island schools. Al Bateen requests tend to arrive mid-term, triggered by a single marked Sciences task rather than a whole-report conversation.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A villa community feeding the Al Raha and Khalifa City schools. Two-child bookings are common here, usually one MYP student and one younger sibling, and the physics hour is the one the household protects.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Longer commutes and later arrivals home. Sessions from six o'clock onwards are the norm, and a weekend morning block is often the only time a full investigation write-up can be worked through properly.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools, newer MYP cohorts, and parents who have not seen a criterion-level report before. The first physics session for a Yas Island family is often spent reading the report rather than teaching mechanics.

regions.name: Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland villas with mixed school destinations across the island and Khalifa City. Scheduling here is set by the driver's return, so a fixed weekly slot matters more than the exact hour chosen.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: The longest-established international cohort in the emirate, and the one where MYP physics requests most often concern extension rather than rescue. Programme offerings change year to year, so check the current offer on the school's own site or on the ADEK school listing before assuming a campus runs the MYP.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island
schoolClusters.note: The corridor that produces most of our MYP Sciences enquiries, partly because it holds the largest concentration of continuum schools and partly because the school-run clock here pushes families towards evening online sessions. Students we support attend schools in this corridor; no affiliation is implied by the listing.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways Abu Dhabi families buy MYP physics support, with what each costs in hours rather than in marketing. All three are delivered live online, one to one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across a term
modes.description: One fifty-minute session a week, held at the same time, following your school's own unit sequence. This is the arrangement that moves criterion levels, because it gives a tutor time to set a task, mark it, and teach into what the marking showed. A term of it is roughly twelve sessions.

modes.title: Pre-task intensive block
modes.description: Three or four sessions in the fortnight before an end-of-unit Sciences assessment. Narrower and more expensive per outcome than weekly work, because it can only polish what is already there. Useful for a student whose understanding is sound and whose exam technique is not.

modes.description: A short run of sessions aimed only at planning a controlled investigation and processing its data. Variables, method, repeats, tables, graphs with units, and an evaluation that names a real limitation. Bought separately because it is the single highest-value purchase in MYP Sciences and transfers to chemistry and biology unchanged.

sections.heading: There is no MYP physics syllabus to buy, and that shapes the first invoice
paragraphs: Parents arriving from a CBSE, Cambridge or American background look for the MYP physics syllabus and cannot find it, because it does not exist. The IB publishes a Sciences subject guide that sets out key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria. It does not prescribe a content list. Your child's school writes the units, chooses the contexts, sets the tasks and marks them against the published criteria. Two MYP 4 students at two Abu Dhabi schools can both be studying physics and be studying completely different physics.

That single fact changes what you are buying. A tutor who walks in with a generic Year 9 physics scheme of work will teach content your child's school is not assessing this term, and the criterion levels will not move. A tutor who reads the unit planner first will know that this term's unit is marked on criteria B and C through a controlled investigation on energy transfer, and will spend the hours on variables and graph work instead of on definitions. The difference between those two tutors is not talent. It is forty minutes of reading before the first lesson.

So ask every provider in Abu Dhabi the same three questions before paying. Who reads the unit planner, and is that time charged? What happens if the school changes the task mid-unit? And will I get a written note after each session saying which criterion was worked on? A provider that cannot answer those is selling hours, not physics. sections.heading: What physics support costs in Abu Dhabi, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. So here is the AED picture, assembled from what providers themselves publish and read in October 2026. Treat every row as that provider's claim about its own service, not as a quote from IB Gram, and treat the spread as information about market segmentation rather than about quality.

The budget online band sits at AED 33 to 65 an hour and is populated by university students and generalist tutors. For MYP physics that band can work for a student who needs company while doing homework and cannot work for a student whose criterion B planning is weak, because planning an investigation is a taught skill that a generalist has usually never been marked on. The qualified subject band at AED 150 to 300 is where most MYP Sciences work genuinely lives. Above that, AED 200 to 450 and beyond buys Diploma and A-Level specialism that an MYP 3 student does not need and should not be sold.

In-home visiting rates are the outlier. Bestimate's Dubai table puts home visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A meaningful part of that premium is the tutor's travel, which buys your child nothing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so that premium does not appear in our model at all; the one-to-one hour runs live online instead, and the money that would have paid for a drive across Khalifa City pays for a Sciences specialist instead of whoever lives nearby.

sections.heading: Where the physics money goes: criteria B and C, not criterion A
paragraphs: MYP Sciences is marked on four criteria, each out of eight, and your child's single 1-7 subject grade is produced by adding those four levels and converting the total through a boundary table the IB publishes in its programme documentation. Ask your MYP coordinator for the version your school applies; it is not something to take from a tutoring page. What matters for spending decisions is that the four criteria are not equally expensive to teach.

Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the cheap one. It rewards explaining scientific knowledge, applying it to solve problems and analysing information. A student who revises will move on criterion A, and a tutor adds least here. Criterion B, inquiring and designing, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, are where hours disappear and where levels stall for years. These ask a thirteen-year-old to write a testable research question, identify and control variables, justify a method, process raw data into something interpretable, present it correctly and then evaluate the method honestly. None of that is physics knowledge. All of it is taught.

Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, is the one Abu Dhabi students most often leave half-finished, because it is a writing task hiding inside a science course. It asks for the application of science to address a specific problem, the implications of using science, and accurate use of scientific language. A physics student who can calculate the efficiency of a solar panel and cannot discuss the consequences of deploying it loses two levels for reasons that have nothing to do with physics. The table sets out where a Year 9 physics student in this emirate typically loses ground, criterion by criterion, and how many sessions it usually takes to move one level.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a visiting tutor, with Abu Dhabi travel costed honestly
paragraphs: The comparison most Abu Dhabi families are actually making is not between tutors. It is between a visiting tutor and a screen. So compare them on the things that differ: the published rate, what the travel does to a weekday evening, how deep the tutor pool goes for a specific subject, and what is included when the hour ends.

Travel is not a small factor in this emirate. A tutor living on the island and teaching in Khalifa City at five o'clock is committing to the bridge in both directions, which in practice means the family pays for ninety minutes of the tutor's time to receive fifty minutes of physics. Rearrange the session to six o'clock and the traffic improves but the student is tired. Cancel at short notice because a sibling has a fixture and the tutor has still spent the drive. None of those costs appear on an advertised hourly rate, and all of them are real.

Depth of pool is the argument that matters more. MYP physics taught as a discrete MYP 5 course is a narrow specialism. The number of tutors who can confidently teach it and mark against criterion C is small anywhere, and the number who can do that and live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Raha Gardens is smaller still. Online delivery replaces the geographic filter with a subject filter. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, which is precisely why the match can be made on the physics rather than on the postcode.

sections.heading: Equations, units and gradients: the line items that repeat every single term
paragraphs: Across MYP physics requests from this emirate the same three technical failures recur, regardless of school or year group. The first is algebraic rearrangement. A student who understands that resistance relates voltage to current, and who cannot make current the subject of the equation without guessing, will lose criterion A marks on a topic they genuinely understand. The fix is not physics teaching. It is twenty minutes a week of rearrangement practice until it stops being a thinking task.

The second is units, and specifically the conversions that MYP tasks quietly require: centimetres into metres before a density calculation, grams into kilograms before anything involving mass, minutes into seconds before a speed. Students lose levels not for failing to convert but for converting inconsistently inside the same calculation, which produces an answer that is numerically wrong and dimensionally meaningless. A tutor who insists on units written at every line of working, every time, removes a whole class of lost marks without teaching any new content.

The third is graph work, which is where criterion C is won and lost. Plotting points is rarely the problem. The problems are choosing a scale that uses the paper, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining the dots, calculating a gradient from two points on the line rather than two data points, and then stating what the gradient physically means with its units attached. A gradient of 9.8 is not an answer; 9.8 metres per second squared, interpreted as the acceleration of free fall, is. That distinction is worth two criterion C levels and takes about three sessions to make automatic.

None of these three are advanced physics. They are the mechanical skills that MYP tasks assume and MYP lessons rarely have time to drill. If a household has budget for one term of physics support and nothing more, spending it on rearrangement, units and gradients will return more criterion levels than spending it on the content of the current unit.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi evening, and the hour you are actually buying
paragraphs: An Abu Dhabi weekday leaves a narrow window for serious physics. School buses on the island routes return students between half past two and half past three; buses serving Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland communities regularly land later. Add a prayer time, a sibling's activity and a meal, and the first realistic start for focused work is somewhere between four and six o'clock depending on which community you live in. The window closes earlier than parents expect, because a tired fourteen-year-old does not plan an investigation well at eight in the evening.

This is where online delivery stops being a compromise and starts being the reason the session happens at all. A fifty-minute slot at five o'clock from a bedroom desk is attainable four weeks out of four. The same slot with a tutor driving in from the island is attainable until the first accident on the bridge. Fixed weekly timing also matters more than most families realise: a session at an unpredictable hour becomes the thing that gets cancelled, and cancelled sessions are how a term of planned criterion work turns into four random hours.

Ramadan reorganises everything, and it is worth planning for rather than pausing through. School days shorten, energy in the afternoon drops, and post-iftar evenings are genuinely productive for many students. Sessions can be moved to a late slot for the month and moved back afterwards. Summer is the opposite case: with no school deadlines, it is the only period in the year when criterion B and C skills can be taught slowly, out of context, without a task breathing down the student's neck. Families who buy their investigation clinic in July rather than in February get noticeably more out of the same hours.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for private physics lessons in this emirate
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the position is clearer than most tutoring pages admit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here or anywhere else on this site.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen can all apply. That breadth is why the AED 33 to 65 band exists: a university student with a permit is operating entirely legally at that price. It is also why asking about the permit tells you about legality, not about teaching quality. Both questions need asking separately.

Abu Dhabi adds a condition worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against ADEK's published policy before relying on it, but treat the principle as settled: your child's own Sciences teacher is not the right person to hire privately, however convenient it looks. No part of our model depends on that arrangement.

sections.heading: Five years of MYP Sciences, and the terms when physics money is worth spending
paragraphs: Spending the same amount in different years produces very different returns. In MYP 1 and 2, Sciences is integrated, the units are short and the criteria are being introduced rather than enforced. Paid physics support here is usually premature. The exception is a student who cannot handle number work, because every subsequent physics problem will be an arithmetic problem wearing a physics costume, and that is worth fixing at eleven rather than at fifteen.

MYP 3 is where the first honest signal arrives. Criterion levels start separating, and a pattern of 5, 3, 3, 4 across the four criteria tells you something specific: knowledge is adequate, investigation and data work are not. A term of targeted criterion B and C support at this point costs the same as a term of general science help and does considerably more, because the skill it builds is used in every Sciences unit for the next three years and again throughout the Diploma.

MYP 4 and 5 are the expensive years, and the ones where families most often overpay for the wrong thing. Here Sciences may split into discrete physics, tasks get longer, and MYP 5 adds the Personal Project and, in some Abu Dhabi schools, on-screen eAssessment. The temptation is to buy an intensive block two weeks before a task. The arithmetic argues against it: three sessions of polish on top of weak criterion C will shift one level, while twelve weekly sessions spread across a term will usually shift two or three and leave the student able to do it unaided. If the budget is one term, buy the term early rather than buying a panic fortnight late.

process.title: Send the three documents
process.description: Email the current Sciences unit planner, the most recent marked task with the teacher's comments, and the latest report card showing criterion levels. Those three tell a tutor more in ten minutes than a phone call does in an hour, and they determine whether the sessions aim at criterion A or at criteria B and C.

process.title: Trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One fifty-minute session with an MYP Sciences specialist, at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. The tutor works on a real task from your school's current unit, not a demonstration topic, so what you see is what the paid sessions look like.

process.title: Agree the target and the price in writing
process.description: Before any payment you receive which criterion the term is aimed at, how many sessions, the rate per session in AED, whether preparation time is charged, and the reschedule terms. Anything a provider will not put in writing is something you will argue about in week six.

process.title: Run the weekly cycle
process.description: Teach, set a task, mark it against the published criterion rubric, teach into the result. A short written note after each session records which criterion strand was worked on and what the student should practise before the next one, so a parent can follow the work without being a physics teacher.

process.title: Review at six weeks on evidence
process.description: Compare marked tasks from week one and week six, strand by strand, and decide whether to continue, change tutor or stop. If the evidence shows no movement we say so and look at why, which is sometimes a tutoring problem and sometimes a timetable problem.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. No price here is presented as an IB Gram price list, and none of it is invented. You can open the sources and verify the bands yourself before deciding what is reasonable.

whyPoints.title: Matched on physics, not on postcode
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is live online across the whole emirate, the filter is which tutor has taught MYP Sciences criterion C well, not which tutor lives near Al Raha Gardens. For a narrow specialism like discrete MYP 5 physics that difference is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

whyPoints.title: The school's own unit, not a generic scheme
whyPoints.description: The MYP prescribes no physics content, so a tutor who ignores your school's unit planner teaches the wrong material. Ours read the planner, the task sheet and the rubric before the first lesson, and the sessions follow the sequence your child's teacher is actually assessing.

whyPoints.title: A clear academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, review and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not supply submissions, and they do not touch the wording of a Personal Project report or an investigation write-up. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session, because it protects them and nobody else benefits from blurring it.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a non-scientist can read
whyPoints.description: Criterion levels, a marked task from week one against a marked task from week six, and a one-paragraph note after each session. No dashboards, no scores we invented. A parent with no physics background can see which strand moved and which did not.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of availability
whyPoints.description: If no MYP Sciences specialist is free in your preferred slot we tell you the earliest one that is, rather than filling the hour with a generalist. For discrete MYP 5 physics that sometimes means waiting a week, and we would rather say so than sell the wrong tutor.

faqs.question: What does an MYP Sciences tutor charge per hour for physics in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, exam-level specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. MYP physics generally sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, below Diploma physics, because the assessment is internally set coursework rather than external papers. Those figures are the providers' own published claims, not an IB Gram price list. For our own pricing, ask on the consultation; the bands above are here so you can judge any quote you receive against the market.

faqs.question: Is there an MYP physics syllabus I can buy for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and this surprises most families. The IB publishes a Sciences subject guide covering key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria, but it prescribes no content list. Your child's Abu Dhabi school writes its own units, chooses its own contexts and sets its own tasks. That is why a tutor needs your school's unit planner rather than a textbook: two MYP 4 students at two schools in the same emirate can be studying genuinely different physics in the same term. Ask your MYP coordinator for the current planner, and ask any prospective tutor whether they will read it.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 3 and his report says Sciences, not physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Because in the MYP, Sciences is one subject group rather than three subjects. Most Abu Dhabi schools teach it as an integrated course in MYP 1 to 3, so physics content appears as units on forces, energy or electricity alongside chemistry and biology units, all marked against the same four criteria and reported as a single Sciences grade. From MYP 4 many schools offer discrete physics. If you want to know how the physics units specifically went, ask for the criterion levels from each unit rather than the overall grade, which averages the lot and hides exactly what you are looking for.

faqs.question: How many hours does a criterion B investigation task usually take to teach?
faqs.answer: Moving one level on criterion B generally takes four to eight sessions, which is more than most parents expect and less than the whole term. The reason is that inquiring and designing is a composite skill: writing a testable question, identifying and controlling variables, justifying a range and a number of repeats, and planning something that could actually be carried out. A student rarely fails all four at once, so the first session is diagnostic. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, runs on a similar timescale. Criterion A moves faster, in two to four sessions, because revision does much of the work.

faqs.question: Why would a first invoice include preparation time?
faqs.answer: Because a competent first lesson requires reading. The unit planner takes twenty to forty minutes, the task sheet and criterion rubric fifteen to thirty, the last marked task twenty to thirty, and the report card around fifteen. Providers handle that cost in different ways: some absorb it into the hourly rate, some bill it separately and openly, and some skip it entirely and then teach material your school is not assessing. None of those is dishonest except the last. Ask which model you are buying before you pay, and get the answer in writing with the rest of the terms.

faqs.question: Is a visiting physics tutor in Abu Dhabi worth the extra AED per hour?
faqs.answer: The published premium for in-home tutoring in this market runs from AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online work, and a real share of that gap is travel. An island-based tutor teaching in Khalifa City at five o'clock spends forty to eighty minutes on the road each way. Your child receives none of that time. The bigger cost is the narrowing of the pool: insisting on a short drive means choosing from tutors who live nearby rather than tutors who teach MYP Sciences well. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: Does my child need a laboratory to do MYP physics investigations properly?
faqs.answer: For the school's assessed practical work, no, because that happens in the school laboratory with the subject teacher. What a tutor works on is everything around the apparatus: the research question, the variables, the method, the data table, the graph and the evaluation. Those are paper and screen tasks, and they are where the criterion levels are won. Where home practicals are genuinely useful, physics is unusually generous: a ruler, a stopwatch, a phone sensor app and a kitchen scale cover motion, period and density work convincingly enough to practise the full inquiry cycle.

faqs.question: How do online physics lessons handle practical data and graph work?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the lab book and sends it before the session, and it goes on the shared screen where the tutor annotates it live. Data gets typed into a spreadsheet and replotted during the lesson, so a student watches a badly scaled axis become a usable graph rather than being told about it. Gradients are calculated on the screen with units attached at every step. In practice this is closer to how physics is actually done than a tutor reading over a shoulder at a kitchen table, because the working is visible to both people at once and is saved afterwards.

faqs.question: What does physics help cost if we only want support before one end-of-unit test?
faqs.answer: A pre-task block is usually three or four sessions in the fortnight before the assessment, so at market rates for a qualified subject tutor you are looking at the equivalent of three to four hours rather than a term. It is the most expensive way to buy criterion levels, because polish can only improve what already exists. It works well for a student whose understanding is sound and whose technique under time pressure is not. It will not build mechanics from nothing in two weeks, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling you something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover physics, chemistry and biology inside MYP Sciences?
faqs.answer: In MYP 1 to 3, usually yes, and often that is the better arrangement. Integrated Sciences is marked against four criteria that are identical across the three strands, so a tutor who teaches investigation design and data processing well improves all three at once. From MYP 4, where schools offer discrete courses, the content depth starts to matter and a physics specialist pulls ahead for physics. A practical rule: buy one tutor for criteria B and C across Sciences, and buy subject depth separately once your child is sitting a discrete physics course.

faqs.question: Does a private physics tutor in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Teachers, public and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen can all apply. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read elsewhere with suspicion. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: My daughter is strong at maths but weak at physics. Will tutoring fix that?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and faster than the reverse case, because the harder half is already in place. A student who is fluent in algebra and poor at physics is typically losing marks on modelling rather than on calculation: choosing which relationship applies, deciding what the question is actually asking, and interpreting an answer physically. Those are teachable in a handful of sessions. The reverse profile, confident with concepts and shaky with rearrangement, takes longer, because every physics problem then carries an arithmetic risk. Send a marked task and the diagnosis takes one session rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: Should we wait until MYP 5 before paying for physics support?
faqs.answer: Waiting is usually the more expensive choice. MYP 3 is where criterion levels first separate clearly, and a pattern like 5, 3, 3, 4 tells you knowledge is fine and investigation work is not. Fixing that at thirteen costs the same per hour as fixing it at fifteen and buys three more years of use, because criteria B and C reappear in every Sciences unit and again throughout the Diploma. MYP 5 is also the busiest year, with the Personal Project and on-screen components in some Abu Dhabi schools competing for the same evenings. Early is cheaper here.

faqs.question: Do quoted MYP physics tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi include VAT?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unresolved until the provider states it. We do not publish a position on the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not going to approximate. What you should insist on is simpler: ask whether the AED figure you have been quoted is the amount that will be charged, and get that confirmed in writing alongside the reschedule terms and the cancellation window. A quote that becomes a different number on the invoice is a commercial problem regardless of how the tax question is answered.

faqs.question: How do we fit physics sessions around the Abu Dhabi school run and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School buses on the island routes typically return students between half past two and half past three, while Khalifa City, Al Raha and mainland runs land later, so realistic start times range from four o'clock to six depending on your community. A fixed weekly slot survives better than a flexible one. During Ramadan, shorter school days and low afternoon energy make post-iftar sessions genuinely productive, and the slot can move for the month and move back afterwards. Summer is the best window for criterion B and C work, because the skills can be taught without a task deadline pressing.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Abu Dhabi for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one to one, live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For physics specifically that is an advantage rather than a concession: the lab book is annotated on a shared screen, data is replotted live, and the match is made on who teaches MYP Sciences criterion C well rather than on who lives within a short drive of your community. Anyone promising a tutor at an Abu Dhabi address is describing a different service.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the numbers, then with one marked task
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingBody: If you have read this far you already know more about MYP physics pricing in this emirate than most of the pages ranking above it. The next step is small: send the current Sciences unit planner, the last marked task with the teacher's comments, and the report card showing criterion levels. A specialist will read the three, tell you in plain language which criterion is actually costing your child levels, and run one fifty-minute session at no charge on a real task from your school's own unit. After that you will have a written note, a quoted rate in AED and a decision to make, rather than a sales conversation.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach MYP sciences as a criterion-marked subject rather than as a body of facts. That means investigation design, data processing on real numbers, evaluation that identifies a specific weakness, and the reflection criterion almost nobody practises. Send a marked task and the four levels from the last report and we will match on the weakest strand.

intro.heading: What a parent can actually check in a science report
paragraphs: An MYP science report gives four numbers between one and eight and no percentages. For a parent who is not a scientist that is close to unreadable, and the instinct is to ask the child how science is going, which produces an answer about how the lessons feel rather than about what is being assessed. The result is a household spending money on tutoring with no instrument for telling whether it is working, which is the problem this page is built to solve.

The four numbers are more informative than they look once you know what each one measures. Criterion A is knowing and understanding: recall, explanation and applying scientific ideas to solve problems. Criterion B is inquiring and designing: writing a hypothesis with scientific reasoning behind it, identifying variables, and setting out a method somebody else could follow. Criterion C is processing and evaluating: tables, graphs, a conclusion that actually answers the question, and an evaluation that names a specific weakness in the method. Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science, which involves applying science to a real problem and considering its consequences.

Those four do not move at the same rate and they do not fail for the same reasons. A low criterion A usually means content gaps, which is the diagnosis families assume and the least common one in practice. A low criterion B means the student has written a prediction rather than a reasoned hypothesis. A low criterion C, which is the single commonest profile we see in Abu Dhabi, means the data were collected and then not processed properly: an unlabelled graph, a conclusion that restates the hypothesis, an evaluation listing generic apologies rather than a specific flaw. A low criterion D almost always means nobody has ever practised it.

So the evidence a parent should be getting from any science tutoring is specific: which criterion, which strand inside it, and what changed between one marked task and the next. Not a topic list, which tells you what happened in the sessions rather than whether it worked. Not a predicted grade, which is an opinion with a number attached. A marked task, a named strand, and a dated note is checkable by somebody with no scientific training at all, which is the entire point.

On delivery: our teaching for UAE families is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, around the school week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For MYP sciences that matters less than families expect, because the marks in this subject sit in design, processing and evaluation rather than in the manipulation of apparatus. The practical work happens at school, where the equipment and the supervision are. What happens in a session is everything that surrounds it, and that is screen work.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.programmesIntro: MYP sciences sits between an inquiry-led primary experience and a Diploma course that will ask for a full scientific investigation. The programmes below are described by what each one expects a student to be able to produce, because that is what determines whether a tutoring hour is useful.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences is taught as an integrated subject in the early years and commonly splits into Biology, Chemistry and Physics in MYP 4 and 5, with four criteria assessed throughout: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is scored one to eight. At least one interdisciplinary unit involving sciences is normally assessed separately each year.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools differ considerably in when they split the sciences and how much laboratory time a year group gets. In newer schools on the Khalifa City and Yas corridor, science departments are often scaling quickly, which tends to show up as strong criterion A teaching and thinner criterion C and D practice. That is the profile most families here arrive with.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry, Physics and other sciences at Standard and Higher Level, each with a scientific investigation worth about a fifth of the subject grade, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Those four headings are recognisably the grown-up version of MYP criteria B and C, which is why a student who never learned to process data in MYP meets the same problem again with higher stakes.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates aiming at medicine, engineering and life sciences at UAE and overseas universities typically need a science at Higher Level. The students who find the Diploma investigation hardest are consistently the ones whose MYP criterion C was never addressed, not the ones with content gaps.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Science sits inside inquiry units with no criterion levels and no formal investigations. What it should leave behind is the habit of asking what would happen if one thing were changed and everything else kept the same, which is the whole of criterion B eight years later in embryonic form.
programmes.countryNote: Families transferring into Abu Dhabi during the primary years often come from systems where science is taught as content to be learned. That child can look very strong in MYP 1 and 2 on criterion A alone, and the gap only becomes visible when investigation marks start counting.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The parallel many Abu Dhabi families compare against. Cambridge offers separate sciences such as Physics 0625 and a combined route, while Pearson runs qualifications including the Science Double Award 4SD0; both assess by written papers, with practical skills examined on paper rather than through a marked investigation.
programmes.countryNote: Because the emirate has large British-curriculum cohorts, MYP students frequently compare their work with friends sitting IGCSE science. The content overlap is substantial and the assessment difference is total: an IGCSE-style answer earns little against criterion C, which rewards the processing and evaluation that written papers only sample.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below is the MYP sciences content Abu Dhabi families most often pay to address, organised by discipline, with a note on the criterion each area tends to expose. Where a topic is listed, the marks are rarely in the recall.

subjects.name: Cells, systems and organisms
subjects.description: Well taught almost everywhere and rarely the problem. Where levels leak is criterion A's application strand: a student who can label a cell diagram perfectly may not be able to explain why a change in one structure affects the whole system, which is what the top band asks for.

subjects.name: Genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares are mechanical and secure for most students. The marks sit in interpreting probability from a cross and in criterion D, where genetics offers the richest material in the whole programme for discussing the consequences of scientific knowledge.

subjects.name: Ecology and interdependence
subjects.description: Strong investigation territory, because sampling produces real variable data. It is also where Abu Dhabi students can do genuinely local work: coastal and mangrove habitats, irrigation, and the effect of temperature on ecosystems that experience a forty-degree summer.

subjects.name: Particles, states and the mole
subjects.description: The conceptual bottleneck of MYP chemistry. Students handle calculations and cannot say what the number represents, which caps criterion A's application strand and then undermines criterion C when the same quantity has to be interpreted from experimental data.

subjects.name: Reactions, rates and energy changes
subjects.description: The best source of criterion B and C tasks in chemistry, because rate experiments produce the kind of data that reward a proper graph. Levels are lost on controlling variables that students do not notice are variables, such as surface area and concentration drift.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and quantitative work
subjects.description: Titration-style tasks introduce precision and repeatability, which is where the discussion of uncertainty begins. Students who record a reading to one decimal place and then state a result to four significant figures lose criterion C marks that ten minutes of teaching would protect.

subjects.name: Forces, motion and graphs
subjects.description: Almost entirely a graph-reading subject at this level. A distance-time or velocity-time graph read as a picture rather than as a relationship is the standard error, and it is a mathematics problem wearing a physics label as often as not.

subjects.name: Energy, work and efficiency
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy and reliably taught. The marks that go missing are in criterion C evaluation, where a student reports an efficiency above one hundred per cent and does not notice that the result is impossible, which is precisely what evaluation is for.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The topic MYP students most often name as the hard one. The underlying difficulty is usually the model rather than the arithmetic: a student who cannot say what current and potential difference physically are will not reason correctly about a circuit however many formulae they hold.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Rich in investigation opportunities and light on content difficulty. It is a good place to practise criterion B design, because variables are easy to isolate and a student can see immediately whether their method would actually work.

subjects.name: Scientific investigation technique
subjects.levels: All sciences · criteria B and C
subjects.description: The skill the whole subject is assessed on and the one least often taught explicitly: a reasoned hypothesis, identified variables, a repeatable method, processed data, a conclusion that answers the question and an evaluation naming a specific flaw.

subjects.name: Reflecting on the impacts of science
subjects.description: Applying science to a real-world problem and discussing consequences, with sources used properly. Students treat it as an essay bolted on at the end, which is exactly why it is the cheapest criterion to improve for most Abu Dhabi students.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.regionsTitle: MYP science students across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.regionsIntro: What varies across the emirate is laboratory access, how early the sciences split, and how much of the week is left once transport and co-curricular commitments are accounted for. All three affect what a session should spend its time on.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Established schools with good laboratory provision, so practical work is usually plentiful and the gap is in processing it. Sessions here most often target criterion C: data a student collected at school, processed properly for the first time with somebody watching.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A high proportion of mid-year arrivals who have come from content-led science teaching. Those students look strong on criterion A and meet criteria B and C with no preparation at all, which a diagnostic across all four exposes in one task.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Long bus journeys mean a tired student in the evening, which suits data processing and graph work better than new content. Marking the previous task at the start of the session is particularly valuable here, because it starts the hour with something concrete.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Dense MYP cohorts where the same investigation deadlines land across many households at once. Families here benefit from booking before the reporting round rather than after it, because the fortnight after reports is when everyone else calls.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island schools with long-settled science departments, and mixed-curriculum streets where MYP students compare work with IGCSE friends. Explaining why a good IGCSE-style answer scores poorly on criterion C is often the first useful thing a session does.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer science departments scaling fast, often with strong criterion A teaching and thinner investigation practice. That profile is very treatable, because the content is already there and what is missing is technique that transfers across all three sciences at once.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Large mainland households with several children and long school runs. A predictable online slot that does not depend on a car being free is the practical difference between a term of sessions happening and a term of sessions being rearranged.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Thin local supply of tutors who have marked MYP science investigations as opposed to teaching science content. Since nearly all the recoverable levels on this subject sit in marking technique, that distinction matters more out here than anywhere else in the emirate.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.modesIntro: Four shapes of MYP sciences support, each producing a different kind of evidence. The one to avoid is a general weekly science hour with no criterion target, because it produces a pleasant relationship and an unchanged report.

modes.title: Criterion C block on the student's own data
modes.description: The highest-yield work in MYP sciences. The student brings data from a school investigation and processes it properly: a correctly structured table, a graph with the right variables on the right axes, a conclusion that answers the question asked, and an evaluation naming one specific methodological flaw. Four to six sessions, with a re-marked task as the measurement.

modes.description: For students who collect good data from a method that could never have earned the marks. Sessions work on writing a hypothesis with reasoning behind it, naming independent, dependent and controlled variables, and writing a method another student could follow without asking a question. Short, and it transfers across all three sciences.

modes.description: Where criterion A is genuinely low, usually in one discipline rather than across the sciences. Typical targets are the mole concept, electricity as a model rather than a formula, and genetics probability. Bounded, and measured by application questions rather than by recall.

sections.heading: Reading a marked MYP science task without being a scientist
paragraphs: A marked investigation is the most informative document in MYP sciences and most parents never look at one, because it appears to require subject knowledge. It does not. The four criteria each divide into strands, and the marking should tell you which strand lost the level. That is a structural fact about the document rather than a scientific one, and checking it needs no chemistry.

Three checks work on any marked science task. First, is the comment tied to a criterion and a strand, or is it a general remark? "Needs more detail" is not feedback against anything; "criterion C, the evaluation strand: the weakness identified is generic rather than specific to this method" is. Second, does the comment separate content error from technique error? Those have completely different remedies, and conflating them is how families end up buying revision for a processing problem.

Third, after reading the marking, can you say in one sentence what the next task should do differently? If yes, the feedback is usable. If you finish the page knowing only that the work was adequate, ask for the strand to be named. That request is entirely reasonable and a tutor who cannot answer it is not marking to the descriptors.

The fourth check is about change rather than about one document. Two marked tasks a fortnight apart, with the same criterion targeted, tell you whether anything is moving. One task tells you where a student is. Two tell you the direction, which is the only thing a paying parent actually needs to know.
bullets: Marking should name a criterion and a strand, not offer a general remark
Content errors and technique errors need opposite responses
You should be able to state what the next task does differently
Two marked tasks a fortnight apart show direction; one shows position

sections.heading: The four sciences criteria, strand by strand
paragraphs: This is the table that should be stuck inside the front of every MYP science folder in Abu Dhabi and almost never is. It sets out what each criterion rewards, the strand inside it where levels most often leak, and what kind of work recovers them. Nothing in it is confidential or complicated; it is simply rarely explained to families in plain language.

The pattern worth noticing is that only one of the four criteria is primarily about knowing science. The other three are about doing it: designing, processing and discussing. That is the structural reason a student who revises hard and scores poorly feels so aggrieved, and the structural reason that revision is often the wrong purchase. Three-quarters of the assessment rewards a skill set that revision does not touch.

The second pattern is the ordering of cost. Criterion C's presentation strands — tables and graphs — move in a session or two because they are conventions. Criterion D moves in two or three because it is a writing structure. Criterion B moves in three or four because it is a habit of thinking about variables. Criterion A, where there are genuine content gaps, is the slowest, because knowledge takes time to build. Families usually assume that order is reversed, which is why so much money goes into revision.

Use the right-hand column to decide what to ask for. If a report shows a low C, asking a tutor for "help with science" will produce content teaching. Asking for processing and evaluation work on your child's own data will produce the thing that moves the level.

table.caption: MYP SCIENCES: THE FOUR CRITERIA AND WHERE LEVELS LEAK

Recall, explanation, and applying science to solve problems
Application to an unfamiliar problem rather than recall
Content repair plus practice on differently framed questions
B · Inquiring and designing
A reasoned hypothesis, variables, and a repeatable method
Hypothesis written as a prediction with no scientific reason

sections.heading: Criterion B: a hypothesis is not a prediction
paragraphs: The single clearest marker of a middle-band criterion B is a hypothesis of the form "I think the reaction will be faster if the temperature is higher". That is a prediction. It states an expectation and gives no scientific reason, and it sits in the middle of the descriptor however correct it turns out to be.

A top-band hypothesis has three parts: the relationship expected, the scientific reasoning that generates the expectation, and ideally a sense of the shape of that relationship. "Increasing temperature will increase the rate of reaction, because particles have greater kinetic energy and collide more frequently with sufficient energy to react, so the rate should rise non-linearly with temperature." Same prediction, entirely different level, and nothing in it requires knowledge the student does not already have.

The variables strand fails differently. Students name the independent and dependent variables confidently and then miss controlled variables they did not recognise as variables at all: surface area in a rate experiment, ambient temperature in a thermal one, light level in a plant investigation. The teaching method that works is to ask what else could change the result, repeatedly, until the student is irritated. That list is the controlled variables, and producing it themselves is what makes it stick.

The method strand has one honest test, which is whether another student could follow it without asking a question. Handing a method to somebody else and watching them get stuck is the fastest teaching available on this strand, and it is work that can be done entirely on screen.

sections.heading: Criterion C, where most MYP science levels are lost
paragraphs: If a single criterion explains most of the lost levels in MYP sciences across Abu Dhabi, it is C. Students collect data competently, often from a well-run school practical, and then process it in a way that discards marks at four separate points. Each of the four is a convention rather than a concept, which is why this criterion is both the biggest loss and the fastest repair.

The table comes first. Raw data belong in a table with units in the headers rather than beside every value, with repeats recorded and a calculated mean where repeats exist, and with the precision of the instrument respected. The graph comes second, and the recurring error is the independent variable on the wrong axis, followed by a line joined dot-to-dot where a trend line was wanted. The conclusion comes third, and here students restate the hypothesis instead of answering the question with reference to the actual data, which is a different sentence.

The evaluation is fourth and is where the top band genuinely lives. A middle-band evaluation lists generic weaknesses: human error, not enough repeats, equipment not accurate. A top-band evaluation names one specific feature of this method, says what effect it had on these results, and proposes an improvement that would address it. Students find this hard not because it is conceptually difficult but because nobody has shown them that "human error" is not a weakness, it is a category.

All four of those can be taught on data the student already has, which is why this work suits online delivery perfectly. The experiment happened at school. The marks were lost afterwards, at a desk, and that is where they are recovered.

sections.heading: The eight-week evidence trail
paragraphs: Evidence-led tutoring needs a schedule of what should exist by when, otherwise it becomes a feeling about progress. What follows is the trail we aim to produce over eight weeks of fortnightly or weekly sessions, and it is deliberately specific enough that a parent can check it in five minutes without understanding the science.

The logic of the order is that the earliest artefacts establish a baseline and the later ones demonstrate movement on the same criterion. A single re-marked task at the end proves nothing on its own, because the task might have been easier. Two tasks of comparable demand, marked against the same strand at week two and week eight, do prove something. That symmetry is the whole design.

Where an artefact is missing, the table says what the absence means rather than leaving you to infer it. A missing baseline mark usually means the first session was spent teaching rather than diagnosing, which feels productive and costs the ability to measure anything later. A missing between-session attempt means the student is not working alone, and no amount of session time compensates for that.

Eight weeks is a realistic horizon for criterion C and criterion D movement. It is short for criterion A content repair, which takes a term, and about right for criterion B habits. Setting the horizon explicitly at the start is what prevents the conversation at week four in which nobody can say whether the money is working.

sections.heading: Criterion D, the one nobody practises
paragraphs: Criterion D asks a student to apply scientific understanding to a real-world problem, discuss the consequences of using science to solve it, and document sources properly. It carries the same weight as the other three criteria. It is also, in most schools, assessed once or twice a year and taught approximately never, which makes it the cheapest level available to almost every MYP science student.

The reason it is cheap is that the task is mostly a writing structure applied to science the student already knows. A usable criterion D response explains the underlying science, states the problem concretely, discusses at least two consequences from different perspectives, acknowledges a limitation or a trade-off, and cites sources that are actually referred to in the text. Students who produce a general essay about how science helps society score in the middle however well written it is.

Abu Dhabi offers unusually good local material for this, which is worth using because specificity is what the top band rewards. Water production and consumption in a desert climate, the energy cost of cooling buildings through a forty-degree summer, coastal and mangrove ecology, air quality, and food supply chains in an import-dependent economy are all genuine problems with real science underneath them and real trade-offs to discuss. A student writing about a local problem they can see has a natural advantage over one writing about deforestation in the abstract.

Source use is the strand that trips up otherwise strong responses. Citing three websites listed at the end without referring to any of them in the text earns little. Using a source, naming what it said, and saying why it is credible earns a great deal more, and it is the direct rehearsal for the referencing standards the Diploma will expect.

sections.heading: Discrete sciences in MYP 4 and 5, and the Diploma behind them
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi IB schools split sciences into Biology, Chemistry and Physics for the final two MYP years, though the timing varies and some keep an integrated course longer. That split is the first point at which a student starts forming a view about which science they are good at, and those views are formed on very little evidence and then act as a constraint for years.

The honest position is that MYP performance in a discipline predicts Diploma performance less well than families assume, because the criteria are the same across the three sciences and most of the difficulty is shared. A student who struggles in Physics and thrives in Biology often has a mathematics issue rather than a physics issue: graph interpretation, rearrangement, proportional reasoning. Fixing that changes the apparent aptitude.

The table maps each discipline onto its Diploma destination and names what a student should have secure before choosing it. Use it as a checklist rather than as a verdict. The common pattern in Abu Dhabi is a student choosing Biology at Higher Level because it felt easier in MYP, and then meeting the Diploma investigation with no processing skills, at which point Biology is not easier at all. The criterion that predicts Diploma science success is C, and it is discipline-independent.

One practical note on timing: the decision about Diploma sciences is usually made late in MYP 5, and the useful preparation is not more content in the favoured subject. It is securing criterion C across whichever sciences the student is taking, because that skill transfers to all of them and is what the Diploma investigation actually marks.

sections.heading: How practical work fits around online lessons
paragraphs: The obvious objection to online science tutoring is that science is practical, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a deflection. The practical work happens at school, in a laboratory, with equipment and supervision. That is correct and appropriate, and no tutoring arrangement anywhere should be substituting for it.

What a session does is everything around the practical. Before an investigation: the hypothesis, the variables, the method, the safety consideration. That is criterion B in its entirety and none of it requires apparatus. After the investigation: the table, the graph, the conclusion and the evaluation. That is criterion C in its entirety and it happens at a desk. Between the two sits criterion A content and criterion D discussion, both of which are screen work by nature.

So the marks in MYP sciences are almost entirely accessible without a laboratory, which is a slightly surprising thing to realise and a genuinely useful one. The one thing a session cannot do is give a student the physical experience of handling equipment, and that is a real gap for a student whose school provides little laboratory time. Where that is the case the honest advice is to raise it with the school rather than to try to buy a substitute, because a home experiment with kitchen equipment teaches habits a marked investigation will penalise.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. A visiting tutor would not bring a laboratory either, so for this subject the comparison is between two people working at a desk, one of whom has priced a car journey into the hour and one of whom has not.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units and the sciences half of them
paragraphs: Most MYP schools assess at least one interdisciplinary unit a year, and sciences is one of the subjects most frequently involved. The unit is graded against its own criteria rather than against the sciences criteria, which is why it appears on a report as a separate line and causes a reliable amount of confusion in Abu Dhabi households every reporting round.

What the unit rewards is synthesis: using understanding from two or more subjects to produce something neither could produce alone, and then reflecting on how the combination changed the outcome. A student who writes a good science section and a good geography section and staples them together has not met the criteria, because nothing was synthesised. That is the standard failure and it is a structural misunderstanding rather than a weakness in either subject.

A tutor's useful contribution here is narrow and worth being honest about. The science content and the science reasoning can be taught. The synthesis has to be the student's own thinking, and the reflection on how the disciplines combined is specifically a reflection on their own process, which nobody else can supply. So sessions on an interdisciplinary unit work best on the science half and on the structure of the reflection, and should stop there.

The practical advice for parents is to read the unit's own criteria when they come home, because they are usually distributed and rarely read. A student who knows the unit is assessing synthesis will write a different piece of work from one who thinks it is assessing science, and that difference is worth more than any amount of content support.
bullets: Interdisciplinary units are graded against their own criteria, not the sciences ones
Two good sections stapled together is the standard failure

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the regulator and the permit
paragraphs: Science investigations are exactly the kind of work someone will offer to produce, so the boundary needs stating rather than implying. An MYP investigation and the Personal Project must be the student's own work. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody should be supplying a hypothesis, writing an evaluation, or fabricating data, and a student who submits an investigation they cannot discuss has been handed a problem rather than helped.

Data fabrication deserves a specific mention because it is the temptation particular to this subject. An experiment that produced messy results is not a disaster; a messy dataset honestly evaluated scores better than a tidy invented one, because the evaluation strand rewards exactly the discussion that messy data make possible. Teaching a student to write about why their results scattered is both the honest route and the higher-scoring one, which is a genuinely convenient alignment.

On the regulator: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, described on the UAE government portal as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK publishes an inspection record for each school. Press reporting also describes ADEK professional-ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE private tuition permit carrying a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school; verify that against ADEK's current policy document. In practice it means your child's own science teacher, who marks the investigation, should not be paid to improve it.

On the permit: private tutoring in the UAE is governed by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The government portal records the permit as granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule, so disregard any amount quoted to you. IB Gram holds no accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no premises in the UAE.
