process.title: Tell us subject, level and the real deadline
process.description: Three pieces of information set a quote: which subject, Higher or Standard Level or which Middle Years year group, and what is actually coming up. A Higher Level Physics block before an internal deadline and a Standard Level Economics weekly slot are different products at different prices, and guessing at either produces a useless number.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: The trial is with the specific tutor rather than a sales call, on a real past-paper question, and nothing is committed afterwards. It is also the point at which you can ask the tutor directly about their MoHRE permit and what they would do with your budget if it were smaller than you had hoped.

process.title: Marked diagnostic before any quote for hours
process.description: One timed paper or criterion-marked task, with every lost mark categorised. This is what decides how many hours are genuinely needed, and it is why we do not publish a rate card: a term quoted before anyone has read your child's work is a guess. Occasionally the honest answer is fewer hours than you expected.

process.title: An itemised quote you can compare
process.description: Rate and session length stated separately, marking and preparation shown as a line, rescheduling notice named, and anything payable up front spelled out. Comparable with any other provider's quote if they will itemise theirs. If a figure is a market band rather than our price, it is labelled as one with its source.

process.title: Review the spend at the halfway point
process.description: At the midpoint of a block or term we compare the running error log against the first diagnostic and say in writing whether the hours are earning their cost. Categories that have closed release their hours; categories that have not moved get a different approach rather than a bigger invoice.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or research source that printed it and the month it was read. Half this market publishes no price, and two ranking providers contradict their own figures on the same page. A dated, attributed band is a lower bar than it sounds and almost nobody clears it.

whyPoints.title: The quote follows the diagnostic
whyPoints.description: We do not price a term before reading a marked script, which is slower to buy and occasionally produces a smaller invoice than expected. It also means the hours are aimed at the category of error that is actually costing marks rather than at the subject that feels worst in the house.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the price and shown as a line
whyPoints.description: Criterion and markband feedback between sessions is the slow part of this work and the most common thing missing from a cheap quote. Ours is included and itemised so the comparison with another provider is like for like. A rate covering only contact time buys less than it appears to.

whyPoints.title: No cost that does not exist
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years. No quote from us includes a permit charge, a registration fee or a materials bundle of past papers and mark schemes, because that material belongs to the boards and should be referenced rather than resold.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one online, so you are not paying for a car
whyPoints.description: Sessions run live over video, one student and one tutor, at Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home rates in this emirate carry a travel loading that is heaviest exactly where specialist supply is thinnest, and removing it is the clearest saving available.

whyPoints.title: No unevidenced number anywhere on this page
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no average score, no student count, no star rating. Not because they would not help the page rank, but because none of them could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method if a parent asked. Apply that test to every provider you speak to.

faqs.question: What is a realistic hourly figure for IB tuition in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Below that, AED 45 to 150 buys budget or university-student support, which suits homework supervision rather than Higher Level exam technique. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those figures come from provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read October 2026, and are the market rather than our price list. For a Higher Level Diploma subject, expect to be choosing within the specialist band rather than below it.

faqs.question: Why do two quotes for the same subject differ by half?
faqs.answer: Usually because one includes marking and preparation between sessions and the other covers contact time only. Criterion-referenced feedback on a written task, or a timed paper marked with the losses categorised, takes real time, and a rate that excludes it is genuinely cheaper and genuinely buys less. The difference does not show until the end of the term when there is nothing to read. The other common cause is level: a Higher Level Diploma subject and a Middle Years one are different products. Ask both providers to itemise rate, session length and marking separately.

faqs.question: Does a longer session work out cheaper per hour?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this emirate it also fits the week better. A ninety-minute slot usually carries a lower per-hour figure than sixty minutes because the preparation overhead is spread further. It also suits the Khalifa City and Al Raha school runs, where students are frequently home only after 16:00 and a single later session is easier to protect than two short ones. The caveat is attention: ninety focused minutes beat two unfocused hours, and for younger students shorter and more frequent genuinely works better even at a higher per-hour rate.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book a whole term up front?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth weighing against what you give up. A term booked up front may carry a lower rate and will certainly secure a slot before the deadline season fills the specialist pool. What it costs you is the ability to stop cheaply if the match is wrong. The compromise most families find useful is a short committed block with a written review at the midpoint, so there is a natural decision point. Ask what happens if you stop after one session, and get the answer before paying anything.

faqs.question: Does where we live in the emirate change what we pay?
faqs.answer: For in-home tuition, substantially. The travel component sits inside the hourly rate whether it is itemised or not, and it is heaviest in Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Mussafah, Al Ain and the Western Region. It is lowest in the central districts around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif, where local tutor supply is densest. For online tuition it changes nothing at all, which is why comparing an in-home quote from a distant community against an online one is comparing two different cost structures rather than two prices for the same thing.

faqs.question: Why would a Higher Level subject cost more than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Because the supply of tutors who have genuinely taught it is smaller, and in Abu Dhabi that is sharper than in a denser market. Diploma cohorts here are small per school, so fewer local teachers have carried a given Higher Level course through to the papers. Higher Level also means an additional paper, more content and more preparation time between sessions. The useful consequence is that the scarcity part of that premium is geographic rather than about expertise, and buying remotely removes it while keeping the specialist.

faqs.question: Should we be paying anything towards the tutor's permit?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge and is valid for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee alongside a two-working-day completion time. Any tutor or agency charging you for it, or citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate, is charging for something that costs nothing. It is also a reasonable question to ask directly: does the tutor hold the permit, and will they show it? Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Does the quoted AED figure include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for a tax registration number if VAT is being charged. This page deliberately does not state the general VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because doing so properly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we do not have one to hand. What we will say is that a quoted figure should be unambiguous about whether it is inclusive, and a provider asserting the tax treatment confidently with no citation is telling you something about how carefully they handle facts generally.

faqs.question: Are the monthly packages advertised online good value?
faqs.answer: Convert them before deciding. A package of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and one of AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions are both real market offers, but the per-hour figures and the tutor levels behind them differ considerably. Divide by the actual hours, then ask whether marking is included and whether the tutor is a subject specialist or a generalist. A package that looks cheap per month and expensive per useful hour is the commonest trap in this market, and the arithmetic takes a minute.

faqs.question: Do rates rise as the papers get closer?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards mostly do not move. The effective price does, because specialist supply is finite and demand is seasonal. Internal assessment and Extended Essay draft deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several Abu Dhabi schools, mock windows cluster similarly, and then the external paper season arrives and everyone calls at once. The same AED 250 buys a different quality of match in October than it does eight weeks before the papers. Booking early is an argument about who is still available rather than a claim about results.

faqs.question: Can we lower the cost by having two children share a tutor?
faqs.answer: Siblings are the one arrangement that genuinely reduces cost per child, and the better version is usually back-to-back individual slots rather than a shared session. Two children in different year groups or on different criteria have almost nothing in common to work on, so a shared hour halves the attention without halving the need. Back-to-back slots keep each child's error log separate while saving on scheduling and often on rate. If both children are in the same subject and year, a genuinely shared session can work.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Diploma subject actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, if the hours are aimed correctly. A marked diagnostic that categorises lost marks as recall, method, command term or timing usually narrows the work to one or two skills rather than a whole subject, and technique losses respond quickly to one-to-one correction. Content gaps are the expensive case and need weeks rather than intensity. The pattern that tends to give the best value across two Diploma years is a diagnostic each term, a short block where it shows a problem, and a core block around the coursework deadlines.

faqs.question: What should I refuse to pay for outright?
faqs.answer: Two things. Any charge connected to the tutor's permit, which is free. And anything described as producing, completing or supplying work that has to be the student's own, whatever it is labelled. One provider in the wider UAE results prices finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. The IB requires that work to be the student's own, submitted through a school accountable for its authenticity, so the risk created by that purchase sits with your child rather than with the seller. A tutor explains criteria, models technique and asks questions about a draft.

faqs.question: Can anyone guarantee an improvement for the money?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is the clearest warning sign available. No tutor can promise a score, a specific grade movement or a university place. Several providers in this market publish satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and student counts with no stated sample, date or method, and one shows two different review figures on the same page. The standard worth applying, to us as much as to anyone, is whether a number could be produced with its sample size, date and method on request. If not, it should not be influencing a purchase.

faqs.question: Are school fees in Abu Dhabi relevant to what we should spend on tuition?
faqs.answer: Practically, yes, because they set what is left. This page does not publish Abu Dhabi fee figures: they vary enormously by school and year group and are set through the emirate's own regulatory process, so a band would be invented. ADEK is the authority that supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and your school publishes its own figures. As context from elsewhere in the country, Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees there would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.closingHeading: Get the quote itemised, then compare
abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.closingBody: The useful next step is not a conversation about rates. It is an itemised quote: hourly figure and session length stated separately, marking and preparation shown as a line, rescheduling notice named, and nothing charged for a permit that is free. Tell us the subject, the level and the real deadline, take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach, and let a marked diagnostic decide how many hours are genuinely needed. Sometimes that is fewer than expected. Sessions run one-to-one over live video at Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: Tutor profiles below name a subject, a level and the components the tutor marks. That combination is what the price is actually for: a Higher Level specialist who marks a named paper costs more than a generalist, and on a narrow component problem they also cost less in total hours.

intro.heading: Why nobody near you will quote a price
paragraphs: The hardest part of buying IB tuition in Abu Dhabi is that the market will not tell you what anything costs. Of the competitor pages examined for this cluster, three publish no price at all, and one of them has a frequently-asked-questions block that asks about the price and then declines to answer it. The two that do publish quote in US dollars, which is not the currency an Abu Dhabi family transacts in, and one of those contradicts its own figure between the visible page and its structured data. So the first thing a parent needs is simply the numbers.

Here they are, as published by the market in 2026. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, runs from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, with travel inside the fee, runs AED 180-500, with Bestimate showing 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising 200-500. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650 and more; BartyED publishes AED 650.

The spread is roughly fourteen-fold between the bottom and the top, which is why a single headline number would be dishonest rather than helpful. What closes the gap is understanding which variables move the price and by how much. Eight of them matter in this emirate: the level, the component, the session length, the group size, whether anyone is travelling, the time of year, the tutor's tier, and the shape of the commitment. Each one has a direction and a rough magnitude, and this page gives both.

Abu Dhabi adds its own cost logic. Private schools here are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and enrolment stretches from the island through the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor out to Al Shamkha, Al Reef and Al Samha. That geography is the single largest driver of the in-home premium: a tutor driving from the island to Al Reef at the afternoon peak spends forty minutes or more each way, which is why in-home work is sold in two-hour blocks and priced above the online bands. Removing the travel removes the surcharge.

IB Gram delivers to Abu Dhabi as one-to-one tuition over live video. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Our own fee depends on subject, level and session length and is quoted after a consultation rather than advertised as one number, and a free trial lesson happens before any payment is taken. Everything else on this page is the market's, with its sources named, so you can price a decision rather than guess at one.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Price varies by programme as much as by subject, because what is being bought changes. Primary work is fluency, Middle Years work is criteria literacy, and Diploma work is component-specific technique with an internal assessment calendar attached. Those are three different products at three different costs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. MYP tuition is usually the cheapest useful IB tuition a family will buy, because the specialism required is narrower: a tutor who can read the school's criteria descriptors and teach against them does not need Higher Level examination experience.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, MYP 4 and MYP 5 are where spending starts, and they are also the stage where spending is most efficient. Fixing criteria literacy and command terms before DP1 costs a fraction of fixing the same problem in DP2, when the internal assessment calendar leaves no room. Families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often make this move a year earlier than families further out, simply because the shorter school run makes a weekly session easy to hold.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of the grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. This is where tuition is most expensive per hour and most variable in total cost, because the number of hours needed depends almost entirely on when the work starts and how narrow the problem is.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi cohorts sit the May session and schools generally run mocks between December and February of DP2. Specialist availability tightens through that window across the whole Gulf, and prices at the top of the market firm up with it. A Higher Level science block bought in October is cheaper and easier to staff than the same block bought in January. Confirm examination and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based learning with no external assessment, so there is no paper to prepare for. Pricing here should reflect shorter sessions: thirty to forty-five minutes twice a week does more for reading accuracy and number fluency than a single hour, and a provider charging an exam-preparation rate for primary work has mispriced the product.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries cluster in the newer mainland communities, where families are least willing to add a second car journey to the afternoon. Two short online sessions a week are affordable in both money and time; the same pattern delivered in-home would require two journeys and is priced accordingly, which is why in-home primary work is almost always sold as one longer visit instead.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject follows scarcity and component difficulty rather than a published tariff. Below is what each subject actually requires of a tutor, which is the thing you are paying more or less for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits in the widest-supplied part of the market, so it is at the lower end of specialist pricing. Higher Level Paper 3 work is a narrower skill, which moves it into the AED 200-450+ band because the pool of people who have marked two extended problems well is small.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology assumed. Supply is reasonable at both levels, and the work most often needed - interpretation sentences next to correct calculations - is quick to teach, so the total hours tend to be low even at a specialist rate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most price-sensitive Higher Level subject in this market, because demand across the Gulf peaks in the same December-to-February window every year. Booking the block in the autumn is the single largest saving available on this subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level organic and energetics carry a concentrated set of lost marks, which is good news for cost: a narrow problem needs few hours. The pool tightens before mocks in the same way Physics does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Reasonable supply at both levels. Most requests are for criterion-based feedback on the scientific investigation rather than content teaching, which is a short block rather than a weekly commitment and prices accordingly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level is widely supplied; Higher Level Paper 3 is not. The internal assessment is three commentaries, which is three short pieces of work rather than one long one, and that shape suits a small number of scheduled sessions.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 support is widely available at mid-market rates. The Higher Level essay is a narrower specialism and is usually bought as a short block at the specialist rate rather than as a weekly session across a year.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: The one subject where a UAE-based tutor is worth paying for specifically, because the Diploma course and the Ministry-mandated Arabic requirement run in the same week and interact. Supply is good inside the UAE and thin outside it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers and a research-based internal assessment. Supply is good, and the common fault - a tool applied without a judgement about the business in the stimulus - is cheap to correct once named.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Music
subjects.description: The thinnest supply in every market, which shows up as waiting time as well as price. These need planning a term ahead, and we would rather decline than place a generalist on a comparative study or a process portfolio.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: What your community does to the price
abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Online delivery removes travel from the fee entirely, but it is worth seeing what the travel would have been, because that is the part of an in-home quote that is not teaching. These are the Abu Dhabi communities we work with and the cost logic in each.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: The shortest real school run in the emirate and the densest local tutor pool, so in-home pricing here is at the lower end of the AED 180-500 band. Even so, the Higher Level specialist shortlist within twenty minutes stays small.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Ten minutes from Khalifa City. Families here often compare a weekly in-home visit against a short online specialist block and find the block cheaper in total because the hours needed are fewer.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: One causeway run. In-home work here is routinely sold as a two-hour minimum, so the real comparison is AED 360-1,000 per visit against a single focused online hour.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Short runs and an early workable slot. The cost advantage here is time rather than money: a session can finish before dinner, which means fewer cancelled and rebooked hours across a term.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Thirty to forty minutes each way at the peak. This is where the in-home premium stops describing teaching, and where the price gap between the two delivery models is at its widest.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: The longest afternoon runs. The subjects most needed here - Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Economics - are the scarcest locally, so a radius search raises the price and lowers the match quality at the same time.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A longer run back from island schools and a steady flow of mid-year arrivals. Transition work is usually a fixed eight to twelve hours rather than an open commitment, which makes it easy to budget.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mixed communities with wide curriculum variety. Group classes are more available here than elsewhere in the emirate, which makes the group-versus-one-to-one cost comparison a live question rather than a theoretical one.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of international provision in Abu Dhabi, with IB continuum schools and British schools offering the Diploma alongside A-Levels. Internal assessment deadlines cluster here, which is why specialist blocks in this corridor are booked earliest and why late booking costs more.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: The island, Saadiyat and Al Reem
schoolClusters.note: Established island schools and newer provision nearby. Several cohorts here offer the Diploma as one route among others at post-16, so families are often pricing two different two-year plans against each other rather than one.

sections.heading: The eight variables that move an IB tuition quote
paragraphs: A fourteen-fold spread between the cheapest and most expensive published hour in this market is not irrationality; it is eight separate variables compounding. Knowing which ones apply to your situation turns an unanswerable question into an estimate you can check. Three of the eight are under your control, three are under the provider's, and two belong to the calendar.

The variables you control are group size, session length and commitment shape. Group size has the largest effect of anything on this page: group rates in Abu Dhabi start around AED 45 per student against AED 200-450 and above for one-to-one specialist work, which is a factor of four to ten. Session length matters less than it looks, because ninety minutes is commonly priced below one and a half times the hourly rate. Commitment shape moves the effective rate down and the risk up, which is why it belongs after a proven six weeks rather than before a first lesson.

The variables the provider controls are tier, specialism and whether anyone travels. Tier is the steepest: the move from a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 to a premium named tutor at AED 500-650 is a tripling, and the question worth asking is what the premium is evidenced by. Examiner status is the most common justification in this market and the least often documented. Travel is the clearest: the in-home band of AED 180-500 against the online band of AED 150-300 is largely a car.

The calendar variables are the ones families notice last. Specialist supply across the Gulf tightens between December and February of DP2 because every school runs mocks off the same session, and prices at the top firm up with it. And the total hours needed shrink the earlier the work starts, which is a far bigger lever on total cost than any hourly rate.

sections.heading: The full AED rate card for this market
paragraphs: This is the table the cluster is missing. Every figure is a published market rate attributed to the provider that published it in 2026, and none of them is IB Gram's price. Ours depends on subject, level and session length and is given after a consultation, because quoting one number for Higher Level Mathematics in DP2 and for MYP 3 science would make the number meaningless.

Read it with two cautions. The first is that a rate describes a seat, not a result: a permit to tutor, which is free and valid for two years from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, tells you somebody may legally teach, and the eligible categories include university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A low rate is often a young tutor, which is entirely appropriate for homework support and entirely wrong for Higher Level Chemistry.

The second is that monthly packages and hourly rates are not comparable until you divide. A package at AED 799 for eight sessions is AED 99 a session, but only if all eight are used, and school holidays in Abu Dhabi eat sessions. Ask what happens to an unused session before taking a monthly plan, and ask whether a pause for mocks or travel is permitted.

Nothing here states a position on the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees, which belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to a tutoring page. What a parent should do is ask any provider whether the number quoted is inclusive, and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: Tuition inside the rest of an Abu Dhabi education budget
paragraphs: Tuition is almost never the largest line in a family's education spending, and seeing it next to the others changes how it gets decided. School fees dominate, and in Abu Dhabi the emirate regulator governs fee levels and the process by which a school may apply for an increase, which is why the school's own published fee schedule is the document to read rather than a third-party summary.

Dubai provides a useful anchor because its numbers are public. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector also gives a sense of scale: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of students against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula.

Against that, Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A full two-year Diploma plan at the middle band is a meaningful sum, and the single most effective way to reduce it is not to negotiate the hourly rate. It is to buy fewer, better-targeted hours earlier, because the number of hours required is the variable with the widest range.

One line families forget is examination entry as a private candidate, which arises for retakes and for students sitting a qualification their school does not offer. That is paid to a centre rather than to a tutor, and the centre publishes it. Ask about it before planning a retake, because it changes whether a single-subject retake is worth the trouble.

sections.heading: What the price does not include
paragraphs: The published hourly rate is the visible part of the cost and rarely the whole of it. The first question to ask is whether marking happens inside or outside the paid hour. A tutor who marks a past-paper section between sessions is doing work you benefit from, and different providers treat that time differently: some include it, some bill it, and some do not do it at all, which is the version that produces no evidence.

The second is session length and what happens at the edges. A sixty-minute booking that starts five minutes late and finishes five minutes early is a fifty-minute lesson. A ninety-minute booking is the right length for sitting a paper section and marking it together, and the wrong length for a Middle Years student. The third is what the fee covers between sessions: a written note, an error log carried forward, or nothing.

Then the commitment questions. What happens to an unused session during an Abu Dhabi school holiday? Can the plan pause during the mock window or a family trip? If the first tutor is not right, is a replacement arranged without an argument, and what happens to hours already paid? None of those is a trick question, and a provider who answers them clearly in writing is giving you more useful information than one who shaves ten dirhams off the rate.

Finally, the questions that are about honesty rather than money. Does the individual teaching hold the private tutor permit, which is free and valid for two years from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation? Is any examiner claim evidenced? Is the tutor employed at your child's school, which reported Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules bar from paid tutoring of their own students? And what exactly will the tutor do with an internal assessment draft, given that a provider offering to produce coursework is offering your child a malpractice finding.

sections.heading: Five ways to spend the same money, and what each buys
paragraphs: Total cost is driven by hours, and hours are driven by how narrow the problem is and when the work starts. The scenarios below are illustrative planning shapes rather than case studies, and they are deliberately priced in hours rather than dirhams so you can apply whichever band from the rate card matches the tutor you are considering.

The pattern they show is consistent. A problem identified early and scoped narrowly costs a handful of hours. The same problem identified in DP2 after the internal assessments are submitted costs more hours and recovers fewer marks, because half the available marks are already locked. And money spread thinly across three subjects reliably achieves less than the same money concentrated in the one subject where the mock showed the most recoverable marks.

The hardest of these for families to accept is the ranking one. Parents rank subjects by anxiety, which puts the hours into the subject that feels worst. A read mock ranks them by marks recoverable per hour of work, which is frequently a different order. Following the second ranking is the cheapest single decision available in DP2.

The second-hardest is stopping. A tutoring plan with no end date drifts, and drifting is expensive in a way nobody notices month to month. Every block we run has a stated finish, and at the six-week review we expect to reduce hours in some subjects rather than only adding them. Families who treat tuition as a subscription rather than as a set of scoped repairs spend two or three times what the repairs would have cost, and they usually cannot say what changed. The honest test is whether you could name, in one sentence, what the next six sessions are for. If you cannot, the hours are not aimed at anything and the money is being spent on reassurance rather than on marks.

sections.heading: Group, pair or one-to-one: cost per recovered mark
paragraphs: Comparing formats on price per hour makes groups look unbeatable and comparing them on outcome makes one-to-one look unbeatable. The useful comparison is cost per recovered mark, and it depends entirely on which problem the student has.

If the problem is a genuine content gap in a topic the whole class found hard, a group class is excellent value. The content can be delivered to twelve students with no loss, and at AED 45-150 per student the arithmetic is obvious. The school's own after-school clinic is better still, because it costs nothing extra and is run by the teacher who set the internal deadline.

If the problem is that marks are disappearing from a specific component, a group class cannot address it, because in a group of twelve the individual error pattern is invisible. The tutor teaches the average student's gap. A student whose issue is a reversed sign convention or a misread Paper 3 stem will sit through content they already know, which is cheap per hour and expensive per mark. Pair sessions sit in between and only work when both students are failing in the same place, which is less common than families hope.

The practical recommendation is to use the formats in sequence rather than choosing one. Free school clinic for cohort-wide content. Group class for a topic the student genuinely missed. One-to-one for component diagnosis and for anything involving an internal assessment, where criterion-level feedback on one student's own draft cannot be given to a group at all.

sections.heading: Making two quotes describe the same thing
paragraphs: Most families collect two or three quotes and compare the numbers, which is the one thing the numbers cannot support. AED 60 from a university student, AED 200 from a qualified subject tutor, AED 270 from a specialist and AED 650 from a named tutor are four different transactions with different session lengths, different group sizes, different marking arrangements and different exit terms. Normalising them takes about six questions.

Start with how many students are in the session, because that single answer can change the effective rate by a factor of four. Then whether the figure is per hour or per session and how long a session is. Then which subject and level the tutor actually teaches and which components they have marked, since "all IB subjects" is not an answer. Then whether the quote is inclusive of any applicable tax, in writing. Then what happens if the first match is wrong. Then whether the individual teaching holds the private tutor permit.

Two answers should end a conversation rather than continue it. The first is any claim of approval, accreditation or licensing from an education authority or an examination board: no tutoring provider in this market holds that, the regulators license schools rather than tutors, and the Dubai institute permit applies to organisations with physical premises. IB Gram holds none of these and claims none. The second is any promise of a specific grade, a point total or a percentage improvement.

Our own answer to the price question is deliberately not a single number. A consultation establishes the subject, the level, the component and the deadline; the fee follows from those; and a free trial lesson happens before any payment is taken. That is less convenient than a figure on a page and it is the only version that does not mislead somebody.

sections.heading: Why starting earlier is the biggest saving available
paragraphs: Every lever on this page except one moves the price by tens of per cent. Timing moves the total by multiples, because it changes how many hours are needed and how many marks are still in play. A Diploma student has eight or nine pieces of internal coursework worth between a fifth and a third of each subject grade. In October of DP1, all of them are still open. In March of DP2, every one of them is submitted.

That means the same money buys different things at different points. Early, it buys content repair, coursework process and two mock seasons, and the hours needed are low because nothing is urgent. Late, it buys paper technique on a narrow set of components, and the hours needed are high because the student is simultaneously revising six subjects. Both purchases are worth making. They are not the same purchase, and a provider who prices them identically is not helping you see that.

The second timing effect is supply. Specialist availability across the Gulf tightens between December and February of DP2, because every school's mock window runs off the same May session. A Higher Level Physics block booked in October is easier to staff and sits lower in the price band than the same block booked in January. For the arts, which are thin everywhere, planning a term ahead is the difference between getting a specialist and not.

The cheapest intervention in the whole two years costs almost nothing: ask the subject teacher which component is losing marks, and read the returned mock script against the mark scheme. Both are free. Doing them first means any money spent afterwards is aimed at something real.

process.title: Do the free diagnostics first
process.description: Ask your child's subject teacher which component is costing marks, and read the most recent marked script against the published mark scheme. Both cost nothing and both narrow the problem. Money spent before this step is money aimed at a guess.

process.title: Get a quote you can compare
process.description: Ask the six questions: students per session, hour or session, subject and level and components, tax position in writing, what happens if the match is wrong, and whether the individual tutor holds the MoHRE permit. Then the numbers mean the same thing.

process.title: Take the free trial before paying
process.description: The trial is a working lesson on the component the script identified, and no payment is taken before it happens. It should end with the tutor stating what the next six weeks would do, in what order, and roughly how many hours that is.

process.title: Buy by the block, not by the term
process.description: Start with an end-dated block scoped to one component rather than an open weekly commitment. A monthly plan has the lowest effective rate and the highest risk, and it belongs after six weeks of evidence rather than before the first lesson.

process.title: Re-price after the school mocks
process.description: Rank the subjects by marks recoverable per hour rather than by how worrying they feel, concentrate the budget on the top of that list, and set an end date. Expect to reduce hours somewhere, not only to add them.

whyPoints.title: The prices are on the page, with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider that published it in 2026, and nothing is presented as our own tariff. Three of the six competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and one of them asks the question in its own FAQ and declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: Our fee follows a consultation, deliberately
whyPoints.description: An hour of Higher Level Mathematics in DP2 and an hour of MYP 3 science are not the same product, so we quote after establishing subject, level, component and deadline. A single headline number for every subject hides exactly the thing you are trying to compare.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the fee
whyPoints.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video, so there is no mileage, no waiting time and no two-hour minimum imposed to justify a journey. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with end dates rather than open commitments
whyPoints.description: Most Diploma problems are component-sized. Scoping a block to one component with a stated finish means the total is known in advance and the plan cannot drift, which is the most common way tutoring budgets get spent without being decided.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: We do not publish satisfaction percentages, tutor headcounts, star ratings or grade guarantees, because we cannot produce the underlying data for any of them. What we publish instead is the market's pricing with its sources and our own method in writing.

whyPoints.title: The permit and regulator position stated plainly
whyPoints.description: The private tutor permit is free, valid for two years and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Education authorities license schools, not tutoring providers. IB Gram holds no regulator approval and does not claim one, and any provider who does should be asked for the number.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition cost near me in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The published 2026 market runs from about AED 45 to AED 650 an hour depending on tier and format. Budget online is AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists are AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one is AED 180-500 with travel inside the fee. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. Our own fee follows a consultation, because subject, level and session length change the product.

faqs.question: Why do two providers quote AED 150 and AED 450 for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different things under the same subject label. At AED 150 you are usually buying a qualified tutor covering syllabus content, possibly in a pair or small group, with little component-level assessment experience. At AED 450 you are buying someone who teaches that subject at that level, has marked the specific paper your child is losing marks on, and can give criterion-level feedback on a coursework draft. Neither is wrong. For a content gap the cheaper option is better value; for eleven marks disappearing from Paper 2 extended response, the expensive option needs fewer hours and recovers more.

faqs.question: Are IB tuition rates quoted per hour or per ninety-minute session?
faqs.answer: Both are common in this market, which is why a quote should never be compared before the question is asked. Ninety minutes is usually priced below one and a half times the hourly rate, so it is often better value, and it is the right length for DP2 work where a paper section needs sitting and then marking in the same sitting. Sixty minutes is right for Middle Years and for Standard Level content work. Also check the real teaching minutes: a session that begins five minutes late and ends five minutes early is not the length you bought.

faqs.question: Does the quoted fee include UAE tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider and get the answer in writing. We deliberately do not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that position belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to a tutoring company, and a page that asserts it without a citation is guessing on your behalf. What a provider can and should tell you is whether the number they have quoted is inclusive or exclusive, and whether they hold a tax registration number. Anything beyond that should come from the authority's own guidance or from an accountant, not from a landing page.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book a whole term in advance?
faqs.answer: Usually yes per hour, and usually a bad idea before the match is proven. Monthly packages in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions, which is a real discount on the hourly bands. The risk is that families who commit before the first lesson routinely overbuy, because nobody yet knows whether the problem is a four-hour problem or a twenty-hour one. Our recommendation is to start with an end-dated block scoped to one component, review at six weeks against fresh marked work, and only then take a longer commitment if the plan has stopped changing.

faqs.question: Do rates rise closer to the May examination session?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, because supply tightens rather than because providers raise a published number. Every school in the Gulf runs its Diploma mocks off the same session, so Higher Level science and Paper 3 specialists are in demand in the same December-to-February window. A family searching in October has a wide choice of specialists at the middle of the band. The same family searching in January has a narrow choice at the top of it, and a longer wait. Booking Higher Level blocks in the autumn term is the simplest saving available on this page.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Diploma subject typically need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which problem the marked script shows, and the range is wide enough that any single figure would mislead. A command-term register problem on extended response is often four to six sessions. A timing fault across multi-part questions is similar. A criterion capping a coursework mark can be two or three sessions plus the student's own rewriting. A genuine content gap across two topics is a term. What drives the total more than anything else is when the work starts: the same problem identified in DP1 needs fewer hours than the same problem identified in March of DP2.

faqs.question: Is a pair session half the price of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, yes; half, rarely. More importantly it is only good value when both students are losing marks in the same place, which is less common than families expect. Two friends taking Physics at Higher Level who both struggle with extended response can share productively. Where one has a data-analysis problem and the other a mechanics problem, each receives half a lesson and both make half the progress, and two shorter individual sessions do more for the same money. We look at both students' recent marked work before agreeing to a shared booking rather than agreeing because it is cheaper.

faqs.question: What hidden extras should I ask about before paying?
faqs.answer: Five. Whether marking between sessions is inside the fee, billed separately, or simply not done. What the real teaching minutes are inside a booked hour. What happens to unused sessions during an Abu Dhabi school holiday. Whether the plan can pause for mocks or a family trip. And what happens to hours already paid if the first tutor is not right. None of these is a trick question, and a provider who answers them clearly in writing is giving you more useful information than one who takes ten dirhams off the rate.

faqs.question: Are Higher Level subjects more expensive than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Standard Level Mathematics and Standard Level sciences are taught by a wide pool, which keeps them in the AED 150-300 band. Higher Level work, and particularly narrow components like Mathematics Paper 3, Economics Paper 3 and the Higher Level English essay, needs someone who has marked that specific paper type, and that pool is small. Those sit in the AED 200-450+ band. The practical response is not to avoid the specialist but to buy them narrowly: a six-session block on one component rather than a weekly slot across a year.

faqs.question: How does Abu Dhabi tuition pricing compare with Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published bands are national rather than emirate-specific, so the headline numbers are much the same. What differs is the in-home premium and the local supply. Abu Dhabi's enrolment is spread from the island through the Khalifa City corridor out to Al Reef and Al Shamkha, and a tutor crossing that at the afternoon peak spends forty minutes or more each way, which pushes in-home work towards the top of the AED 180-500 band and towards two-hour minimum bookings. Online, the geography stops mattering and the price reflects the tutor rather than the drive.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we pause for examinations or travel?
faqs.answer: Ask before you pay, because practice varies and this is where monthly packages catch families out. Our own approach is that end-dated blocks are the default precisely so a pause is not needed: the block finishes, and a new one starts when it is useful. Where a plan is running weekly, pausing for a school mock window or a family trip is normal and expected, since Abu Dhabi households travel more than most. What we would not do is bill for sessions nobody could attend, and what you should insist on from any provider is that the position is written down rather than described on a call.

faqs.question: Does an examiner-marketed tutor justify AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim is evidenced, and in this market it usually is not. Examiner status appears frequently in tutoring marketing and is rarely documented, and it is also often used to imply something it cannot deliver: no examiner has access to unreleased papers, future grade boundaries or marking in progress. We do not describe tutors as examiners for any board unless current status can be shown, and we would not use the label to imply access of any kind. If a premium rests on it, ask what the evidence is before paying the premium.

faqs.question: Is IB tuition more expensive than IGCSE tuition here?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and the published rates show it: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The reason is the coursework load rather than the content. A Diploma student carries eight or nine pieces of internally assessed work with their own criteria and limits, and giving criterion-level feedback on a draft is a narrower skill than teaching syllabus content. Higher Level Diploma components concentrate that further. For a family moving from IGCSE support into Diploma support, expect the hourly rate to rise modestly and the shape of the work to change more than the rate does.

faqs.question: Can we start with a few hours and increase later if it works?
faqs.answer: That is what we recommend, and it is the opposite of what most providers sell. Start by paying per session or buying a short end-dated block scoped to the one component the marked script identified. Review at six weeks against a fresh marked attempt at the same task type. If the evidence shows the named error has stopped recurring, you can decide whether to extend, and only then is a monthly plan at a lower effective rate a sensible purchase. Committing first and diagnosing afterwards is how families end up paying for hours nobody had established were needed.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Price the problem, then price the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.closingBody: The hourly rate is the smaller half of what IB tuition near me in Abu Dhabi will cost you. The larger half is how many hours the problem actually needs, and that is set by how narrowly it has been diagnosed and how early the work starts. Do the two free diagnostics first: ask the subject teacher which component is losing marks, and read the last marked script against the mark scheme. Then send it to us with the subject and level. A specialist will read it before a free trial lesson, no payment is taken before that lesson happens, and every session runs one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Evidence, not reassurance
paragraphs: Most families looking for Diploma Programme support in Abu Dhabi start from the same place: a mid-term report with a number on it, a child who says the lessons are fine, and no way to tell which of those two is right. The number is a teacher's best judgement built from classwork and one or two assessments. It is not a diagnosis. It does not say whether the 5 came from thin content knowledge, from answers that describe when the command term asked for explanation, or from running out of time on the last two questions of Paper 2.

The useful standard for a tutor is therefore not how the sessions feel. It is what exists on paper four weeks in. A marked script with the mark scheme wording beside each dropped mark. An Internal Assessment draft carrying criterion letters in the margin and a note explaining why criterion C is sitting at 1 out of 3. A short written summary every fortnight that a parent who does not teach the subject can still read and act on. Those three artefacts are cheap to produce and almost impossible to fake, which is why this page is built around them.

Abu Dhabi makes this more useful than it would be elsewhere, because the emirate's Diploma cohort is spread thinly across a lot of schools. Enrolment sits in three broad bands: the island schools around Saadiyat, Al Bateen and the Corniche, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Zayed City. A family in one band rarely knows how another band's school marks a mock, so the only reliable comparison is against the IB criteria themselves rather than against a neighbour's report card.

The Department of Education and Knowledge licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, which tells you about the school as an institution. It does not tell you about one student's Paper 1 technique. Those are different instruments measuring different things, and conflating them is how a family at a highly rated school concludes there cannot be a problem while a Chemistry grade slides from 6 to 4 across two terms.

What follows is the whole apparatus: what a tutor can show you after four weeks, how to read a marked Diploma script, what the Internal Assessment criteria actually reward letter by letter, how an Abu Dhabi school arrives at a predicted grade, where the honest limits sit on coursework, and what the tutor pool in this time zone genuinely covers. Sessions are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and the reason that is an advantage rather than an apology is explained below.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Support splits by programme, because the assessment machinery is different in each. These are the four IB stages Abu Dhabi families ask about, with what evidence of progress looks like in each. The Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme are not simply harder and easier versions of the same thing; they reward different behaviours and are marked on different instruments.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Up to 45 points, with 24 the minimum for the Diploma to be awarded and failing conditions attached. Evidence of progress here is specific: marks on past-paper sections under time, criterion scores on an exploration draft, and the gap between a predicted grade and what the scripts actually show.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP students carry a timetable constraint most descriptions ignore. Mandatory UAE subject requirements run alongside the Diploma, and several schools in the emirate also stream Arabic separately, so a DP1 student can be carrying eight or nine timetabled commitments rather than six. When something slips it is usually the subject with the latest internal deadline, not the hardest one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject on a one-to-eight scale, converted to a grade out of seven. The useful work here is translating criterion language into something a student can act on, because an MYP report gives a profile across criteria and most students read only the final number. Progress evidence is a criterion score moving, not a percentage.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP transition is the single most common reason an Abu Dhabi family makes contact. MYP rewards process, reflection and an approach to learning; the Diploma rewards precision under time. A student who was comfortably achieving 6s in MYP Mathematics can land at 4 in the first DP1 test without anything having gone wrong, because the instrument changed.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills and language development. Fewer schools offer it, so families often find little written about it. Support looks much like DP support for the academic courses, with separate attention to the reflective project, which is assessed on its own criteria and is frequently left too late.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school in the emirate runs the Career-related Programme alongside the Diploma, the two cohorts often share teachers and timetables. That can mean the reflective project gets less supervision time than an Extended Essay, which is exactly when an outside reader annotating a draft against the criteria is worth most.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examinations. Tutoring at this stage is narrow and should stay narrow: number fluency, reading comprehension and written expression, taught in short sessions. Evidence of progress is a reading level, a timed arithmetic score, or a piece of writing next to the same task six weeks earlier.
programmes.countryNote: PYP families in Abu Dhabi usually make contact for one of two reasons: a move between curricula mid-year, or preparation for an entrance assessment at a school with a waiting list. Both are short, defined pieces of work rather than ongoing tuition, and that is how they should be quoted.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Nine Diploma subjects account for most of the Abu Dhabi enquiry volume. Each note below says what the component weightings reward and where the marks tend to go, because that is the level of detail a tutor's first session has to work at. Confirm the current weightings for your child's cohort with the school's Diploma coordinator, since subject guides are revised between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries everything above it, and HL adds proof, complex numbers and substantially harder calculus. The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the grade and is marked out of 20 across five criteria. Most lost paper marks come from method not being written down, so partial credit is unavailable when a final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work, with a graphing calculator assumed throughout. Students who chose this course to avoid algebra discover the regression and hypothesis-testing content is unforgiving in its own way. The exploration suits this course well, because real data is easier to find than an original pure-mathematics question.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The 2023 subject guide reorganised the content into themes, and the Internal Assessment is a single scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria worth 20 per cent of the grade. Paper marks go missing in the extended-response questions, where a correct physical idea is stated without the derivation the mark scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms produce the widest mark spread. Students who are secure on the mole and on reaction mechanisms tend to be secure overall. The investigation criteria reward a controlled research design and an honest evaluation far more than an impressive-sounding title, and drafts routinely lose marks on evaluation alone.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty. The command terms do most of the damage: an answer that describes a process when the question asked the student to explain or to compare loses marks on knowledge the student plainly has. Data-based questions are the most coachable component in the subject and are usually the least practised.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation decide grades. A labelled diagram with the axes correct and the shift explained earns marks that prose alone will not, and the top band requires a judgement with a reason attached. HL adds policy analysis and quantitative work that students consistently underestimate until the first full paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, plus the individual oral and, at HL, the HL essay. Marks are awarded against criteria rather than a content checklist, so a student who has never read the criteria is guessing. The oral is the most improvable component because it is rehearsable.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is the hidden skill: knowing which framework the question invites and applying it to the stimulus rather than reciting it. The HL extension and the case study reward preparation done months ahead. Evaluation at the top band needs a conclusion that chooses, not one that lists considerations and stops.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three bonus points. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria with a 4,000-word ceiling, and criterion C on critical thinking carries 12 of those marks. Most drafts are strong on knowledge and weak on critical thinking, which is precisely where the marks are concentrated.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities and what the evidence cycle looks like in each
abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical everywhere because the sessions run over live video. What differs by community is the school cluster a student sits in, which internal deadlines they are working to, and when a session can realistically start. These seven generate most of the Diploma enquiries in the emirate.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A small, high-attainment Diploma cohort where predicted grades are set early and competitively. Families here most often want an outside reading of an exploration draft against the criteria, rather than content teaching, and they want it before the school's first internal deadline.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Fast-growing and school-dense, with students who have often moved curricula within the last two years. The first piece of evidence worth producing here is a timed paper section, because a transferred student's report history is not comparable with their current cohort's marking.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest single source of DP enquiries in the emirate, and the one with the most sibling bookings. Two students in the same household on different Diploma years is common, which makes a fortnightly written note more useful than a verbal update nobody can audit.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa and waterfront households with long school runs and a 17:00 that frequently becomes 17:40. Evening slots after 19:00 are routine here, and a recorded session matters because the student is often tired at the time the session has to happen.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A mixed curriculum catchment where some students are in an American diploma stream and taking IB courses alongside it. Clarifying which assessment instrument a given piece of work is being marked on is the first job, and it is less obvious than it sounds.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the Corniche
regions.note: Long-established schools with experienced Diploma departments and detailed internal marking. Evidence here is best framed as a second opinion: the same script read against the published criteria by someone who did not teach the course.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central, with a high proportion of students carrying Arabic as a first language alongside the Diploma. Timetable load rather than subject difficulty is the usual problem, and the evidence that matters is which commitments are actually slipping.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Bateen and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: The island cluster, where Diploma teaching is long established and internal assessment is tightly managed. Students we support from these schools most often arrive with a draft and a deadline rather than a content gap, which changes what the first session is for.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's densest band of private provision and the source of most Diploma enquiries. A wide attainment spread inside single year groups means two students from the same school can need entirely different evidence from a first session.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island and Yas Island
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with growing Diploma cohorts and a high proportion of students who transferred curricula mid-course. Report history is the least reliable evidence in this cluster, which is why a timed script comes first.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as the context Abu Dhabi families live in. IB Gram has no affiliation with, and claims no endorsement from, any school named on this page.
abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of booking cover almost every Diploma enquiry in the emirate, and they differ in what they produce rather than in how many hours they consume. Choose by the artefact you need at the end, not by the hours at the start.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with fortnightly evidence
modes.description: One subject, one level, one tutor, with a timed section marked every second session and a written note to the parent on the same cycle. This is the default for a student whose grade has drifted and who needs the drift explained before it is treated. It runs across a term rather than in a burst.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes weekly, at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time
Timed questions marked to the published criteria every fortnight
A one-page note to the parent, written to be acted on
Session recordings retained for revision

modes.title: Draft reading against the criteria
modes.description: A defined piece of work rather than ongoing tuition. The student's own exploration, investigation, Extended Essay or reflective project draft is read and annotated criterion by criterion, with the mark allocation named and the gap to the next band explained. The student then revises it themselves, which is the only version that is permissible.
bullets: Criterion letters and mark allocations quoted explicitly
Annotations explain the band gap, they do not supply replacement text
One follow-up session to work through the annotations
Nothing is written, supplied or edited to completion for the student

modes.title: Pre-examination intensive
modes.description: A short block in the weeks before a mock or the May session, built from past-paper volume and timing rather than from content. Sessions are longer and closer together, and the measurement is marks per paper under time. It suits a student whose knowledge is reasonable and whose execution is not.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for four to six weeks
A full paper under exam conditions in the first week, marked
Error log maintained as the planning document
Timing per mark practised explicitly, with a clock visible

sections.heading: What an IB tutor in Abu Dhabi can show you after four weeks
paragraphs: Four weeks is eight sessions at two a week, or four at one. It is enough to produce a complete evidence set and not enough to disguise its absence. If, at the end of four weeks, the only available account of progress is that the student seems more confident, then nothing has been measured and nothing can be corrected. Confidence is a pleasant side effect of competence and a poor proxy for it, and a student can feel markedly better about a subject while scoring exactly the same.

The artefacts in the table below are deliberately cheap. Marking a timed section against a published mark scheme takes a tutor twenty minutes. Annotating a draft with criterion letters takes thirty. Writing a one-page note takes ten. None of it requires a platform, a dashboard or a progress percentage, and the absence of any of it after a month is information in its own right. A tutor who will not produce them is either not marking or not willing to show you what the marking found.

The one artefact worth insisting on is the annotated script itself, returned to you rather than described. A tutor who marks a paper and reports that it went reasonably well has given you their judgement. A tutor who returns the script with three dropped marks circled and the mark scheme phrasing written beside each has given you something your child can use on the next paper, and something you can compare against the same exercise six weeks later.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Diploma script: the difference between a 5 and a 6
paragraphs: A grade boundary is a total, and totals are assembled from small, repeated decisions. Across a full Diploma paper the gap between a 5 and a 6 is commonly six or seven raw marks, which in practice is three questions where an answer stopped one step short. That is the most important thing a parent can understand about a marked script: the difference is rarely a topic, and almost never intelligence. It is a pattern, and patterns are teachable.

The patterns repeat across subjects. Method not written down, so a slip in the final line costs all the marks instead of one. A causal chain with one link missing, which reads perfectly well and scores half. An evaluation that lists considerations without choosing between them, when the top band explicitly requires a judgement. A data question answered from memory rather than from the data supplied. A diagram with unlabelled axes. None of these is a knowledge problem, and all of them are visible in twenty minutes of marking.

The second thing a marked script shows is time. Diploma papers are tight, and a student who writes a beautiful answer to question three has borrowed the minutes from question eleven. Where the last page of a paper is thinner than the first, the problem is triage rather than content, and the remedy is practice with a clock visible and a review afterwards of what the clock cost. Neither of those can be diagnosed from a report card, which is why the first session is a paper rather than a conversation.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: Every Diploma Internal Assessment is marked against named criteria with published mark allocations, and no competitor page in this market names a single one. That is the gap this section fills, because a student who knows criterion C carries three marks and is awarded for personal engagement behaves differently from a student who has only been told to make the work their own and to show some personal engagement.

The two most commonly tutored examples make the point. A Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with the last carrying the largest share. A science investigation under the current guide is marked out of 24 across four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and is worth 20 per cent of the final grade at both levels. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34, with critical thinking alone worth 12.

Knowing the allocation changes where effort goes. Students routinely spend a fortnight polishing presentation, worth four marks, and an afternoon on evaluation, worth six. Drafts arrive strong on description and weak on the criterion that pays most. Reading a draft against the letters, naming the band it currently sits in and explaining the gap is a thirty-minute job that often moves more marks than six hours of content teaching, and it is entirely compatible with the student having written every word of it themselves.

sections.heading: How an Abu Dhabi school arrives at a predicted grade
paragraphs: Predicted grades matter more to Diploma families in this emirate than they do in many places, because university applications to the United Kingdom, North America and the UAE all run on them, and they are set before the examinations exist. A predicted grade is a professional judgement by the subject teacher, moderated across a department and signed off by the Diploma coordinator. It is built from mock performance, classwork, internal assessment marks and the teacher's read on trajectory.

Two things follow. The first is that mock papers carry disproportionate weight, so a student who underperforms in a January mock for reasons of timing rather than knowledge can be predicted below their real level for the whole application cycle. The second is that evidence outside the school counts for very little on its own. A tutor cannot and should not try to change a prediction. What a tutor can do is produce marked work, under time, that a student can take to a teacher as a basis for a conversation about whether the prediction still reflects the trajectory.

That conversation goes better with artefacts than with assertions. A script marked to the published criteria, dated, with the error log showing the same mistakes disappearing over six weeks, is a reasonable thing to put in front of a subject teacher. An assurance that the student has been working hard with a tutor is not, and teachers hear it constantly. The tone matters too: the aim is to give the department information it did not have, not to dispute its judgement.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection ratings and what a school report does not measure
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, according to the UAE government's own portal, and publishes inspection outcomes for them. That is worth knowing and it is also worth bounding. ADEK is named by none of the competitors researched for this market, so parents who do read inspection reports are usually doing it alone and without a sense of what the instrument covers.

An inspection rates a school: leadership, teaching quality, provision, outcomes at a cohort level. It is an institutional measurement. It cannot tell you whether your child's Paper 2 technique is sound, and a school rated highly can contain a student whose Chemistry has quietly slipped two grades across a year. The reverse also holds. Treating the inspection band as a proxy for one student's position is a category error, and it is one that costs families a term of inaction.

The regulator map across the UAE is worth having straight for another reason: families move between emirates and the rules change with them. The table below is drawn from the government's own description of each body. Nothing on it implies any relationship between IB Gram and any regulator, and none exists. ADEK also sets professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, which have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school; verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy before relying on it.
