sections.heading: Grade movement: what can be measured and what cannot
paragraphs: No honest tutor promises a grade. The examination is marked by someone else, the boundaries move between sessions, and the student has five other subjects competing for the same evenings. Anyone promising a specific number in advance should be asked how they propose to control a paper they do not mark, and any page quoting a success percentage without naming the sample size, the date and the method is quoting a figure it cannot support.

What can be measured is narrower and more useful. Raw marks on comparable timed sections, four weeks apart. The count of recurring errors in the log, which should fall. Criterion scores on successive drafts of the student's own Internal Assessment. Completion of the weekly named output. Time taken per mark on a full paper. These are all countable, all dated, and all produced as a by-product of the teaching rather than as a separate reporting exercise.

The honest shape of movement is also worth saying out loud, because expectations set wrongly in September cause families to stop in November. Technique problems move fastest, often inside a month, because the knowledge is already there. Missing foundational content takes a term, because it has to be taught and then integrated. Reading speed and written fluency in a second language move slowest of all and need a year. A tutor who cannot say which of the three your child has is not yet in a position to predict anything.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line around an Internal Assessment draft
paragraphs: This boundary is the most important thing on the page, and it is the thing this market gets worst. At least one site ranking for these queries sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student's own certification rather than on the seller. No amount of time pressure makes that a sensible purchase, and no reputable tutor will go near it.

The permissible version is narrower and genuinely more useful. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards and how many marks it carries. A tutor reads a draft the student has produced and writes down what the criteria would and would not credit in it. A tutor asks the questions that make the student notice the weak link in their own reasoning. Then the student revises it. The revision has to be theirs, in their own words, with their own judgements.

Two practical consequences. Feedback is written rather than spoken, so what was said can be checked later by the student, by a parent or by a coordinator who asks. And board materials are referenced and linked rather than reproduced: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB and are used on screen from the official source, not redistributed as files. Both of those are also what a supervisor would want to see if they asked how the support worked.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and annotates; the student revises their own work
Criterion letters and mark allocations are explained, not applied on the student's behalf
No assessed work is authored, supplied or edited to completion
Feedback is written down so it can be audited by a supervisor or a parent

sections.heading: Delivery, and the Abu Dhabi tutor pool as it actually is
paragraphs: Every session is one-to-one and runs over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates; in-home visiting exists only as an India service. The reason this is a feature rather than a limitation is arithmetic. The number of people who can teach Diploma Physics HL to a high standard and who also live within a reasonable drive of Al Shamkha and are free at 17:30 on a Tuesday is very small. The number who can do it over a shared screen is much larger.

The second reason is subject scarcity. Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is smaller than Dubai's and spread across more schools, so niche combinations are genuinely thin on the ground: Higher Level Further Mathematics, Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish, Design Technology, Music. A family insisting on a tutor who can physically attend is choosing from whoever is nearby, which in these subjects frequently means nobody at all.

Where coverage is thin, you are told before booking rather than after. The options are a specialist in another time zone with the session times that implies, a wait for a slot with a UAE-hours tutor, or a straight no. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without mentioning it. Disclosure costs us some bookings and is the only version of this that survives contact with a parent who asks a direct question.

sections.heading: The first fortnight, step by step
paragraphs: Nothing useful happens until the right document is on the table. For a Diploma student that means three things: the subject and level exactly as the school has entered it, the most recent report or mock mark, and one piece of marked work. The third is the one families forget and the one that matters most, because a teacher's annotations on a real script tell a tutor more in five minutes than a term of report grades.

The free trial lesson comes next and is a real lesson with the tutor who would teach the course, not a sales call with a coordinator. No card details are needed to book it. The point of the trial is to find out whether the student will talk to this particular person about something they find difficult, which is not a question any amount of credential-reading answers.

Session one proper is a timed section of a past paper at the correct level, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches. That produces the error log. Session two works the single highest-cost item in the log. By the end of the fortnight there is a written plan with a named weekly output, a marked script, a log and a one-page note to you. If any of those four is missing at the end of two weeks, the arrangement is not yet doing what this page describes, and that is worth saying out loud rather than waiting until March.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and one marked script
process.description: The subject and level as the school entered them, the latest report or mock mark, and one piece of work a teacher has already annotated. The marked script is the item that shortens the diagnosis most, because it shows how the student's own department is reading their work rather than how a report grade summarises it.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: A real lesson on real content, booked without card details, with the person who would take the course rather than a coordinator. The question it answers is whether the student will say out loud that they do not understand something, in front of this particular adult. Credentials cannot tell you that.

process.title: A timed diagnostic, marked while the student watches
process.description: Session one is a past-paper section at the correct level, marked against the published mark scheme in real time. The student sees each mark awarded and refused, with the scheme's own wording. The output is an error log classified by topic and command term, which becomes the planning document for everything after.

process.title: Fortnightly marked work and a one-page note
process.description: Every second session ends with timed questions, marked and annotated, returned to you rather than described. The note that follows names what moved, what has not, and what the next fortnight targets. It is written so a parent who does not teach the subject can still tell whether the arrangement is working.

process.title: A term review against the error log
process.description: At the end of a term, the first diagnostic is set beside the most recent one and the recurring-error count is compared. That comparison is the only honest measure of whether the hours bought anything. Where it shows little movement, the right response is to change the approach or stop, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not assurances
whyPoints.description: A marked script, an annotated draft, an error log and a one-page note exist after four weeks or the arrangement is not working. Every one of them is cheap to produce and hard to fake, which is exactly why they are the standard this page asks you to hold any tutor to, including ours.

whyPoints.title: Criteria quoted by letter
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment feedback names the criterion, its mark allocation and the band the draft currently sits in. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion letter. A student who knows critical thinking carries 12 of the Extended Essay's 34 marks spends their time differently.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, and measurement instead
whyPoints.description: Nobody here promises a particular number, because the paper is marked elsewhere and the boundaries move between sessions. What is offered instead is comparable timed marks four weeks apart, a falling recurring-error count, and dated criterion scores on successive drafts of the student's own work.

whyPoints.title: The honest line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and annotates. The student writes. Nothing assessed is authored, supplied or edited to completion, and feedback is written down so a supervisor can see how the support worked. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are openly for sale, saying this plainly is a real differentiator.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Some Diploma subjects are genuinely thin in UAE evening hours, and you are told which before anything is paid for. The alternatives are a different time slot, a wait, or a straight no. Filling a Further Mathematics HL request with a generalist helps nobody and is the kind of thing that only surfaces in week three.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Abu Dhabi week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are fixed in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around a school run that often overruns, and recorded so a tired 19:30 session is still usable the next morning. During Ramadan slots move to post-Iftar timing by arrangement rather than being quietly cancelled.

faqs.question: What should an IB tutor be able to show me after a month in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Four things, all on paper. A timed past-paper section marked against the published mark scheme and returned to you rather than summarised. An error log classifying every dropped mark by topic and command term, with the recurring items visible. A written plan naming one output a week. And a one-page note every fortnight saying what moved and what did not. Each takes a tutor under half an hour to produce. If none of them exists after four weeks, nothing has been measured, and a pleasant improvement in confidence is not a substitute. That is the standard to hold any tutor to, including ours.

faqs.question: My son's report says 5 but his teacher says he is capable of 7. Who is right?
faqs.answer: Both, usually, and a marked script settles it in an hour. A report grade is a professional judgement assembled from classwork and one or two assessments; it does not decompose into causes. A timed paper marked against the criteria does. The common finding is that the 5 is built on reasonable content knowledge plus three repeating technique faults: method not written down, causal chains missing a link, and the last two questions thinned out by poor timing. Those move fast because the knowledge is already there. A 5 built on two untaught topics is a different problem and takes a term rather than a month.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating precisely. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses, explains what each criterion rewards and how many marks it carries, reads a draft your daughter has produced and writes down what the criteria would credit and refuse in it. She then revises it herself, in her own words, with her own judgements. What is never acceptable is authoring, supplying or editing assessed work to completion. At least one site ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments; that is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student's certification.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Mathematics exploration worth and how is it split?
faqs.answer: The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the final Mathematics grade and is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with the last of those carrying the largest single allocation. The practical consequence is that students usually spend their time in the wrong place, polishing presentation and treating reflection as a closing paragraph when it is meant to run through the whole piece. Confirm the current allocation against your child's own subject guide with the Diploma coordinator, because guides are revised between cohorts and a stale allocation is worse than none.

faqs.question: Will tutoring change the predicted grade my school has given?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and no tutor should claim otherwise. A prediction is the subject teacher's judgement, moderated in the department and signed off by the coordinator, built mainly from mock performance and internal assessment. What tutoring can produce is evidence to put in front of that teacher: timed scripts marked to the published criteria, dated, with an error log showing the same mistakes disappearing over six weeks. That gives the department information it did not have. It is a conversation about trajectory, not a challenge to a professional judgement, and framing it the second way reliably goes badly.

faqs.question: Does an ADEK inspection rating tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and the two are frequently confused. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, which measure the school: leadership, teaching quality, provision and cohort-level results. That is an institutional instrument. It says nothing about one student's Paper 2 timing or their standing within their own cohort. A strong school can contain a student whose Chemistry has drifted from 6 to 4 over a year, and a weaker rating does not mean a given student is behind. For an individual, the only reliable evidence is a marked script.

faqs.question: How quickly can an Abu Dhabi family get a first Diploma session?
faqs.answer: For the common subjects, two to five days. Mathematics at either level, the three sciences, English A, Economics and Business Management are all reasonably covered in UAE evening hours, with the 17:00 to 19:00 band being the tightest because every family wants it. Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish take one to three weeks. Further Mathematics HL, Design Technology and Music are genuinely thin and can take longer or be unavailable, in which case you are told that rather than offered a generalist. Coverage is disclosed before booking, which no competitor page in this market does.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective as having someone sit next to my child?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work the trade favours video, and the reason is the size of the pool you are choosing from. In-home means choosing whoever teaches the subject, lives within a reasonable drive and is free at 17:30. Online means choosing from everyone who teaches that paper at that level. In Abu Dhabi, where the Diploma cohort is spread across many schools and niche subjects are thin, that difference is often the difference between a specialist and a generalist. Sessions use a shared whiteboard, a document camera so handwritten working is visible both ways, and the real past paper annotated live.

faqs.question: What does a fortnightly note actually say?
faqs.answer: One page, four parts. What was taught, in specification language rather than in adjectives. What the marked work showed, with the raw mark and the comparison against the last one. Which items in the error log have stopped recurring and which have not. And what the next fortnight targets, with the named output. It is deliberately written for a parent who does not teach the subject, which means no jargon without a translation and no progress percentage, because a percentage invented by a tutor measures nothing and sounds like it measures everything.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and already behind. Is it too early for a full plan?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the best possible time, and the reason is the Internal Assessment calendar rather than the content. School-set internal deadlines for explorations, investigations and the Extended Essay cluster in the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2, and a student who is behind on content will meet those deadlines while still behind. Fixing a foundational gap in DP1 costs a term; fixing it in DP2 competes with coursework that has a fixed date. Starting early also means the error log has two full terms of history by the time mock papers set predicted grades.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Abu Dhabi need a government permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with caution.

faqs.question: Can my child's own subject teacher tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: Reported ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before acting on it. The practical point stands regardless: the person who sets your child's predicted grade should not also be paid by you, and an outside reader marking against the published criteria gives you a genuinely independent second opinion rather than a reinforced one.

faqs.question: How long before marked evidence shows real movement?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of three problems the student has, which is why the diagnosis comes first. Technique faults, such as missing working or absent causal links, often clear inside a month because the knowledge is present and only the output is wrong. Missing foundational content takes a term, because it has to be taught and then integrated into harder questions. Reading speed and written fluency in a second language take closer to a year and improve through volume rather than instruction. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the three applies after the first diagnostic should not be predicting timelines.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of a term if the evidence shows little change?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the two diagnostics side by side and the recurring-error count from the log. That comparison is the only honest measure of whether the hours bought anything, and sometimes the answer is that they did not. The useful responses are specific: change the tutor, because the subject match or the personal fit is wrong; change the approach, because the problem was volume and the sessions were treating it as understanding; or stop, because the constraint is sleep, timetable load or something outside a tutor's reach. Continuing without saying any of that is how families spend a year on nothing.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth agreeing the pattern in advance rather than improvising. During Ramadan most Abu Dhabi families move sessions to post-Iftar timing, which usually means a later and shorter slot, and the plan is compressed rather than paused so that the Internal Assessment calendar does not slip. In school examination weeks the sensible move is often a genuine pause, because an extra session the night before a mock produces fatigue rather than marks. Both are arranged by asking. What is not acceptable is a quiet cancellation that leaves a block of paid hours unexplained.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor.closingBody: If you do only one thing after reading this, send the subject and level exactly as the school entered them, the most recent mock mark, and one piece of work a teacher has already annotated. The free trial lesson can usually be sat within the week, with the tutor who would take the course. Session one is a timed paper section marked against the published mark scheme while your child watches, and by the end of a fortnight you will have a written plan, an error log, a marked script and a one-page note. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the coverage position for your subject is stated before anything is booked.

intro.heading: The problem with searching by radius
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Abu Dhabi is usually driven by logistics rather than pedagogy. School finishes somewhere between half past two and half past three. There is a drive home. There is homework, and in most households there is a younger sibling with a different timetable. Inside that window a parent is looking for something that will not collapse the evening, and "near" feels like the variable that protects it. For in-home tutoring it genuinely is: a tutor who lives twenty minutes away can hold a half past four slot, and one who lives forty minutes away cannot.

The difficulty is that proximity and specialism are close to independent of each other. The Diploma Programme is six subjects at two levels with eight or nine pieces of assessed coursework, and the help a student needs is almost always narrower than a subject. A Chemistry HL candidate losing twelve marks on organic mechanisms needs a tutor who marks organic mechanisms. The chance that such a person lives within twenty minutes of Al Reef, is free at half past six, and is not already booked by three other families in the same compound is not high. Searching by radius quietly converts a subject requirement into whoever is available.

Abu Dhabi makes this sharper than most cities because the emirate is spread across three belts that do not behave like one city. The island holds long-established schools and short internal distances, but pickup queues and parking eat the time that distance saves. The Khalifa City, Shakhbout City, Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach corridor is the densest concentration of international provision in the emirate and has a genuinely short internal commute. The newer mainland communities - Al Shamkha, Al Falah, Al Reef, Al Samha, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Baniyas - are where the drives get long and where the local tutor pool thins out at exactly the same time.

Private schools across all three belts are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Families moving in from Dubai sometimes assume the Knowledge and Human Development Authority covers them; it does not. One practical consequence is that school listings, inspection reports and fee rules all sit with a different authority, and so does the school calendar your tutoring plan has to fit around.

IB Gram's answer is to remove distance from the equation entirely. Tutoring for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and we do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What that buys is a different shortlist. Instead of the three tutors willing to drive to Al Samha at seven, you are choosing from the tutors who teach that subject at that level, and the slot is set by your child's school run rather than by somebody else's traffic. The rest of this page is the arithmetic behind that claim: drive times by community, availability by subject, the permit position, and what the local market charges for the travel you would otherwise be funding.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: A request for a tutor near you can come from any stage of the IB, and the stages behave differently when you remove travel from the plan. Younger students benefit from shorter, more frequent sessions, which only works if nobody is driving. Diploma students need a specialist for a specific component, which is where the radius hurts most.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based learning with no external assessment, so the useful work is fluency: reading accuracy, number facts, written structure and the habit of explaining a method. Younger children concentrate better in thirty to forty-five minutes than in an hour, and two short sessions a week beat one long one. That pattern is only affordable in time terms when nobody has to travel to deliver it.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in Abu Dhabi cluster in the newer mainland communities, where families are furthest from the island schools and least willing to add a second car journey to the evening. Two thirty-minute sessions on a shared screen, immediately after the school run, is the shape that survives a term in Al Reef or Al Shamkha.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The marking is the thing families cannot interpret, and a tutor who has read the school's criteria descriptors is worth more than one who merely knows the content. MYP 4 and 5 also carry the personal project and the Diploma subject decision in the same eighteen months.
programmes.countryNote: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor produces most of our Abu Dhabi MYP work, partly because the IB continuum schools sit there and partly because criteria-based marking first becomes decisive in MYP 4. Sessions here can genuinely start at half past four, which makes a weekly rhythm easy to hold.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. This is where the radius problem is most acute: the help needed is component-specific, the specialist pool for Higher Level sciences and Paper 3 papers is thin in every market, and the student has the least spare time in the week to absorb a long commute.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session and the school builds its internal deadlines backwards from it. Confirm the examination window and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring site. What a tutor can plan around confidently is the school's own mock window, usually between December and February of DP2.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Availability is the honest subject of this page, so the grid below is organised by how findable a specialist actually is rather than by syllabus order. Each entry names the level, what the component load looks like, and whether the pool for it is deep or thin in this time zone.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at SL, three at HL, plus a 20-mark exploration. The SL pool is the deepest of any DP subject; the HL Paper 3 pool is noticeably thinner, because marking two long multi-part problems well is a narrower skill than teaching calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a calculator or software assumed throughout. Marks are lost in interpretation rather than method: a correct regression with no sentence about what the gradient means in context scores half of what it could.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two papers plus a 20% scientific investigation. Higher Level Physics specialists are in demand across the whole Gulf at the same points in the year, so this is the subject where a match most often takes a few days rather than a day.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across two papers plus the investigation. Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the heaviest concentration of lost marks at Higher Level, and the pool tightens sharply in the weeks before school mocks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content with heavy command-term weighting. The pool is reasonable at both levels, and the most requested work is criterion-based feedback on the scientific investigation rather than content teaching.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries as the internal assessment, diagrams expected throughout, and at Higher Level a Paper 3 that rewards calculation plus evaluation. Finding someone who marks Paper 3 specifically is harder than finding an economics teacher.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, comparative essay, individual oral, and at Higher Level a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Paper 1 support is widely available; the Higher Level essay is a narrower specialism and often best handled as a short block.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Literature at A level and language acquisition at B level, with oral components to prepare. This is the one subject group where a UAE-based tutor has a real advantage, because the school context and the parallel Ministry requirement both matter.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers and a research-based internal assessment. Marks go missing where a tool is applied mechanically without a judgement about the business in the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals and computational thinking, with a developed solution as the internal assessment. Students build something that works and then under-document the design decisions the criteria reward.

sections.heading: What "near me" actually buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Proximity buys three real things. It buys a tutor who can physically be present, which matters for very young children and for students who genuinely will not engage with a screen. It buys local knowledge: a tutor teaching in Abu Dhabi knows which schools set which internal deadlines and how the emirate's term dates fall. And it buys a kind of accountability that some families value, where the person teaching your child is someone you have met in your own living room.

It costs three things in return, and they are rarely itemised. The first is choice. A twenty-minute radius around Al Samha contains a small number of IB tutors and a smaller number who teach the subject and level you need. The second is money: the in-home band in this market runs AED 180-500 an hour, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and a share of that gap is the driving. The third is reliability. A session that depends on a car arriving at half past six in Abu Dhabi afternoon traffic will be cancelled several times a term, and the cancellations cluster in the weeks when they hurt most.

The trade only looks obvious once you decide what the tutoring is for. If the job is homework supervision and company while a Year 7 student works, proximity is worth a lot and specialism is worth little. If the job is finding the eleven marks disappearing from Physics Paper 2 extended response, specialism is worth almost everything and proximity is worth nothing at all, because the diagnosis happens on a shared screen with the student's own script open.

IB Gram only does the second job, which is why we deliver online and say so before anything else. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and in-home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell at any price; that service exists only in India. sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi school run, and what it does to a half past four session
paragraphs: Most private schools in the emirate release students between about half past two and half past three. Everything after that is geography. The island is compact, but the delay there is not distance: it is the pickup queue and the parking, which routinely add twenty minutes to a five-minute journey. The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor has the shortest real-world school run in Abu Dhabi, because the schools and the housing are in the same place. The mainland communities have the longest, and they get longer at the afternoon peak.

The practical effect is that the same nominal slot means different things in different communities. A half past four session is comfortable in Khalifa City, tight on Saadiyat, and unrealistic in Al Reef. Families who book the slot that sounds convenient rather than the slot that matches the drive lose the first month to late starts, and then conclude that tutoring does not work for them. It is worth being pessimistic about the drive when choosing the time, because the slot you can keep is worth more than the slot you would prefer.

The second thing the calendar does is seasonal. Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier each year and now falls inside the spring term, which is also the window in which most Abu Dhabi schools run Diploma mocks. School days shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but concentration moves to after Iftar for many families. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards; what does not work is pretending the month is the same as any other and then cancelling half of it.

Because our delivery is online, the latest workable slot is set by the student's stamina rather than by a tutor's drive home. That is the one scheduling advantage worth naming plainly: a nine o'clock session in Al Samha is a reasonable request to us and an unreasonable one to anybody who would have to get there.

sections.heading: Why the subject you need is the one nobody local teaches
paragraphs: Scarcity in IB tutoring is not random. It follows the assessment. Standard Level Mathematics is taught by a large number of people because the content is widely held and the papers are conventional. Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, which is two extended multi-part problems, is taught well by far fewer, because it requires someone who has marked that paper type and knows how partial credit falls across the sub-parts. The same pattern repeats in every subject group: the general version is abundant and the component-specific version is thin.

Then the calendar concentrates it. Diploma mocks in Abu Dhabi usually fall between December and February, and the same few weeks see Higher Level science and Paper 3 specialists booked out across the Gulf simultaneously. A family searching in November has a wide choice. The same family searching in January has a narrow one, at a higher price, with a longer wait. Nothing about this is specific to one provider; it is the shape of demand in a market where every school's internal calendar runs off the same session.

The group where scarcity is structural rather than seasonal is the arts. Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film are thin in every market we operate in, and a tutoring site that implies otherwise is telling you something about its marketing rather than its roster. Our position on those subjects is to say no when we cannot cover them properly and to tell a family when that changes, because placing a generalist on a Visual Arts comparative study wastes a term that the student does not have.

Where a UAE-based tutor does carry a genuine advantage is Arabic. Arabic A and Arabic B students in Abu Dhabi are usually also meeting the Ministry requirement for Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, and a tutor inside the system understands how those two bodies of work interact in one week. For that subject we prioritise UAE-based tutors deliberately. For Physics HL we do not, because the component skill matters more than the postcode.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor near you is permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of pages in this market either skip the subject or imply it is optional. It is not. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. The official service is named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That last pair is worth noticing when a very low hourly rate is quoted to you, because a permit says a person may tutor legally; it says nothing about whether they can teach Higher Level Chemistry. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted as unverified.

There is a separate regime for anything with premises and staff. In Dubai, an institute needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. This is why a claim that tutors carry the approval of a Dubai education authority should stop a conversation: that permit is issued to institutions with a physical site, not as a badge an individual or an online platform can carry.

IB Gram is independent. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or registration from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and we would not claim one. What we can tell you is what to ask for and where to verify it, which is the table below.

sections.heading: The one option to rule out: a tutor at your child's own school
paragraphs: Among tutors near you, the most tempting is the one who already teaches your child. They know the student, the cohort, the internal deadlines and the marking. Parents ask for this constantly and it is the single arrangement we will not help with, for reasons that are both regulatory and practical.

On the regulatory side, Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Both of these should be verified against the current policy documents directly rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one. Treat them as the reason to ask the question rather than as the final word on it.

On the practical side, the conflict is obvious once stated. The person marking your child's internal assessment should not be paid by you to improve it. If the grade goes up, nobody can tell whether the teaching or the marking moved, and the student cannot tell either. If a dispute arises about a predicted grade, the family has no independent voice to appeal to. An outside tutor with no stake in the grade can be blunt about a draft in a way an invested teacher cannot.

What a school teacher is genuinely useful for is free. Ask the subject teacher which component is costing marks and what the internal deadline calendar looks like for the next term. That conversation costs nothing, takes ten minutes, and makes any tutoring you then arrange substantially more accurate.

sections.heading: What a match actually involves, and how long it takes
paragraphs: Matching is the step most providers describe in a sentence and most families judge a provider on. The input that makes it fast is a document rather than a conversation: the most recent marked paper, or the returned internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments on it. From a marked script a specialist can usually name the failure pattern before the first session, which means the trial lesson is spent testing a hypothesis instead of gathering history.

Times vary by subject and by season, and the table earlier on this page gives the honest spread. Standard Level Mathematics is usually a two-day match. Higher Level Physics in January is not. Where the wait is real, we would rather give a date than fill the slot, because the cost of a mismatched tutor is not the money; it is the six weeks a family spends hoping it improves before admitting it has not.

Occasionally the only suitable specialist for a narrow component sits outside the Gulf time zone, most often in India, which is an hour and a half ahead of Gulf Standard Time. That moves a session earlier in the Abu Dhabi evening rather than later. We say so at the point of matching rather than after, because a family who agreed to half past eight and then discovers it has to be seven has been told something late that should have been said first.

The trial lesson is the real test and it is free, with no payment taken before it happens. It is a working session, not a sales call: the tutor teaches the component the script identified and finishes by saying what they would do over the next six weeks and in what order. If the match is wrong after it, we change the tutor rather than defend the first choice.

sections.heading: Comparing two quotes without comparing two different things
paragraphs: Hourly rates in this market are not comparable as printed, because they describe different products. AED 60 an hour from a university student, AED 200 from a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 270 from an IB specialist and AED 450 from a named tutor are four different transactions. The published bands for 2026 run roughly: budget online AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; qualified subject tutor online AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; specialists AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+; and premium named tutors AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650.

Before comparing the numbers, make them describe the same thing. Ask how many students are in the session, because a group rate and a one-to-one rate differ by a factor of three or four. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, since ninety-minute sessions are common. Ask who marks the work between sessions and whether that time is included. Ask whether the quoted figure is inclusive of any applicable tax, and get the answer in writing; we do not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees on this page because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to us.

Then ask the questions that are not about money. Which subject and level does the tutor actually teach, and which components have they marked? Will the same tutor take every session, or is the booking with an agency that allocates whoever is free? What happens if the first match is wrong - a replacement, or a refund argument? Is there a written note after each session? Does the provider hold a MoHRE permit for the individual teaching, and will they show it?

One final warning about the top of the market. Examiner status is used heavily in tutoring marketing and is rarely evidenced. We do not describe tutors as examiners for the boards unless current status can be shown, and we would not use examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists. If a page is charging a premium for that claim, ask what the claim is based on.

sections.heading: Where the regulator fits, and what it does not cover
paragraphs: Parents sometimes hope that a regulator vets tutors the way it vets schools. It does not, and understanding the split saves money. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes. Dubai's schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah's sit with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, as does Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

All of those bodies regulate schools. None of them accredits a tutoring platform. The individual tutor sits under the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime instead, and a physical institute in Dubai sits under a separate educational services permit. So when a tutoring page tells you its tutors are approved by an education authority, the claim is either describing a school permit it does not hold or inventing a status that does not exist for its category.

What the regulator is genuinely useful for is checking a school. If a tutoring provider names schools it works with, those schools should appear on the authority's own listing, and the current inspection report should be read there. We deliberately do not publish inspection ratings on these pages, because a rating copied second-hand ages badly and the authority's own site is one click away. The same applies to the federal position on curriculum: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The honest summary is short. Use the regulator to verify schools. Use the ministry permit to verify an individual tutor. Use a marked paper and a trial lesson to verify teaching. Nothing else in this market verifies anything.

process.description: Pick the time that works on a bad traffic day in your community, not the one that works on a good one. Because nobody is travelling to deliver the session, a later slot costs nothing extra, and a slot you can keep every week is worth more than an earlier one you cancel.

process.description: Six weeks is long enough for a pattern to show up in a fresh marked paper and short enough that a plan which is not working gets changed. We expect to reduce hours in some subjects at that review, not only to add them.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the criteria, read drafts and name what is capping a mark. They do not supply prose, pick the research question or submit anything. In a market where completed internal assessments are openly advertised, that boundary protects the student from a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Does it matter where my child's IB tutor is based if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma work it matters much less than the subject match. What the tutor needs is the component skill: someone who has marked Paper 3, or who knows what criterion D of a scientific investigation is asking for. Where location does matter is the clock and the context. A tutor in the Gulf shares your evening, so the slot is simple. A tutor an hour and a half ahead shifts the session earlier. And for Arabic A and Arabic B, a UAE-based tutor genuinely understands how the Diploma course and the Ministry requirement interact in the same week, which is why we prioritise one there.

faqs.question: How do I check whether an IB tutor advertising near me holds a UAE tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Ask them to show it. The private tutor work permit is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge and valid for two years, through the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing on the ministry's app, website and e-services system. A tutor holding one can produce it. If the answer is that the agency handles it, ask which named individual the permit covers. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so ignore any specific figure quoted at you.

faqs.question: I live in Al Reef. Can I find a Physics Higher Level tutor nearby?
faqs.answer: Probably not quickly, and that is the clearest argument on this page. Al Reef sits forty minutes or more from the island schools at the afternoon peak, which shrinks the set of tutors willing to travel there, and Higher Level Physics is one of the thinner specialisms in the whole Gulf. The combination means a local search usually ends with a general science tutor rather than a Physics specialist. Online, the shortlist is everyone who teaches Physics at Higher Level, and the session can start at seven without anybody driving. Expect two to four working days for the match, and longer in the weeks before school mocks.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after school in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on your community. Most private schools release between about half past two and half past three. On Al Reem Island a half past three start is workable. Inside the island, pickup and parking push it to a quarter to four or later, and five o'clock is the common choice. In Khalifa City and Shakhbout City, half past four works. From Saadiyat or Al Raha Beach, five o'clock. From Al Shamkha or Mohammed Bin Zayed City, half past six. From Al Reef, Al Samha or Baniyas, seven. Pick the time that survives a bad traffic day rather than the one you would prefer.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to be matched with a tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Two to five working days for most Diploma subjects, with the spread driven by subject, level and the time of year. Standard Level Mathematics is usually two days. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry and Paper 3 Economics take longer, and in the weeks before school mocks they take longer still, because every school in the Gulf runs mocks off the same May session. The arts are the exception at a week or more. Sending a marked paper with the enquiry shortens all of these, because the match is then made against a component rather than against a subject label.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components are the hardest to staff with a real specialist?
faqs.answer: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film are the thinnest group in every market we work in, and we would rather decline than place a generalist on a comparative study or a process portfolio. After the arts, the difficulty is component-specific rather than subject-specific: Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Economics Paper 3 and the Higher Level English essay are each narrower specialisms than the subjects they sit inside. Sciences at Higher Level are available but squeeze hard around mocks. Standard Level Mathematics, Biology and Business Management are the easiest to cover at short notice.

faqs.question: If the tutor is in another time zone, what does that do to our lesson slot?
faqs.answer: Usually it moves the session earlier in the Abu Dhabi evening rather than later. The specialists we most often draw on outside the Gulf sit in India, which is an hour and a half ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so a session that is eight in the evening for you is half past nine for them. That is workable once or twice a week and unworkable as a nine o'clock slot. We tell you at the point of matching that the tutor sits outside the Gulf, so you can decide before agreeing a time rather than discovering the constraint in week three.

faqs.question: Do you add a travel charge if the tutor is further away?
faqs.answer: No, because nobody travels. Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs one-to-one over live video, so there is no mileage, no waiting time and no minimum session length imposed to make a journey worthwhile. That last point is worth noticing: in-home tutoring in this market is often sold in two-hour blocks because an hour does not justify the drive, which is why the monthly in-home packages advertised here run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online, a single focused hour is a sensible purchase, and a thirty-minute follow-up is too.

faqs.question: How does a shortened Ramadan school day change the tutoring timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and now falls inside the spring term, which overlaps the window when many Abu Dhabi schools run Diploma mocks. School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, but for a lot of households concentration genuinely sits after Iftar. We move the slot for the month and move it back afterwards. The thing that does not work is leaving the timetable unchanged and then losing half the month to cancellations, which costs more continuity than the shift ever would.

faqs.question: We travel between Abu Dhabi and abroad often. Can the same tutor continue?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because delivery is online, the only thing that changes when the family moves is the clock. The same tutor keeps the plan, the error log and the marked work, which is the part that would be lost in a new search. Families who spend summers in another country commonly keep a reduced schedule running through it, and families relocating mid-year avoid the gap that normally opens between leaving one tutor and finding another. For a permanent move out of the UAE, the plan continues with a recalculated slot rather than starting again.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches at a school near us a better choice?
faqs.answer: Not if it is your child's own school. Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the ministry permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same arrangement; both are worth verifying against the current policy documents. The practical objection stands on its own: the person marking the work should not be paid by you to improve it, because then nobody can tell whether the teaching or the marking moved. A teacher at a different school carries no such conflict.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for a tutor, to get a useful answer fastest?
faqs.answer: Four things. The subject and the level, written as the school writes it, since Higher and Standard Level are different assessments. A photograph of the most recent marked paper or returned internal assessment draft, with the teacher's comments visible. The school's next deadline that matters, whether that is an internal assessment date or the mock window. And your community, so the slot is set against a realistic drive. With those four, a specialist can usually name the failure pattern before the trial lesson, which is the difference between a diagnostic first session and an introductory one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IB subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and Physics is the most common genuine pairing, because the overlap in algebraic technique is real. Chemistry and Biology is plausible at Standard Level and rarely sensible at Higher Level, where the component skills diverge. Pairing a science with a humanities subject almost never works well. Where a single tutor can cover both, the continuity is a real advantage: one error log, one plan, one person who notices that a Maths problem is actually a reading problem. Where it cannot, two shorter sessions with specialists beat one generalist hour.

faqs.question: What happens if the match turns out to be wrong after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: We change the tutor. The honest reason this matters is that families do not act on a bad match quickly; they wait, hoping the next session is better, and the cost of that patience is measured in weeks of a two-year programme. So the review point is set in advance at six weeks, against fresh marked work rather than against impressions. If the component that was leaking marks is still leaking them, the plan changes or the tutor does. No payment is taken before the first trial lesson, and a replacement is not treated as a complaint to be defended.

faqs.question: Does ADEK approve or register tutoring companies in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; it does not accredit tutoring providers. Individual tutors sit under the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime instead. In Dubai, an institute with physical premises needs a separate educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. So any tutoring page claiming to be approved by an education authority is either describing a school or institute permit it does not hold, or inventing a status that does not exist for its category. IB Gram holds no regulator approval and does not claim one.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.tutorsIntro: The teachers below run one-to-one IGCSE classes over live video for Abu Dhabi students. Each teaches to a named specification rather than to a general subject, and will tell you which paper codes a student is entered for before the first class is scheduled.

intro.heading: A class is only useful if it matches the specification
paragraphs: Parents searching for IGCSE classes in Abu Dhabi usually mean one of four different things: a group class at a centre, a small online class with a handful of students, one-to-one teaching sold by the hour, or a holiday revision course. These are not variations of one product. They differ in how much individual attention an hour contains, in whether a student can ask a question mid-explanation, and above all in whether the material matches the specification that child is entered for.

The specification question is the one almost nobody asks first, and it decides everything else. Mathematics is Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and those are different papers with different tiering language and a different balance of question types. Physics is 0625 or 4PH1. Chemistry is 0620 or 4CH1. A class advertised as IGCSE Physics with no code attached is a class that will match some of its students and quietly mismatch the rest, and the mismatch shows up in April rather than in October.

Science is where this bites hardest. A student on a combined or co-ordinated award is not studying a shortened version of three separate sciences; the content map is different, and the papers are different. Every term, families discover that their child has spent months revising from separate-science notes for material that will never be examined, while leaving gaps in the parts the award does assess. Establishing the route before booking a class is a ten-minute conversation with the school that saves a term.

There is a second timetable running alongside the international one. Under the federal position, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. Those subjects compete for the same evenings as IGCSE revision, and a class plan that ignores them is a plan that falls over in November.

All classes described here are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run a centre, a campus or a visiting service anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we offer only in India. That is relevant to the comparison this page makes, because the honest case for a one-to-one online class is the individual attention per hour and the match to the specification, not convenience. The sections below give you the code map, the attention arithmetic, the science routes, the Arabic and Islamic Education position and the equivalency rules that outlast all of it. Read the tables as reference material you can take to a parents' evening. The code map, the attention arithmetic and the science routes are all questions a school will answer in one email, and the answers decide which class is worth paying for long before any provider is compared on price.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.programmesIntro: An IGCSE class plan has to fit four things: the board, the tier, the year group and the mandatory subjects running in parallel. The blocks below set out what each of those changes about the class a student should actually be sitting in.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE specifications
programmes.description: Cambridge codes are four digits and they are not interchangeable with anything else: 0580 Mathematics, 0607 International Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0653 Combined Science, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language, 0455 Economics, 0460 Geography, 0470 History, 0478 Computer Science. The tiering language is Core and Extended.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your Abu Dhabi school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications
programmes.description: Pearson codes begin with a 4: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A, 4EB1 English Language B, 4ET1 English Literature. The tiering language is Foundation and Higher. Question style, mark distribution across papers and the balance of short to extended responses all differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and provisional timetables are published ahead of each series. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Build a class schedule against the live official timetable rather than a remembered date, because provisional dates can be revised.

programmes.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
programmes.description: These subjects run alongside the international curriculum rather than instead of it, and the first-language and additional-language Arabic routes assess very different things. For students who later seek UAE equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required IGCSE subjects, which surprises many families and changes how they allocate revision time.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's regulator KHDA publishes detailed mandatory-subject guidelines, including that instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and that classes for Arabs and non-Arabs must be organised separately. Abu Dhabi families should confirm the current requirements with their school and with ADEK, since the emirate publishes its own regulatory framework.

programmes.name: After Year 11: A Level, IB Diploma and equivalency
programmes.description: IGCSE results act as the entry gate to A Level and the IB Diploma Programme, and as part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file for students applying to UAE universities. That makes subject and tier choices in Year 9 consequential for Year 13, particularly where a sixth-form course names a specific IGCSE grade as a prerequisite.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track, Gulf Today reported the requirement as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competing site publishes a six-subject figure; verify on the Ministry's own channel.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for classes in, each with the code that decides which papers are sat. If a provider cannot tell you which code their class teaches, that is the question to settle before any other.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most commonly taught IGCSE class and the most commonly mismatched, because Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher cover overlapping but non-identical content. A class built on one board's past papers leaves a student from the other rehearsing the wrong distribution of question types for a year.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580, with its own assessment structure including an investigation component at the Extended tier. Students entered for 0607 who join a 0580 class are sitting in the wrong room, and the mismatch is usually noticed late because the topic names look familiar.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The practical assessment route is the decision that changes a class plan: an alternative-to-practical paper rewards method description, scale reading and control-variable identification, which are teachable skills and rarely taught at home. Confirm which route the school enters before booking.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Classes here live or die on calculation fluency and extended-response structure. Moles work splits into a mass-to-moles step and a ratio step, and the second is where most marks go; organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition rather than memorised lists.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The widest content map of the three sciences, which makes class pace the critical variable. A group class moving at the mean leaves the quickest students bored and the slowest unable to ask, and Biology is the subject where that gap compounds fastest across a year.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, single or double award
subjects.description: A distinct content map rather than a reduced one. Students on these awards sit their own papers, and revising from separate-science material wastes hours on content that will not be examined while leaving the assessed parts thin. Establish the route before anything else.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading marks go to selection and inference rather than retelling, and the directed writing task is marked on audience and register. Classes work best when every session includes writing produced under time, because the skill is performative rather than informational.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The choice between First and Second Language English sets a ceiling that can affect later applications, so it deserves a deliberate conversation with the school. Within the paper, summary and note-making tasks respond quickly to structured class work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward a definition or a diagram before the explanation, and both award evaluation marks only for a judgement with a stated condition. These are class-friendly skills, because a modelled answer discussed aloud teaches several students at once.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study recall decides Geography and source handling decides History, and both need specific named detail rather than general understanding. A class that produces one case-study card per topic per week leaves a student with a usable revision set by March.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are examined and rarely practised, which makes them reliable class material. The practical components reward methodical evidence in the format the mark scheme expects rather than the shorthand a student invents for themselves.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Two genuinely different qualifications sharing a language. Treating the foreign-language route as an easier version of the first-language one is the most frequent planning error in this emirate, and the routes need separate class material from the start.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.regionsIntro: Class format and class timing are decided more by geography than parents expect. Where a household sits in Abu Dhabi determines whether a centre-based group class is realistic at all, and what time a live class can start on a school night.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Rawdah
regions.note: Close to several of the emirate's long-established British-curriculum schools, so centre-based group classes are a genuine option here. The trade-off is pace: a group moving at the mean rarely matches a student who is strong in two topics and weak in one.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Villa communities with several children per household, where the practical constraint is the family calendar rather than the drive. Staggered one-to-one slots usually work better than a shared group class booked around one child's timetable.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: A corridor where a centre class means a real round trip on a school night. Families here commonly compare the drive plus the class against a live class starting at the same hour with no travel attached at either end.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Smaller catchments with high rates of mid-course transfer between curricula. New arrivals need a specification audit before a class is booked, because the subject names transfer across systems and the papers do not.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise addresses where study space is often shared. A one-to-one class with headphones and a fixed sixty minutes is more workable than a group session that assumes a quiet desk and a printer in the room.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Newer residential pockets with a mixed school map, so siblings are frequently on different boards. A household here can need a Cambridge class for one child and a Pearson class for the other in the same subject.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: The longest drives to the island school cluster. A centre-based class on a weekday evening usually cannot start before seven here once traffic is counted, which is why live classes and weekend slots dominate.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities with large school cohorts and busy mandatory-subject timetables. Class plans here have to account for Arabic and Islamic Education commitments as well as nine IGCSE subjects.

schoolClusters.city: The island cluster: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: Established British-curriculum cohorts entering large IGCSE cohorts each year, with both boards represented across the cluster. Students we support here most often need Mathematics and the separate sciences, and most often arrive knowing their syllabus codes.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Khalifa City to Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: Academies serving the newer residential bands, with a high proportion of students joining mid-course. Specification audits are the most common first request from this cluster, because transferring students often do not know which award they have been entered for.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland: Mussafah, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Shamkha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: Large entries across a wide fee range, with several schools running combined and co-ordinated science awards alongside separate sciences in the same year group. Confirming which award applies is the first step for almost every class here.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.modesIntro: Three ways to take a class, all delivered one-to-one over live video. The differences are in pace, in what the hour produces, and in how a student's own questions get answered, which is the thing group formats cannot guarantee.

modes.title: Specification class, weekly through the course
modes.description: A weekly class following the entered specification in order, with the syllabus code written on the plan. The pace is set by one student's understanding rather than a cohort mean, so a topic already secure is covered in ten minutes and a topic that is not gets a full session. The record shows which specification points have been covered and when.
bullets: Specification points ticked off against the board's own order
Pace set by the student, not by a group average
Questions answered inside the explanation, not afterwards
A coverage record you can compare against the school's scheme of work

modes.title: Topic class, booked where the gap is
modes.description: Single classes aimed at one topic that has not landed, bought as needed rather than on a subscription. Families use this where the school is covering the course competently and one or two topics have gone past without sticking. Each class ends with a short piece of written work that tests whether the gap has actually closed.
bullets: One named topic per class, agreed in advance
No ongoing commitment or minimum block
A short written check at the end of each class
Useful where the school's teaching is otherwise sound

modes.title: Holiday intensive, between terms
modes.description: Concentrated classes in the school holidays, when there is time for several sessions a week. The usual purpose is a catch-up across a whole unit, or a head start on a Year 11 topic known to be difficult. Sessions are shorter and more frequent than during term, which suits content consolidation better than long single blocks.
bullets: Several shorter classes per week rather than one long one
Whole-unit catch-up or Year 11 head start
Scheduled around travel, with slots held in advance
A written summary of what was covered at the end

sections.heading: What an Abu Dhabi parent means by IGCSE classes
paragraphs: The search phrase covers four products with very different economics. A group class at a centre, typically six to fifteen students working through a specification at a shared pace. A small online class, often four to eight. One-to-one teaching sold by the hour. And a holiday revision course, compressed into a week or two. Families usually compare them on price per hour, which is the least informative comparison available.

The comparison that matters is individual attention per hour and match to the specification. In a class of twelve, a student gets perhaps four or five minutes of attention directed at their own understanding across an hour, even with an excellent teacher. That is not a criticism of group teaching; it is arithmetic. Group teaching earns its place when the material is new to everybody and the cohort is genuinely at a similar point, which is exactly the condition a school already provides for six hours a day.

The second question is whether the class teaches the specification your child is entered for. A centre running a mixed class of Cambridge and Pearson candidates has to teach the intersection of two specifications, and the intersection is smaller than either. A class advertised as IGCSE Chemistry without a code is a warning sign rather than a convenience, because somebody in that room is being taught to the wrong paper.

The third is pace. A student who is secure in half a specification and lost in the other half is poorly served by any class moving linearly through all of it, group or otherwise. That is the single strongest argument for one-to-one at this stage of a course: not more attention in the abstract, but the ability to spend forty minutes on electrolysis and four on the states of matter, because that is what this particular student needs this particular week.

sections.heading: The code map: the same subject, two different specifications
paragraphs: Every IGCSE subject exists in more than one version, and the version decides the papers. The table below maps the codes Abu Dhabi families meet most often. Read it with your child's option sheet beside you, because a single nine-subject timetable in this emirate frequently spans both boards, and the mismatch between what a class teaches and what a student sits is almost always invisible until a mock paper arrives.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge tiers are Core and Extended; Pearson tiers are Foundation and Higher, and the content included in each differs. The number of papers sat, how marks are distributed across them, and the balance of short-answer to extended-response questions all vary. In the sciences, the practical assessment route differs again, with alternative-to-practical papers assessing a specific set of method and data skills.

There is also a within-board trap. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are separate syllabuses with different assessment structures, and the topic names look similar enough that a student entered for 0607 can sit happily in a 0580 class for months. Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 are likewise distinct from each other and from the separate sciences.

Getting this right costs one email. Ask the school for each subject's syllabus code, the tier entered, and the series the entry is for. Write the answers on a single sheet and give a copy to any provider before a class is booked. A provider who does not want that sheet is telling you how specific their teaching is going to be.
