sections.heading: Individual attention per hour: the arithmetic of class size
paragraphs: Dividing an hour by the number of students in the room gives a number that explains most of what families observe about classes. In a group of twelve, even distribution gives each student five minutes of teacher attention directed at their own work. In practice distribution is never even: confident students ask and receive, quiet students watch. A student who needs to interrupt an explanation three times to follow it cannot do that in a group without stopping eleven other people.

That arithmetic is why group classes are good value for some purposes and poor value for others. New content delivered to a cohort at a similar level works well in a group, and the school is already doing it. Diagnosis of one student's specific errors, or re-teaching a topic a student has already failed to absorb once, does not work in a group at any price per hour.

Published rates in this market help place the comparison. Providers quote roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Group formats are cheaper per student per hour, as they must be. The useful question is cost per minute of attention your child actually receives, which often inverts the ranking.

One practical test before booking any group class: ask how the provider handles a student who is behind the group on one topic and ahead on another. The answers divide neatly. Some will say the student should book an additional one-to-one session, which is honest and tells you what the group class is actually for. Others will say the class is paced to suit everybody, which is not a thing a class can do.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: This is the most consequential thing on the page and the thing families most often get wrong. IGCSE science comes in separate subjects, a co-ordinated award and a combined award, and they are not versions of each other. The papers differ, the content differs, and the number of IGCSE grades the student walks away with differs, which matters for the five-subject equivalency count later.

The practical damage is always the same shape. A student on Cambridge Combined Science 0653 revises from a friend's separate Chemistry 0620 notes, spends weeks on content their paper will not assess, and arrives in the exam thin on the material it does. Nobody notices because the topic headings overlap. The reverse happens too: a separate-science student using combined-award material finds the depth insufficient and does not know why.

Then there is the practical assessment question, which sits alongside the route. Where a centre enters students for an alternative-to-practical paper, that paper assesses specific skills: reading a scale accurately, identifying independent and control variables, describing a method precisely enough to be repeated, and handling data from an experiment the student never performed. These are teachable in a class and are rarely taught at home.

Ask the school three things in one email. Which award each science is entered for and its code. Which papers that award sits. And which practical route the centre uses. The answers take five minutes to obtain and they determine every past paper your child should be practising for the next two years. Any provider should want them before scheduling a first class.

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 need different classes
paragraphs: The same subject, the same code and the same teacher should produce a visibly different class in each of the two years, and a provider who runs them identically is not paying attention. Year 10 is a content year with a long horizon. Year 11 is an assessment year with a fixed deadline and nine subjects competing for the same evenings.

A Year 10 class should be covering specification points in order, building the vocabulary of the subject, and establishing habits that will still be there in eighteen months: showing working, annotating command words, keeping a topic list with a confidence rating against each item. There is time to go back and reteach, and time for a topic to be learned twice. Mistakes in Year 10 are cheap, which is exactly why Year 10 is the efficient place to spend.

A Year 11 class cannot work that way, because there is not enough time to teach everything a second time. It has to triage: identify which specification points carry the most marks on the papers still to be sat, establish which of those are insecure, and work in that order. That means a Year 11 class should be driven by past papers and mark distributions rather than by the textbook's chapter order.

The handover between them is the summer between Year 10 and Year 11, and it is the most useful two weeks in the course. A short holiday intensive that audits the whole Year 10 specification, topic by topic, produces a priority list for Year 11 that saves more time than any number of weekly hours bought in a panic in February.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Families planning IGCSE classes frequently treat the mandatory UAE subjects as an administrative detail. They are not: they occupy real timetable space, they are assessed, and for some students they are the subjects causing the most distress. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed public guidance on how this works in practice, and it is worth reading even from Abu Dhabi for the shape of the requirement. KHDA states that instructional time for mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for the two groups because of differing curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It also states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited.

That last rule constrains what any tutor can honestly offer. Support for these subjects means working with the material the school uses and the student's own exercises rather than importing a parallel curriculum. Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which publishes its own requirements, so confirm the current position for your child's school rather than assuming the Dubai guidance applies unchanged.

The planning consequence is simple arithmetic. If Arabic and Islamic Education take four or five lessons a week in school plus homework, the evening available for IGCSE revision is smaller than a parent counting nine subjects assumes. A class plan that does not account for it is the plan that collapses in November, usually blamed on the student.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what the certificate has to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which a school-leaving certificate earned on an international curriculum is recognised for use in the UAE, including for university applications. It is a Ministry process rather than anything a tutoring provider performs, and no provider should present it as a service they deliver or an outcome they can assure.

On the British track, the reported requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That exclusion is the detail families most often miss, and it changes which subjects a Year 10 should be protecting.

On the American track, the same reporting sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma no points threshold appears in that reporting, so no figure is published here; it has to be read on the Ministry's own channel.

Two cautions. First, a competing site in this market publishes a six-subject figure for the IGCSE count, which does not match the sourced five, so check the number against the authority rather than against a tutoring page, including this one. Second, nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency; the certificate and the grades are what matter, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Nine subjects is the real constraint on class choice
paragraphs: Most IGCSE students in this emirate are entered for eight to ten subjects, plus the mandatory UAE subjects, plus whatever the school requires in physical education and enrichment. That is the frame inside which any class plan has to fit, and it is why ambitious plans fail more often than lazy ones.

Run the arithmetic honestly on paper. School hours, homework, Arabic and Islamic Education, travel across the emirate, sleep, and one activity the student would resent losing. What remains is the budget for classes and independent revision combined, and for most households it is four to six hours a week in total, not per subject. Two classes plus the independent work they generate usually fills it.

That constraint produces a priority rule. Buy a class where the subject is both weak and still has substantial assessment ahead of it. A subject that is weak but nearly finished is a poor investment; a subject that is strong is not an investment at all. And a student who is weak across six subjects has a workload or method problem, which another class will not solve and may make worse by adding to the load.

The uncomfortable implication is that sometimes the right decision is to drop a subject rather than to add a class. That decision belongs to the school and the family, has entry and timetable consequences, and must be made before the entry deadline, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026. A good provider will raise it where the evidence points that way, even though it costs them the booking.

sections.heading: Choosing between two class offers in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Two providers quoting for the same subject are usually selling different things, and the quote rarely says so. Six questions settle it, and all six can be asked by email before anybody commits money.

Which syllabus code does the class teach, and what happens if my child is entered for a different one? How many students are in the room, and how many minutes of attention directed at my child's own work does an hour contain? What is produced each week that I can read without being a subject teacher? Who teaches the class if the named teacher is unavailable? What does the hourly figure include, specifically whether marking a full paper against the published scheme is inside it or billed separately? And is the person teaching permitted to tutor privately in the UAE?

That last question has a concrete answer. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted at no charge for two years, with eligibility extending to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

There is also a rule worth knowing before asking your child's own teacher for paid classes. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. Treat that as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK policy document before relying on it, but do not build a plan around it.

process.title: Get the code sheet from the school
process.description: One email to the exams officer: the syllabus code, tier and series for every subject. Write the answers on a single sheet. That sheet determines which past papers your child should practise for two years and which class material is relevant, and it is the first thing any provider should ask you for.

process.title: Confirm the science route separately
process.description: Separate, co-ordinated or combined, and which practical route the centre enters. These are different awards with different papers, not grades of difficulty. Getting this wrong is the most expensive mistake available in an IGCSE science plan, and the answer takes five minutes to obtain.

process.title: Decide what the class is actually for
process.description: New content, re-teaching a topic that did not land, or examination mechanics. Each has a different format. Group classes suit the first, one-to-one suits the second, and the third is usually a short block rather than an open-ended weekly booking.

process.title: Use the free first class as an audit
process.description: The first class costs nothing and no card details are taken beforehand. It is spent confirming the specification, checking where the student actually is against it, and producing a short coverage plan. If the audit says the school's teaching is fine and one topic needs an hour, that is what you will be told.

process.title: Compare coverage against the school's scheme of work
process.description: Ask the class for a coverage record listing specification points and dates. Set it beside what the school has covered. Gaps, overlaps and drift become visible in two minutes, and the comparison is the simplest way to tell whether a class is adding anything.

whyPoints.title: Every class names its specification
whyPoints.description: The syllabus code goes on the plan before the first session, because a class that teaches the intersection of two specifications teaches less than either. If your child is entered for 0607 rather than 0580, or 4CH1 rather than 0620, the material is built for that code from the start.

whyPoints.title: Attention per hour, stated as a number
whyPoints.description: A one-to-one class gives one student sixty minutes of attention. A group of twelve gives roughly five, unevenly distributed. We publish that arithmetic rather than describing classes as personalised, because the number is what you are actually buying and it is easy to check.

whyPoints.title: Science routes confirmed before anything is booked
whyPoints.description: Combined, co-ordinated and separate awards have different content maps and different papers. We ask which one your child is entered for before scheduling a class, because a term spent on the wrong award's material is the most costly error in an IGCSE plan.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory subjects counted into the week
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies occupy real timetable space alongside nine IGCSE subjects. A class plan that pretends otherwise collapses in November. We count the actual hours available before recommending how many classes a household should take on.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency described, never promised
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education equivalency rules are set out here with the source named, including the five-subject British-track count that excludes Arabic and Islamic education. It is a Ministry process. No tutoring provider performs it, assures its outcome, or is required for it.

whyPoints.title: One honest delivery format
whyPoints.description: Classes are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram operates no centre or campus in the UAE and sends nobody to a UAE address; visiting tuition is an India-only service. The comparison on this page is therefore about attention and specification match rather than a sales position.

faqs.question: How many students should an IGCSE class have?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the class is for. New content delivered to a cohort at a similar level works in a group of ten or twelve, which is roughly what the school already provides. Re-teaching a topic one student has missed does not work in a group at any size, because the other students have no reason to be there for it. Do the arithmetic before booking: an hour divided by twelve students is about five minutes of attention on your child's own work, and in practice the confident students take more than their share.

faqs.question: Our provider advertises IGCSE Physics with no code. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Because the code decides the papers. Mathematics might be Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics or Pearson 4MA1, and those are three different qualifications with different assessment structures and different tiering language. A class advertised as IGCSE Mathematics has to teach the intersection of whatever its students are entered for, which is narrower than any single specification. Ask the school for the code, tier and series for every subject, write them on one sheet, and give it to any provider before booking a class.

faqs.question: My child takes Combined Science. Can they join a separate Chemistry class?
faqs.answer: Only if the teacher knows which parts to leave out, and most do not without being told. Combined Science has its own content map and its own papers; it is not a shortened version of three separate sciences. Students revising from separate-science notes spend weeks on material their paper will not assess while leaving thin the parts it does. Confirm the award code with the school, then build the practice set from that award's past papers only. That usually frees several hours a week immediately.

faqs.question: Are group classes in Abu Dhabi worth the saving?
faqs.answer: For the right purpose, yes. Published figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and group formats are necessarily cheaper per student. The honest measure is cost per minute of attention your child actually receives, which often reverses the ranking. Ask any group provider one question: what happens to a student who is behind the group on one topic and ahead on another. The answer tells you what the class is really for.

faqs.question: Our school enters nine subjects. How many of those carry the recognition load?
faqs.answer: Schools here typically enter students for eight to ten, but the figure that matters for later recognition is smaller. On the British track, the publicly reported equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One competing site publishes a six-subject figure. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel rather than on any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Is Arabic one of the five subjects the Ministry counts?
faqs.answer: No. The reported rule is explicit that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. They remain part of the school timetable under the federal requirement that private schools teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and they are assessed by the school. What the exclusion changes is planning: the five subjects carrying the recognition load are the international ones, which is worth knowing in Year 10 rather than in Year 13.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach the UAE mandatory subjects as well?
faqs.answer: Support is possible but constrained, and the constraint is worth stating. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai says that for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. The honest form of help is therefore working with the school's own material and the student's own exercises rather than importing a parallel course. Private schools in Abu Dhabi answer to ADEK, which publishes its own requirements, so confirm the position for your child's school directly.

faqs.question: Should classes follow the textbook order or the past papers?
faqs.answer: In Year 10, the specification order, because there is time to build the subject properly and habits formed now last two years. In Year 11, the papers, because there is not enough time to teach everything twice and the question is which specification points carry the most marks on the assessments still to come. A Year 11 class still working linearly through chapter one in January is using a Year 10 plan on a Year 11 timetable, and the student will run out of weeks before the book runs out of chapters.

faqs.question: What should a class produce each week that I can actually read?
faqs.answer: A coverage record naming the specification points taught and the date, a short piece of the student's own written work, and one line on what was not secure. None of that requires you to be a subject teacher to interpret. Set the coverage record beside what the school has covered and the gaps, overlaps and drift appear in two minutes. A provider who offers only a cheerful message after each session is giving you nothing you can check next term.

faqs.question: Is a holiday intensive better value than weekly classes?
faqs.answer: For whole-unit catch-up, often yes, because consolidation benefits from several shorter sessions close together rather than one hour a week separated by school. The most useful intensive in the whole course is the summer between Year 10 and Year 11: a topic-by-topic audit of the Year 10 specification that produces a priority list for Year 11. That saves more time than hours bought in a panic in February. For installing habits, weekly contact across term works better than compression.

faqs.question: My child is entered for 0607 but the class teaches 0580. Does it matter?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are separate syllabuses with different assessment structures, including an investigation component at the Extended tier of 0607. The topic names overlap enough that a student can sit in the wrong class for months without anybody noticing, and the mismatch usually surfaces at a mock. Check the code on the option sheet or with the exams officer, then ask the provider directly which syllabus their material is built from before continuing.

faqs.question: Can one class cover two siblings on the same subject?
faqs.answer: If both are entered for the same code and the same tier and are at a similar point, a pair class is genuinely efficient and gives each student around half an hour of direct attention. If they are on different boards, different tiers or different years, it is a false economy: the teacher ends up alternating, and each child receives a fragmented version of a different course. Check the codes before assuming siblings can share, because households in this emirate frequently have children on different boards in the same subject.

faqs.question: Can we take classes while travelling between terms?
faqs.answer: Yes, since delivery is over live video and slots are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Families travelling in the summer or at Eid usually keep a reduced schedule rather than pausing entirely, because a four-week gap in Year 11 is expensive to recover. The practical approach is to set the slots before travel starts, agree which weeks are off, and keep the coverage record running so the plan picks up where it stopped rather than being rebuilt on return.

faqs.question: Is the person teaching the class permitted to tutor privately here?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted at no charge for two years. Eligible holders include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we ask my child's own school teacher to run private classes?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the private tuition permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK document before quoting it, but do not plan around the arrangement. A different teacher who knows the same specification carries none of that difficulty.

faqs.question: Should we drop a subject instead of adding a class?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a conversation most providers avoid because it costs them the booking. If a student is weak across six subjects, the problem is workload or method and another class will add to the load rather than reduce the problem. Dropping has entry, timetable and equivalency consequences and belongs to the school and family together, and it has to happen before the entry deadline: for the Cambridge March 2027 series that was 27 November 2026. Ask for the evidence either way before deciding.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.closingHeading: Send the code sheet and we will tell you which class you need
abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.closingBody: The first thing worth doing is getting one sheet of paper from your child's school listing the syllabus code, the tier and the series for every subject, plus which award each science is entered for. Send it over and a subject teacher will say which classes actually match it, which format gives the attention that particular student needs, and whether the school's own teaching has already covered the ground. The first class costs nothing and no card details are taken beforehand. If the honest answer is one topic class rather than a weekly booking, that is what you will hear.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.heroSubtitle: IGCSE coaching in Abu Dhabi for the student who already understands the content and still loses marks. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, and the work is examination mechanics: minutes per mark, command words, the shape a six-mark answer has to take, and the difference between a question read quickly and a question read properly. Coaching here is the second half of the job the school has started, aimed squarely at the paper rather than at the syllabus.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: Coaching tutors here are subject teachers who mark to published schemes rather than to instinct. Each works one-to-one over live video, sets papers under exam timing, and spends the session on the mechanics that turn knowledge already in a student's head into marks an examiner can award.

intro.heading: The student knows it. The paper says otherwise.
paragraphs: There is a particular kind of IGCSE student who is badly served by more teaching. They can explain photosynthesis at the dinner table, they did the homework, they revised, and the paper comes back as a grade 5. Nothing in that picture is a content problem, so buying content hours will not move it. What will move it is coaching: the mechanics of reading a question, allocating minutes, answering the command word, and structuring a longer response so that a stranger marking at speed can find the points and award them.

That distinction is the whole of this page. Coaching is not a gentler word for tuition and it is not motivational work. It is a narrow technical craft with four or five teachable components, and the reason it is worth paying for separately is that schools rarely have time for it. A teacher covering the specification for a class of twenty-eight has to prioritise content delivery. The twenty minutes it takes to sit with one student and show them that they spent eleven minutes on a three-mark question is not time a timetable contains.

Abu Dhabi households meet this problem on a particular timetable. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and most of them run mock examinations in the winter term. The mock result is where the coaching problem usually surfaces, because it is the first time the student sits a full paper under something like real conditions. A family in Al Raha Gardens or Mohammed Bin Zayed City often arrives in January with a mock grade, a bewildered student and no diagnosis.

All coaching here is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run visiting tuition anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a household is a service we offer only in India. For coaching specifically that matters less than it might sound, because the work is screen work: a scanned script, a shared mark scheme, a timer, and a student talking through why they chose that answer. Several things coaching needs are easier over video than across a kitchen table.

What follows is the arithmetic of a timed paper, a command-word reference you can keep, the tier conversation that families in this emirate are often not invited into, the structure of a six-week block, and the things coaching genuinely cannot fix. The last of those matters as much as the rest. A student who has not learned the content does not need coaching yet, and selling it to them would be taking money for the wrong product. Read the tables as reference rather than as argument. The minutes-per-mark arithmetic works on any paper your child sits, the command-word list is the published vocabulary both boards mark against, and the six-week structure is there so you can ask a provider to show you their equivalent of it.
bullets: Minutes-per-mark arithmetic worked out for your child's actual papers
Command words drilled against mark schemes, not against definitions
Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tiering checked before a block starts
Six-week blocks with one written output per week that you can read
A clear statement of what coaching will not repair

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Coaching looks different in each of the three stages of an IGCSE course, and different again across the two boards. The blocks below describe what the work actually consists of at each point, because a Year 10 autumn and a Year 11 February are not the same purchase at all.

programmes.name: Year 10: building the habits before the stakes arrive
programmes.description: The cheapest coaching a family will ever buy, because nothing has gone wrong yet. Work focuses on reading a question properly, learning the command-word vocabulary that will be used for two years, and establishing a checking protocol. A Year 10 who learns to allocate minutes against marks carries that habit into every paper they ever sit, in every subject, at no further cost.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools typically confirm tier entries late in Year 10 or early in Year 11, which makes the Year 10 summer assessment unusually consequential here. A coaching block in the spring term, aimed at making that assessment a fair reflection of what the student knows, protects the tier decision that follows it.

programmes.name: Year 11: mocks, mechanics and the run to the series
programmes.description: The year coaching is most often bought and most often bought late. The sequence that works is a diagnosis from the mock scripts, then a block on whichever of the four loss causes dominates, then full papers under time at increasing frequency. Each paper is marked against the published scheme and the timing is audited question by question rather than overall.
programmes.countryNote: Mock season in the emirate's British-curriculum schools usually lands between late November and January, which puts the useful coaching window immediately after the mock papers come back. Families who wait until March are coaching a student who is already revising nine subjects at once and has no capacity left to change a habit.

programmes.name: Resits and the November and March series
programmes.description: A student resitting one or two subjects is the ideal coaching candidate: the content has been taught twice, the gap is usually mechanical, and the timetable has room. Work is almost entirely paper practice with forensic marking, because the task is to convert a known near-miss into marks rather than to learn anything new.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, so a resit rarely means waiting twelve months. Confirm which series your child's centre enters, and the entry deadline for it, before planning any block around it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson: the same subject, different mechanics
programmes.description: Coaching is board-specific in a way content teaching is not. Question style, mark allocation across papers, tier naming and the balance of short to extended responses all differ between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, or between 0620 and 4CH1. A student coached on the wrong board's past papers practises the wrong distribution of question types.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in Abu Dhabi enter students across both boards within one nine-subject timetable, so a single household can need Cambridge mechanics for the sciences and Pearson mechanics for mathematics. Confirm the code for each subject with the exams officer, and keep the practice papers separated by board.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Coaching work is specific to the paper, so the notes below describe the mechanical failure that costs the most marks in each subject rather than the content. In every case the fix is a habit rehearsed under time, not an explanation delivered once.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Method marks are available even when the final answer is wrong, and students who rub out their working throw those marks away. Coaching work: show every line, read the units in the question stem, and translate the wordy later questions into a diagram before attempting any arithmetic.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The recurring mechanical loss is unit conversion inside a rearranged formula, closely followed by graph work where axes are read but not scaled. Coaching work: a fixed four-step layout for every calculation, written out even when the student can do it in their head.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended-response questions on rates, electrolysis and energetics reward a structure: statement, mechanism, consequence. Students who know the chemistry but write a paragraph of observations score in the middle. Coaching work: the three-move structure rehearsed on six past questions until it is automatic.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-value coaching in Biology is command-word discipline, because describe, explain and suggest questions sit next to each other and are marked differently. Coaching work: annotate the command word before writing, and count whether the answer contains as many distinct points as there are marks.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading marks go to selection and inference; students lose them by retelling the passage. The directed writing task is assessed on audience and register as much as on accuracy. Coaching work: plan in two minutes against the marks available, then write to that plan rather than around it.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The summary and note-making tasks respond faster to coaching than almost anything else on an IGCSE timetable, because both are formula-driven. Coaching work: identify the number of required points from the mark allocation, then write nothing that is not one of them.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Evaluation marks need a judgement with a reason attached, and most students stop at the two sides of the argument. Coaching work: a closing sentence that commits to a position and names the condition it depends on, rehearsed on every extended question.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward specific named detail, and both have a timing trap in the longest question. Coaching work: a case-study card per topic with three facts and one figure, plus a rule that the final long answer gets its allocated minutes even if earlier questions overran.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, double or single award
subjects.description: Students on these awards often revise from separate-science materials and practise question types they will never meet. Coaching work: establish exactly which papers are sat, then build the practice set from those papers only, which usually frees several hours a week.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are both examined and both rarely practised, which makes them the cheapest marks on the paper. Coaching work: complete a trace table by hand for every algorithm question, in the format the mark scheme expects rather than a personal shorthand.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Coaching needs a quiet hour and a printer more than it needs a location, but where a household sits in Abu Dhabi still decides when that hour can start and what the evening has to survive. These are the patterns we see most often by area.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Short school runs mean a session can start soon after four, which is the single biggest advantage in coaching work. A student who is not yet tired will sit a full timed paper; one arriving at seven usually will not.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Apartment living with limited desk space, so timed papers often happen at a dining table. Coaching plans here assume the paper is sat in two halves on separate evenings rather than in one ninety-minute block.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa communities where several children in a household are often on different timetables. The practical fix is a fixed coaching slot per child on different evenings, rather than a shared slot that becomes whoever is free.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Families here frequently join mid-course from other systems, which means the first coaching session is usually a diagnostic on question style rather than on content. Transfer students lose marks to unfamiliar paper formats more than to gaps.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: High-rise addresses where evening noise and shared study space are real constraints. Headphones, a defined sixty minutes and a timer on the screen do more for coaching here than any change of tutor would.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Long drives to the island schools make the post-school window tight, so weekend morning coaching is common. A Saturday morning timed paper under proper conditions is worth more than two tired weekday hours.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Newer mainland communities with large school cohorts and busy mock calendars. Blocks here are often booked immediately after the winter mock results, which is the right moment rather than a late one.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: Outer addresses where a weekday session realistically starts late. Coaching works around that by shifting the timed papers to weekends and keeping weekday sessions short and mechanical.

schoolClusters.city: Island schools: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum cohorts with substantial mock programmes, which means coaching requests from this cluster usually arrive with a full set of mock scripts attached. That is the ideal starting point, because the diagnosis takes one reading rather than one term.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Academies serving the corridor between the island and the inland communities, with a high proportion of mid-course transfers. Students we support from this cluster most often need question-style coaching after moving between boards or between curricula.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland cohorts: Mussafah, Al Shamkha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: Large IGCSE entries across a wide fee range, with a correspondingly wide spread of mock marking practice. Coaching here often begins by establishing how a mock was marked before anybody draws a conclusion from the grade it produced.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.modesIntro: Three coaching formats, all one-to-one over live video. They differ in intensity and in what they produce, and the right one depends almost entirely on how many weeks remain before the series your child is entered for.

modes.title: Weekly mechanics session
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week on one paper's mechanics. The session opens with the previous week's timed work, isolates one habit, drills it on four or five past questions and sets the next timed task. Progress is measured in marks recovered on the same question type rather than in topics covered, which makes the record short and readable.
bullets: One paper and one habit per session
Four or five past questions of the same type each week
Timing recorded question by question
A single named task set between sessions

modes.title: Six-week block before a series
modes.description: A structured block aimed at a specific paper in a specific series. Week one diagnoses from scripts, weeks two to four drill the dominant loss cause, week five is a full paper under real timing, and week six is the forensic mark and the plan for the remaining weeks. Each week produces one written output.
bullets: Diagnosis from the student's own marked scripts
Full paper under real timing in week five
Marking against the published scheme, not a summary of it
A written output each week that the parent can read

modes.title: Post-mock diagnostic
modes.description: A single long session, or two shorter ones, immediately after mock results. The tutor reads every script, sorts the lost marks into the four causes, and produces a one-page diagnosis saying which of them is worth paying to fix. Some families stop there, which is a legitimate outcome and sometimes the right one.
bullets: Every mock script read, not just the weakest
Lost marks sorted by cause and counted
A written recommendation that may be to stop
No obligation to book a block afterwards

sections.heading: What changes when a parent says coaching rather than tuition
paragraphs: The two words are used interchangeably in this market, which costs families money. Tuition adds teaching to a student who has not learned something. Coaching converts knowledge the student already has into marks an examiner can award. They have different diagnoses, different session structures and different success measures, and buying the wrong one is the most common way an hour a week produces nothing.

The test is simple enough to run at the kitchen table. Take a question your child lost marks on and ask them to explain the topic aloud, without the paper. If the explanation is sound, the problem is mechanical and coaching is the right purchase. If the explanation falls apart, the problem is content and coaching will frustrate everybody. Most households can run that test across three subjects in half an hour, and it is worth doing before any money is committed.

Mechanical problems come in a small number of shapes, which is why coaching is teachable. A student misreads command words. A student spends eleven minutes on a three-mark question and leaves the last page blank. A student writes everything they know instead of the number of points the marks require. A student knows the method but shows no working, so the method marks are unavailable. A student answers the question they expected rather than the one printed. Five patterns, and nearly every mechanical mark loss in an IGCSE paper fits one of them.

What follows takes those patterns one at a time. The arithmetic of minutes against marks, which almost no student has ever been shown. The command words, which are a published vocabulary rather than a matter of interpretation. The tier question, which quietly caps what coaching can achieve. And the limits, because coaching sold to a student who has not learned the content is a way of taking money while the real problem gets later and more expensive.

sections.heading: Minutes per mark: the arithmetic nobody shows the student
paragraphs: Every IGCSE paper has a mark total and a duration, and dividing one by the other gives a number that changes how a student behaves. On a 100-mark paper in two hours it is roughly 1.2 minutes per mark, which means a six-mark question deserves about seven minutes and a two-mark question deserves about two and a half. Students who have never done this arithmetic routinely spend eleven minutes on a three-mark question because it is interesting, and then run out of paper time entirely.

Work the numbers from the front of your child's actual paper rather than from an average. The useful exercise takes five minutes: write the mark total and the duration at the top of a sheet, divide, then go through a past paper writing the deserved minutes beside each question. The first time a student does this they usually discover that two or three questions they have always laboured over are worth almost nothing, and that the long question at the end, which they habitually rush, is worth a tenth of the paper.

The second half of the technique is a checkpoint rule. Pick the halfway mark by marks rather than by questions, note what time it should be reached, and write that time on the paper before starting. A student who is behind at the checkpoint has a decision to make with forty minutes left rather than a crisis with five. In coaching sessions this single habit is responsible for more recovered marks than any amount of content revision, because the marks were available and simply never got attempted.

Timing work is also the easiest thing to practise without a tutor at all, which is why we say so on the page. A household can run a timed half-paper on a Saturday morning with a kitchen timer and gain most of the benefit. The part that genuinely needs a subject specialist is the marking afterwards, because the question is not how many marks were scored but which of the four causes took each missing one.

sections.heading: The four causes of a lost mark, and only two respond to teaching
paragraphs: Marking a script forensically means attributing every missing mark to a cause, and there are only four worth distinguishing. Content never learned. Method known but carelessly executed. Structure missing on an extended response. Time ran out. Sorting a mock paper this way takes a subject specialist about twenty minutes and tells a parent more than a term of reassuring messages.

The reason the sort matters is that the four causes have different prices. Content gaps need teaching hours, which cost money. Structure needs coaching hours, which also cost money but fewer of them, because structure is a pattern rather than a body of knowledge. Careless execution needs a checking protocol, which costs nothing and which no tutor should be charging to install. Timing needs timed practice, which also costs nothing beyond a printer and a clock.

So a parent reading a forensic mark should expect roughly half the recommendations to be free. If a provider's diagnosis concludes that every problem requires more paid hours in every subject, that is worth noticing. The honest version of this conversation often ends with one subject funded, one habit assigned to the student, and one request made to the school's head of department.

The counts also tell you where the ceiling is. A script losing eighteen marks to content and four to timing is not a coaching case yet, whatever the student says about running out of time. A script losing fifteen marks to structure and two to content is almost pure coaching work, and will usually move within a block. Those two students need different purchases, and the only way to tell them apart is to count.

sections.heading: Command words are a published vocabulary, not a matter of style
paragraphs: Examiners use a defined set of command words and mark to what those words require. Students treat them as synonyms for write about this. The gap between those two positions is one of the largest and cheapest sources of recoverable marks on any IGCSE paper, in any subject, at either tier.

State and give ask for recall with no reasoning, and a student who adds a paragraph of explanation gains nothing for the extra ink. Describe asks what happens, without a cause. Explain asks why, and an answer with no causal link cannot score even if every fact in it is correct. Suggest invites an application of principle to an unfamiliar situation, so a textbook answer often misses. Compare requires both sides in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. Evaluate needs a judgement with a condition attached.

The coaching method is mechanical: before writing anything, underline the command word, write the number of marks in the margin, and then count the distinct points in the answer against that number. A four-mark explain question needs four causal statements, not one good idea expressed at length. Running that routine on twenty past questions moves it from a conscious procedure to a habit, and the habit survives into A Level and beyond.

There is a parental version too. When your child shows you an answer, ask what the command word was and what it required. If they cannot say, you have found something worth paying to fix, and it is faster to fix than any content gap. Boards publish their command-word glossaries in the syllabus documents on their own sites, which is the right place to read them rather than any summary on a tutoring page.

sections.heading: The tier decision quietly caps what coaching can achieve
paragraphs: IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier a student is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade available. Cambridge calls the routes Core and Extended; Pearson calls them Foundation and Higher. The decision is usually taken by the school, sometimes without a conversation with the family, and it is fixed at the entry deadline rather than at the exam. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries fell on 27 November 2026.

Coaching cannot lift a grade above the ceiling of the tier entered, so the tier question has to be asked before a block is bought. Ask the school three things: which tier each subject is entered at, what the reported grade range is for that tier in that syllabus and series, and what evidence the decision rests on. The exact grade range differs by syllabus and board, so confirm it with the exams officer rather than taking a general figure from any web page.

The decision cuts both ways and neither direction is automatically right. A student placed on the higher tier who is losing most marks to unattempted content may be better served by a secure, uncapped-feeling result at the lower tier than by a scrappy one at the higher. A student capped at the lower tier who is scoring near the top of its range every time is being held below what they can do, and the conversation needs to happen while the entry is still open.

Coaching has a specific role here, which is to produce the evidence the conversation needs. Three timed papers at each tier, marked against the published schemes, turn a judgement call into an arithmetic one. That is a fortnight's work, it costs the price of a couple of sessions, and it is a far better use of money than a term of hours spent revising for a tier that was wrong from the start.

sections.heading: A six-week coaching block, week by week
paragraphs: Coaching sold as an open-ended weekly hour tends to drift into tuition within a month, because every session finds something to explain. A block with a fixed length and a written output per week resists that. Six weeks is long enough to install two habits and short enough that nobody loses track of why it was bought.

The sequence matters more than the content. Diagnosis comes first, from the student's own marked scripts rather than from a fresh diagnostic test, because the scripts show behaviour under real conditions. Then three weeks on whichever loss cause dominates the count. Then a full paper under genuine timing, in one sitting, which is the week most families want to skip and the week that produces the evidence. Then a forensic mark and a decision.

Each week should leave something you can read without a subject degree. A page of annotated questions. A timing audit showing minutes spent against minutes deserved. A marked script with lost marks labelled by cause. A one-line statement of the habit being installed. By week six you are looking at a comparison between two full papers sat a month apart, which is as close to proof as this work gets.

What a block should not contain is a syllabus tour. If weeks two to four turn into content teaching, the diagnosis was wrong and the honest move is to say so and change the purchase rather than quietly deliver a different product. We would rather convert a coaching block into two tuition sessions and a free timing protocol than bill six weeks for the wrong thing.

sections.heading: Running a timed paper properly in an Abu Dhabi household
paragraphs: A paper sat with interruptions, with notes open and with a phone on the desk is not evidence of anything. Since the most valuable coaching input is a script produced under real conditions, the household has to be able to create those conditions roughly once a fortnight. In practice that is easier to arrange than families expect, and it is free.

The conditions that matter are few. One sitting, with the full duration on a visible timer. No notes, no phone, no questions answered. The correct equipment on the desk, including whichever calculator the paper allows and nothing else. Reading time budgeted inside the duration rather than taken before the clock starts. And the script handed over unmarked, so the tutor sees exactly what an examiner would see, including the crossings-out.

Geography makes the timing of this awkward in parts of the emirate. A student in Al Shamkha or Al Reef who gets home at half past five has no two-hour window on a school night that is worth anything. The workable pattern is a Saturday or Friday morning paper, with weekday sessions kept short and mechanical. Households on the island, where the school run is short, can often manage a full paper on a weekday evening, which is a real advantage and worth using.

Ramadan and the examination calendar need thinking about in advance rather than in the week itself. Session timing commonly moves later in the evening during Ramadan, and concentration patterns change. A coaching block that spans it should put the full timed papers either side and keep the intervening weeks to short mechanical work, which is easier to sustain and loses nothing.

sections.heading: What coaching cannot fix, and what to buy instead
paragraphs: Coaching does not install content. A student who cannot explain the topic without the paper in front of them needs teaching hours, and coaching bought in that situation produces a well-structured answer about something the student does not understand. The forensic mark is the test: if content is the largest category by a distance, the purchase is tuition and this page is the wrong page.

Coaching also does not repair a wrongly entered tier, an option block that put a student in a subject they never wanted, or eighteen months of missed lessons. Those are school conversations, and the useful output of a coaching diagnostic is sometimes a one-page document a parent takes to a head of department. We would rather produce that document than sell a block that cannot address the cause.

Nor does coaching substitute for sleep, or fix a student who does not want to sit the examination. Both of those turn up regularly and neither responds to another hour a week. A fifteen-year-old revising nine subjects on six hours of sleep will lose marks to concentration failures that look exactly like timing failures on the script, and the fix is not a tutor. An honest diagnostic says so.

The last limit is the one providers rarely state. Nobody can promise a particular outcome from a coaching block, and any figure attached to a promised grade improvement should be treated with real scepticism. What coaching can show you is a comparison between two full papers sat a month apart, marked the same way, with the lost marks counted. That is evidence. Everything beyond it is a sales position dressed as a prediction.

sections.heading: Mock results in the emirate, and what to do in the fortnight after
paragraphs: Mock season in most British-curriculum schools here runs from late November into January, and the fortnight after results is the highest-value coaching window in the year. The scripts are fresh, the student has just experienced real timing, and there is still a full term before the series. Families who act in that fortnight get a different year from families who act in March.

Start by establishing how the mock was marked, because the grade on the cover is often the least informative thing about it. Was the whole paper marked to the published scheme, or marked generously to encourage a cohort, or marked harshly to produce a shock? Was the paper a genuine past paper or a composite? Was it sat under full timing? Schools answer these questions readily and the answers change what the grade means.

Then read the scripts rather than the grades. A student with a grade 5 who lost most marks to timing is in a very different position from a student with the same grade who left whole topics blank. The first is weeks of mechanical work away from a materially better outcome; the second needs content teaching and a frank conversation about how much of it fits before the series.

The output of that fortnight should be short: which subject gets funded, which habit the student installs without help, and what gets raised with the school. Everything else can wait. A family that leaves mock season with those three decisions written down has done more for the summer than one that books four weekly hours in a panic and reviews none of them until April.

process.title: Send the mock scripts, not the mock grades
process.description: Photographs of the marked papers are enough. The grade on the cover tells a coach almost nothing; the crossings-out, the blank final page and the eleven minutes visibly spent on question three tell them everything. Two scripts are usually enough to produce a diagnosis worth acting on.

process.title: Take the free first session as a diagnostic
process.description: The first session costs nothing and no card details are taken beforehand. It is spent counting lost marks by cause and watching the student attempt one question aloud. The output is a recommendation, which is sometimes that coaching is not what this student needs yet.

process.title: Confirm the tier and the series
process.description: Before any block is agreed, confirm with the school which tier each subject is entered at and which series the entry is for. Practice sets, past-paper choices and the whole plan depend on both, and a block built on the wrong tier wastes every hour in it.

process.title: Run a fixed-length block with weekly outputs
process.description: Six weeks, one written output each week, a full timed paper in week five. The block has an end date, which is what stops coaching drifting into open-ended tuition. At the end you have two comparable scripts a month apart rather than a feeling about progress.

process.title: Decide on the evidence, not on the calendar
process.description: Compare the week-one and week-five scripts, marked the same way, with lost marks counted by cause. Continue, change the focus, switch to content teaching or stop. All four are reasonable, and the point of the fixed block is that the decision actually gets made.

whyPoints.title: Coaching and tuition are priced and planned separately
whyPoints.description: We run the content test before selling a coaching block, because the two products fix different problems. A student whose lost marks are mostly content gaps is told that, and offered teaching hours instead. Selling the wrong one is how a term disappears with nothing to show.

whyPoints.title: Half the recommendations usually cost nothing
whyPoints.description: Checking protocols, minutes-per-mark arithmetic and timed half-papers at the kitchen table are free, and they account for two of the four causes of a lost mark. A diagnosis that concludes everything needs paid hours in every subject is a diagnosis worth questioning.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific practice, not generic IGCSE practice
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 reward different things, and a student practising the wrong board's papers rehearses the wrong distribution of question types. Every block names the board and the code, and the practice set is built from that specification only.

whyPoints.title: Blocks end, and the ending is scheduled
whyPoints.description: A six-week block with a written output each week and a decision at the end resists the drift that turns coaching into an indefinite weekly hour. You know when the review is, what will be on the table at it, and that stopping is one of the listed outcomes.

whyPoints.title: No promises about a final grade
whyPoints.description: Nobody can promise a particular outcome, and this page will not pretend otherwise. What coaching produces is two comparable scripts a month apart with the lost marks counted the same way, which lets you judge the work yourself rather than take anybody's word for it.

whyPoints.title: One delivery format, stated clearly
whyPoints.description: Every session is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits in the UAE, and for coaching work the screen is a genuine advantage: scripts, mark schemes and a timer are all more easily shared than passed across a table.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE coaching and IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Tuition teaches content a student has not learned. Coaching converts content they already hold into marks an examiner can award, by working on command words, minutes per mark, answer structure and checking habits. You can tell which one you need in ten minutes: take a question your child lost marks on and ask them to explain the topic aloud without the paper. A sound explanation means the problem is mechanical, so coaching is the right purchase. An explanation that falls apart means content teaching comes first, and coaching bought now will frustrate everybody involved.

faqs.question: How do I work out whether my child is running out of time or running out of knowledge?
faqs.answer: Look at where the blanks are. Time failures leave the final page empty while the early questions are over-written and often over-correct. Knowledge failures leave gaps scattered through the paper, including on short questions near the start. Then do the arithmetic: divide the paper's mark total by its duration, go through the script writing the deserved minutes beside each question, and compare that with what was actually spent. A student who gave eleven minutes to a three-mark question has a timing problem, whatever they say about not knowing the content.

faqs.question: Which command words cost Abu Dhabi students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain and suggest, consistently. Explain requires a causal link for every mark available, so an answer full of correct facts with no because scores far below what the student knows. Suggest asks for a principle applied to an unfamiliar situation, and students reproduce the textbook example instead. Evaluate is the third, because most answers give two balanced sides and never commit to a judgement, which is where the final marks sit. The fix is a routine: underline the command word, write the mark count in the margin, then check the answer contains that many distinct points.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the exams should a coaching block start?
faqs.answer: The fortnight after mock results is the best window, which in most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools falls between late November and January. That gives a full term of runway with fresh scripts in hand. Six weeks before the papers is still useful for timing and structure work, because both move quickly. Two weeks before is too late to install a habit, and at that point the honest advice is to practise timed papers at home and spend nothing. Habits need repetition under pressure, and pressure without repetition just produces anxiety.

faqs.question: Can coaching lift my child above the grade cap on their tier?
faqs.answer: No. The tier entered sets a ceiling, and no amount of coaching passes it. Cambridge entries are Core or Extended, Pearson entries are Foundation or Higher, and the reported range differs by syllabus and series, so confirm the exact range with your child's exams officer rather than trusting a general figure. Tier entries are fixed at the entry deadline, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series was 27 November 2026. If you think the tier is wrong, the conversation needs marked evidence and it needs to happen before that date.

faqs.question: Is group coaching as effective as one-to-one for exam technique?
faqs.answer: For some of it, yes. Command-word work and minutes-per-mark arithmetic generalise well, so a small group learning them together loses little. The forensic marking does not generalise, because the whole value is in attributing one student's missing marks to one student's causes, and that cannot be done usefully for six children at once. A workable compromise is group work on the mechanics and one-to-one for the script review. Ask any group provider how many minutes of individual script feedback each student actually receives per session.

faqs.question: What should a coaching session actually look like from the next room?
faqs.answer: Mostly the student talking and writing, with a timer visible on the screen. A session where the tutor explains for fifty minutes is a tuition session wearing a coaching label. You should hear questions, pauses while something is attempted, and a mark scheme being read aloud. At the end there should be one named thing to practise rather than a list. If you can hear a lecture, ask what the diagnosis was and which of the four causes of a lost mark this hour was addressing.

faqs.question: How do we run a proper timed paper at home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: One sitting, full duration on a visible timer, no notes, no phone, nobody answering questions, and only the equipment the paper permits. Reading time comes out of the duration rather than before it. Hand the script over unmarked so the tutor sees what an examiner would see, crossings-out included. On the island a weekday evening often works; in Al Shamkha, Al Reef or Mussafah the school run usually makes a weekend morning the only honest option. A fortnightly paper is enough.

faqs.question: Does a mock grade tell us how the real series will go?
faqs.answer: Less than families assume, and the first question is how the paper was marked. Some mocks are marked strictly to the published scheme, some generously to encourage a cohort, some harshly to produce a shock, and the three produce very different grades from identical work. Ask the school which it was, whether the paper was a genuine past paper and whether it was sat under full timing. Then read the scripts rather than the grade: a timing failure and a content gap can produce the same number on the cover.

faqs.question: My child writes too much and still loses marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost always a command-word and mark-allocation problem. On state and give questions, extra explanation earns nothing and costs minutes that the later questions needed. On explain questions, volume without causal links scores at the bottom of the band. The fix is counting: a four-mark question needs four distinct creditable points, and anything beyond that is donated time. Coaching work here is quick, because the student already has the material; they have simply never been shown how the marks are distributed across an answer.

faqs.question: What does a coaching block cost in Abu Dhabi, and who sets that price?
faqs.answer: Published figures in this market put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are other providers' numbers, quoted so you can place any figure you are offered. A six-week block is six of those hours plus marking time. Ask specifically whether forensic marking of a full paper is inside the hourly rate or billed separately, because that is where quotes diverge.

faqs.question: Can one coach handle both Cambridge and Pearson papers for the same subject?
faqs.answer: A strong specialist usually can, but test it on detail rather than principle. Ask which tiering language each board uses, how marks are distributed across the papers in each specification, and what differs in question style between them. Precise answers mean they have taught both. Vague answers about IGCSE in general mean they have taught one and assumed the other is close enough, which produces practice sets drawn from the wrong board and a student rehearsing question types they will never meet.

faqs.question: Does coaching help a student who has simply stopped working?
faqs.answer: Not on its own, and a provider who says otherwise is selling you something. Disengagement shows up on a script as scattered careless losses that look like timing failures, and another paid hour a week rarely changes it. What sometimes helps is a very short block with a visible, winnable target, such as recovering the method marks on one question type, because a fifteen-year-old who sees a number move will often re-engage. If that does not land within a few sessions, the issue is not a tutoring issue.

faqs.question: Can sessions move later during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning for it in advance works better than improvising in the week itself. Session times commonly shift later in the evening, after Iftar, and concentration patterns change for most students. The practical approach for a coaching block that spans it is to place the full timed papers either side of the month and keep the intervening weeks to short mechanical work, which is easier to sustain and loses nothing from the plan. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can be rescheduled week by week.

faqs.question: What happens if the diagnosis says coaching is the wrong purchase?
faqs.answer: We say so, in writing, and you owe nothing for the diagnostic session. The usual alternatives are content teaching hours in one subject, a free checking protocol the student installs themselves, a timed-paper routine at home, or a conversation with the school's head of department, for which we will produce a one-page summary of the script evidence. Several of those cost nothing. A diagnostic that only ever concludes that more paid hours are needed is not a diagnostic, and it is worth testing any provider against that.

abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Send two scripts and we will count the marks by cause
abu-dhabi/igcse-coaching.closingBody: The fastest way to find out whether IGCSE coaching in Abu Dhabi will help is to send two marked papers, ideally mock scripts, and tell us the board and code for each subject. A subject specialist counts the lost marks, sorts them into content, method, structure and timing, and says which of those is worth paying to fix. The first session costs nothing and no card details are taken beforehand. If the count says content teaching comes first, or that a free timing protocol would do most of the work, that is what you will be told.

abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.tutorsIntro: The tutors below run intensive Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE blocks for Abu Dhabi students over live video. Each profile names the board, the tier and the papers they work on, because an intensive block is auditable only when its target is specific.

intro.heading: Start from the script, because that is the only thing in this process that cannot flatter anyone
paragraphs: Intensive IGCSE tutoring is bought in a hurry and assessed, if at all, by how the sessions felt. That is the wrong instrument. A student can enjoy ten hours of teaching, understand everything said in them, and sit the same paper with the same losses, because understanding in the room and performance under timed conditions are different skills. The only reliable instrument is written work with marks on it, read before the block and again during it, and this page is organised around that one idea.

The reason the script matters more than the conversation is that IGCSE marks are lost in patterns, and the patterns are visible on paper and invisible in discussion. A candidate who leaves the last two questions blank has a timing problem worth several marks regardless of subject knowledge. A candidate who writes the correct final figure with no working visible has forfeited step marks that were available. A candidate who answers "explain" questions as though they said "describe" is losing a mark allocation in every paper simultaneously. None of those students would say anything in a conversation that revealed the cause; all of them are obvious within ten minutes of a marked script.

This matters especially in Abu Dhabi, where intensive blocks are usually bought in the window between January mocks and a February or June series, and where the enquiry almost always arrives as a subject rather than as a diagnosis. "She needs help with Chemistry" is where the conversation begins. "She lost nine marks on Paper 4, six of them to unshown working in mole calculations and three to the last question not attempted" is where it becomes buyable, because now the hours have a target and the result is measurable.

Measurability also protects you from the other failure mode, which is the block that continues out of nervousness. If the record shows the same error recurring in week one, week two and week three, more hours will not change it: either the diagnosis is wrong or the practice between sessions is not happening, and both are conversations rather than purchases. A tutor willing to say that is worth considerably more than one who books another six sessions, and you should be able to see it in the notes without understanding the subject.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For an evidence-led block this has one concrete advantage: a shared screen puts the marked script in front of both student and tutor at the same time, annotated live, which is how a loss gets attributed to a cause rather than discussed in the abstract.
bullets: A marked script before the block, not a report and not a topic list
Three or four named losses, each attributed to a cause, with marks estimated
Session notes that name the correction rather than the topic
A re-sat paper under the same timed conditions as the measurement
