abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage, because what is being measured changes. These are the four points at which an Abu Dhabi family buys intensive IGCSE hours.

programmes.name: Year 10, early in the course
programmes.description: The evidence available is end-of-topic tests and the first internal assessments, which are noisy but honest. An intensive block here is the best value in the sequence because the tier decision is still fully open and because habits such as showing method are still forming rather than entrenched. Progress is measured against the next school assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi families buy intensive support in Year 10, and the enquiries that arrive are usually prompted by a first-year report. A short block aimed at method and number fluency now removes most of what becomes an emergency eighteen months later.

programmes.name: Year 11, after the mocks
programmes.description: The richest evidence of the whole course: a full set of mock papers marked by the school, under conditions close to the real thing. This is the moment an intensive block can be aimed precisely, because the losses are documented rather than inferred, and the time remaining is still enough for a correction to be practised.
programmes.countryNote: This window is when specialist availability in Abu Dhabi narrows fastest, particularly in Chemistry, Physics and Additional Mathematics. A block booked in November runs with the tutor you chose; one booked in March runs with whoever has a slot left.

programmes.name: The final weeks before the papers
programmes.description: Evidence here comes from papers sat to time and marked in the session, and the only reachable gains are timing, accuracy, command-term discipline, method shown and paper-specific technique. Content coverage in this window produces recognition rather than competence, which the exam does not reward.
programmes.countryNote: The honest recommendation to an Abu Dhabi family arriving in the last fortnight is usually fewer hours than they came for, on one or two subjects nearest a boundary, finishing before the first paper rather than running into the series.

programmes.name: Retakes and private candidacy
programmes.description: The clearest evidence base available, because a result gives the component breakdown. A retake block can be aimed at two named papers with a known starting mark, which is why intensive hours tend to outperform weekly sessions here. Entry is arranged through a centre rather than by a tutor.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June and a November series, with a March series in some regions; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Confirm with the centre which series your child can enter before planning the block around a date.

abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.subjectsIntro: For each subject, the measurable indicator an intensive block should move, and how quickly it shows up in the record. These are the things to look for in a session note.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Measure method marks retained on multi-step questions and the proportion of the paper attempted. Both move within two weeks of timed practice and are countable on any marked script, which makes Mathematics the subject where evidence of progress appears fastest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Measure marks lost to calculations presented without working, and to organic naming conventions. Both are mechanical and both respond inside three weeks. A paper re-sat under the same conditions should show the calculation losses closing before anything else does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Measure formula selection errors and unit losses separately from conceptual errors, because they have different timescales. Unit and formula discipline moves in days; understanding why a circuit behaves as it does moves in months. A marked script separates the two cleanly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Measure command-term accuracy on long-answer questions: how often a six-mark "explain" answer scores below four because it described instead. This is the single largest avoidable loss in the subject and it responds quickly to marked practice.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Measure structure marks rather than overall impression: paragraph control, whether the directed task addressed the audience named, and whether the response answered the question asked. Slower to move than the sciences, so expect visible change over four weeks rather than one.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Measure application marks: how many answers referred to the firm or country in the stimulus rather than offering general theory. Countable on a marked script and correctable in two or three sessions, which makes it unusually good evidence.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Measure completion of long multi-stage questions, since partial attempts are where this entry bleeds marks. Supported by a much smaller tutor pool in Abu Dhabi, so blocks here need booking earlier than other subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Measure pseudocode convention errors and trace-table accuracy, both of which are board-specific and both of which a candidate can fix quickly once shown. Confirm the tutor knows your board's conventions before the block starts.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Measure case-study specificity: how many answers named a place and a figure rather than describing a region. Easy to count, slow to change, so judge these subjects over a month rather than a fortnight.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Measure against the correct component list first, because families frequently buy single-science hours for a combined-science entry and pay for content not being examined. The syllabus code on the statement of entry settles it.

subjects.name: French and Spanish
subjects.description: Measure the speaking component separately, since it is practised last and assessed differently. Written accuracy moves faster than spoken fluency, so expect the evidence in each to appear on different timescales.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: A Ministry-mandated subject in UAE private schools, examined on its own terms. The tutor pool barely overlaps with the subject pool, so an intensive block here has to be arranged earlier and measured against the school's own assessments.

abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.regionsTitle: Where intensive IGCSE blocks run from across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.regionsIntro: Intensive blocks run in near-daily sequences, which makes the family's routine the binding constraint. These are the communities we schedule blocks for and what shapes them locally.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Close to several large British-curriculum schools that run their own revision programmes, so the evidence to gather first is what the school already covers. Private hours here should target what those sessions explicitly skip.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The largest source of intensive IGCSE enquiries in the emirate, frequently involving two children in different year groups, which makes a shared daily window the practical arrangement rather than two separate ones.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment households with limited quiet study space, where the measurable benefit of a daily block is often the structure it imposes on independent practice as much as the teaching itself.

sections.heading: Reading a marked IGCSE script when you do not know the subject
paragraphs: A parent does not need to understand Chemistry to read a marked Chemistry paper usefully. The information you want is about the shape of the losses rather than their content, and it is visible to anyone willing to spend twenty minutes with the script and a pen. This is the most valuable twenty minutes available before buying any intensive block.

Start at the back. Look at the last two or three questions and check whether they were attempted at all, and whether the handwriting deteriorates towards the end. Blank or hurried final questions are a timing problem, and timing is the cheapest thing in this entire process to fix. Count the marks sitting in those unattempted questions; on a full IGCSE paper it is commonly three to six, which is frequently the whole distance to the next grade.

Then look for answers where a figure appears alone with no working above it. In Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, marks are allocated to steps as well as to answers, so a correct figure without visible method forfeits credit that was available, and a wrong figure with clear method keeps most of it. Count how many answers show only a result. This is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, which is why it responds to a short block and why it is worth finding before you pay anyone.

Then compare the question's first word with the length of the answer. Where a question says "explain" and the answer is one line, or where it says "state" and the answer is a paragraph, the candidate is not reading the instruction vocabulary, and that loss repeats across every paper in every subject. Finally, mark where the losses cluster. If they sit inside one topic, the gap is content. If they scatter evenly across the paper, the gap is technique, and technique is what an intensive block is genuinely good at.

sections.heading: What the record should show by the end of week one, two and three
paragraphs: An intensive block should generate a written record you can audit, and the record should change shape as it goes. Knowing in advance what each week ought to produce is what lets you tell a working block from a comfortable one, and it is a conversation worth having before the first paid session rather than after the fourth.

Week one is diagnosis and the first mechanical corrections. By the end of it you should have the named losses in writing with marks estimated, and you should have seen the quickest of them already move: accuracy conventions, units, rounding instructions. These are days-to-fix items and they should not still be appearing in week three. If they are, the practice between sessions is not happening, which is a different problem from the one you bought tutoring for.

Week two is where method and command terms start to show. The record should contain examples: a question where working was shown that previously would not have been, or a six-mark answer that now addresses the instruction rather than describing. These are the corrections that generalise across papers, so a note naming them is worth more than a note reporting a topic covered. Week two is also where a wrong diagnosis becomes visible, because a correctly identified mechanical loss will have started to move and a misidentified one will not.

Week three is measurement. A paper sat to time under the same conditions as the original, marked the same way, with the mark compared honestly. Expect a modest and real movement rather than a transformation: a few marks recovered from timing and method is a normal, useful result, and it is often exactly the distance to a grade boundary. What you should not accept is a block that reaches week three with no comparable measurement, because at that point nobody involved can say whether the money did anything.

sections.heading: What a few marks mean once boundaries are involved
paragraphs: Families often describe a target as a grade and a result as a mark, without connecting the two. The connection is the grade boundary, and understanding roughly how it behaves changes how an intensive block should be aimed. The short version is that small mark movements matter disproportionately, and they matter most to candidates already close to a threshold.

Boundaries are set after each series by the board, using the performance of that cohort on that paper, which means they move between sessions and cannot be known in advance. That has two consequences worth stating plainly. The first is that no tutor can tell you how many marks a grade will require, and anyone offering that number is guessing. The second is that the sensible target is not a boundary but a margin above wherever a boundary is likely to fall, because a candidate sitting exactly on an estimate has no protection against a harder paper.

What this does to the arithmetic of an intensive block is make the mechanical losses extremely valuable. A timing correction worth four marks and a method correction worth three are, together, often the entire distance between adjacent grades on a single paper. They are also the losses that move fastest and are easiest to evidence. A content project worth fifteen marks is theoretically larger and practically unreachable in three weeks, which is why ranking by reachability rather than by size is the right method.

It also explains why the choice of which subject receives the hours should be driven by proximity to a threshold. A student four marks short across two subjects is a better investment than one twenty marks short in a single subject, because the first case has two reachable grade changes and the second has none. The school's own mock analysis is usually the best available guide to proximity, and it costs nothing to ask for it.

sections.heading: The re-sat paper, and how to keep the measurement honest
paragraphs: The cleanest evidence an intensive block can produce is the same paper sat twice. It is also the easiest measurement to corrupt, usually without anyone intending to, so it is worth setting the conditions deliberately before the first session rather than improvising them in week three.

Three things have to match between the two sittings. The time allowed must be the same, including whatever the student is entitled to. The conditions must be the same: no notes, no formula sheet unless the real paper provides one, no pausing. And the marking must be the same, against the official mark scheme rather than generously. A re-sit under easier conditions produces a higher mark and no information, which is worse than no measurement because it ends the conversation about whether to continue.

There is also a familiarity effect to account for. A student re-sitting a paper they have already seen will do better partly because they remember it, and that portion of the improvement is not transferable. The usual way round this is to re-sit a different paper of the same type from the same board and tier, matched for difficulty as closely as the available past material allows. Where the original is re-sat, the honest reading is to look at where the marks were recovered rather than at the total: timing and method recovered are real, remembered answers are not.

What to do with the result is the part families find hardest. A modest improvement, three to six marks from mechanical corrections, is a good outcome and a reason to continue narrowly. A large improvement usually indicates familiarity rather than progress and should be checked against a fresh paper. No improvement, after the quick-fix items have been addressed, means the diagnosis was wrong, and the right response is to re-diagnose rather than to buy more of the same hours. A tutor who proposes exactly that is behaving properly.

sections.heading: Separating a technique gap from a content gap
paragraphs: Almost every decision about an intensive IGCSE block turns on this distinction, and it is diagnosable from a marked script in under half an hour. Technique gaps respond to days and weeks of corrected practice. Content gaps respond to months. Buying an intensive block for a content gap is the most common way IGCSE tutoring money is wasted in this market, and it is avoidable.

The signature of a technique gap is scattered loss. Marks disappear in small amounts across the whole paper, in questions on topics the student can discuss competently, and the specific causes recur: unshown method, misread instruction, missing units, unfinished final questions. Ask the student to explain a question they lost marks on and they will often explain it correctly, which is the clearest possible sign that the knowledge is present and the delivery is not.

The signature of a content gap is clustered loss. Marks disappear in blocks, inside particular topics, and the student cannot explain those questions when asked. Where the clusters sit in a small, lightly weighted topic, a short block can close them. Where they sit across several major topics, the honest position is that an intensive course will produce recognition rather than competence, and the exam rewards competence.

There is a third case worth naming because it is frequently misread as content: the entry mismatch. A candidate sitting Combined Science who has been taught single-science material, or a Pearson Edexcel candidate taught Cambridge conventions, or a Core candidate practising Extended papers, will produce a script that looks like a content disaster and is actually an administrative error. The syllabus code on the statement of entry resolves it in a minute, and checking it before buying hours has saved several Abu Dhabi families an entire block's fee.
bullets: Scattered losses on explicable topics: technique, and reachable in weeks
Clustered losses the student cannot explain: content, and slower
A small clustered gap in a weighted topic: worth a short block

sections.heading: Fixing the block to the board's calendar
paragraphs: An intensive block has to finish somewhere, and the right end point is set by the board rather than by the budget. The dates are published, and anchoring the plan to them avoids the common pattern of a block that drifts into the examination fortnight, when its marginal value is at its lowest and the cost to rest is at its highest.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The March 2027 series is a useful worked example of how far ahead the fixed points sit: Cambridge's own key-dates document puts the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline sitting more than two months before the paper is the detail that matters most, because it is when tier is fixed.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date that can be revised.

One Cambridge administrative detail is worth checking before a block is scheduled around any date. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in, then set the block's finish date from that timetable with a week's margin.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are assessed by terminal papers, but several carry a coursework or practical component, and an intensive block run close to a deadline is where the boundary around that work comes under pressure. It belongs on this page because one of the sites competing for these searches sells completed assessed work, and the consequence of using such a service falls on the candidate.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial. They can teach the skills the component assesses. They can explain in plain language what the mark scheme is asking for, which is often harder to extract from a specification than it should be. They can question a plan or a design until the student can defend it. They can read a student's own draft and identify where a criterion is not yet met and why. They can teach referencing and explain what counts as the student's own work.

What a tutor must not do is produce any part of what is submitted. Not a paragraph, not a rewritten section, not an edit that replaces the student's sentences with the tutor's. The student produces every word submitted, and the school declares the support the candidate received. A tutor who raises this in the first session unprompted and is willing to put it in writing is protecting your child; one who treats a deadline as grounds for flexibility is not, however good the teaching looks.

Material follows the same rule. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor references them and links the official source rather than distributing copies, and nobody outside an examination centre has lawful access to unreleased material. Any hint of such access in the weeks before a series should end the arrangement immediately, whatever has already been paid for.
bullets: Teaching the assessed skill and explaining the mark scheme: proper

sections.heading: Who may lawfully tutor in the UAE, and what IB Gram claims
paragraphs: An intensive block is subject to the same permit rules as a weekly session. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is wider than parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why no amount appears on this page, and any page quoting one is quoting something unverified.

Abu Dhabi adds a restriction that becomes relevant under deadline pressure, because a family in a hurry often thinks first of a teacher who already knows the child's work. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it.

A centre with premises and staff requires an educational services permit from the emirate regulator, which is a different instrument from an individual tutor's permit and is not a quality rating. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none. It is an independent tutor-matching platform, delivery is online and one-to-one, and no tutor here is described as approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. Every rate quoted on this page is another provider's published figure, named and dated.

sections.heading: What the record looks like when it is time to stop
paragraphs: Every intensive block should have an exit written into it, and the exit should be triggered by the record rather than by the calendar or the budget. Three patterns in the session notes say stop, and they are all readable by a parent who does not know the subject.

The first is repetition. If the same named loss appears in week one, week two and week three, the hours are not reaching it. Either the diagnosis was wrong or the practice between sessions is not happening, and in both cases buying more sessions changes nothing. The correct response is a conversation and a re-diagnosis, which may cost one session and save six. A tutor who proposes that rather than another block is the one to keep.

The second is drift. If the notes stop naming losses and start naming topics covered, the session has become a lecture. That happens gradually and usually when the original plan has been exhausted without anyone saying so. It is the most expensive failure mode in intensive tutoring because it feels productive from inside the room and shows nothing in the record.

The third is success, which families resist hardest. When a student starts arriving with their own marked paper and their own account of where the marks went, the tutoring has done what it was bought for. The right move then is to stop the block and keep one review session before the series, not to continue weekly out of nervousness. The final fortnight belongs to the student's own practice and to rest, both of which have a higher marginal value at that point than any additional hour of instruction. And if no UAE-based specialist is free in the subject and tier you need, we say so rather than putting a generalist into a specialist-priced block.
bullets: Same loss named three weeks running: re-diagnose, do not re-book

process.title: Send the marked paper and the statement of entry
process.description: The script gives the diagnosis; the statement of entry gives the board, syllabus code, tier and component list. Together they prevent the two commonest errors in intensive IGCSE tutoring: aiming at the wrong losses, and aiming at content the entry does not examine.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full lesson, no payment and no card held. It should end with three or four named losses, each attributed to a cause and with marks estimated, plus an honest statement of which are reachable in the time available. Ask for that in writing.

process.title: Agree the block, the measurement and the end date
process.description: How many sessions, aimed at which losses, measured how and finishing when. Agree the re-sit conditions at this point rather than in week three, because a measurement designed after the fact is not a measurement.

process.title: Read the notes weekly against the plan
process.description: Each session produces a note naming the loss worked on. Week one should show the quick conventions already corrected, week two should show method and command terms moving, week three should carry a comparable mark. Read them in sequence, not individually.

process.title: Decide at the measurement point
process.description: After the re-sit, continue narrowly, re-diagnose, or stop. All three are legitimate outcomes and we will recommend whichever the record supports, including the one that ends the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Every block opens from a script
whyPoints.description: No intensive block starts with "what would you like to go over?". It starts with a marked paper read against the mark scheme, because that is the only input in this process that cannot be flattered by a good conversation.

whyPoints.title: Notes you can audit without the subject
whyPoints.description: Session notes name the loss corrected and the evidence for it, not the topic covered. That makes the decision to continue or stop readable by a parent, which is the point: the evidence belongs to you rather than to the tutor.

whyPoints.title: A measurement agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: The re-sit conditions, the paper and the marking standard are fixed before the block begins. A measurement designed after the result is known is not evidence, and it is how open-ended tutoring arrangements get justified.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable regardless of distance
whyPoints.description: Delivery is online and one-to-one, so a daily block for a family in Al Shamkha draws on the same pool as one in Al Mushrif. For a compressed run that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated before the deadline
whyPoints.description: On any coursework or practical component the tutor teaches, explains the mark scheme and gives feedback on the student's own work, and produces no part of a submission. Stated at the first session and recorded.

whyPoints.title: An exit written into the plan
whyPoints.description: Blocks finish on a planned date, normally a week before the first paper. Where the record shows repetition rather than movement, we say so and re-diagnose rather than selling another run of hours.

faqs.question: What evidence should I see before paying for an intensive IGCSE block?
faqs.answer: A marked script and a diagnosis drawn from it. Before any money moves, you should have three or four specific losses named, each attributed to a cause such as timing, unshown method or a misread command term, with an estimate of the marks each is worth and whether it is reachable in the time left. You should also have an explicit statement of what the block will not attempt. If the proposal is a number of hours in a subject with no such list behind it, nobody has yet established what the hours are for.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's marked IGCSE paper without knowing the subject?
faqs.answer: Four passes, about twenty minutes. First, look at the last questions: blank or rushed endings mean a timing problem, and count the marks sitting there. Second, find answers where a figure appears with no working above it, which forfeits step marks. Third, compare each question's first word with the answer's length; a one-line response to a six-mark "explain" is an instruction-vocabulary loss. Fourth, see whether losses cluster in one topic or scatter across the paper. Clustered means content, scattered means technique, and technique is what a short block reaches.

faqs.question: How soon should an IGCSE intensive block show measurable movement?
faqs.answer: The quickest items inside the first week: rounding instructions followed, units written, accuracy conventions applied. Those are days-to-fix and should not still be appearing in week three. Method shown and command-term discipline start to appear in week two, with specific examples in the notes. A comparable measurement, a paper sat to time and marked against the scheme, belongs in week three. If week three arrives with no comparable mark, nobody in the arrangement can say whether the block is working.

faqs.question: Is re-sitting the same past paper a fair way to measure progress?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest reading is to look at where the marks were recovered rather than at the total, because some of the improvement is memory. A cleaner measurement is a different paper of the same type, board and tier, sat under identical conditions: same time allowed, no notes unless the real paper provides them, uninterrupted, marked against the official scheme rather than generously. Agree those conditions before the block starts. A re-sit under easier conditions produces a higher mark and no information at all.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE grade boundaries actually mean for a child a few marks short?
faqs.answer: They mean small movements matter disproportionately. Boundaries are set after each series by the board using that cohort's performance, so they shift between sessions and cannot be known in advance; anyone quoting you the mark a grade will need is guessing. What follows practically is that a timing correction worth four marks and a method correction worth three can together be the whole distance between adjacent grades, and that the sensible target is a margin above any estimate rather than the estimate itself.

faqs.question: How many marks is a timing problem usually worth on an IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: Commonly three to six on a full paper, and sometimes more, because the final questions often carry higher tariffs than the opening ones. It is also the cheapest loss in the whole taxonomy to correct: one to two weeks of timed practice with a per-question clock usually closes most of it, since the problem is pacing rather than knowledge. That combination, a meaningful number of marks and a short correction time, is why timing is the first thing an evidence-led block addresses rather than the last.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE session note contain to be worth reading?
faqs.answer: The specific loss worked on, the evidence it was worked on, and what was set as practice. "Mole calculations: six answers rewritten with working shown; three of four follow-up questions showed method unprompted; six similar questions set for Thursday" is useful. "Covered moles and stoichiometry" is not, because it records the topic rather than the correction. The test is whether a parent who does not know Chemistry can tell from the note what changed. If they cannot, the note is not doing its job.

faqs.question: My child's mock went down after tutoring started. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Most often that the two papers were not comparable: a different paper, different conditions, a harder set of questions, or a mock marked more strictly than the previous one. Before drawing conclusions, check the time allowed, the materials permitted and the marking standard. Where the comparison is genuinely like for like, a drop after several weeks usually means the diagnosis was wrong rather than that the teaching was bad, and the right response is to re-diagnose from the new script rather than to add hours to the existing plan.

faqs.question: Can a short IGCSE block move a grade in three weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a candidate already close to a threshold whose losses are mechanical. Three to six marks from timing plus two to five from method shown is frequently the distance between adjacent grades on a single paper, and both respond inside three weeks of corrected practice. No, for a candidate well below a threshold with clustered content gaps across several topics: intensive teaching there produces recognition rather than competence. One diagnostic session on a marked script tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects give the clearest evidence of progress fastest?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Chemistry, because their losses are the most countable. Method marks retained on multi-step questions and marks lost to calculations without working are both visible on any marked script and both respond within two or three weeks. Biology follows, where command-term accuracy on long answers is easy to count. English, Geography and History move more slowly and should be judged over a month rather than a fortnight, because structure and case-study specificity take longer to become habitual.

faqs.question: Does a predicted grade change if mock performance improves?
faqs.answer: It can, but the school decides, using its own evidence and its own policy, and that policy varies between Abu Dhabi schools. The practical consequence is that if a predicted grade is the problem you are solving, the intervention has to land before whatever assessment the school uses as evidence, not before the final papers. Ask the school directly which assessments feed the prediction and when they fall, then set the block's dates from that answer rather than from the exam timetable.

faqs.question: How do I tell a content gap from a technique gap on an IGCSE script?
faqs.answer: Ask your child to explain a question they lost marks on. If they explain it correctly, the knowledge is present and the loss is technique: unshown method, misread instruction, missing units, unfinished questions. If they cannot explain it, it is content. Then look at the pattern on the paper. Technique gaps scatter small losses across the whole script; content gaps cluster them inside particular topics. Also check the syllabus code, because a candidate taught the wrong board's or tier's material produces a script that imitates a content disaster.

faqs.question: What record should I ask for at the end of an IGCSE intensive block?
faqs.answer: A written summary with four things: the losses identified at the start with their estimated marks, which of them stopped recurring and on what evidence, the comparable measurement with its conditions stated, and a recommendation about whether further hours are justified. Ask for it at the point of agreeing the block rather than at the end, so it is a term of the arrangement. A block that finishes with no summary leaves you unable to decide anything about the next one.

faqs.question: Should we keep going if two subjects improved and one did not?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for the two and no for the third, at least not in the same form. The subject that did not move needs a re-diagnosis rather than more hours of the same plan, and the likeliest explanations are a misidentified loss, a content gap too wide for the window, or practice not happening between sessions. Where time is short, the better use of the remaining budget is to protect the gains in the two subjects that responded and leave the third to school provision, because reachable marks outrank worrying ones.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying an IGCSE block with no marked work to start from?
faqs.answer: Not without creating some first. If no mock or marked assignment exists, the first session should be a paper sat to time and marked against the scheme, which produces the diagnosis the rest of the block depends on. That costs one session and saves several, because without it the plan defaults to topic coverage and nobody can measure the outcome. Ask the school for the most recent marked work as well; even a single internal assessment with a teacher's annotations is better than starting blind.

abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.closingHeading: Send a marked paper and we will tell you what it says
abu-dhabi/igcse-crash-course.closingBody: The useful first step is not booking hours, it is reading the evidence. Send the statement of entry, the most recent marked script, and the date of the next assessment. We will come back with the losses we can see, what each is likely to be worth in marks, which of them are reachable in the time available, and the rate before anything is paid. Where the honest answer is fewer hours than you came for, that is what you will get. The first lesson is free and takes no card. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are listed by subject and board, with the tier they usually teach. For an eight-subject candidate the question is rarely who is best in the abstract; it is who covers the two or three papers the budget has been allocated to, in the slots the household can actually keep.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one budget
paragraphs: An Abu Dhabi family looking for IGCSE exam preparation is usually holding a statement of entry with eight or nine subjects on it and a quotation for one. The rate on the quotation is the least interesting thing in the conversation. At published market bands of roughly AED 150 to 450 an hour for qualified to specialist online tuition, funding weekly one-to-one work in nine subjects for a full exam term is not a decision most households will make, and it is not one they should have to. The real question is which subjects get the hours.

There is a rule that makes part of that decision for you, and most providers in this market never mention it. For the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One widely ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject figure. The sourced number is five.

That rule reframes the budget. Five subjects have to clear a floor. The rest matter for school progression and for university subject requirements rather than for equivalency. So the allocation question splits in two: which five are safely above the floor and which are not, and separately, which subjects are needed at a high grade for the sixth-form course your child intends to take. A subject that is secure on both counts does not need funding this term however much the household worries about it.

The board matters to the plan as well. Cambridge International runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a plan should link the official live timetable rather than copy dates that can be revised. Where a household has children on both boards, the two calendars will not align.

What follows is the allocation worked through: the hours each subject type genuinely needs, the five-subject protection list, what the board changes, where group teaching saves money honestly and where it does not, and how practical science is assessed for a candidate taught online. Every AED figure is a market observation from October 2026 with the kind of source it came from named, and none of them is IB Gram's price list.

abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Spend on IGCSE preparation behaves differently depending on when it happens, and the three stages below have different cost-per-grade profiles for an Abu Dhabi family planning across years rather than weeks.

programmes.name: Year 9 and option choices
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention in the whole sequence is getting the option block right. A candidate who takes nine subjects including three sciences and two languages has a workload that converts directly into tutoring demand two years later. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, available in March, May and October, give a dated external reading before the choices are made.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi timetables also carry Arabic and Islamic education alongside the licensed international curriculum, which is a genuine addition to the Year 9 load rather than a substitution. Families who account for that when choosing options usually need fewer funded hours in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: The year where an hour of teaching is worth most and costs the same. Content is being met for the first time, there is room for consolidation, and a gap closed here does not reappear as a technique problem under exam pressure. One subject at one session a week across a year is a smaller total than three subjects crammed into a final term.
programmes.countryNote: Few families in this emirate buy in Year 10, which is why the Year 11 market is as busy and as expensive as it is. Where a household can only fund one year of support across the two, the arithmetic favours the earlier one unless a specific grade requirement has already slipped.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11 and the exam term
programmes.description: The year the search happens in. Spend here is triage: a marked paper per subject, a ranking by recoverable marks per hour, and funding for the two or three subjects that top the list. Hours bought after the entry deadline cannot change the tier, which narrows what is available to change.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series show the shape of the constraint: final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Whatever series your child sits, the entry closes well before the paper and fixes the tier the plan has to work with.

abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often fund, with the hours each typically needs for a one-grade move in the exam year. Treat the hour figures as planning estimates drawn from how these papers behave, not as promises about any individual candidate, and confirm syllabus codes against the statement of entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Usually the first subject funded and usually the right call, because a large share of its lost marks are method and working marks rather than knowledge. Twelve to twenty hours across a term is a realistic block, split between non-calculator and calculator papers.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Needs more hours than Mathematics for the same movement, because electricity, waves and the practical paper each behave differently. Fifteen to twenty-five hours is typical, and the practical or alternative-to-practical component is worth planning separately.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic, ionic equations and organic naming are finite and therefore efficient to fund. Candidates often need fewer hours here than they expect, around twelve to eighteen, provided the arithmetic foundation is intact.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest hour count per grade of the three sciences because the content volume is largest and the marks sit in precise terminology. Twenty hours upwards, which is why it is often the science a family decides not to fund.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Hours convert into marks through marked timed writing rather than through teaching, so the cost profile is unusual: fewer, longer-spaced sessions with substantial marking between them work better than weekly contact.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Efficient to fund because the exercises are predictable and the discipline they test, close reading and summary within a word ceiling, responds quickly. Eight to fifteen hours is often enough to move a grade.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
subjects.description: Analysis and evaluation marks are the target and they are habit-based, so short repeated drills are cheaper than content teaching. Ten to fifteen hours, concentrated on case-study response structure.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus data-response discipline. Both are drillable, which keeps the hour count low at around ten to fifteen, and both transfer directly into AS Level if that is the intended route.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further maths options
subjects.description: Rarely the right place for a constrained budget unless a sixth-form entry requirement depends on it. Where it is funded, it should be funded alongside the main Mathematics paper rather than instead of it.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed international curriculum, and explicitly not counted among the five subjects the Ministry of Education equivalency rule requires. That makes them a school-progression priority rather than an equivalency one, which changes where they sit in a ranked budget.

abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes what support costs in practice, because travel, slot timing and local tutor supply all vary across the emirate. These are the communities that most often raise a specific cost question.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Zayed City
regions.note: A long run from the island, so any visiting arrangement carries real travel inside the fee. Households here tend to compare the cost of two online sessions against one in-home visit and reach the obvious conclusion themselves.

regions.name: Baniyas
regions.note: Large year groups at nearby schools mean group revision is widely available and cheap at market group rates, which makes the useful question whether individual diagnosis is needed on top rather than instead.

regions.name: Mussafah
regions.note: Working patterns here push sessions late, and families often ask for two short weekday slots rather than a weekend block. Short frequent sessions also happen to suit exam-technique work, so the constraint is not a compromise.

regions.name: Al Rahba and Al Bahia
regions.note: On the northern edge of the emirate with a long school run already absorbed into the day. The budget question is usually how many subjects can be funded once the commute has taken the late afternoon.

regions.name: Al Samha
regions.note: Close enough to the Dubai boundary that families compare provision across both emirates. Tutor supply in specialist IGCSE subjects is thin locally, which is the clearest case for widening the pool rather than narrowing it to a drive radius.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central and well served by tuition centres, so group pricing is competitive and visible. That makes it the area where the group-versus-one-to-one comparison is most often asked as a straight cost question.

regions.name: Hydra Village and Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Peripheral communities where a visiting tutor would spend more time driving than teaching. Households here usually arrive having already decided on video delivery and want the subject match discussed instead.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bahia
schoolClusters.note: Broad option blocks and large Year 11 cohorts, which means nine-subject candidates are common and the allocation problem on this page is the normal case rather than the exception. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: The island, Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: Established British-curriculum provision where internal mock timetables are set early and school revision programmes are substantial, so the question is often what one-to-one adds to what is already provided.

sections.heading: What nine subjects would cost, and what to fund instead
paragraphs: Start with the figure nobody writes down. At published market bands of AED 150 to 450 an hour for qualified to specialist online tuition, weekly one-to-one support in nine subjects across a twenty-week exam term is 180 hours. That is a number in the tens of thousands of dirhams and it is not a sensible purchase even for a household that could make it, because several of those subjects would be receiving hours they did not need while the school was already covering them adequately.

The alternative is not cheaper tutoring, it is fewer funded subjects chosen properly. Three subjects at one session a week for twenty weeks is 60 hours. A diagnostic across all nine, bought once, is nine to twelve hours. Together that is roughly 70 hours against 180, and the three subjects chosen on evidence will usually move more than nine subjects shallowly supported, because the hours land where marks are reachable.

The group option is real and worth pricing honestly rather than dismissing. Market group rates run around AED 45 to 150 per student per hour, which is a genuine saving, and group revision does the job it is good at: broad syllabus coverage for a cohort at a similar level. What it cannot do is work from one candidate's marked script. For a subject where the gap is coverage, group is the right purchase. For a subject where the gap is this candidate's specific technique, it is not.
The table applies all of this to the three scenarios Abu Dhabi families actually choose between. AED figures are market bands from October 2026, applied arithmetically, not quotations.

sections.heading: Which five subjects have to clear the floor
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the single most useful thing an Abu Dhabi family can know before allocating a tutoring budget, and it is absent from almost every competing page in this market. On the British track, candidates must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

Read that against a nine-subject entry and the budget sorts itself into tiers. Five subjects must clear a floor that is low but absolute. Separately, the subjects your child needs at a strong grade for a particular sixth-form course have their own, higher requirement set by the school. A subject that is neither in the protected five nor a sixth-form prerequisite is the first candidate to be left on school support, whatever the household's instinct says.

The American-track figures are published too and are worth knowing if a sibling is on that curriculum: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold we can source, so this page publishes none; verify any IB figure on the Ministry's own site before relying on it.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs or secures. It is a process run by the authority, with its own documents and channels, and any provider implying they can obtain it or that tutoring is required for it is making a false claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: what the board changes about the plan
paragraphs: Families often assume the board is a detail the school chose and nothing more. It changes four practical things about an exam-preparation plan: when the papers are sat, which timetable applies, how tiering is labelled, and how far ahead the dates can be trusted. A household with two children on different boards has two calendars, and planning against the wrong one is a mistake that cannot be corrected afterwards.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Its published March 2027 key dates run from final entries on 27 November 2026 to an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is the reason to link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that may be revised.

For the budget, the consequence is sequencing. Work backwards from the entry deadline, not from the exam, because entry fixes the tier and the series. Then check which timetable version applies before fixing session slots in the exam fortnight.

sections.heading: Year 10 money works harder than Year 11 money
paragraphs: The least popular finding on this page is that the cheapest IGCSE exam preparation happens a year before anyone searches for it. In Year 10 a gap can be closed while content is still being met for the first time, and a closed gap stays closed. In Year 11 the same gap has usually become a technique problem as well, because the candidate has spent a year writing answers around the thing they did not understand, and now both the knowledge and the habit need work.

The arithmetic is plain. One subject at one session a week across Year 10, say thirty hours, is a smaller total than three subjects funded in a final term at sixty hours, and it is spent when each hour returns more. Families who fund Year 10 arrive in Year 11 needing diagnosis and a short targeted block rather than a broad rescue. Very few do it, which is exactly why the Year 11 market in this emirate is as crowded and as expensive as it is.

That does not help a household already in Year 11, so here is the version that does. Fund the diagnostic, fund two or three subjects, and treat the rest as school-supported. Then, if there is a younger sibling in Year 9 or 10, spend there next year rather than repeating the final-term rescue. The second time through the same household, the bill is usually smaller and the outcome calmer.

The one case where Year 11 spending genuinely outperforms is a tier or sixth-form requirement that has already slipped and has a hard deadline. There, concentrated hours in a single subject are the correct purchase even at the worst price in the year.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and what you would be paying for twice
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools vary widely in the revision support they run, and the variation is worth mapping before a single hour is bought. Several schools timetable substantial revision programmes, run full mock cycles with marked scripts returned, hold clinics for specific papers, and publish a study-leave schedule with staff availability. Where that is happening, buying broad content coverage privately duplicates it at market rates.

The questions to ask the school are short. Will marked mock scripts be returned, or only grades. Are there subject clinics in study leave, and for which papers. Who can a candidate approach for help on a specific past-paper question after study leave starts. Is there a revision timetable for the exam fortnight. The answers tell you precisely where the gap is, and the gap is what a budget should cover.

In practice the thing schools rarely provide is individual diagnosis from a marked script. Thirty students in a set makes it impractical, not negligent. That is the service worth buying privately, and it is also the cheapest thing on this page: one paper per subject, marked, with a written note. Content coverage, by contrast, is the thing schools do provide and the thing most commonly bought twice.

ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, so your child's school sits under its oversight and its inspection reporting. That tells you something about the school; it does not tell you whether your child's Physics script is losing marks to method omission. Only the script does.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the teaching happens over video
paragraphs: This is the question Abu Dhabi families ask most often about online preparation and the one competitors answer least clearly. The practical component of an IGCSE science is assessed by the school and the board, not by a tutor, and the candidate sits whatever component their entry specifies, commonly a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the syllabus and the centre. Nothing a tutor does changes which component applies; the school's entry does.

What preparation for those components actually involves is largely writing, and writing is well suited to video teaching. Candidates lose marks for describing a method another student could not follow, for recording results to inconsistent precision, for plotting a graph with a poorly chosen scale, for drawing a line that follows the points rather than the trend, and for stating a conclusion the data does not support. All of those are correctable on a shared screen with a past-paper question in front of both people.

What video cannot do is replace time at a bench. Handling apparatus, measuring, and the physical judgement that comes with repetition belong in the school laboratory, and a tutor should say so plainly rather than imply otherwise. The honest division of labour is that the school supplies the practical experience and the tutor works on the recording, processing and evaluation marks, which is where most of the paper's marks sit anyway.
Confirm with the school which practical component your child is entered for, because it differs between syllabuses and between centres, and the preparation differs with it.

sections.heading: Coursework, feedback and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Where an IGCSE subject carries internally assessed work, your child is the author and the only author. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, ask questions about a plan, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. No text is supplied, nothing is edited to completion, and no model answer is handed over to be adapted into a submission.

That boundary is worth stating on a cost page because exam-term pressure is when the request gets made and when a provider short of scruples is most willing to be paid for crossing it. Boards treat work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the helper. At least one provider in this market openly sells finished internal assessments; a family paying for legitimate help deserves to know the difference before they ask for it.

The auditable version is simple and costs nothing to run. The student sends the draft they wrote. The tutor returns questions and criterion references rather than replacement sentences. Every version is kept, so if the school asks how the work was supported there is a trail that answers honestly. The same trail protects the candidate and the tutor.

Where the deadline has already passed, the mark is fixed and the hours belong to the written papers. A provider who takes a booking against a closed component without saying so is selling calendar time, which is why the question is worth asking directly of anyone quoting you.

sections.heading: Delivery, and why a wider pool costs less than a nearer one
paragraphs: Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, the paper on screen and a recording the candidate can rewatch. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. On a page about cost, the argument for that is mostly arithmetic rather than preference.

Travel sits inside an in-home fee whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice, which is why market rates for visiting work run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 450 for online tuition, and why visits are commonly quoted with a two-hour minimum. For a household in Al Samha or Hydra Village, the fee difference and the session-length minimum together mean the same money buys noticeably fewer, longer sessions than it would online.

The second effect is on the match. Restricting the search to tutors who can reach your community at a fixed hour makes subject depth a matter of local supply, and in specialist IGCSE subjects local supply in this emirate is genuinely thin. Removing the journey means the person teaching Physics 0625 Extended is chosen because they mark that paper, which is the variable that decides whether the hours work.

The limit is coverage, and it is disclosed before any booking. If no tutor who teaches your child's exact paper has hours in the window you need, you are told that and offered a named alternative with its trade-off stated: a specialist working Gulf Standard Time from another country, a subject split across two tutors with one shared progress record, reallocation to a subject where the match is right, or a later start. Filling a slot with a generalist is how exam-term money disappears.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: The single most useful document is the statement of entry, because it settles the board, the syllabus codes, the tiers and the series. With that plus a note of which subjects worry you, we can say what the allocation problem looks like before anyone discusses rates.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A single sixty-minute session at no charge with the tutor you would keep, taken before any payment. It is one lesson rather than a trial period, and it is used to check the subject match and to set the first timed paper for marking.

process.title: Diagnose broadly, then rank
process.description: One timed paper per subject under consideration, marked against the published mark scheme, producing a marks-per-topic sheet and a ranking by recoverable marks per hour. The ranking is what the funding decision is made from, and it regularly closes subjects down rather than opening them.

process.title: Fund two or three subjects, name the rest
process.description: Hours go to the top of the ranking. The subjects left on school support are named in writing, with the reason, so the decision is explicit and reviewable rather than an omission nobody mentioned. The protected five under the equivalency rule are flagged separately.

process.title: Review at the halfway point
process.description: Topic sheets at the midpoint show which funded subject is responding. Hours move between subjects on that evidence, or stop. Where the evidence says the plan should shrink, that is the recommendation given, in writing, with the sheets attached.

whyPoints.title: The allocation is the service
whyPoints.description: Most providers sell hours in whichever subject a parent names first. The work that changes an outcome for a nine-subject candidate is deciding which two or three subjects those hours belong in, and that decision is made from marked papers rather than from the order of the family's worries.

whyPoints.title: The five-subject rule is published here, correctly
whyPoints.description: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A widely ranking competitor states six. Getting it right changes which subjects a family protects.

whyPoints.title: Group teaching is priced honestly rather than dismissed
whyPoints.description: Market group rates of roughly AED 45 to 150 per student per hour are a real saving and group revision does broad coverage well. What it cannot do is work from one candidate's script, so this page says which gap each format actually fits instead of selling against the cheaper one.

whyPoints.title: Board dates come from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's six administrative zones and March 2027 key dates, and Pearson's May/June and November series with provisional timetables, are taken from the boards' own published guidance and linked rather than restated as settled fact. Dates that can be revised are described as revisable.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on your child's own draft, keeping every version so the trail can be shown to the school. Where a component is already submitted, you are told the mark is fixed and the hours redirected.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, no invented figures
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Every AED band on this page is labelled as a market observation from October 2026 with the kind of source it came from.

faqs.question: My child sits nine IGCSEs in Abu Dhabi. How many subjects should we actually pay to tutor?
faqs.answer: Two or three, chosen from marked papers rather than from instinct, with a broad diagnostic across the rest. At market bands of AED 150 to 450 an hour, nine subjects at one weekly session across a twenty-week term is 180 hours and a bill in the tens of thousands of dirhams, much of it duplicating what the school already covers. Three funded subjects plus a one-off diagnostic across all nine is roughly 70 hours, and the hours land where the marks are actually reachable.

faqs.question: Which five subjects matter most for UAE certificate equivalency on the British track?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. A further requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Which five your child uses is a decision worth making with the school, because it determines which grades must clear a floor and which only matter for sixth-form entry.

faqs.question: Is group IGCSE revision in Abu Dhabi worth it at the lower price, or a false economy?
faqs.answer: Neither, once you separate the two jobs. Group revision at market rates of roughly AED 45 to 150 per student per hour does broad syllabus coverage well, and for a subject where your child's gap is simply coverage it is the correct purchase. What it cannot do is respond to one candidate's marked script, so for a technique fault specific to your child it buys attendance rather than improvement. Many families get the best value by grouping the coverage subjects and funding one-to-one only where the script says something individual is wrong.

faqs.question: How many hours does one grade of movement usually take in an IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject rather than by candidate temperament. Mathematics often responds in twelve to twenty hours because its losses are patterned method and working marks. English as a Second Language can move in eight to fifteen because the exercises are predictable. Chemistry sits around twelve to eighteen where the arithmetic foundation is intact. Biology is the slowest of the common subjects at twenty hours upwards, because the content volume is largest. Those are planning estimates from how the papers behave, not predictions for an individual, and a marked paper refines them in week one.

faqs.question: Does it matter for our planning whether the school uses Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, in four practical ways. The series available differ, with Cambridge running June and November and Pearson running May/June and November. Cambridge allocates centres to one of six administrative zones and states the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson publishes provisional timetables before each series, so dates can be revised before the final version. And tiering is labelled differently, Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. A household with children on both boards is planning against two calendars that will not align.

faqs.question: Why is Year 10 tutoring better value than Year 11 tutoring at the same hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Because in Year 10 a gap can be closed while the content is still being met for the first time, and a closed gap stays closed. By Year 11 the same gap has usually acquired a habit around it, as the candidate has spent a year writing answers that avoid the thing they did not understand, so both the knowledge and the habit need hours. One subject across Year 10 is a smaller total than three subjects rescued in a final term, and each hour returns more. Very few families do it, which is why the Year 11 market is so busy.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if my child is taught online?
faqs.answer: The practical component is assessed by the school and the board according to your child's entry, commonly a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the syllabus and centre, and nothing a tutor does changes which applies. Preparation for those papers is mostly writing: method description another student could follow, consistent precision, sensible graph scales, a line of best fit rather than a dot-to-dot, and conclusions the data supports. All of that is taught well on a shared screen. Bench time and apparatus handling belong in the school laboratory.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring provider help us get Ministry of Education equivalency for IGCSE certificates?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying otherwise is misdescribing a regulatory process. Equivalency is run by the Ministry and the emirate's attestation channel, with their own documents, fees and timelines, and no tutoring company performs, accelerates or guarantees it. What this page can do is state the published requirement accurately so you know which grades have to clear a floor. Tutoring is also not required for equivalency; the requirement is about grades held, not about how they were prepared for.

faqs.question: What should I ask our school before spending anything on exam preparation?
faqs.answer: Four questions, all short. Will marked mock scripts be returned or only grades. Are there subject clinics during study leave, and for which papers. Who can my child approach with a specific past-paper question once study leave starts. Is there a published revision timetable for the exam fortnight. The answers show exactly where the school's provision stops, and that gap is what a budget should cover. The commonest wasted purchase in this emirate is broad content coverage that the school was already providing.

faqs.question: Our child is already entered at Core when Extended looks achievable. What now?
faqs.answer: Check whether the entry window is still open with the school, because once entries are filed the tier is generally fixed for that series. Cambridge's March 2027 key dates illustrate the gap: final entries 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Where the entry is settled, the plan has to target the best outcome available on that paper, and the conversation shifts to whether a later series in that subject is worth entering. Where there is still time, diagnose first, then decide the tier, then enter.

faqs.question: Do visiting tutors cost more in Abu Dhabi than online tutors, and by how much?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one work at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150 to 450 for qualified to specialist online tuition, and visits are commonly quoted with a two-hour minimum so the journey is worth making. For a household in a peripheral community the practical gap is wider than the headline rates suggest, because the minimum session length is set by the drive rather than by what the work needs. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; this is delivered online.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched for a subject like Computer Science 0478?
faqs.answer: Expect one to two weeks for the narrower specialist subjects, against a few days for Mathematics, where cover is widest. If nobody who teaches your child's exact paper has hours in the window you need, you are told that rather than matched to whoever is free, and offered a named alternative with its trade-off: a specialist working Gulf Standard Time from another country, the subject split across two tutors with one shared progress record, the hours reallocated to a better-matched subject, or a later start with the right person.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share sessions to bring the cost down?
faqs.answer: Yes where they are in the same subject and tier and their current marks are in a similar range, which brings the cost per student well below the one-to-one band. Content and technique teach jointly without much loss. Marking does not, because two scripts fail in different places and each needs its own conversation, so marked work is returned individually. Where the two candidates' scripts show different faults, paying for two shorter individual sessions usually beats one shared longer one, even though the invoice looks worse.

faqs.question: Is there any point buying tutoring two weeks before the first IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: Only with a narrowed target. Two weeks will not add content and should not try to. What it can do is fix question selection and timing so the final questions stop being blank, rehearse command terms so full-knowledge answers stop scoring partial marks, build a salvage routine for a question that has gone wrong, and run short daily paper sections with immediate correction. Priced by the session rather than as a block, that is a reasonable purchase. Sold as a crash course that will transform a grade, it is not.

faqs.question: Do you publish your own hourly rate on this page?
faqs.answer: No. Every AED figure here is a market observation from October 2026, drawn from providers' published pages and from rate trackers, and labelled as such. Our own figure depends on the subject, the tier, the number of subjects and the hours, and it is quoted after the diagnostic because a quotation given before anyone has seen a marked paper is a guess with a decimal point. What you can hold us to beforehand is the shape: a free first lesson, a diagnostic with its own end point, and blocks with stated end dates.

abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Send the statement of entry first
abu-dhabi/igcse-exam-preparation.closingBody: The decision in front of you is not which tutor to hire. It is which two or three of your child's nine subjects deserve funded hours, and which five have to clear the Ministry of Education floor regardless. The statement of entry answers the first half of that question and a set of marked papers answers the second. Send the entry document and a note of which subjects worry you, take the free diagnostic lesson, and you will get back a ranking by recoverable marks per hour with the unfunded subjects named and the reason written down.
